body.text:
The Yogasūtras of Patañjali with Vācaspatimiśra's commentary Pātañjalabhāṣyavyākhyāyāṃ
      (a.k.a. Tattvavaiśāradī)
body.translated_text: The <s>Yogasūtras</s> of <s>Patañjali</s> with <s>Vācaspatimiśra</s>'s commentary: A Gloss on the <s>Pātañjalabhāṣya</s> (also known as <s>Tattvavaiśāradī</s>)

children.text: samādhipādaḥ prathamaḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Samādhipāda</s> (Chapter on Concentration), the first.

children.text: atha pātañjalasūtrāṇi/
children.translated_text: Now the <s>sūtras</s> of <s>Patañjali</s>.

children.text: atha yogānuśāsanam //1.1//
children.translated_text: Now, the instruction on <s>Yoga</s>. (1.1)

children.text:
namāmi jagadutpattihetave vṛṣaketave/ kleśakarmavipākādirahitāya hitāya ca //1// natvā patañjalim ṛṣiṃ vedavyāsena bhāṣite/
	  saṃkṣiptaspaṣṭabahvarthā bhāṣye vyākhyā vidhāsyate //2//
children.translated_text: I bow to the one who is the cause of the world's creation, who bears the bull as emblem, who is free from <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>karma</s> (actions), <s>vipāka</s> (fruitions), and so forth, and who is beneficial. (1) Having bowed to the sage <s>Patañjali</s>, a gloss — concise, clear, and rich in meaning — will be composed on the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) spoken by <s>Vedavyāsa</s>. (2)

children.text:
iha hi bhagavān patañjaliḥ prāripsitasya śāstrasya saṃkṣepatas tātparyārthaṃ
	  prekṣāvatpravṛttyaṅgaṃ śrotuś ca sukhāvabodhārtham ācikhyāsur ādāv idaṃ sūtraṃ racayāṃ
	  cakāra --- atha yogānuśāsanam/ tatra prathamāvayavam athaśabdaṃ vyācaṣṭe --- athety ayam
	  adhikārārthaḥ/ athaiṣa jyotir itivat, na tv ānantaryārthaḥ/ anuśāsanam iti hi śāstram
	  āhānuśiṣyate 'neneti vyutpattyā/ na cāsya śamadamādyanantaraṃ pravṛttir api tu
	  tattvajñānacikhyāpayiṣānantaram/ jijāsājñānayos tu syāt/ yathāmnāyate --- "tasmāc chānto
	  dānta uparatas titikṣuḥ samāhito bhūtvātmany evātmānaṃ paśyet"

bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣat
	  4.4.23
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 4.4.23

children.text:
iti/ śiṣyapraśnatapaścaraṇarasāyanādyupayogānantaryasya ca saṃbhave+api
	  nābhidhānaṃ, śiṣyapratītipravṛttyor anupayogāt prāmāṇikatve yogānuśāsanasya tadabhāve
	  'py upeyatvād aprāmāṇikatve ca tadbhāve+api heyatvāt/ etena tattvajñānacikhyāpayiṣayor
	  ānantaryābhidhānaṃ parāstam/ adhikārārthatve tu śāstreṇādhikriyamāṇasya
children.translated_text: And even though there is the possibility of sequence after the student's question, the practice of austerity, the use of elixirs, and the like, no mention [of them] is made, because they are of no use for the student's understanding and engagement — since if the instruction on <s>Yoga</s> is authoritative, it is to be adopted even in the absence of those [conditions], and if it is not authoritative, it is to be rejected even in the presence of those. By this, the mention of sequence after the desire to teach the knowledge of reality is set aside. When [the word 'atha'] has the sense of introducing the subject matter, the student is easily both informed and set in motion by the exposition of the purport of the entire treatise, since <s>Yoga</s> — which is being introduced —

children.text:
prastūyamānasya yogasyābhidhānāt sakalaśāstratātparyārthavyākhyānena śiṣyaḥ sukhenaiva
	  bodhitaś ca pravartitaś ca bhavatīti/ niḥśreyasasya hetuḥ samādhir iti hi
	  śrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇeṣu prasiddham/ nanu kiṃ
	  sarvasaṃdarbhagato+athaśabdo+adhikārārthaḥ, tathā sati "athāto brahmajijñāsā"
children.translated_text: is being presented. And <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is the cause of the highest good — this is well established in <s>Śruti</s> (revealed scripture), <s>Smṛti</s> (remembered tradition), <s>Itihāsa</s> (epic), and <s>Purāṇa</s> (ancient lore). Now, is the word 'atha' in every textual context used in the sense of introducing a subject? If so, there would be the same implication in 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>'

children.text: brahmasūtram 1.1.1
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.1

children.text: ityādāv api prasaṅga ity ata āha --- ayam iti/ nanu ---
children.translated_text: and so forth as well — hence he says 'this [particular one].' But —

Here, the blessed <s>Patañjali</s>, wishing to indicate concisely the purport of the treatise he intended to compose — as a basis for the engagement of the discerning, and for the easy comprehension of the listener — first composed this <s>sūtra</s>: 'Now, the instruction on <s>Yoga</s>.' Therein, he glosses the first component, the word 'atha' (now): 'This [word] atha serves the purpose of introducing the subject matter (<s>adhikāra</s>)' — as in 'Now, this is the light,' and not in the sense of sequence (<s>ānantarya</s>). The word '<s>anuśāsana</s>' (instruction) means a <s>śāstra</s> (treatise), by the etymological derivation 'that by which one is instructed.' And this [treatise] does not commence after [the practice of] tranquility (<s>śama</s>), restraint (<s>dama</s>), and the like, but rather after the desire to teach the knowledge of reality. For there may be a desire to know and a desire to teach. As it is recorded: 'Therefore, having become tranquil, controlled, withdrawn, patient, and concentrated, one should see the Self in the self alone.'

children.text: "hiraṇyagarbho yogasya vaktā nānyaḥ purātanaḥ"
children.translated_text: "<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is the expounder of <s>Yoga</s>; no other one more ancient [exists]."

children.text:
iti yogiyājñavalkyasmṛteḥ kathaṃ patañjaler yogaśāstrakartṛtvam ity āśaṅkya
	  sūtrakāreṇānuśāsanam ity uktam/ śiṣṭasya śāsanam anuśāsanam ity arthaḥ/ yadāyam
	  athaśabdo+adhikārārthas tadaiṣa vākyārthaḥ saṃpadyata ity āha --- yogānuśāsanaṃ śāstram
	  adhikṛtam iti/ nanu vyutpādyamānatayā yogo+atrādhikṛto na tu śāstram ity ata āha ---
	  veditavyam iti/ satyaṃ vyutpādyamānatayā yogaḥ prastutaḥ, sa tu tadviṣayeṇa śāstreṇa
	  karaṇena vyutpādyaḥ/ karaṇagocaraś ca vyutpādakasya vyāpāro na karmagocara iti
	  kartṛvyāpāravivakṣayā yogaviṣayasya śāstrasyādhikṛtatvaṃ veditavyam/
	  śāstravyāpāragocaratayā tu yoga evādhikṛta iti bhāvaḥ/ adhikārārthasya
	  cāthaśabdasyānyārthaṃ nīyamānodakumbhadarśanam iva śravaṇaṃ maṅgalāyāpi kalpata iti
	  mantavyam/ śabdasaṃdehanimittam arthasaṃdeham apanayati --- yogaḥ samādhir iti/ "yuja
	  samādhau"
dhātupāṭhaḥ 4
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātupāṭha</s> 4

children.text: ity asmād vyutpannaḥ samādhyartho na tu "yujir yoge"
children.translated_text: the meaning is <s>samādhi</s>, and not conjunction — as would follow from the root 'yujir' in the sense of joining,

children.text: dhātupāṭhaḥ 7
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātupāṭha</s> 7

children.text:
ity asmāt saṃyogārtha ity arthaḥ/ nanu samādhir api vakṣyamāṇasyāṅgino
	  yogasyāṅgam/ na cāṅgam evāṅgīty ata āha --- sa ca sārvabhaumaḥ/ cas tvartho+aṅgād
	  aṅginaṃ bhinatti/ bhūmayo+avasthā vakṣyamāṇā madhumatī madhupratīkā viśokā saṃskāraśeṣās
	  tāś cittasya, tāsu sarvāsu viditaḥ sārvabhaumaś cittavṛttinirodhalakṣaṇo yogaḥ/ tadaṅgaṃ
	  tu samādhir naivaṃbhūtaḥ/ vyutpattinimittamātrābhidhānaṃ caitad yogaḥ samādhir iti/
	  aṅgāṅginor abhedavivakṣāmātreṇa pravṛttinimittaṃ tu yogaśabdasya cittavṛttinirodha eveti
	  paramārthaḥ/ vṛttayo jñānāny ātmāśrayāṇy atas tannirodho 'py ātmāśraya eveti ye paśyanti
	  tannirāsāyāha --- cittasya dharma iti/ cittaśabdenāntaḥkaraṇaṃ buddhim upalakṣayati/ na
	  hi kūṭasthanityā citiśaktir apariṇāminī jñānadharmā bhavitum arhati buddhis tu bhaved
	  iti bhāvaḥ/ syād etat sārvabhaumaś ced yogo hanta bhoḥ kṣitamūḍhavikṣiptā api
	  cittabhūmayaḥ/ asti ca parasparāpekṣayā vṛttinirodho+apy āsv iti tatrāpi yogatvaprasaṅga
	  ity āśaṅkya heyopādeyabhūmīr upanyasyati ---
children.translated_text: — such is the meaning. Now, <s>samādhi</s> is also a limb (<s>aṅga</s>) of <s>Yoga</s> as the whole (<s>aṅgin</s>) to be described hereafter; and a limb is not the same as the whole — hence he says: 'And that is universal (<s>sārvabhauma</s>).' The word 'ca' (and) here has an adversative force, distinguishing the whole from the limb. The stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) are the states to be described: <s>Madhumatī</s>, <s>Madhupratīkā</s>, <s>Viśokā</s>, and <s>Saṃskāraśeṣā</s> — these are stages of the mind. <s>Yoga</s>, characterized as the cessation of the modifications (<s>vṛttis</s>) of the mind, is that which operates across all of them — hence 'universal.' <s>Samādhi</s> as a limb, however, is not of such nature. And this statement '<s>Yoga</s> is <s>samādhi</s>' is merely an indication of the etymological basis. The ultimate truth is that the ground for applying the word '<s>Yoga</s>' is nothing other than the cessation of the modifications of the mind — by virtue merely of the intention to express non-difference between limb and whole. To those who hold that modifications are cognitions (<s>jñānas</s>) belonging to the self, and hence that their cessation too belongs to the self — to refute them he says: '[it is] a property of the mind.' By the word 'mind' (<s>citta</s>) he designates the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), namely the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>). For the <s>citi-śakti</s> (power of consciousness), which is eternally immutable, incapable of transformation, cannot be a locus of cognition as a property; but the intellect can — such is the purport. One might object: if <s>Yoga</s> is universal, then the <s>kṣipta</s> (scattered), <s>mūḍha</s> (deluded), and <s>vikṣipta</s> (distracted) states of the mind are also stages, and there is a relative cessation of modifications in those too, leading to the undesirable consequence that those would also be <s>Yoga</s> — anticipating this, he sets forth the stages to be accepted and rejected:

children.text:
kṣiptam ityādi/ kṣiptaṃ sadaiva
	  rajasā teṣu teṣu viṣayeṣu kṣipyamāṇam atyantam asthiram/ mūḍhaṃ tu tamaḥsamudrekān
	  nidrāvṛttimat/ kṣiptād viśiṣṭaṃ vikṣiptam/ viśeṣo+asthemabahulasya kādācitkaḥ sthemā/ sā
	  cāsyāsthemabahulatā sāṃsiddhikī vā vakṣyamāṇavyādhistyānādyantarāyajanitā vā/ ekāgram
	  ekatānam/ niruddhasakalavṛttikaṃ saṃskāramātraśeṣaṃ cittaṃ niruddham/ tatra
	  kṣiptamūḍhayoḥ saty api parasparāpekṣayā vṛttinirodhe pāramparyeṇāpi
	  niḥśreyasahetubhāvābhāvāt tadupaghātakatvāc ca yogapakṣād dūrotsāritatvam iti na tayor
	  yogtvaṃ niṣiddham/ vikṣiptasya tu kādācitkasadbhūtaviṣayasthemaśālinaḥ saṃbhāvyeta
	  yogatvam iti niṣedhati/ tatra vikṣipte cetasi samādhiḥ kādācitkasadbhūtaviṣayasya
	  cittasya sthemā na yogapakṣe vartate/ kasmāt/ yatas tadvipakṣavikṣepopasarjanībhūtaḥ/
	  vipakṣavargāntargatasya hi svarūpam eva durlabhaṃ prāg eva kāryakaraṇaṃ na khalu
	  dahanāntargataṃ bījaṃ tricaturākṣaṇāvasthitam uptam apy aṅkurāya kalpata iti bhāvaḥ/
	  yadi vikṣepopasarjanībhūtaḥ samādhir na yogaḥ kas tarhīty ata āha --- yas tv ekāgre
	  cetasīti/ bhūtam iti samāropitam arthaṃ nivartayati/ nidrāvṛttir api svālambane tamasi
	  bhūte bhavaty ekāgrety ata uktam --- sad iti/ śobhanaṃ nitāntāvirbhūtaṃ sattvaṃ
	  tamaḥsamudrekas tv aśobhanas tasya kleśahetutvād iti/ dyotanaṃ hi tattvajñānam āgamād
	  vānumānād vā bhavad api parokṣarūpatayā na sākṣātkāravatīm avidyām ucchinatti
	  dvicandradiṅmohādiṣv anucchedakatvād ata āha --- preti/ prakāro hi prakarṣaṃ dyotayan
	  sākṣātkāraṃ sūcayati/ avidyāmūlatvād asmitādīnāṃ kleśānāṃ, vidyāyāś
	  cāvidyocchedarūpatvād vidyodaye cāvidyādikleśasamucchedo virodhitvāt kāraṇavināśāc cety
	  āha --- kṣiṇoti ceti/ ata eva karmarūpāṇi bandhanāni ślathayati/ karma cātrāpūrvam
	  abhimataṃ kārye kāraṇopacārāt/ ślathayati svakāryād avasādayati/ vakṣyati hi --- "sati
	  mūle tadvipākaḥ"
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṣipta</s>' (scattered) and so forth. The <s>kṣipta</s> [mind] is constantly scattered by <s>rajas</s> (activity) toward various objects, utterly unstable. The <s>mūḍha</s> (deluded) [mind] possesses the modification of sleep due to the excess of <s>tamas</s> (inertia). The <s>vikṣipta</s> (distracted) is superior to the scattered; its distinguishing feature is occasional stability in one whose instability is predominant. And this predominant instability of it is either natural or produced by the obstacles such as illness, languor, and so forth, which will be described. The <s>ekāgra</s> (one-pointed) is single-focused. The mind in the <s>niruddha</s> (arrested) state has all its modifications ceased, with only <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions) remaining. There, in the case of the scattered and deluded states, even though there is a relative cessation of modifications compared to each other, because there is no causal connection to the highest good even indirectly, and because they are destructive of it, they are removed far from the domain of <s>Yoga</s> — thus <s>Yoga</s> is denied in their case, not [merely] prohibited. But for the distracted state, which occasionally possesses real stability regarding an [actual] object, <s>Yoga</s> might be supposed — hence he negates it. In the distracted mind, <s>samādhi</s> — the occasional stability of the mind upon a real object — does not belong to the domain of <s>Yoga</s>. Why? Because it is subordinate to the distraction that is its opposite. For something included within the opposing camp can hardly maintain its own nature, let alone produce its effect — just as a seed placed within fire, remaining for three or four moments, even if planted does not conduce to a sprout — such is the purport. If <s>samādhi</s> subordinated to distraction is not <s>Yoga</s>, then what is? Hence he says: 'But that which [arises] in the one-pointed mind.' The word 'real' (<s>bhūta</s>) eliminates what is superimposed. Even the modification of sleep occurs in a one-pointed way with respect to its own support, namely <s>tamas</s> — therefore the word 'good' (<s>sat</s>) is used — meaning the good, fully manifest <s>sattva</s>; an excess of <s>tamas</s>, however, is not good, because it is the cause of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Illumination, which is the knowledge of reality, arising either from scripture or from inference, being of an indirect nature, does not cut off <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) as direct realization does — just as it does not remove [the illusion of] double moons, confusion of directions, etc. — hence he says 'pra' (intensely). The prefix 'pra' indicates intensity, thereby pointing to direct realization. Since <s>asmitā</s> (egoism) and other <s>kleśas</s> are rooted in <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and since <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) has the nature of destroying <s>avidyā</s>, upon the arising of <s>vidyā</s> there is the complete eradication of <s>avidyā</s> and the other <s>kleśas</s>, by virtue of opposition and the destruction of the cause — hence he says: 'and it destroys.' For this very reason it loosens the bonds that are in the form of <s>karma</s>. And <s>karma</s> here is understood as <s>apūrva</s> (the unseen potency), by metonymy of effect for cause. 'Loosens' means causes to decline from their effect. For it will be stated: 'When the root exists, there is the fruition of that.'

children.text: yogasūtram 2.13
children.translated_text: <s>Yogasūtra</s> 2.13

children.text:
iti/ kiṃ ca nirodham abhumukhaṃ karoty
	  abhimukhīkaroti/ sa ca saṃprajñātaś catuṣprakāra
children.translated_text: Moreover, it makes [the mind] face toward <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) — causes it to face cessation. And that [<s>samādhi</s>] is of four kinds when accompanied by discernment (<s>saṃprajñāta</s>),

children.text:
ity āha --- sa ceti/
	  asaṃprajñātam āha --- sarvavṛttīti/ rajastamomayī kila pramāṇādivṛttiḥ sāttvikīṃ vṛttim
	  upādāya saṃprajñāte niruddhā/ asaṃprajñāte tu sarvāsām eva nirodha ity arthaḥ/ tad iha
	  bhūmidvaye samāptā yā madhumatyādayo bhūmayas tāḥ sarvās tāsu viditaḥ sārvabhauma iti
	  siddham //1.1//
children.translated_text: hence he says: 'And that.' Regarding <s>asaṃprajñāta</s> (without discernment), he says: 'Of all modifications.' The modifications such as valid cognition and the rest, which are composed of <s>rajas</s> (activity) and <s>tamas</s> (inertia), are ceased in <s>saṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi] through the adoption of <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) modification. But in <s>asaṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi] there is the cessation of all [modifications] whatsoever — such is the meaning. Here then, in [these] two stages [of samādhi], all the stages such as <s>Madhumatī</s> and the rest are completed; [<s>Yoga</s>] which operates across all of them is 'universal' — thus it is established. (1.1)

Anticipating the objection from the <s>Yogiyājñavalkyasmṛti</s> — 'How can <s>Patañjali</s> be the author of the <s>Yoga</s> treatise?' — the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the sūtras) used the word '<s>anuśāsana</s>' (re-instruction). The meaning is: <s>anuśāsana</s> is the instruction (<s>śāsana</s>) of one who has been [already] instructed (<s>śiṣṭa</s>). When this word 'atha' has the sense of introducing the subject, this sentence-meaning becomes established — hence he says: 'The treatise that is the instruction on <s>Yoga</s> is introduced as the subject.' Now, it is <s>Yoga</s> that is introduced here as the thing to be explained, not the treatise — hence he says: 'it should be understood.' True, <s>Yoga</s> is presented as the thing to be explained, but it is to be explained by the treatise that has it as its subject — the treatise being the instrument. And the operation of the instrument falls within the scope of the instrument, not of the object; thus, with the intention of expressing the agent's operation, it should be understood that the treatise whose subject is <s>Yoga</s> is what is introduced. But in terms of being the object of the treatise's operation, it is <s>Yoga</s> itself that is introduced — such is the purport. And the hearing of the word 'atha,' which has the sense of introducing the subject, serves also as an auspicious opening — like seeing a water-pot being carried for another purpose — thus it should be considered. He removes the doubt about the meaning caused by a doubt about the word: '<s>Yoga</s> is <s>samādhi</s> (concentration).' Derived from the root 'yuja' in the sense of <s>samādhi</s>

children.text: yogaś cittavṛttinirodhaḥ //1.2//
children.translated_text: <s>Yoga</s> is the cessation of the modifications of the mind. (1.2)

children.text:
dvitīyaṃ sūtram avatārayati --- tasya lakṣaṇeti/ tasyeti pūrvasūtropāttaṃ dvividhaṃ
	    yogaṃ parāmṛśati --- yogaś cittavṛttinirodhaḥ/ nirudhyante yasmin pramāṇādivṛttayo
	    'vasthāviśeṣe cittasya so+avasthāviśeṣo yogaḥ/ nanu saṃprajñātasya yogasyāvyāpakatvād
	    alakṣaṇam idam/ aniruddhā hi tatra sāttvikī cittavṛttir ity ata āha ---
	    sarvaśabdāgrahaṇād iti/ yadi sarvacittavṛttinirodha ity ucyeta bhaved avyāpakaṃ
	    saṃprajñātasya/ kleśakarmavipākāśayaparipanthī cittavṛttinirodhas tu tam api saṃgṛhṇāti/
	    tatrāpi rājasatāmasacittavṛttinirodhāt tasya ca tadbhāvād ity arthaḥ/ kutaḥ punar ekasya
	    cittasya kṣiptādibhūmisaṃbandhaḥ kimarthaṃ caivamavasthasya cittasya vṛttayo niroddhavyā
	    ity āśaṅkya prathamaṃ tāvad avasthāsaṃbandhe hetum upanyasyati --- cittaṃ hīti/
	    prakhyāśīlatvāt sattvaguṇam/ pravṛttiśīlatvād rajoguṇam/ sthitiśīlatvāt tamoguṇam/
	    prakhyāgrahaṇam upalakṣaṇārtham/ tenānye+api sāttvikāḥ prasādalāghavaprītyādayaḥ
	    sūcyante/ pravṛttyā ca paritāpaśokādayā rājasāḥ/ pravṛttivirodhī tamovṛttidharmaḥ
	    sthitiḥ/ sthitigrahaṇād gauravāvaraṇadainyādaya upalakṣyante/ etad uktaṃ bhavati ---
	    ekam api cittaṃ triguṇanirmitatayā guṇānāṃ ca vaiṣamyeṇa parasparavimardavaicitryād
	    vicitrapariṇāmaṃ sad anekāvastham upapadyata iti/ kṣiptādyā eva cittasya bhūmīr
	    yathāsaṃbhavam avāntarāvasthābhedavatīr ādarśayati --- prakhyārūpaṃ hīti/ cittarūpeṇa
	    pariṇataṃ sattvaṃ cittasattvam/ tad evaṃ prakhyārūpatayā sattvaprādhānyaṃ cittasya
	    darśitam/ tatra citte sattvāt kiṃcid ūne rajastamasī

yadā mithaḥ same ca
	    bhavatas tadaiśvaryaṃ ca viṣayāś ca śabdādayas tāny eva priyāṇi yasya tat tathoktam/
	    sattvaprādhānyāt khalu cittaṃ tattve praṇidhitsad api tattvasya tamasā pihitatvād
	    aṇimādikam aiśvaryam eva tattvam abhimanyamānaṃ tat praṇidhitsati praṇidhatte ca kṣaṇam/
	    atha rajasā kṣipyamāṇaṃ tatrāpy alabdhasthitiṃ tatpriyamātraṃ bhavati/ śabdādiṣu punar
	    asya svarasavāhī premā nirūḍha eva/ tad anena vikṣiptaṃ cittam uktam/ kṣiptaṃ cittaṃ
	    darśayan mūḍham api sūcayati --- tad eva tamaseti/ yadā hi tamo rajo vijitya prasṛtaṃ
	    tadā cittasattvāvarakatamaḥsamutsāraṇe 'śaktatvād rajasas tamaḥsthagitaṃ cittam
	    adharmādy upagacchati/ ajñānaṃ ca viparyayajñānam/ abhāvapratyayālambanaṃ ca nidrājñānam
	    uktam/ tataś ca mūḍhāvasthāpi sūciteti/ anaiśvaryaṃ sarvatrecchāpratīghātaḥ/
	    adharmādivyāptaṃ cittaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ/ yadā tu tad eva cittasattvam āvirbhūtasattvam
	    apagatatamaḥpaṭalaṃ sarajaskaṃ bhavati tadā dharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryāṇy upagacchatīty
	    āha --- prakṣīṇetyādi/ mohas tamas tad eva cāvaraṇaṃ prakarṣeṇa kṣīṇaṃ yasya tat
	    tathoktam/ ata eva sarvato viśeṣāviśeṣaliṅgamātrāliṅgapuruṣeṣu pradyotamānam/ tathāpi na
	    dharmāyaiśvaryāya ca kalpate pravṛttyabhāvād ity ata āha --- anuviddhaṃ rajomātrayā/
	    rajasaḥ pravartakatvād asti dharmādipravṛttir ity arthaḥ/ tad anena
	    saṃprajñātasamādhisaṃpannayor madhubhūmikaprajñājyotiṣor madhyamayor yoginoś
	    cittasattvaṃ saṃgṛhītam/ saṃpraty atikrāntabhāvanīyasya dhyāyinaś caturthasya
	    cittāvasthām āha --- tad eva cittaṃ rajoleśān malād apetam ata eva svarūpapratiṣṭham/
	    abhyāsavairāgyapuṭapākaprabandhavidhūtarajastamomalasya hi buddhisattvatapanīyasya
	    svarūpapratiṣṭhasya viṣayendriyapratyāhṛtasyānavasitādhikāratayā ca kāryakāriṇo
	    vivekakhyātiḥ paraṃ kāryam avaśiṣyata ity āha --- sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātraṃ cittaṃ
	    dharmameghadhyānopagaṃ bhavati/ dharmameghaś ca vakṣyate/ atraiva yogijanaprasiddhim āha
	    --- tad iti/ sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātraṃ cittaṃ dharmameghaparyantaṃ paraṃ
	    prasaṃkhyānam ity ācakṣate dhyāyinaḥ/ cittasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ ca dharmadharmiṇor
	    abhedavivakṣayā draṣṭavyam/ vivekakhyāter
children.translated_text: when both are mutually equal, then there is mastery (<s>aiśvarya</s>), and the objects such as sound, etc. — those very ones are dear to it; thus it is stated. Indeed, the mind, by the predominance of <s>sattva</s>, though aspiring toward the truth (<s>tattva</s>), because <s>tattva</s> is concealed by <s>tamas</s>, considers supernatural powers (<s>aṇimā</s>, etc.) as the very <s>tattva</s>, aspires toward and attains them for a moment. Then, being agitated by <s>rajas</s>, unable to gain stability even in those [powers], it becomes merely fond of them. As for sounds and other [sense objects], its spontaneous love for them is deeply rooted indeed. By this, the distracted (<s>vikṣipta</s>) mind is described. Showing the distracted mind, he also indicates the deluded (<s>mūḍha</s>) [state] — 'that very [mind], by <s>tamas</s>.' For when <s>tamas</s>, having overcome <s>rajas</s>, has spread, then, unable to dispel the <s>tamas</s> that covers the <s>sattva</s> of the mind, <s>rajas</s> being obscured by <s>tamas</s>, the mind proceeds toward <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) and the like. And ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) is erroneous knowledge (<s>viparyaya</s>). And sleep-knowledge (<s>nidrājñāna</s>) is said to have the absence of experience as its object. Therefore the deluded state is also indicated. Non-mastery (<s>anaiśvarya</s>) is the frustration of desire in all things. The meaning is: the mind becomes pervaded by <s>adharma</s> and the like. But when that very mind-<s>sattva</s> has its <s>sattva</s> manifested, the veil of <s>tamas</s> removed, and possesses [only residual] <s>rajas</s>, then it attains <s>dharma</s> (virtue), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and <s>aiśvarya</s> (mastery) — he says 'when diminished' (<s>prakṣīṇa</s>), etc. <s>Moha</s> (delusion) is <s>tamas</s>; that itself is the obscuration; one in whom it is greatly diminished — he is so called. Hence, shining forth everywhere in the <s>viśeṣa</s> (specific), <s>aviśeṣa</s> (non-specific), <s>liṅgamātra</s> (the mere mark), <s>aliṅga</s> (the unmanifest), and <s>Puruṣa</s>. Yet it is not fit for <s>dharma</s> and <s>aiśvarya</s> because of the absence of activity — therefore he says 'permeated by a trace of <s>rajas</s> only.' The meaning is: since <s>rajas</s> is the impeller, there is activity toward <s>dharma</s>, etc. By this, the mind-<s>sattva</s> of the two intermediate <s>yogins</s> — those endowed with <s>saṃprajñāta-samādhi</s>, the <s>madhubhūmika</s> (honey-staged) and the <s>prajñājyotiṣ</s> (light-of-wisdom) — is included. Now he describes the state of the mind of the fourth <s>yogin</s>, the meditator who has transcended [all that is] to be cultivated — 'that very mind, freed from the stain of even a trace of <s>rajas</s>, therefore established in its own nature (<s>svarūpapratiṣṭha</s>).' For when the impurity of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> has been purged through the successive refinement of practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), like gold refined in the furnace, and the intellect-<s>sattva</s> is established in its own nature, withdrawn from objects and senses, and having no remaining jurisdiction for action — then discriminative discernment (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) remains as the final function — he says 'the mind, consisting only of the discernment of the distinction between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, becomes fit for the <s>dharmamegha</s> (cloud of <s>dharma</s>) meditation.' And <s>dharmamegha</s> will be explained [later]. He states the well-known [designation] among <s>yogins</s> — 'that' (<s>tat</s>). The mind consisting only of the discernment of the distinction between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, culminating in <s>dharmamegha</s>, is called 'supreme <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (meditative discernment)' by the meditators. And the co-referentiality of the mind [with both <s>dharma</s> and <s>dharmin</s>] should be understood as an expression of non-difference. Of <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative discernment),

children.text:
hānahetuṃ citiśakteś copādānahetuṃ
	    nirodhasamādhim avatārayituṃ citiśakteḥ sādhutām asādhutāṃ ca vivekakhyāter darśayati
	    --- citiśaktir ityādi/ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakatvam aśuddhiḥ/ sukhamohāv api hi vivekinaṃ
	    duḥkhākurutaḥ/ ato duḥkhavad dheyau/ tathā cātisundaram apy antavad dunoti/ tena tad api
	    heyam eva vivekinaḥ/ seyam aśuddhir antaś ca citiśaktau puruṣe na sta ity uktam ---
	    śuddhā cānantā ceti/ nanu sukhaduḥkhamohātmakaśabdādīn iyaṃ cetayamānā tadākārāpannā
	    kathaṃ viśuddhā tadākāraparigrahaparivarjane ca kurvatī katham anantety ata uktam ---
	    darśitaviṣayeti/ darśito viṣayaḥ śabdādir yasyai sā tathoktā/ bhaved etad evaṃ yadi
	    buddhivac citiśaktir viṣayākāratām āpadyeta, kiṃ tu buddhir eva viṣayākāreṇa pariṇatā
	    saty atadākārāyai citiśaktyai viṣayam ādarśayati/ tataḥ puruṣaś cetayata ity ucyate/
	    nanu viṣayākārāṃ buddhim anārūḍhāyāś citiśakteḥ kathaṃ viṣayavedanaṃ viṣayārohe vā
	    kathaṃ na tadākārāpattir ity ata uktam --- apratisaṃkrameti/ pratisaṃkramaḥ saṃcāraḥ/ sa
	    citer nāstīty arthaḥ/ sa eva kuto+asyā nāstīty ata uktam --- apariṇāminīti/ na cites
	    trividho 'pi dharmalakṣaṇāvasthālakṣaṇaḥ pariṇāmo+asti/ yena kriyārūpeṇa pariṇatā satī
	    buddhisaṃyogena pariṇameta citiśaktiḥ/ asaṃkrāntāyā api viṣayasaṃvedanam upapādayiṣyate/
	    tat siddhaṃ citiśaktiḥ śobhaneti/ vivekakhyātis tu buddhisattvātmikāśobhanety uktam ---
	    ataś citiśakter viparīteti/ yadā ca vivekakhyātir api heyā tadā kaiva kathā
	    vṛttyantarāṇāṃ doṣabahulānām iti bhāvaḥ/ tatas taddhetor nirodhasamādher avatāro yujyata
	    ity āha --- atas tasyām iti/ jñānaprasādamātreṇa hi pareṇa vairāgyeṇa vivekakhyātim api
	    niruṇaddhīty arthaḥ/ atha niruddhāśeṣavṛttiṃ cittaṃ kīdṛśam ity ata āha --- tadavastham
	    ityādi/ sa nirodho+avasthā yasya tat tathoktam/ nirodhasya svarūpam āha --- sa nirbīja
	    iti/ kleśasahitaḥ karmāśayo jātyāyurbhogabījaṃ tasmān nirgata iti nirbījaḥ/ asyaiva
	    yogijanaprasiddhām anvarthasaṃjñām ādarśayati --- na tatreti/ upasaṃharati --- dvividhaḥ
	    sa yogaś cittavṛttinirodha iti //1.2//
children.translated_text: to introduce <s>nirodha-samādhi</s> (cessation-absorption) as the cause of the abandonment [of <s>vivekakhyāti</s>] and as the cause of the reception of <s>citiśakti</s> (the power of consciousness), he shows the excellence of <s>citiśakti</s> and the deficiency of <s>vivekakhyāti</s> — '<s>citiśakti</s>' etc. Consisting of pleasure, pain, and delusion (<s>moha</s>) is impurity. For even pleasure and delusion torment the discerning one. Therefore, like pain, they are to be abandoned. And thus, even what is supremely beautiful but finite causes suffering. Hence that too is to be abandoned by the discerning one. This impurity and finitude do not exist in <s>citiśakti</s>, the <s>Puruṣa</s> — it is said: 'pure and infinite.' [Objection:] But this [<s>citiśakti</s>], cognizing objects such as sound, etc., which consist of pleasure, pain, and delusion, and assuming their forms — how is it pure? And if it refrains from grasping their forms — how is it infinite? Therefore it is said: 'one for whom the object has been shown' (<s>darśitaviṣayā</s>). One for whom the object — sound, etc. — has been shown [by <s>buddhi</s>] — she is so called. It would be so if, like <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>citiśakti</s> were to assume the form of objects. But it is <s>buddhi</s> itself that, having transformed into the form of objects, shows the object to <s>citiśakti</s>, which has not assumed that form. Hence it is said: '<s>Puruṣa</s> cognizes.' [Objection:] But how does <s>citiśakti</s>, not having mounted [upon] the object-formed <s>buddhi</s>, experience objects? And if it does mount [upon them], how is there no assumption of their form? Therefore it is said: 'without transference' (<s>apratisaṃkrama</s>). <s>Pratisaṃkrama</s> is transference; that does not exist for <s>citi</s> (consciousness) — such is the meaning. Why does it not exist for it? Therefore it is said: 'because it is non-transforming' (<s>apariṇāminī</s>). For <s>citi</s>, there is no threefold transformation — of <s>dharma</s> (property), <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (characteristic), or <s>avasthā</s> (state) — by which <s>citiśakti</s>, having transformed into the form of action, could further transform through conjunction with <s>buddhi</s>. Yet the experience of objects even without transference will be established [later]. Thus it is proven: <s>citiśakti</s> is excellent (<s>śobhana</s>). But <s>vivekakhyāti</s>, consisting of <s>buddhi-sattva</s>, is not excellent — it is said: 'therefore, opposite to <s>citiśakti</s>.' And when even <s>vivekakhyāti</s> is to be abandoned, what need is there to speak of other modifications, which are full of defects? — such is the purport. Therefore, the introduction of <s>nirodha-samādhi</s>, which is the cause of that [abandonment], is appropriate — he says 'therefore, in that' (<s>atas tasyām</s>). The meaning is: by mere clarity of knowledge (<s>jñānaprasāda</s>), through supreme dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), one ceases even <s>vivekakhyāti</s>. Now, what is the mind like when all modifications have been ceased? Therefore he says 'that-stated' (<s>tadavastham</s>), etc. That which has cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) as its state — it is so called. He states the essential nature of <s>nirodha</s> — 'that is seedless' (<s>sa nirbījaḥ</s>). The repository of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāśaya</s>) accompanied by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) is the seed of birth, lifespan, and enjoyment; having gone forth from that — [the state is] seedless (<s>nirbīja</s>). He shows the well-known synonym among <s>yogins</s> for this very [state] — 'not therein' (<s>na tatra</s>). He summarizes — 'twofold is that <s>yoga</s>, [which is] the cessation of mental modifications.' //1.2//

He introduces the second <s>sūtra</s> — 'its definition' (<s>tasya lakṣaṇa</s>). By 'its' (<s>tasya</s>) he refers back to the twofold <s>yoga</s> mentioned in the preceding <s>sūtra</s> — '<s>Yoga</s> is the cessation of the modifications of the mind (<s>yogaś cittavṛttinirodhaḥ</s>).' The particular state of the mind in which the modifications such as valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), etc., are ceased — that particular state is <s>yoga</s>. [Objection:] Since this does not apply to <s>saṃprajñāta</s> (cognitive) <s>yoga</s>, this definition is too narrow. For in that [state], the <s>sāttvika</s> (lucid) modification of the mind is not ceased. Therefore he says — 'because of the absence of the word "all" (<s>sarva</s>).' If it were said 'cessation of all mental modifications,' then it would be inapplicable to <s>saṃprajñāta</s> [yoga]. But 'the cessation of mental modifications that are obstructed by <s>kleśa</s> (afflictions), <s>karma</s> (action), <s>vipāka</s> (fruition), and <s>āśaya</s> (latent deposit)' — that includes [saṃprajñāta yoga] as well. For in that [state] too, the <s>rājasa</s> (active) and <s>tāmasa</s> (inert) mental modifications are ceased, and it [saṃprajñāta yoga] partakes of that [cessation] — such is the meaning. Now, how does one mind have connection with the <s>kṣipta</s> (distracted) and other stages? And for what purpose should the modifications of a mind in such states be ceased? — anticipating [these questions], he first sets forth the reason for the connection with [various] states — 'For the mind' (<s>cittaṃ hi</s>). On account of its nature of luminosity (<s>prakhyā</s>), it partakes of <s>sattva-guṇa</s>. On account of its nature of activity, it partakes of <s>rajo-guṇa</s>. On account of its nature of inertia (<s>sthiti</s>), it partakes of <s>tamo-guṇa</s>. The mention of 'luminosity' (<s>prakhyā</s>) is by way of indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>); thereby other <s>sāttvika</s> [properties] such as clarity, lightness, joy, etc., are also suggested. And through activity, [properties] such as agitation, grief, etc., which are <s>rājasa</s>, [are indicated]. The <s>dharma</s> (property) of the <s>tamas</s>-modification opposing activity is inertia (<s>sthiti</s>). By the mention of 'inertia,' heaviness, obstruction, wretchedness, and the like are also indicated. The purport is this: even a single mind, being fashioned by the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), and because of the mutual conflict and variety arising from the imbalance of the <s>guṇas</s>, undergoes manifold transformations and is found to have multiple states. He shows the stages of the mind — <s>kṣipta</s> (distracted), etc. — with their respective sub-states as applicable — 'For luminosity-form' (<s>prakhyārūpaṃ hi</s>). <s>Sattva</s> transformed in the form of mind is the 'mind-<s>sattva</s>' (<s>cittasattva</s>). Thus, by its luminous form, the predominance of <s>sattva</s> in the mind is shown. Now, in the mind, when <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> are somewhat less than <s>sattva</s> —

children.text: tadā draṣṭuḥ svarūpe+avasthānam //1.3//
children.translated_text: 'Then there is the abiding of the Seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>) in its own nature.' //1.3//

children.text:
saṃpraty uttarasūtram avatārayituṃ codayati --- tadavasthe cetasīti/ kim ākṣepe/
	    tattadākārapariṇatabuddhibodhātmā khalv ayaṃ puruṣaḥ sadānubhūyate na tu
	    buddhibodharahito+ato 'sya puruṣasya buddhibodhaḥ svabhāvaḥ savitur iva prakāśaḥ/ na ca
	    saṃskāraśeṣe cetasi so+asti/ na ca svabhāvam apahāya bhāvo vartitum arhatīti bhāvaḥ/
	    syād etat/ saṃskāraśeṣām api buddhiṃ kasmāt puruṣo na budhyata ity ata āha ---
	    viṣayābhāvād iti/ na buddhimātraṃ puruṣasya viṣayo+api tu puruṣārthavatī buddhiḥ/
	    vivekakhyātiviṣayabhogau ca puruṣārthau/ tau ca niruddhāvasthāyāṃ na sta iti siddho
	    viṣayābhāva ity arthaḥ/ sūtreṇa pariharati --- tadā draṣṭuḥ svarūpe 'vasthānam/ svarūpa
	    ity āropitaṃ śāntaghoramūḍhasvarūpaṃ nivartayati/ puruṣasya hi caitanyaṃ svarūpam
	    anaupādhikaṃ na tu buddhibodhaḥ śāntādirūpa aupādhiko hi sa sphaṭikasyeva
	    svabhāvasvacchadhavalasya japākusumasaṃnidhānopādhir aruṇimā/ na copādhinivṛttāv
	    upahitanivṛttir atiprasaṅgād iti bhāvaḥ/ svarūpasya cābhede+api bhedaṃ
	    vikalpyādhikaraṇabhāva ukta iti/ ayam evārtho bhāṣyakṛtā dyotyate ---
	    svarūpapratiṣṭheti/ tadānīṃ nirodhāvasthāyāṃ na vyutthānāvasthāyām iti bhāvaḥ/ syād etad
	    vyutthānāvasthāyām apratiṣṭhitā svarūpe citiśaktir nirodhāvasthāyāṃ pratitiṣṭhantī
	    pariṇāminī syāt/ vyutthāne vā svarūpapratiṣṭhāne vyutthānanirodhayor aviśeṣa ity ata āha
	    --- vyutthānacitte tv iti/ na jātu kūṭasthanityā citiśaktiḥ svarūpāc cyavate tena yathā
	    nirodhe tathaiva vyutthāne+api/ na khalu śuktikāyāḥ pramāṇaviparyayajñānagocaratve+api
	    svarūpodayavyayau bhavataḥ/ pratipattā tu tathābhūtam apy atathātvenābhimanyate/
	    nirodhasamādhim apekṣya saṃprajñāto+api vyutthānam eveti //1.3//
children.translated_text: Now, in order to introduce the next <s>sūtra</s>, he raises [an objection]: 'when the mind is in that state' — what is the objection? This <s>puruṣa</s> (Self), whose nature is the awareness of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) transformed into various forms, is always experienced; but [he is] never [experienced as] devoid of <s>buddhi</s>-awareness. Therefore, <s>buddhi</s>-awareness is the essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of this <s>puruṣa</s>, just as luminosity is [the essential nature] of the sun. And in the mind that is a mere residue of <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions), that [<s>buddhi</s>-awareness] does not exist. And a thing cannot continue to exist while abandoning its essential nature — such is the purport. One might say: why does the <s>puruṣa</s> not cognize even the <s>buddhi</s> that is a mere residue of <s>saṃskāras</s>? To this he replies: 'due to the absence of the object' — not mere <s>buddhi</s> is the object of <s>puruṣa</s>, but rather <s>buddhi</s> that serves the <s>puruṣa</s>'s purpose. And <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative discernment) and <s>bhoga</s> (experience) [of objects] are the <s>puruṣa</s>'s purposes. And in the state of cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), these do not exist — thus the absence of the object is established. This is the meaning. He resolves [the objection] with the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Then there is the abiding of the seer in [its] own form' (<s>tadā draṣṭuḥ svarūpe 'vasthānam</s>). The word 'own form' (<s>svarūpa</s>) removes the superimposed nature of calm (<s>śānta</s>), terrifying (<s>ghora</s>), and deluded (<s>mūḍha</s>). For the essential nature of <s>puruṣa</s> is consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>), unconditioned — not <s>buddhi</s>-awareness, which has the form of calm, etc., and is conditioned. For that [<s>buddhi</s>-awareness] is like the redness of a crystal — which is naturally clear and white — that is a condition caused by the proximity of a hibiscus flower. And upon the removal of the conditioning, there is no removal of the conditioned [appearance] — since that would lead to overextension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>). This is the purport. And although there is no difference in the essential nature, difference [is spoken of] by way of the substratum, which is conceptually imagined — thus it has been said. This very meaning is indicated by the commentator (<s>bhāṣyakṛt</s>): 'abiding in its own form' — then, in the state of cessation, not in the state of emergence (<s>vyutthāna</s>). This is the purport. One might object: the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>), not established in its own form in the state of emergence, when becoming established in the state of cessation, would be subject to transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>). Or, if there is abiding in its own form even in emergence, then there would be no difference between emergence and cessation. To this he replies: 'But in the emergent mind...' The eternally unchanging (<s>kūṭasthanitya</s>) power of consciousness never deviates from its own form. Therefore, just as in cessation, so too in emergence. Indeed, even though a mother-of-pearl is the object of both valid knowledge and erroneous knowledge, there is no arising or passing away of its own form. But the perceiver, though [the object] is of such a nature, apprehends it as being otherwise. Even the cognitive state of <s>saṃprajñāta</s> [concentration] is 'emergence' in relation to the cessation-<s>samādhi</s>. (1.3)

children.text: vṛttisārūpyam itaratra //1.4//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 1.4:] <s>Vṛttisārūpyam itaratra</s> — 'Otherwise, [there is] conformity with the modifications.' (1.4)

children.text:
sūtrāntaram avatārayituṃ pṛcchati --- kathaṃ tarhīti/ yadi tathā bhavantī na tathā kena
	    tarhi prakāreṇa prakāśata ity arthaḥ/ hetupadam adhyāhṛtya sūtraṃ paṭhati ---
	    darśitaviṣayatvād vṛttisārūpyam itaratra/ itaratra vyutthāne yāś cittavṛttayaḥ
	    śāntaghoramūḍhās tā evāviśiṣṭā

abhinnā vṛttayo yasya puruṣasya sa tathoktaḥ/
	    sārūpyam ity atra saśabda ekaparyāyaḥ/ etad uktaṃ bhavati --- japākusumasphaṭikayor iva
	    buddhipuruṣayoḥ saṃnidhānād abhedagrahe buddhivṛttīḥ puruṣe samāropya śānto+asmi
	    duḥkhito+asmi mūḍho+asmīty adhyavasyati/ yathā maline darpaṇatale pratibimbitaṃ mukhaṃ
	    malinam āropya śocaty ātmānaṃ malino+asmīti/ yady api puruṣasamāropo+api
	    śabdādivijñānavad buddhivṛttir yady api ca prākṛtatvenācidrūpatayānubhāvyas tathāpi
	    buddheḥ puruṣatvam āpādayan puruṣavṛttir ivānubhava ivāvabhāsate/ tathā cāyam
	    aviparyayo+apy ātmā viparyayavān ivābhoktāpi bhokteva vivekakhyātirahito+api tatsahita
	    iva vivekakhyātyā prakāśate/ etac ca "citer apratisaṃkramāyās tadākārāpattau
	    svabuddhisaṃvedanam"
children.translated_text: modifications belonging to which <s>puruṣa</s>, that [<s>puruṣa</s>] is spoken of thus [as having that form]. 'Conformity' (<s>sārūpya</s>) — here the prefix 'sa' is used as a synonym [for sameness of form]. What is meant is this: just as [there is] non-apprehension of difference between a hibiscus flower and a crystal [placed near it], so from the proximity of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and <s>puruṣa</s>, superimposing the modifications of <s>buddhi</s> onto the <s>puruṣa</s>, one determines: 'I am calm,' 'I am suffering,' 'I am deluded.' Just as one grieves at seeing a face reflected in a dirty mirror-surface, superimposing the dirt upon it: 'I am dirty.' Although the superimposition on the <s>puruṣa</s> is also a modification of <s>buddhi</s>, like the cognition of sound, etc.; and although, being a product of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), it is of non-conscious nature and thus [merely] to be experienced — nevertheless, attributing <s>puruṣa</s>-hood to <s>buddhi</s>, it appears as if it were a modification of the <s>puruṣa</s>, as if it were experience. And thus this Self, though not [truly] subject to error, appears as if subject to error; though not [truly] an experiencer, appears as if an experiencer; though devoid of <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative discernment), appears as if endowed with it — [all this] is illuminated by <s>vivekakhyāti</s>. And this [will be established in the <s>sūtra</s>]: 'For the non-migrating power of consciousness (<s>citi</s>), in the assumption of that form, [there is] the awareness of its own <s>buddhi</s>'

children.text: yogasūtram 4.22
children.translated_text: <s>Yogasūtra</s> 4.22

children.text:
ity atra "sattvapuruṣayor atyantāsaṃkīrṇayoḥ
	    pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ"
children.translated_text: and in [the <s>sūtra</s>]: 'For <s>sattva</s> (pure being) and <s>puruṣa</s>, which are absolutely unmixed, the non-distinction of cognition is [the cause of] experience (<s>bhoga</s>)'

children.text: yogasūtram 3.35
children.translated_text: <s>Yogasūtra</s> 3.35

children.text:
ity atra copapādayiṣyate/ etac ca matāntare+api
	    siddham ity āha --- tathā ceti/ pañcaśikhācāryasya sūtram "ekam eva darśanaṃ khyātir eva
	    darśanam" iti/ nanu katham ekaṃ darśanaṃ yāvatā buddheḥ śabdādiviṣayā vivekaviṣayā ca
	    vṛttiḥ prākṛtatayā jaḍatvenānubhāvyā darśanaṃ tato+anyat puruṣasya caitanyam anubhavo
	    darśanam ity ata āha --- khyātir eva darśanam iti/ udayavyayadharmiṇīṃ vṛttiṃ khyātiṃ
	    laukikīm abhipretyaitad uktam --- ekam eveti/ caitanyaṃ tu puruṣasya svabhāvo na
	    khyāteḥ/ tat tu na lokapratyakṣagocaro+api tv āgamānumānagocara ity arthaḥ/ tad anena
	    vyutthānāvasthāyāṃ mūlakāraṇam avidyāṃ darśayatā taddhetukaḥ saṃyogo bhogahetuḥ
	    svasvāmibhāvo+api sūcita iti tam upapādayann āha --- cittaṃ svaṃ bhavati puruṣasya
	    svāmina iti saṃbandhaḥ/ nanu cittajanitam upakāraṃ bhajamāno hi cetanaś cittasyeśitā/ na
	    cāsya tajjanitopakārasaṃbhavas tadasaṃbandhād anupakāryatvāt
	    tatsaṃyogatadupakārabhāgitve pariṇāmaprasaṅgād ity ata āha --- ayaskāntamaṇikalpaṃ
	    saṃnidhimātropakāri dṛśyatveneti/ na puruṣasaṃyuktaṃ cittam api tu tatsaṃnihitam/
	    saṃnidhiś ca puruṣasya na deśataḥ kālato vā tadasaṃyogāt kiṃ tu yogyatālakṣaṇaḥ/ asti ca
	    puruṣasya bhoktṛśaktiś cittasya bhogaśaktiḥ/ tad uktam --- dṛśyatveneti/
	    śabdādyākārapariṇatasya bhogyatvenety arthaḥ/ bhogaś ca yady api śabdādyākārā vṛttiś
	    cittasya dharmas tathāpi cittacaitanyayor abhedasamāropād vṛttisārūpyāt puruṣasyety
	    uktam/ tasmāc cittenāsaṃyoge+api tajjanitopakārabhāgitā puruṣasyāpariṇāmitā
children.translated_text: — [these will be] established there. And this is established even in another philosophical system — thus he says: 'And so...' The <s>sūtra</s> of the teacher <s>Pañcaśikha</s> is: 'Seeing is one alone; discernment (<s>khyāti</s>) alone is seeing.' Now, how can seeing be one, since <s>buddhi</s>'s modification directed at sound, etc., and at discrimination, being a product of <s>Prakṛti</s>, is insentient and thus [merely] to be experienced, while the <s>puruṣa</s>'s consciousness — experience — is a different kind of seeing? To this he replies: '<s>khyāti</s> alone is seeing.' Intending the worldly <s>khyāti</s> (discernment), which is characterized by arising and passing away, this was said: 'one alone.' But the consciousness of the <s>puruṣa</s> is its essential nature, not [a property] of <s>khyāti</s>. And that [consciousness] is not an object of worldly perception, but rather an object of scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and inference (<s>anumāna</s>). This is the meaning. By thus showing <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) as the root cause in the state of emergence, the conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) caused by it — the cause of experience, the relation of property and owner (<s>svasvāmibhāva</s>) — is also indicated. Establishing that, he says: 'The mind (<s>citta</s>) is the property (<s>sva</s>), the <s>puruṣa</s> is the owner (<s>svāmin</s>)' — this is the connection. Now, one who is conscious, enjoying the benefit produced by the mind, is the mind's master. But it is impossible for him to receive a benefit produced by it, because of the absence of [real] connection with it, because he is not [truly] affected by it — [for] if he were to partake of conjunction with it and of its benefits, there would be the unwanted consequence of transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>). To this he replies: '[The mind] is like a magnet-stone, beneficial merely by proximity, by being the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>).' The mind is not conjoined with the <s>puruṣa</s> but merely proximate to it. And the proximity of the <s>puruṣa</s> is not spatial or temporal — since there is no [real] conjunction with it — but rather is characterized by fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>). And the <s>puruṣa</s> has the power of being the experiencer; the mind has the power of being the experienced. Thus it is said: 'by being the seen' — meaning: by being the object of experience, being transformed into the form of sound, etc. And although experience (<s>bhoga</s>) — the modification in the form of sound, etc. — is a property of the mind, nevertheless, due to the superimposition of non-difference between mind and consciousness, it is said to belong to the <s>puruṣa</s> through 'conformity with the modifications.' Therefore, even without conjunction with the mind, the partaking of the benefit produced by it [belongs to] the <s>puruṣa</s> — and [his] non-transformation

children.text:
ceti siddham/ nanu svasvāmisaṃbandho bhogahetur avidyānimitto 'vidyā tu kiṃnimittā na
	    khalv animittaṃ kāryam utpadyate/ yathāhuḥ ---
children.translated_text: is also established. Now, the property-owner relation is the cause of experience; it is caused by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). But what is the cause of <s>avidyā</s>? For surely an effect does not arise without a cause. As they say:

In order to introduce the next <s>sūtra</s>, he asks: 'How then?' — if [the <s>puruṣa</s>] is of such a nature but does not [appear] so, then in what manner does it manifest? This is the meaning. Supplying the causal word, he reads the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Because the object has been shown, [there is] conformity with the modifications, otherwise' — 'otherwise,' i.e., in emergence (<s>vyutthāna</s>), the mental modifications (<s>cittavṛttis</s>) — calm (<s>śānta</s>), terrifying (<s>ghora</s>), and deluded (<s>mūḍha</s>) — those very undifferentiated

children.text: svapnādivad avidyāyāḥ pravṛttis tasya kiṃkṛtā/
children.translated_text: 'The operation of <s>avidyā</s>, like a dream, etc. — what is its cause?'

children.text:
iti śaṅkām upasaṃhāravyājenoddharati --- tasmāc cittavṛttibodhe
	    śāntaghoramūḍhākāracittavṛttyupabhoge+anādyavidyānimittatvād anādiḥ saṃyogo hetur
	    avidyāvāsanayoś ca saṃtāno bījāṅkurasaṃtānavad anādir iti bhāvaḥ //1.4//
children.translated_text: He resolves this doubt under the guise of a conclusion: therefore, [because] the experience of the mind's modifications — the enjoyment of mental modifications in the forms of calm, terrifying, and deluded — is caused by beginningless <s>avidyā</s>, the conjunction [between <s>puruṣa</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s>] is beginningless as cause. And the continuity of <s>avidyā</s> and <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) is beginningless, like the continuity of seed and sprout. This is the purport. (1.4)

children.text: vṛttayaḥ pañcatayyaḥ kliṣṭākliṣṭāḥ //1.5//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 1.5:] <s>Vṛttayaḥ pañcatayyaḥ kliṣṭākliṣṭāḥ</s> — 'The modifications are fivefold, [either] afflicted or non-afflicted.' (1.5)

children.text:
syād etat puruṣo hi śakya upadiśyate/ na ca vṛttinirodho vṛttīr avijñāya śakyaḥ/ na ca
	    sahasreṇāpi puruṣāyuṣair alam imāḥ kaścit parigaṇayitum/ asaṃkhyātāś ca kathaṃ
	    niroddhavyā ity āśaṅkya tāsām iyattāsvarūpapratipādanaparaṃ sūtram avatārayati --- tāḥ
	    punar niroddhavyā bahutve sati cittasya --- vṛttayaḥ pañcatayyaḥ kliṣṭākliṣṭāḥ/
	    vṛttirūpo+avayavy ekas tasya pramāṇādayo+avayavāḥ pañca/ tatas tadavayavā pañcatayī
	    pañcāvayavā vṛttir bhavati/ tāś ca vṛttayaś caitramaitrādicittabhedād bahvya iti
	    bahuvacanam upapannam/ etad uktaṃ bhavati --- caitro vā maitro vānyo vā kaścit sarveṣām
	    eva teṣāṃ vṛttayaḥ pañcatayya eva nādhikā iti/ cittasyeti caikavacanaṃ jātyabhiprāyam/
	    cittānām iti tu draṣṭavyam/ tāsām avāntaraviśeṣam anuṣṭhānopayoginaṃ darśayati ---
	    kliṣṭākliṣṭā iti/ akliṣṭā upādāya kliṣṭā niroddhavyās tā api pareṇa vairāgyeṇeti/ asya
	    vyākhyānaṃ --- kleśahetukā iti/ kleśā asmitādayo hetavaḥ pravṛttikāraṇaṃ yāsāṃ vṛttīnāṃ
	    tās tathoktāḥ/ yad vā puruṣārthapradhānasya rajastamomayīnāṃ hi vṛttīnāṃ
	    kleśakāraṇatvena kleśāyaiva pravṛttiḥ/ kleśaḥ kliṣṭaṃ tad āsām astīti kliṣṭā iti/ yata
	    eva kleśopārjanārtham amūṣāṃ pravṛttir ata eva karmāśayapracaye kṣetrībhūtāḥ/
	    pramāṇādinā khalv ayaṃ pratipattārtham avasāya tatra sakto dviṣṭo vā karmāśayam
	    ācinotīti bhavanti dharmādharmapracayaprasavabhūmayo vṛttayaḥ kliṣṭā iti/ akliṣṭā
	    vyācaṣṭe --- khyātiviṣayā iti/ vidhūtarajastamaso buddhisattvasya praśāntavāhinaḥ
	    prajñāprasādaḥ khyātis tayā viṣayiṇyā tadviṣayaṃ sattvapuruṣavivekam upalakṣayati/ tena

sattvapuruṣavivekaviṣayā yato+ata eva guṇādhikāravirodhinyaḥ/
	    kāryārambhaṇaṃ hi guṇānām adhikāro vivekakhyātiparyavasānaṃ ca tad iti caritādhikārāṇāṃ
	    guṇānām adhikāraṃ virundhantīti/ atas tā akliṣṭāḥ pramāṇaprabhṛtayo vṛttayaḥ/ syād etad
	    vītarāgajanmādarśanāt kliṣṭavṛttaya eva sarve prāṇabhṛtaḥ/ na ca kliṣṭavṛttipravāhe
	    bhavitum arhanty akliṣṭā vṛttayo na cāmūṣāṃ bhāve+api kāryakāritā virodhim adhyapātitvāt
	    tasmāt kliṣṭānām akliṣṭābhir nirodhas tāsāṃ ca vairāgyeṇa pareṇeti manorathamātram ity
	    ata āha --- kliṣṭapravāheti/ āgamānumānācāryopadeśapariśīlanalabdhajanmanī
	    abhyāsavairāgye kliṣṭacchidram antarā tatra patitāḥ svayam akliṣṭā eva yady api
	    kliṣṭapravāhapatitāḥ/ na khalu śālagrāme kirātaśatasaṃkīrṇe prativasann api brāhmaṇaḥ
	    kirāto bhavati/ akliṣṭacchidreṣv iti nidarśanam/ kliṣṭāntaravartitayā ca kliṣṭābhir
	    anabhibhūtā akliṣṭāḥ/ svasaṃskāraparipākakrameṇa kliṣṭā eva tāvad abhibhavantīty āha ---
	    tathājātīyakā iti/ akliṣṭābhir vṛttibhir akliṣṭāḥ saṃskārā ity arthaḥ/ tad idaṃ
	    vṛttisaṃskāracakram aniśam āvartate, ā nirodhasamādheḥ/ tad evaṃbhūtaṃ cittaṃ
	    nirodhāvasthaṃ saṃskāraśeṣaṃ bhūtvātmakalpenāvatiṣṭhata ity āpātataḥ pralayaṃ vā
	    gacchatīti paramārthataḥ/ piṇḍīkṛtya sūtrārtham āha --- tā iti/ pañcadhety
	    arthakathanamātraṃ na tu śabdavṛttivyākhyānam/ tayapaḥ prakāre+asmaraṇāt //1.5//
children.translated_text: Those [modifications] that pertain to the discrimination of <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> — and hence, being opposed to the operation of the <s>guṇas</s> — for the operation of the <s>guṇas</s> is their activity, and the culmination of discrimination-knowledge (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) is [their cessation]; having thus fulfilled their operation ...

One might object: the <s>puruṣa</s> (Self) is indeed what can be instructed. But the cessation of mental modifications (<s>vṛttinirodha</s>) is not possible without knowing the <s>vṛttis</s> (modifications). And not even with a thousand human lifespans could anyone enumerate all of them ...

children.text: pramāṇaviparyayavikalpanidrāsmṛtayaḥ //1.6//
children.translated_text: [Yogasūtra 1.6:] Valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), error (<s>viparyaya</s>), conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), sleep (<s>nidrā</s>), and memory (<s>smṛti</s>).

children.text:
tāḥ svasaṃjñābhir uddiśati --- pramāṇaviparyayavikalpanidrāsmṛtayaḥ/ nirdeśe
	    yathāvacanaṃ vigrahaś cārthe dvaṃdvaḥ samāsa itaretarayoge/ yathā ---
	    anityāśuciduḥkhānātmasu nityaśucisukhātmakhyātir avidyā
yogasūtram 2.5
children.translated_text: [Reference to] <s>Yogasūtra</s> 2.5.

children.text:
ity ukte+api na
	    diṅmohālātacakrādivibhramā vyudasyanta evam ihāpi pramāṇādyabhidhāne+api
	    vṛttyantarasadbhāvaśaṅkā na vyudasyateti tannirāsāya vaktavyaṃ pañcatayya iti/ etāvatya
	    eva vṛttayo nāparāḥ santīti darśitaṃ bhavati //1.6//
children.translated_text: Even when this is stated, just as the illusions of directional confusion and the [apparent] circle of a firebrand (<s>alātacakra</s>) are not thereby refuted, so too here, even when <s>pramāṇa</s> and the others are enumerated, the suspicion that other <s>vṛttis</s> exist is not refuted. Therefore, to remove that [suspicion] —

He indicates those [five vṛttis] by their proper designations — 'valid cognition, error, conceptual construction, sleep, and memory.' In the enumeration, the grammatical analysis follows the wording: the compound is a <s>dvaṃdva</s> (copulative compound) denoting mutual conjunction (<s>itaretarayoga</s>). Just as —

children.text: pratyakṣānumānāgamāḥ pramāṇāni //1.7//
children.translated_text: [Yogasūtra 1.7:] Perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and verbal testimony (<s>āgama</s>) are the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge).

children.text:
tatra pramāṇavṛttiṃ vibhajan sāmānyalakṣaṇam āha --- pratyakṣānumānāgamāḥ pramāṇāni/
	    anadhigatatattvabodhaḥ

pauruṣeyo vyavahārahetuḥ pramā/ tatkāraṇaṃ pramāṇam/
	    vibhāgavacanaṃ ca nyūnādhikasaṃkhyāvyavacchedārtham/ tatra sakalapramāṇamūlatvāt
	    prathamataḥ pratyakṣaṃ lakṣayati --- indriyeti/ arthasyeti samāropitatvaṃ niṣedhati/
	    tadviṣayeti bāhyagocaratayā jñānākāragocaratvaṃ nivārayati/ cittavartino jñānākārasya
	    bāhyajñeyasaṃbandhaṃ darśayati --- bāhyavastūparāgād iti/ vyavahitasya taduparāge hetum
	    āha --- indriyapraṇālikayeti/ sāmānyamātram artha ity eke/ viśeṣā evety anye/
	    sāmānyaviśeṣatadvattety apare vādinaḥ pratipannās tannirāsāyāha --- sāmānyaviśeṣātmana
	    iti/ na tadvattā kiṃ tu tādātmyam arthasya/ etac caikāntānabhypagama ity atra
	    pratipādayiṣyate/ anumānāgamaviṣayāt pratyakṣaviṣayaṃ vyavacchinatti ---
	    viśeṣāvadhāraṇapradhāneti/ yady api sāmānyam api pratyakṣe pratibhāsate tathāpi viśeṣaṃ
	    pratyupasarjanībhūtam ity arthaḥ/ etac ca sākṣātkāropalakṣaṇaparam/ tathā ca
	    vivekakhyātir api lakṣitā bhavati/ phalavipratipattiṃ nirākaroti --- phalaṃ pauruṣeyaś
	    cittavṛttibodha iti/ nanu puruṣavartī bodhaḥ kathaṃ cittagatāyā vṛtteḥ phalam/ na hi
	    khadiragocaravyāpāreṇa paraśunā palāśe chidā kriyata ity ata āha --- aviśiṣṭa iti/ na hi
	    puruṣagato bodho janyate, api tu caitanyam eva buddhidarpaṇapratibimbitaṃ
	    buddhivṛttyārthākārayā tadākāratām āpadyamānaṃ phalam/ tac ca tathābhūtaṃ buddher
	    aviśiṣṭaṃ buddhyātmakaṃ, vṛttiś ca buddhyātmiketi sāmānādhikaraṇyād yuktaḥ
	    pramāṇaphalabhāva ity arthaḥ/ etac copapādayiṣyāma ity āha --- pratisaṃvedīti/
	    pratyakṣānantaraṃ
	    pravṛttyādiliṅgakaśrotṛbuddhyanumānaprabhavasaṃbandhadarśanasamutthatayāgamasyānumānajatvād
	    anumitasya cāgamenānvākhyānād āgamāt prāg anumānaṃ lakṣayati --- anumeyasyeti/
	    jijñāsitadharmaviśiṣṭo dharmyanumeyas tasya tulyajātīyāḥ sādhyadharmasāmānyena
	    samānārthāḥ sapakṣās teṣv anuvṛtta ity anena viruddhatvam asādhāraṇatvaṃ ca
	    sādhanadharmasya nirākaroti/ bhinnajātīyā asapakṣās te ca sapakṣād anye tadviruddhās
	    tadabhāvavantaś ca, tebhyo vyāvṛttas tad anena sādhāraṇānaikāntikatvam apākaroti/
	    saṃbadhyata iti saṃbandho liṅgam anena pakṣadharmatāṃ darśayann asiddhatāṃ nivārayati/
	    tadviṣayā tannibandhanā, "ṣiñ bandhane"
children.translated_text: — which is of human [origin], which is a cause of practical activity — that is valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>). Its instrument is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge). The specification of division is for the purpose of excluding a lesser or greater number [of pramāṇas]. Among these, since [perception] is the root of all means of valid knowledge, first —

children.text: dhātupāṭhaḥ 5
children.translated_text: [Reference to] <s>Dhātupāṭha</s> [root list] 5.

children.text:
ity asmād viṣayapadavyutpatteḥ/
	    sāmānyāvadhāraṇeti pratyakṣaviṣayād vyavacchinatti/ saṃbandhasaṃvedanādhīnajanmānumānaṃ
children.translated_text: From the derivation of the word <s>viṣaya</s> (object) from that [root]. 'The ascertainment of universals' — this distinguishes [inference] from the domain of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). Inference, whose origin depends on the cognition of a relation (<s>saṃbandhasaṃvedana</s>) —

children.text:
viśeṣeṣu saṃbandhagrahaṇābhāvena sāmānyam eva sukarasaṃbandhagrahaṇaṃ
	    gocarayatīti/ udāharaṇam āha --- yatheti/ co hetvarthe/ vindhyo 'gatir yatas tasmāt
	    tasyāprāptir ato gatinivṛttau prāpter nivṛttir deśāntaraprāpter gatimac candratārakaṃ
	    caitravad iti siddham/ āgamasya vṛtter lakṣaṇam āha --- āpteneti/
	    tattvadarśanakāruṇyakaraṇapāṭavābhisaṃbandha āptis tayā vartata ity āptas tena
	    dṛṣṭo+anumito vārthaḥ/ śrutasya pṛthag anupādānaṃ tasya dṛṣṭānumitamūlatvena tābhyām eva
	    caritārthatvād āptacittavartijñānasadṛśasya jñānasya śrotṛcitte samutpādaḥ
	    svabodhasaṃkrāntis tasyai, artha upadiśyate śrotṛhitāhitaprāptiparihāropāyatayā
	    prajñāpyate/ śeṣaṃ sugamam/ yasyāgamasyāśraddheyārtho vaktā, yathā yāny eva daśa
	    dāḍimāni tāni ṣaḍ apūpā bhaviṣyantīti/ na dṛṣṭānumitārtho yathā caityaṃ vandeta
	    svargakāma iti/ sa āgamaḥ plavate/ nanv evaṃ manvādīnām apy āgamaḥ plaveta/ na hi te+api
	    dṛṣṭānumitārthāḥ/ yathāhuḥ ---

children.translated_text: There, analyzing the <s>pramāṇa</s> modification, he states its general characteristic — 'perception, inference, and verbal testimony are the <s>pramāṇas</s>.' The ascertainment of a reality not previously known —

children.text:
"yaḥ kaścit kasyacid dharmo manunā parikīrtitaḥ/ sa sarvo+abhihito vede sarvajñānamayo
	    hi saḥ/"
manusmṛtiḥ 2.7

ity ata āha --- mūlavaktari tv iti/ mūlavaktā hi tatreśvaro dṛṣṭānumitārtha ity
	    arthaḥ //1.7//
viparyayo mithyājñānam atadrūpapratiṣṭham //1.8//

viparyayo mithyājñānam atadrūpapratiṣṭham/ viparyaya iti lakṣyanirdeśaḥ/ mithyājñānam
	    ityādi lakṣaṇam/ yaj jñānapratibhāsirūpaṃ, tadrūpāpratiṣṭham evātadrūpapratiṣṭham/
	    yathāśrāddhabhojīti/ ataḥ saṃśayo+api saṃgṛhītaḥ/ etāvāṃs tu viśeṣaḥ --- tatra
	    jñānārūḍhaivāpratiṣṭhatā dvicandrādes tu bādhajñānena/ nanv evaṃ vikalpo+api
	    tadrūpāpratiṣṭhānād vicārato viparyayaḥ prasajyetety ata āha --- mithyājñānam iti/ anena
	    hi sarvajanīnānubhavasiddho bādha uktaḥ/ sa cāsti viparyaye na tu vikalpe, tena
	    vyavahārāt/ paṇḍitarūpāṇām eva

tu vicārayatāṃ tatra bādhabuddher iti/
	    codayati --- sa kasmān na pramāṇam/ nottareṇopajātavirodhinā jñānena pūrvaṃ bādhanīyam
	    api tu pūrveṇaiva prathamam upajātenānupajātavirodhinā param iti bhāvaḥ/ pariharati ---
	    yataḥ pramāṇeneti/ yatra hi pūrvāpekṣā parotpattis tatraivam iha tu svakāraṇād
	    anyonyānapekṣe jñāne jāyete/ tenottarasya pūrvam anupamṛdyodayam anāsādayatas
	    tadapabādhātmaivodayo na tu pūrvasyottarabādhātmā, tasya tadānīm aprasakteḥ/ tasmād
	    anupajātavirodhitā bādhyatve hetur upajātavirodhitā ca bādhakatve/ tasmād
	    bhūtārthaviṣayatvāt pramāṇenāpramāṇasya bādhanaṃ siddham/ udāharaṇam āha --- tatra
	    pramāṇeneti/ asya kutsitatvaṃ hānāya darśayati --- seyaṃ pañceti/ avidyāsāmānyam
	    avidyāsmitādiṣu pañcasu parvasv ity arthaḥ/ avyaktamahadahaṃkārapañcatanmātreṣv aṣṭasv
	    anātmasv ātmabuddhir avidyā tamaḥ/ evaṃ yoginām aṣṭasv aṇimādikeṣv aiśvaryeṣv aśreyaḥsu
	    śreyobuddhir aṣṭavidho mohaḥ pūrvasmāj jaghanyaḥ/ sa cāsmitocyate/ yathā yogenāṣṭavidham
	    aiśvaryam upādāya siddho bhūtvā dṛṣṭānuśravikāñ śabdādīn daśa viṣayān bhokṣya
	    ityevamātmikā pratipattir mahāmoho rāgaḥ/ evam etenaivābhisaṃdhinā pravartamānasya
	    kenacit pratibaddhatvād aṇimādīnām anutpattau tannibandhanasya
	    dṛṣṭānuśravikaviṣayopabhogasyāsiddheḥ pratibandhakaviṣayaḥ krodhaḥ sa tāmisrākhyo
	    dveṣaḥ/ evam aṇimādiguṇasaṃpattau dṛṣṭānuśravikaviṣayapratyupasthāne ca kalpānte sarvam
	    etan naṅkṣyatīti yas trāsaḥ so+abhiniveśo 'ndhatāmisraḥ/ tad uktam ---

"bhedas tamaso+aṣṭavidho mohasya ca daśavidho mahāmohaḥ/ tāmisro 'ṣṭādaśadhā tathā
	    bhavaty andhatāmisraḥ"
sāṃkhyakārikā 48
śabdajñānānupātī vastuśūnyo vikalpaḥ //1.9//

śabdajñānānupātī vastuśūnyo vikalpaḥ/ nanu śabdajñānānupātī ced āgamapramāṇāntaragato
	    (āgamapramāṇāntargato) vikalpaḥ prasajyeta nirvastukatve vā viparyayaḥ syād ity ata āha
	    --- sa neti/ na pramāṇaviparyayāntargataḥ/ kasmād yato vastuśūnyatve+apīti
	    pramāṇāntargatiṃ niṣedhati/

śabdajñānamāhātmyanibandhana iti
	    viparyayāntargatim/ etad uktaṃ bhavati --- kvacid abhede bhedam āropayati kvacit punar
	    bhinnānām abhedam/ tato bhedasyābhedasya ca vastuno+abhāvāt tadābhāso vikalpo na
	    pramāṇaṃ nāpi viparyayo vyavahārāvisaṃvādād iti/ śāstraprasiddham udāharaṇam āha ---
	    tadyatheti/ kiṃ viśeṣyaṃ kena vyapadiśyate viśeṣyate nābhede viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇabhāvo na hi
	    gavā gaur viśeṣyate/ kiṃ tu bhinnenaiva caitreṇa/ tad idam āha --- bhavati ca vyapadeśe
	    vṛttiḥ/ vyapadeśavyapadeśyayor bhāvo vyapadeśaḥ/ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva iti yāvat/ tasmin
	    vṛttir vākyasya yathā caitrasya gaur iti/ śāstrīyam evodāharaṇāntaraṃ samuccinoti ---
	    tatheti/ pratiṣiddho vastunaḥ pṛthivyāder dharmaḥ parispando yasya sa tathoktaḥ/ ko+asau
	    niṣkriyaḥ puruṣaḥ/ na khalu sāṃkhyīye rāddhānte+abhāvo nāma kaścid asti vastudharmo yena
	    puruṣo viśeṣyetety arthaḥ/ kvacit pāṭhaḥ pratiṣiddhā vastudharmā iti/ tasyārthaḥ ---
	    pratiṣedhavyāptāḥ pratiṣiddhā na vastudharmāṇāṃ tadvyāpyatā bhāvābhāvayor asaṃbandhād
	    atha ca tathā pratītir iti/ laukikam udāharaṇam āha --- tiṣṭhati bāṇa iti/ yathā hi
	    pacati bhinattīty atra pūrvāparībhūtaḥ karmakṣaṇapracaya ekaphalāvacchinnaḥ pratīyata
	    evaṃ tiṣṭhatīty atrāpi/ pūrvāparībhāvam evāha --- sthāsyati sthita iti/ nanu bhavatu
	    pākavat pūrvāparībhūtayāvasthānakriyayā bāṇād bhinnayā bāṇasya vyapadeśa ity ata āha ---
	    gatinivṛttau dhātvarthamātraṃ gamyate/ gatinivṛttir eva tāvat kalpitā tasyā api
	    bhāvarūpatvaṃ tatrāpi pūrvāparībhāva ity aho kalpanāparamparety arthaḥ/ abhāvaḥ kalpito
	    bhāva iva cānugata iva ca sarvapuruṣeṣu gamyate na punaḥ puruṣavyatirikto dharmaḥ kaścid
	    ity udāharaṇāntaram āha --- tathānutpattidharmeti/ pramāṇaviparyayābhyām anyā na
	    vikalpavṛttir iti vādino bahavaḥ pratipedire/ tatpratibodhanāyodāharaṇaprapañca iti
	    mantavyam //1.9//
abhāvapratyayālambanā vṛttir nidrā //1.10//

abhāvapratyayālambanā vṛttir nidrā/ adhikṛtaṃ hi vṛttipadam anuvādakam/
	    pramāṇaviparyayavikalpasmṛtīnāṃ vṛttitvaṃ prati parīkṣakāṇām avipratipatteḥ/ atas tad
	    anūdyate viśeṣavidhānāya/ nidrāyās tu vṛttitve parīkṣakāṇām asti vipratipattir iti
	    vṛttitvaṃ vidheyam/ na ca prakṛtam anuvādakaṃ vidhānāya kalpata iti punar vṛttigrahaṇam/
	    jāgratsvapnavṛttīnām abhāvas tasya pratyayaḥ kāraṇaṃ buddhisattvāc chādakaṃ tamas tad
	    evālambanaṃ viṣayo yasyāḥ sā tathoktā vṛttir nidrā/ buddhisattve hi triguṇe yadā
	    sattvarajasī abhibhūya samastakaraṇāvarakam āvirasti tamas tadā buddher
	    viṣayākārapariṇāmābhāvād udbhūtatamomayīṃ buddhim avabudhyamānaḥ puruṣaḥ
	    suṣupto+antaḥsaṃjña ity ucyate/ kasmāt punar niruddhakaivalyayor iva vṛttyabhāva eva na
	    nidrety ata āha --- sā ca saṃprabodhe pratyavamarśāt sopapattikāt smaraṇāt
	    pratyayaviśeṣaḥ/ kathaṃ, yadā hi sattvasacivaṃ tama āvirasti tadedṛśaḥ pratyavamarśaḥ
	    suptotthitasya bhavati sukham aham asvāpsaṃ prasannaṃ me manaḥ prajñāṃ me viśāradīkaroti
	    svacchīkarotīti/ yadā tu rajaḥsacivaṃ tama āvirasti tadedṛśaḥ pratyavamarśa ity āha ---
	    duḥkham aham asvāpsaṃ styānam akarmaṇyaṃ me manaḥ kasmād yato bhramaty anavasthitam/
	    nitāntābhibhūtarajaḥsattve tamaḥsamullāse svāpe prabuddhasya pratyavamarśam āha ---
	    gāḍhaṃ mūḍho+aham asvāpsaṃ gurūṇi me gātrāṇi klāntaṃ me cittamalasaṃ muṣitam iva
	    tiṣṭhatīti/ sādhyavyatireke hetuvyatirekam āha --- na khalv ayam iti/ prabuddhasya
	    prabuddhamātrasya/ tadāśritāś ceti bodhakāle, pratyayānubhave vṛttyabhāvakāraṇānubhava
	    ity arthaḥ/ nanu pramāṇādayo vyutthānacittādhikaraṇā nirudhyantāṃ samādhipratipakṣatvān
	    nidrāyās tv ekāgravṛttitulyāyāḥ kathaṃ samādhipratipakṣatety ata āha --- sā ca samādhāv
	    iti/ ekāgratulyāpi tāmasatvena nidrā sabījanirbījasamādhipratipakṣeti sāpi niroddhavyety
	    arthaḥ //1.10//
children.translated_text: Sleep (<s>nidrā</s>) is a <s>vṛtti</s> (mental modification) whose support (<s>ālambana</s>) is the cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>) of absence (<s>abhāva</s>). The word '<s>vṛtti</s>' [in the sūtra] is being reiterated, for there is no disagreement among examiners regarding the <s>vṛtti</s>-nature of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition), <s>viparyaya</s> (error), <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction), and <s>smṛti</s> (memory). Therefore that [word] is reiterated for the purpose of specifying a distinction. But regarding the <s>vṛtti</s>-nature of <s>nidrā</s>, there is disagreement among examiners, so its <s>vṛtti</s>-nature is what is to be established. And since what is already the topic [as reiterated] cannot serve for establishing [something new], the word <s>vṛtti</s> is taken again. The absence of the <s>vṛttis</s> of waking and dream — the <s>pratyaya</s> (cognition) of that, namely the <s>tamas</s> (darkness) that covers the <s>sattva</s> of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) — that itself is the <s>ālambana</s> (support), the object of which [<s>vṛtti</s>]; such is the <s>vṛtti</s> called <s>nidrā</s>. For in the <s>buddhi-sattva</s>, which is composed of the three <s>guṇas</s>, when <s>tamas</s> manifests overpowering <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> and covering all the sense faculties, then — due to the absence of <s>buddhi</s>'s transformation into the form of objects — <s>Puruṣa</s>, cognizing the <s>buddhi</s> that has become suffused with arisen <s>tamas</s>, is said to be 'in deep sleep, with internal consciousness.' Why then is <s>nidrā</s> not simply the absence of <s>vṛtti</s>, as in the states of <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) and <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation)? To this he says — 'And that [<s>nidrā</s>] is a specific <s>pratyaya</s>, because of reflective awareness (<s>pratyavamarśa</s>) upon awakening, which is a well-reasoned recollection.' How so? When <s>tamas</s> manifests accompanied by <s>sattva</s>, such reflective awareness occurs in one who has arisen from sleep: 'I slept happily; my mind is clear; it sharpens my understanding, makes it lucid.' But when <s>tamas</s> manifests accompanied by <s>rajas</s>, he says such reflective awareness [occurs]: 'I slept miserably; my mind is dull and unfit for action — why? Because it wanders and is unsettled.' When <s>rajas</s> and <s>sattva</s> are completely overpowered and <s>tamas</s> is fully dominant in sleep, he states the reflective awareness of one who has awakened: 'I slept deeply in a stupor; my limbs are heavy; my mind is exhausted, impure, as though robbed.' Regarding the absence of the effect [establishing] the absence of the cause, he says — 'Surely this [recollection] is not [without a cause].' Of one who has just merely awakened. 'And those [recollections] based on that' — at the time of waking, the experience of the <s>pratyaya</s> means the experience of the cause of the absence of <s>vṛtti</s> — this is the meaning. Now, <s>pramāṇa</s> and the others, having their locus in the outward-turned (<s>vyutthāna</s>) mind, should be restrained because they are opposed to <s>samādhi</s>; but how can <s>nidrā</s>, which resembles a one-pointed <s>vṛtti</s>, be opposed to <s>samādhi</s>? To this he says — 'And that [<s>nidrā</s>] in <s>samādhi</s>...' Even though resembling one-pointedness, <s>nidrā</s>, being <s>tāmasic</s>, is opposed to both <s>sabīja</s> (seeded) and <s>nirbīja</s> (seedless) <s>samādhi</s> — therefore it too must be restrained: this is the meaning. (1.10)

children.text: anubhūtaviṣayāsaṃpramoṣaḥ smṛtiḥ //1.11//
children.translated_text: <s>Smṛti</s> (memory) is the non-deprivation (<s>asaṃpramoṣa</s>) of an experienced object. (1.11)

children.text:
anubhūtaviṣayāsaṃpramoṣaḥ smṛtiḥ/ pramāṇādibhir anubhūte viṣaye yo+asaṃpramoṣo 'steyaṃ
	    sā smṛtiḥ/ saṃskāramātrajasya hi jñānasya saṃskārakāraṇānubhavāvabhāsito viṣaya ātmīyas
	    tadadhikaviṣayaparigrahas tu saṃpramoṣaḥ steyam/ kasmāt sādṛśyāt/ "muṣa steye"
dhātupāṭhaḥ 9
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātupāṭha</s> 9

children.text:
ity asmāt pramoṣapadavyutpatteḥ/ etad uktaṃ bhavati --- sarve
	    pramāṇādayo+anadhigatam arthaṃ sāmānyataḥ prakārato vādhigamayanti/ smṛtiḥ punar na
	    pūrvānubhavamaryādām atikrāmati/ tadviṣayā tadūnaviṣayā vā na tu tadadhikaviṣayā/
	    so+ayaṃ vṛttyantarād viśeṣaḥ smṛter iti/ vimṛśati --- kiṃ pratyayasyeti/
	    grāhyapravaṇatvād anubhavasya svānubhavābhāvāt tajjaḥ saṃskāro grāhyam eva smārayatīti
	    pratibhāti/ anubhavamātrajanitatvāc cānubhavam eveti/ vimṛśyopapattita ubhayasmaraṇam
	    avadhārayati --- grāhyapravaṇatayā grāhyoparaktaḥ/ paramārthatas tu grāhyagrahaṇe
	    evobhayaṃ tayor ākāraṃ svarūpaṃ nirbhāsayati prakāśayati/ svavyañjakaṃ kāraṇam añjanam
	    ākāro yasya sa tathoktaḥ/ svakāraṇākāra ity arthaḥ/ vyañjakam udbodhakaṃ tenāñjanaṃ
	    phalābhimukhīkaraṇaṃ yasyeti vety arthaḥ/ nanu yadi kāraṇavicāreṇa buddhismaraṇayoḥ
	    sārūpyaṃ kas tarhi bheda ity ata āha --- tatra grahaṇeti/ grahaṇam upādānaṃ, na ca
	    gṛhītasyopāttasyopādānaṃ saṃbhavati/ tad anenānadhigatabodhanaṃ buddhir ity uktam/
	    grahaṇākāro grahaṇarūpaṃ pūrvaṃ pradhānaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathoktā/ vikalpitaś cāyam
	    abhede+api guṇapradhānabhāva iti/ grāhyākāraḥ pūrvaḥ prathamo yasyāḥ sā tathoktā/ idam
	    eva ca grāhyākārasya grāhyasya pūrvatvaṃ yad vṛttyantaraviṣayīkṛtatvam arthasya/ tad
	    anena vṛttyantaraviṣayīkṛtagocarā smṛtir ity uktaṃ bhavati/ so+ayam asaṃpramoṣa iti/
	    nanv asti smṛter api saṃpramoṣaḥ/ darśayati hi pitrāder atītasya
	    deśakālāntarānubhūtasyānanubhūtacaradeśakālāntarasaṃbandhaḥ svapna ity ata āha --- sā ca
	    dvayīti/ bhāvitaḥ kalpitaḥ smartavyo yayā sā tathoktā/ abhāvito+akalpitaḥ
children.translated_text: — from this is the etymological derivation of the word <s>pramoṣa</s>. What has been said amounts to this: all <s>pramāṇa</s> and the rest make known an object not previously apprehended, either in its universal or particular aspect. But <s>smṛti</s> does not transgress the boundary of prior experience. Its object is either the same as what was experienced or less than it, but never more. This is the distinction of <s>smṛti</s> from other <s>vṛttis</s>. He deliberates — 'Whether of the <s>pratyaya</s> [the cognition itself]...' Because experience is inclined toward the apprehended object (<s>grāhya</s>), and because there is no experience of itself, the <s>saṃskāra</s> born from it seems to cause recollection only of the apprehended — so it appears. And because [<s>smṛti</s>] is born solely from experience, [it should recall] experience itself. Having deliberated, he ascertains from reasoning that both [the object and the experience] are remembered: 'Being inclined toward the <s>grāhya</s>,' [the cognition is] colored by the apprehended. But in ultimate truth, in the apprehension of the <s>grāhya</s>, [the cognition] manifests, illuminates, the form (<s>ākāra</s>) of both of them. 'Having a form that reveals its own cause' (<s>svavyañjaka-kāraṇa-añjana-ākāra</s>) — <s>svakāraṇākāra</s>, 'having the form of its own cause,' is the meaning. <s>Vyañjaka</s> means that which brings to light; <s>añjana</s> means directing toward fruition — this is the meaning. Now, if through analysis of the cause there is similarity of form between cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) and memory (<s>smaraṇa</s>), what then is their difference? To this he says — 'There, the apprehension (<s>grahaṇa</s>)...' <s>Grahaṇa</s> means acquisition, and there cannot be acquisition of what has already been acquired. By this, it is stated that <s>buddhi</s> makes known what was not previously known. 'Having the form of apprehension as primary' — that [<s>buddhi</s>] in which the form of apprehension is predominant. And this distinction of predominant vs. subordinate is conceptually constructed, even though there is no real difference. 'Having the form of the apprehended as primary' — that [<s>smṛti</s>] in which the <s>grāhya-ākāra</s> (form of the apprehended) is primary, i.e., comes first. And this priority of the <s>grāhya-ākāra</s> means precisely that the object has been made the object of another <s>vṛtti</s> [previously]. By this, it is stated that <s>smṛti</s> has as its domain what has been made the object of another <s>vṛtti</s>. 'This is the non-deprivation (<s>asaṃpramoṣa</s>)...' But isn't there also <s>saṃpramoṣa</s> (deprivation) even in <s>smṛti</s>? For it is shown that a dream is the connection, in another place and time where one has not experienced, of [someone who was] experienced in a different place and time, such as one's deceased father. To this he says — 'And that [<s>smṛti</s>] is of two kinds...' '<s>Bhāvita</s>' means imagined, constructed — [an object] to be remembered by which [<s>smṛti</s>] is so called. '<s>Abhāvita</s>' means unconstructed,

children.text:
pāramārthika iti yāvat/ neyaṃ smṛtir api tu viparyayas tallakṣaṇopapannatvāt
	    smṛtyābhāsatayā tu smṛtir uktā/ pramāṇābhāsam iva pramāṇam iti bhāvaḥ/ kasmāt punar ante
	    smṛter upanyāsa ity ata āha --- sarvāḥ smṛtaya iti/ anubhavaḥ prāptiḥ/ prāptipūrvā
	    vṛttiḥ smṛtis tataḥ smṛtīnām upajana ity arthaḥ/ nanu ye puruṣaṃ kliśnanti te
	    niroddhavyāḥ prekṣāvatā/ kleśāś ca tathā/ na ca vṛttayaḥ, tat kimartham āsāṃ nirodha ity
	    ata āha --- sarvāś caitā iti/ sugamam //1.11//
children.translated_text: [i.e.,] real — that is the meaning. This [dream-<s>smṛti</s>] is not true <s>smṛti</s> but rather <s>viparyaya</s> (error), because it fits the definition of that [<s>viparyaya</s>]. It is called <s>smṛti</s> only in the sense of being a semblance of <s>smṛti</s>, just as <s>pramāṇābhāsa</s> (semblance of valid cognition) [is called] <s>pramāṇa</s> — this is the idea. Why then is <s>smṛti</s> presented last? To this he says — 'All <s>smṛtis</s>...' Experience means attainment. A <s>vṛtti</s> preceded by attainment is <s>smṛti</s>; from that, <s>smṛtis</s> arise — this is the meaning. Now, those [mental states] that afflict <s>Puruṣa</s> should be restrained by the discerning person. And <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are indeed such. But <s>vṛttis</s> are not [afflictions in themselves], so for what purpose is their restraint? To this he says — 'And all these [<s>vṛttis</s>]...' This is easily understood. (1.11)

<s>Smṛti</s> (memory) is the non-deprivation (<s>asaṃpramoṣa</s>) of an experienced object. The non-deprivation, i.e., the non-stealing, regarding an object experienced through <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) and the rest — that is <s>smṛti</s>. For the object of a cognition born solely from <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) is one's own [object], illuminated by the experience that is the cause of the <s>saṃskāra</s>. But the appropriation of an object beyond that [experienced one] would be <s>saṃpramoṣa</s> (deprivation), i.e., theft. Why? Because of the similarity [in etymology]. '<s>muṣa steye</s>' (the root <s>muṣ</s> means 'to steal') —

children.text: abhyāsavairāgyābhyāṃ tannirodhaḥ //1.12//
children.translated_text: The restraint (<s>nirodha</s>) of those [<s>vṛttis</s> is achieved] through <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice) and <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion). (1.12)

children.text:
nirodhopāyaṃ pṛcchati --- atheti/ sūtreṇottaram āha --- abhyāsavairāgyābhyāṃ
	    tannirodhaḥ/ abhyāsavairāgyayor nirodhe janayitavye+avāntaravyāpārabhedena samuccayo na
	    tu vikalpa ity āha --- cittanadīti/ prāgbhāraḥ prabandhaḥ/ nimnatā gambhīratā,
	    agādhateti yāvat //1.12//
children.translated_text: He asks about the means of restraint — 'Now...' With the <s>sūtra</s> he answers — 'The restraint of those [<s>vṛttis</s> is achieved] through <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice) and <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion).' Regarding <s>abhyāsa</s> and <s>vairāgya</s>, there is a combination — not an alternative — in producing the <s>nirodha</s> (restraint) to be achieved, each having a different intermediate function. This is what [<s>Vyāsa</s>] says [with the metaphor] — 'The river of mind...' '<s>Prāgbhāra</s>' means continuity, flow. '<s>Nimnatā</s>' means depth, i.e., profundity. (1.12)

children.text: tatra sthitau yatno+abhyāsaḥ //1.13//
children.translated_text: Of these, <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice) is the effort toward steadiness (<s>sthiti</s>). (1.13)

children.text:
tatrābhyāsasya svarūpaprayojanābhyāṃ lakṣaṇam āha --- tatra sthitau yatno+abhyāsaḥ/ tad
	    vyācaṣṭe --- cittasyāvṛttikasya rājasatāmasavṛttirahitasya praśāntavāhitā vimalatā
	    sāttvikavṛttivāhitaikāgratā sthitiḥ/ tadartha iti/ sthitāv iti nimittasaptamī

vyākhyātā/ yathā "carmaṇi dvīpinaṃ hanti" iti/ prayatnam eva paryāyābhyāṃ viśadayati
	    --- vīryam utsāha iti/ tasyecchāyonitām āha --- tatsaṃpipādayiṣayā/ tad iti sthitiṃ
	    parāmṛśati/ prayatnasya viṣayam āha --- tatsādhaneti/ sthitisādhanāny
	    antaraṅgabahiraṅgāṇi yamaniyamādīni/ sādhanagocaraḥ kartṛvyāpāro na phalagocara iti //1.13//
children.translated_text: as illustrated [by the example]: 'He kills the leopard for its skin,' [where 'for the skin' uses the locative in a causal sense]. He clarifies the effort itself through two synonyms — 'vigor' and 'enthusiasm.' He states its origin in desire — 'With the wish to accomplish that.' 'That' refers to <s>sthiti</s> (steadiness). He states the object of effort — 'Toward the means of that...'
