The means to <s>sthiti</s> are the inner (<s>antaraṅga</s>) and outer (<s>bahiraṅga</s>) [limbs of yoga], such as <s>yama</s> (restraints), <s>niyama</s> (observances), and so on. The agent's activity is directed toward the means, not toward the result [directly]. (1.13)

He states the definition of <s>abhyāsa</s> in terms of its essential nature and purpose — 'Of these, <s>abhyāsa</s> is the effort toward steadiness.' He explains that — '<s>Sthiti</s> (steadiness) of the mind that is without [fluctuating] <s>vṛttis</s>, free from <s>rājasic</s> and <s>tāmasic</s> <s>vṛttis</s>, is the tranquil flow (<s>praśāntavāhitā</s>), the purity (<s>vimalatā</s>), the one-pointedness (<s>ekāgratā</s>) which is the flow of <s>sāttvic</s> <s>vṛttis</s>.' 'For that purpose' — 'toward <s>sthiti</s>' is explained as a causal locative (<s>nimittasaptamī</s>),

children.text: sa tu dīrghakālanairantaryasatkārāsevito dṛḍhabhūmiḥ //1.14//
children.translated_text: But that [practice] becomes firmly grounded (<s>dṛḍhabhūmi</s>) when cultivated for a long time, without interruption, and with devotion (<s>satkāra</s>). (1.14)

children.text:
nanu vyutthānasaṃskāreṇānādinā paripanthinā pratibaddho 'bhyāsaḥ kathaṃ sthityai
	    kalpata ity ata āha --- sa tu dīrghakālanairantaryasatkārāsevito dṛḍhabhūmiḥ/ so+ayam
	    abhyāso viśeṣaṇatrayasaṃpannaḥ san dṛḍhāvastho na sahasā vyutthānasaṃskārair
	    abhibhūtasthitirūpaviṣayo bhavati/ yadi punar evaṃbhūtam apy abhyāsaṃ kṛtvoparamet tataḥ
	    kālaparivāsenābhibhūyeta/ tasmān noparantavyam iti bhāvaḥ //1.14//
children.translated_text: But since practice is obstructed by the beginningless <s>vyutthāna-saṃskāra</s> (impressions of outward-turning), how can it be conducive to <s>sthiti</s> (steadiness)? To this he says — 'But that [practice] becomes firmly grounded when cultivated for a long time, without interruption, and with devotion.' This practice, when endowed with these three qualifications, becomes firmly established, and its object — the state of <s>sthiti</s> — is not suddenly overpowered by the <s>vyutthāna-saṃskāras</s>. But if one were to desist even after having practiced in such a manner, then in the course of time [the practice] would be overpowered. Therefore, one must not desist — this is the purport. (1.14)

children.text: dṛṣṭānuśravikaviṣayavitṛṣṇasya vaśīkārasaṃjñā vairāgyam //1.15//
children.translated_text: <s>Vairāgya</s> (dispassion) is the controlled consciousness (<s>vaśīkāra-saṃjñā</s>) of one who is free from thirst for objects seen or heard about (<s>anuśravika</s>). (1.15)

children.text:
vairāgyam āha --- dṛṣṭānuśravikaviṣayavitṛṣṇasya vaśīkārasaṃjñā vairāgyam/
	    cetanācetaneṣu dṛṣṭaviṣayeṣu vitṛṣṇatām āha --- striya iti/ aiśvaryam ādhipatyam/
	    anuśravo vedas tato+adhigatā ānuśravikāḥ svargādayaḥ/ tatrāpi vaitṛṣṇyam āha ---
	    svargeti/ deharahitā videhāḥ karaṇeṣu līnās teṣāṃ bhāvo vaidehyam/ anye tu prakṛtim
	    evātmānam abhimanyamānāḥ prakṛtyupāsakāḥ prakṛtau sādhikārāyām eva līnās teṣāṃ bhāvaḥ
	    prakṛtilayatvaṃ tatprāptiviṣaye, ānuśravikaviṣaye vitṛṣṇasyānuśravikaviṣaye vitṛṣṇo hi
	    svargādiprāptiviṣaye vitṛṣṇa ity ucyate/ nanu yadi vaitṛṣṇyamātraṃ vairāgyaṃ hanta
	    viṣayāprāptāv

api tad astīti vairāgyaṃ syād ity ata āha --- divyādivyeti/
	    na vaitṛṣṇyamātraṃ vairāgyam api tu divyādivyaviṣaysaṃprayoge 'pi cittasyānābhogātmikā/
	    tām eva spaṣṭayati --- heyopādeyaśūnyā/ āsaṅgadveṣarahitopekṣābuddhir vaśīkārasaṃjñā/
	    kutaḥ punar iyam ity atrāha --- prasaṃkhyānabalād iti/ tāpatrayaparītatā viṣayāṇāṃ doṣas
	    tatparibhāvanayā tatsākṣātkāraḥ prasaṃkhyānaṃ tadbalād ity arthaḥ/ yatamānasaṃjñā,
	    vyatirekasaṃjñā, ekendriyasaṃjñā, vaśīkārasaṃjñā ceti catasraḥ saṃjñā ity āgaminaḥ/
	    rāgādayaḥ khalu kaṣāyāś cittavartinas tair indriyāṇi yathāsvaṃ viṣayeṣu pravartante, tan
	    mā pravartiṣatendriyāṇi tattadviṣayeṣv iti tatparipācanāyārambhaḥ prayatnaḥ sā
	    yatamānasaṃjñā/ tadārambhe sati kecit kaṣāyāḥ pakvāḥ pacyante pakṣyante ca kecit/ tatra
	    pakṣyamāṇebhyaḥ pakvānāṃ vyatirekeṇāvadhāraṇaṃ vyatirekasaṃjñā/
	    indriyapravartanāsamarthatayā pakvānām autsukyamātreṇa manasi vyavasthānam
	    ekendriyasaṃjñā/ autsukyamātrasyāpi nivṛttir upasthiteṣv api
	    divyādivyaviṣayeṣūpekṣābuddhiḥ saṃjñātrayāt parā vaśīkārasaṃjñā/ etayaiva ca pūrvāsāṃ
	    caritārthatvān na tāḥ pṛthag uktā iti sarvam avadātam //1.15//
children.translated_text: that [freedom from craving] would exist, and so it would [already] be <s>vairāgya</s> — hence he says: 'divine and non-divine,' etc. <s>Vairāgya</s> is not mere freedom from craving, but rather the state of non-engagement (<s>anābhogātmikā</s>) of the mind even when in contact with divine and non-divine objects. He clarifies that very thing: 'devoid of [notions of] what is to be rejected and what is to be adopted' — an attitude of equanimity (<s>upekṣā-buddhi</s>), free from attachment and aversion, [this] is the consciousness of mastery (<s>vaśīkārasaṃjñā</s>). Whence does this [arise]? To this he says: 'from the strength of <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (discernment).' The defect of objects is their being afflicted by the threefold suffering (<s>tāpatraya</s>); the contemplation of that [defect], leading to its direct realization, is <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>; 'from its strength' — such is the meaning. The <s>Yatamānasaṃjñā</s> (stage of effort), <s>Vyatirekasaṃjñā</s> (stage of discrimination), <s>Ekendriyasaṃjñā</s> (stage of single-sense [attachment]), and <s>Vaśīkārasaṃjñā</s> (stage of mastery) — these are the four stages, according to the tradition. The passions (<s>kaṣāyas</s>) such as <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and the like, dwelling in the mind, cause the sense organs to operate upon their respective objects. The effort undertaken to ripen [those passions] so that the senses may not operate upon their respective objects — that is the <s>Yatamānasaṃjñā</s>. When that effort is underway, some passions are ripened, some are being ripened, and some are yet to be ripened. There, the ascertainment by distinguishing the ripened ones from those yet to be ripened is the <s>Vyatirekasaṃjñā</s>. The persistence of the ripened [passions] in the mind merely as eagerness, without the capacity to drive the senses — that is the <s>Ekendriyasaṃjñā</s>. The cessation of even that mere eagerness, resulting in an attitude of equanimity toward divine and non-divine objects even when they are present, superior to the [previous] three stages — that is the <s>Vaśīkārasaṃjñā</s>. And since the previous stages are fulfilled by this very [final stage], they are not mentioned separately — thus everything is clear. (1.15)

He states <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion): '<s>Vairāgya</s> is the consciousness of mastery (<s>vaśīkārasaṃjñā</s>) of one who is free from craving for seen and heard-of objects.' He states freedom from craving with respect to seen objects, whether sentient or insentient: 'Women,' etc. '<s>Aiśvarya</s>' means sovereignty. '<s>Anuśrava</s>' means the <s>Veda</s>; objects known from it are '<s>ānuśravika</s>' — such as heaven and the like. He states freedom from craving with respect to those as well: 'Heaven,' etc. '<s>Videhas</s>' are those who are without a body, dissolved into the sense organs; their state is '<s>vaidehya</s>.' Others, regarding <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) itself as the Self, are worshippers of <s>Prakṛti</s>, dissolved into <s>Prakṛti</s> while it still retains its function; their state is '<s>prakṛtilayatva</s>' (absorption into Prakṛti) — with respect to the attainment of that. One who is free from craving for heard-of objects is said to be free from craving for the attainment of heaven and the like. Now, if mere freedom from craving were <s>vairāgya</s>, then even when objects are not attained

children.text: tat paraṃ puruṣakhyāter guṇavaitṛṣṇyam //1.16//
children.translated_text: The supreme [dispassion] is the freedom from craving for the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents of nature), arising from the discernment of <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self). (1.16)

children.text:
aparaṃ vairāgyam uktvā param āha --- tat paraṃ puruṣakhyāter guṇavaitṛṣṇyam/
	    aparavairāgyasya paraṃ vairāgyaṃ prati kāraṇatvam/ tatra ca dvāram ādarśayati ---
	    dṛṣṭānuśravikaviṣayadoṣadarśī virakta iti/ anenāparaṃ vairāgyaṃ darśitam/
	    puruṣadarśanābhyāsād āgamānumānācāryopadeśasamadhigatasya puruṣasya darśanaṃ
	    tasyābhyāsaḥ paunaḥpunyena niṣevaṇaṃ tasmāt tasya darśanasya śuddhī rajastamaḥparihāṇyā
	    sattvaikatānatā tayā yo guṇapuruṣayoḥ prakarṣeṇa vivekaḥ puruṣaḥ śuddho 'nantas
	    tadviparītā guṇā iti, tenāpyāyitā buddhir yasya yoginaḥ sa tathoktaḥ/ tad anena
	    dharmameghākhyaḥ samādhir uktaḥ/ sa tathābhūto yogī guṇebhyo vyaktāvyaktadharmakebhyaḥ
	    sarvathā viraktaḥ sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātāv api guṇātmikāyāṃ yāvad virakta iti/ tat
	    tasmād dvayaṃ vairāgyam/ pūrvaṃ hi vairāgyaṃ sattvasamudrekavidhūtatamasi
	    rajaḥkaṇakalaṅkasaṃpṛkte cittasattve/ tac ca tauṣṭikānām api samānam/ te hi

tenaiva prakṛtilayā babhūvuḥ/ yathoktam --- vairāgyāt prakṛtilaya iti/ tatra tayor
	    dvayor madhye yad uttaraṃ tajjñānaprasādamātram/ mātragrahaṇena nirviṣayatāṃ sūcayati/
	    tad eva hi tādṛśaṃ cittasattvaṃ rajoleśamalenāpy aparāmṛṣṭam asyāśrayo+ata eva
	    jñānaprasāda ity ucyate/ cittasattvaṃ hi prasādasvabhāvam api rajastamaḥsaṃparkān
	    malinatām anubhavati/ vairāgyābhyāsavimalavāridhārādhautasamastarajastamomalaṃ tv
	    atiprasannaṃ jñānaprasādamātrapariśeṣaṃ bhavati/ tasya guṇānupādeyatvāya darśayati ---
	    yasyodaye sati yogī pratyuditakhyātiḥ/ khyātiviśeṣe sati vartamānakhyātimān ity arthaḥ/
	    prāpaṇīyaṃ kaivalyaṃ prāptam/ yathā vakṣyati --- jīvann eva vidvān mukto bhavati/
	    saṃskāramātrasya cchinnamūlasya siddhatvād iti bhāvaḥ/ kutaḥ prāptaṃ, yataḥ --- kṣīṇāḥ
	    kṣetavyāḥ kleśā avidyādayaḥ savāsanāḥ/ nanv asti dharmādharmasamūho bhavasya
	    janmamaraṇaprabandhasya saṃkramaḥ prāṇinām/ tat kutaḥ kaivalyam ity ata āha --- chinna
	    iti/ śliṣṭāni niḥsaṃdhīni parvāṇi yasya sa tathoktaḥ/ dharmādharmasamūhasya samūhinaḥ
	    parvāṇi tāni śliṣṭāni/ na hi jātu jantur maraṇajanmaprabandhena tyakṣyate/ so+ayaṃ
	    bhavasaṃkramaḥ kleśakṣaye chinnaḥ/ yathā vakṣyati --- "kleśamūlaḥ karmāśayaḥ"
children.translated_text: became absorbed into <s>Prakṛti</s> through that very [lower dispassion]. As stated: 'Through <s>vairāgya</s>, absorption into <s>Prakṛti</s>.' Now, between those two, the latter is merely the clarity of knowledge (<s>jñānaprasādamātra</s>). The word 'merely' (<s>mātra</s>) indicates its objectlessness. For that very <s>sattva</s> of the mind, of such a nature, untouched even by a trace of the impurity of <s>rajas</s> — it is the basis of [this state], and hence is called 'clarity of knowledge.' For the <s>sattva</s> of the mind, though clarity is its essential nature, experiences impurity due to its contact with <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>. But when all impurity of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> has been washed away by the stream of pure water of <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) and <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice), it becomes exceedingly clear, with nothing remaining but the clarity of knowledge. To show that for such a [yogin] the <s>guṇas</s> are not to be adopted, he says: 'When that [knowledge] has arisen, the <s>yogin</s> possesses arisen discernment' — meaning that when the special discernment is present, he possesses present discernment. <s>Kaivalya</s> (liberation), which is to be attained, is attained. As will be stated: 'The wise one, even while living, becomes liberated.' Because only the residue of <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions), whose root has been cut, remains as established — such is the purport. How is it attained? Because: 'The <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) such as <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the rest, together with their residual traces (<s>vāsanās</s>), have been destroyed — that is, are to be destroyed.' Now, there exists the mass of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), the transmigration of beings through the continuity of birth and death. Then how [can there be] <s>kaivalya</s>? Hence he says: 'cut,' etc. 'One whose joints are closely joined' is so described. The joints of the mass of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — of the one possessing the mass — those joints are closely joined. For never is a being abandoned by the continuity of death and birth. But this transmigration of existence (<s>bhavasaṃkrama</s>) is cut through the destruction of the <s>kleśas</s>. As will be stated: 'The repository of <s>karma</s> has the <s>kleśas</s> as its root'

children.text:
iti/ nanu
	    prasaṃkhyānaparipākaṃ dharmameghaṃ ca nirodham antarā kiṃ tad asti yaj
	    jñānaprasādamātram ity ata āha --- jñānasyaiveti/ dharmameghabheda eva paraṃ vairāgyaṃ
	    nānyat/ yathā vakṣyati --- "prasaṃkhyāne+apy akusīdasya sarvathā vivekakhyāter
	    dharmameghaḥ samādhiḥ"
children.translated_text: Now, between the maturation of <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (discernment), the <s>Dharmamegha</s> [samādhi], and <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), what is that which is merely the clarity of knowledge? Hence he says: 'Of knowledge alone,' etc. The supreme <s>vairāgya</s> is nothing other than a variety of <s>Dharmamegha</s> [samādhi]. As will be stated: 'For one who is not self-interested even in <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>, from the discernment of discrimination (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) in every way, [arises] the <s>Dharmamegha</s> <s>samādhi</s>'

children.text: yogasūtram 4.29
children.translated_text: <s>Yogasūtra</s> 4.29

children.text:
[iti,] "tadā sarvāvaraṇamalāpetasya
	    jñānasyānantyāj jñeyam alpam"
children.translated_text: and 'Then, because knowledge from which all covering and impurity has departed is infinite, what remains to be known is little'

children.text: yogasūtram 4.31
children.translated_text: <s>Yogasūtra</s> 4.31

children.text:
iti ca/ tasmād etasya hi nāntarīyakam
	    avinābhāvi kaivalyam iti //1.16//
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) is the inevitable, inseparable [result] of this. (1.16)

Having stated the lower <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), he states the supreme: 'The supreme [dispassion] is the freedom from craving for the <s>guṇas</s>, arising from the discernment of <s>Puruṣa</s>.' The lower <s>vairāgya</s> serves as a cause for the supreme <s>vairāgya</s>. And therein he shows the gateway: 'One who sees the defects in seen and heard-of objects becomes dispassionate' — by this, the lower <s>vairāgya</s> is indicated. The practice of the vision of <s>Puruṣa</s> — the repeated cultivation of the vision of <s>Puruṣa</s> as ascertained through scripture, inference, and the teacher's instruction — from that, the purification of that vision [occurs] through the diminishment of <s>rajas</s> (activity) and <s>tamas</s> (inertia), [resulting in] exclusive predominance of <s>sattva</s> (purity); by that [comes] the supreme discrimination between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — '<s>Puruṣa</s> is pure and infinite; the <s>guṇas</s> are the opposite of that' — the <s>yogin</s> whose intellect is nourished by this [discrimination] is so described. By this, the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Dharmamegha</s> (cloud of virtue) is indicated. That <s>yogin</s>, being thus [established], is completely dispassionate toward the <s>guṇas</s> having manifest and unmanifest properties — dispassionate even toward the discernment of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>sattvapuruṣānyatākhyāti</s>), which itself is of the nature of the <s>guṇas</s>. Hence, from that, <s>vairāgya</s> is twofold. For the earlier <s>vairāgya</s> [arises] in the <s>sattva</s> of the mind when <s>tamas</s> is dispelled by the predominance of <s>sattva</s>, though still tainted by specks of <s>rajas</s>. And that is common even to the <s>Tauṣṭikas</s> (those content [with lower attainments]). For they

children.text: vitarkavicārānandāsmitārūpānugamāt saṃprajñātaḥ //1.17//
children.translated_text: [<s>Saṃprajñāta</s> samādhi] is accompanied by <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation), <s>vicāra</s> (reflection), <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), and <s>asmitā</s> (sense of I-am-ness). (1.17)

children.text:
upāyam abhidhāya saprakāropeyakathanāya pṛcchati --- athopāyadvayeneti/
	    vitarkavicārānandāsmitārūpānugamāt saṃprajñātaḥ/ saṃprajñātapūrvakatvād asaṃprajñātasya
	    prathamaṃ saṃprajñātopavarṇanam/

saṃprajñātasāmānyaṃ
	    vitarkavicārānandāsmitānāṃ rūpaiḥ svarūpair anugamāt pratipattavyam/ vitarkaṃ vivṛṇoti
	    --- cittasyeti/ svarūpasākṣātkāravatī prajñābhogaḥ/ sa ca sthūlaviṣayatvāt sthūlaḥ/
	    yathā hi prāthamiko dhānuṣkaḥ sthūlam eva lakṣyaṃ vidhyaty atha sūkṣmam evaṃ prāthamiko
	    yogī sthūlam eva pāñcabhautikaṃ caturbhujādi dhyeyaṃ sākṣātkaroty atha sūkṣmam iti/ evaṃ
	    cittasyālambane sūkṣma ābhogaḥ/ sthūlakāraṇabhūtasūkṣmapañcatanmātraliṅgāliṅgaviṣayo
	    vicāraḥ/ tad evaṃ grāhyaviṣayaṃ darśayitvā grahaṇaviṣayaṃ darśayati --- ānanda iti/
	    indriye sthūla ālambane cittasyābhogo hlāda ānandaḥ/ prakāśaśīlatayāṃ khalu
	    sattvapradhānād ahaṃkārād indriyāṇy utpannāni/ sattvaṃ sukham iti tāny api sukhānīti
	    tasminn ābhogo hlāda iti/ grahītṛviṣayaṃ saṃprajñātam āha --- ekātmikā saṃvid iti/
	    asmitāprabhavānīndriyāṇi/ tenaiṣām asmitā sūkṣmaṃ rūpam/ sā cātmanā grahītrā saha
	    buddhir ekātmikā saṃvit/ tasyāṃ ca grahītur antarbhāvād bhavati grahītṛviṣayaḥ
	    saṃprajñāta iti/ caturṇām aparam apy avāntaraviśeṣam āha --- tatra prathama iti/ kāryaṃ
	    kāraṇānupraviṣṭaṃ na kāraṇaṃ kāryeṇa tad ayaṃ sthūla ābhogaḥ
	    sthūlasūkṣmendriyāsmitākāraṇacatuṣṭayānugato bhavati/ uttare tu tridvyekakāraṇakās
	    tridvyekarūpā bhavanti/ asaṃprajñātād bhinatti --- sarva eta iti //1.17//
children.translated_text: The general [nature of] <s>saṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi] is to be understood through the accompaniment of the forms — that is, the essential natures — of <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation), <s>vicāra</s> (reflection), <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), and <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness). He explains <s>vitarka</s>: 'of the mind' — the direct realization of its own nature ...

Having stated the means, in order to describe the goal along with its varieties, he asks: 'Now, by the twofold means,' etc. '[<s>Saṃprajñāta</s>] is accompanied by <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation), <s>vicāra</s> (reflection), <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), and <s>asmitā</s> (sense of I-am-ness).' Because <s>asaṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi] is preceded by <s>saṃprajñāta</s>, the description of <s>saṃprajñāta</s> comes first.

children.text: virāmapratyayābhyāsapūrvaḥ saṃskāraśeṣo+anyaḥ //1.18//
children.translated_text: [Yogasūtra 1.18:] The other [<s>asaṃprajñāta samādhi</s>] is preceded by the practice of the cause of cessation (<s>virāmapratyaya</s>), and has only <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions) remaining.

children.text:
kramaprāptam asaṃprajñātam avatārayituṃ pṛcchati --- atheti/ virāmapratyayābhyāsapūrvaḥ
	    saṃskāraśeṣo+anyaḥ/ pūrvapadenopāyakathanam uttarābhyāṃ ca svarūpakathanam/ madhyamaṃ
	    padaṃ vivṛṇoti --- sarvavṛttīti/ prathamaṃ padaṃ vyācaṣṭe --- tasya param iti/ virāmo
	    vṛttīnām abhāvas tasya pratyayaḥ kāraṇaṃ tasyābhyāsas tadanuṣṭhānaṃ paunaḥpunyaṃ tad eva
	    pūrvaṃ yasya sa tathoktaḥ/ athāparaṃ vairāgyaṃ nirodhakāraṇaṃ kasmān na bhavatīty ata
	    āha --- sālambano hīti/ kāryasarūpaṃ kāraṇaṃ

yujyate na virūpam/ virūpaṃ
	    cāparaṃ vairāgyaṃ sālambanaṃ nirālambanasamādhinā kāryeṇa/ tasmān nirālambanād eva
	    jñānaprasādamātrāt tasyotpattir yuktā/ dharmameghasamādhir eva hi
	    nitāntavigalitarajastamomalād buddhisattvād upajātas tattadviṣayātikrameṇa
	    pravartamāno+ananto viṣayāvadyadarśī samastaviṣayaparityāgāc ca svarūpapratiṣṭhaḥ san
	    nirālambanaḥ saṃskāramātraśeṣasya nirālambanasya samādheḥ kāraṇam upapadyate sārūpyād
	    iti/ ālambanīkaraṇam āśrayaṇam abhāvaprāptam iva vṛttirūpakāryākaraṇān nirbījo
	    nirālambanaḥ/ athavā bījaṃ kleśakarmāśayās te niṣkrāntā yasmāt sa tathā //1.18//
children.translated_text: It is consistent, not dissimilar [in nature]. The other dissimilarity is that dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) possessing a support [is the means], while objectless <s>samādhi</s> (<s>nirālambana</s>) is its effect. Therefore, from the objectless [samādhi] alone, from mere clarity of knowledge, its arising ...

To introduce <s>asaṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi], which has come in due order, he asks — 'now' — 'the other is preceded by the practice of the cause of cessation, and has only saṃskāras remaining.' The first part of the compound states the means, and the latter two ...

children.text: bhavapratyayo videhaprakṛtilayānām //1.19//
children.translated_text: [Yogasūtra 1.19:] [It is] caused by worldly existence (<s>bhavapratyaya</s>) for the <s>videha</s> (bodiless ones) and the <s>prakṛtilaya</s> (those merged in primordial nature).

children.text:
nirodhasamādher avāntarabhedaṃ hānopādānāṅgam ādarśayati --- sa khalv ayaṃ
	    nirodhasamādhir dvividhaḥ --- upāyapratyayo bhavapratyayaś ca/ upāyo vakṣyamāṇaḥ
	    śraddhādiḥ pratyayaḥ kāraṇaṃ yasya nirodhasamādheḥ sa tathoktaḥ/ bhavanti jāyante 'syāṃ
	    jantava iti bhavo+avidyā, bhūtendriyeṣu vā vikāreṣu prakṛtiṣu
	    vāvyaktamahadahaṃkārapañcatanmātreṣv anātmasv ātmakhyātis tauṣṭikānāṃ
	    vairāgyasaṃpannānāṃ, sa khalv ayaṃ bhavaḥ pratyayaḥ kāraṇaṃ yasya nirodhasamādheḥ sa
	    bhavapratyayaḥ/ tatra tayor madhya upāyapratyayo yogināṃ mokṣyamāṇānāṃ bhavati/
	    viśeṣavidhānena śeṣasya mumukṣusaṃbandhaṃ niṣedhati/ keṣāṃ tarhi bhavapratyaya ity atra
	    sūtreṇottaram āha --- bhavapratyayo videhaprakṛtilayānām/ videhāś ca prakṛtilayāś ca
	    teṣām ity arthaḥ/ tad vyācaṣṭe --- videhānāṃ devānāṃ bhavapratyayaḥ/ bhūtendriyāṇām
	    anyatamadātmatvena (anyatamam ātmatvena) pratipannās tadupāsanayā
	    tadvāsanāvāsitāntaḥkaraṇāḥ piṇḍapātānantaram indriyeṣu bhūteṣu vā līnāḥ
	    saṃskāramātrāvaśeṣamanasaḥ ṣāṭkauśikaśarīrarahitā videhāḥ/ te hi
	    svasaṃskāramātropayogena cittena kaivalyapadam ivānubhavantaḥ prāpnuvanto videhāḥ/
	    avṛttikatvaṃ ca kaivalyena

sārūpyaṃ, sādhikārasaṃskāraśeṣatā ca vairūpyam/
	    saṃskāramātropabhogeneti kvacit pāṭhaḥ/ tasyārthaḥ --- saṃskāramātram evopabhogo yasya
	    na tu cittavṛttir ity arthaḥ/ prāptāvadhayaḥ svasaṃskāravipākaṃ tathājātīyakam
	    ativāhayanty atikrāmanti punar api saṃsāre viśanti/ tathā ca vāyuproktam ---
children.translated_text: Similarity [is defined as having the same form], and dissimilarity is having residual <s>saṃskāras</s> with continued operation. 'By the experience of mere <s>saṃskāras</s>' — this is a variant reading in some [manuscripts]. Its meaning is: one whose experience consists of <s>saṃskāras</s> alone and not ...

He shows the internal subdivision of <s>nirodha-samādhi</s> (cessation-absorption) as a factor for abandonment and acquisition — 'This <s>nirodha-samādhi</s> is indeed of two kinds: caused by means (<s>upāyapratyaya</s>) and caused by [mere] worldly existence (<s>bhavapratyaya</s>). The means is dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) ...'

children.text: "daśa manvantarāṇīha tiṣṭhantīndriyacintakāḥ/ bhautikās tu śataṃ pūrṇam" iti/
children.translated_text: 'Those who contemplate the senses abide here for ten <s>manvantaras</s> (cosmic ages); those concerned with the gross elements, for a full hundred [manvantaras].'

children.text:
tathā prakṛtilayāś cāvyaktamahadahaṃkārapañcatanmātreṣv anyatamadātmatvena (anyatamam
	    ātmatvena) pratipannās tadupāsanayā tadvāsanāvāsitāntaḥkaraṇāḥ piṇḍapātānantaram
	    avyaktādīnām anyatamasmiṃl līnāḥ (anyatame līnāḥ) sādhikāre+acaritārthe/ evaṃ hi
	    caritārthaṃ cetaḥ syād yadi vivekakhyātim api janayed ajanitasattvapuruṣānyatākhyātes tu
	    cetaso+acaritārthasyāsti sādhikārateti/ sādhikāre cetasi prakṛtilīne kaivalyapadam
	    ivānubhavanti, yāvan na punar āvartate 'dhikāravaśāc cittam iti/ prakṛtisāmyam upagatam
	    apy avadhiṃ prāpya punar api prādurbhavati tato vivicyate/ yathā varṣātipāte mṛdbhāvam
	    upagato maṇḍūkadehaḥ punar ambhodavāridhārāvasekān maṇḍūkadehabhāvam anubhavatīti/ tathā
	    ca vāyuproktam ---
children.translated_text: Likewise, the <s>prakṛtilaya</s> (those merged in primordial nature), having identified themselves with one or another of the [principles] — the Unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), the Great (<s>mahat</s>), the Ego-sense (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), or the five subtle elements (<s>tanmātras</s>) — through meditation on that [principle], their inner organ becomes imbued with the impressions of that ...

children.text:
"sahasraṃ tv ābhimānikāḥ/ bauddhā daśa sahasrāṇi tiṣṭhanti vigatajvarāḥ// pūrṇaṃ
	    śatasahasraṃ tu tiṣṭhanty avyaktacintakāḥ/ puruṣaṃ nirguṇaṃ prāpya kālasaṃkhyā na
	    vidyate" iti//
children.translated_text: 'Those attached to ego abide for a thousand [manvantaras]; the <s>Bauddhas</s> (Buddhist contemplatives) abide for ten thousand, free from affliction; those who contemplate the Unmanifest abide for a full hundred thousand; those who have attained the <s>puruṣa</s> devoid of qualities ...'

children.text: tas asya punarbhavaprāptihetutayā heyatvaṃ siddham //1.19//
children.translated_text: Thus its being something to be abandoned (<s>heya</s>) is established, since it is a cause for the attainment of rebirth.

children.text: śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñāpūrvaka itareṣām //1.20//
children.translated_text: [Yogasūtra 1.20:] For others, [it is] preceded by faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), energy (<s>vīrya</s>), memory (<s>smṛti</s>), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>).

children.text:
yogināṃ tu samādher upāyakramam āha --- śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñāpūrvaka itareṣām/
	    nanv indriyādicintakā api śraddhāvanta evety ata āha --- śraddhā cetasaḥ saṃprasādaḥ/ sa
	    cāgamānumānācāryopadeśasamadhigatatattvaviṣayo bhavati hi cetasaḥ saṃprasādo

+abhirucir atīcchā śraddhā nendriyādiṣv ātmābhimāninām abhirucir asaṃprasādo hi sa
	    vyāmohamūlatvād ity arthaḥ/ kuto+asāv eva śraddhety ata āha --- sā hi jananīva kalyāṇī
	    yoginaṃ pāti vimārgapātajanmano 'narthāt/ so+ayam icchāviśeṣa iṣyamāṇaviṣayaṃ prayatnaṃ
	    prasūta ity āha --- tasya hi śraddadhānasya/ tasya vivaraṇaṃ --- vivekārthino vīryam
	    upajāyate/ smṛtir dhyānam anākulam avikṣiptaṃ, samādhīyate yogāṅgasamādhiyuktaṃ bhavati/
	    yamaniyamādināntarīyakasamādhyupanyāsena ca yamaniyamādayo+api sūcitāḥ/ tad evam
	    akhilayogāṅgasaṃpannasya saṃprajñāto jāyata ity āha --- samāhitacittasyeti/ prajñāyā
	    vivekaḥ prakarṣa upajāyate/ saṃprajñātapūrvam asaṃprajñātotpādam āha --- tadabhyāsāt
	    tatraiva tattadbhūmiprāptau tattadviṣayāc ca vairāgyād asaṃprajñātaḥ samādhir bhavati/
	    sa hi kaivalyahetuḥ sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātipūrvo hi nirodhaś cittam akhilakāryakaraṇena
	    caritārtham adhikārād avasādayati //1.20//
children.translated_text: An inclination (<s>abhiruci</s>) that surpasses [mere] desire is <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) — not the inclination of those who falsely identify themselves with the sense-organs, etc., for that is a lack of clarity (<s>asaṃprasāda</s>), since it is rooted in delusion. This is the meaning. Why is it that this alone is <s>śraddhā</s>? To this he replies: 'For she, like a good mother, protects the <s>yogin</s> from the calamity born of falling into a wrong path.' This special form of desire gives rise to effort directed toward the desired object — thus he says: 'For him who has faith...' The explanation of that: 'For the one who seeks discrimination (<s>vivekārthin</s>), energy (<s>vīrya</s>) arises.' '<s>Smṛti</s>' (memory/mindfulness) [means] meditation that is untroubled and undistracted; 'is concentrated' (<s>samādhīyate</s>) means it becomes endowed with <s>samādhi</s> as a limb of <s>Yoga</s>. And by the mention of <s>samādhi</s> as the essential accompaniment of <s>yama</s> (restraints), <s>niyama</s> (observances), etc., the <s>yama</s>, <s>niyama</s>, and the rest are also indicated. Thus, for one endowed with all the limbs of <s>Yoga</s>, <s>saṃprajñāta</s> [<s>samādhi</s>] arises — hence he says: 'For one whose mind is concentrated.' The excellence of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) — [namely] discrimination (<s>viveka</s>) — arises. He states the arising of <s>asaṃprajñāta</s> [<s>samādhi</s>] preceded by <s>saṃprajñāta</s>: from the practice of that [<s>saṃprajñāta</s>], upon attaining each successive stage, and from <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) regarding the respective objects, <s>asaṃprajñāta samādhi</s> arises. For that [<s>asaṃprajñāta</s>] is the cause of <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation), since <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), preceded by the discernment of the otherness of <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> (<s>sattvapuruṣānyatākhyāti</s>), causes the mind — which has served its purpose through all its functions and instruments — to subside from its operation. (1.20)

But for yogins, he states the order of means for <s>samādhi</s> — 'For others, [it is] preceded by faith, energy, memory, <s>samādhi</s>, and wisdom.' [Objection:] But do not even those who contemplate the senses and the like also possess faith? To this he says —

children.text: tīvrasaṃvegānām āsannaḥ //1.21//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 1.21:] <s>Tīvrasaṃvegānām āsannaḥ</s> — 'For those of intense ardor, [<s>samādhi</s>] is near.' (1.21)

children.text:
nanu śraddhādayaś ced yogopāyās tarhi sarveṣām aviśeṣeṇa samādhitatphale syātām/
	    dṛśyate tu kasyacit siddhiḥ kasyacid asiddhiḥ kasyacic cireṇa siddhiḥ kasyacic
	    ciratareṇa kasyacit kṣipram ity ata āha --- te khalu nava yogina iti/ upāyāḥ śraddhādayo
	    mṛdumadhyādhimātrāḥ prāgbhavīyasaṃskārādṛṣṭavaśād yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ/ saṃvego vairāgyaṃ
	    tasyāpi mṛdumadhyatīvratā prāgbhavīyavāsanādṛṣṭavaśād eveti teṣu yādṛśāṃ kṣepīyasī
	    siddhis tān darśayati sūtreṇa --- tīvrasaṃvegānām āsanna iti sūtram/ śeṣaṃ bhāṣyam/
	    samādheḥ saṃprajñātasya phalam asaṃprajñātas tasyāpi kaivalyam //1.21//
children.translated_text: Now, if faith and the rest are the means of <s>Yoga</s>, then <s>samādhi</s> and its fruit should be the same for all without distinction. But it is observed that some attain success, some do not, some attain it after a long time, some after a very long time, and some quickly. To this he replies: 'These nine <s>yogins</s>...' The means — faith and the rest — are mild (<s>mṛdu</s>), medium (<s>madhya</s>), or intense (<s>adhimātra</s>) for those [whose means are such] due to the force of <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions) and <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) from previous births — they are spoken of thus. <s>Saṃvega</s> (ardor) is <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion); that too has mild, medium, and intense [degrees] due to the force of <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) and <s>adṛṣṭa</s> from previous births. Among those, to show those for whom success is swiftest, he cites the <s>sūtra</s>: 'For those of intense ardor, [<s>samādhi</s>] is near.' The rest is [explained in] the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. The fruit of <s>saṃprajñāta samādhi</s> is <s>asaṃprajñāta</s>; the fruit of that too is <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). (1.21)

children.text: mṛdumadhyādhimātratvāt tato+api viśeṣaḥ //1.22//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 1.22:] <s>Mṛdumadhyādhimātratvāt tato 'pi viśeṣaḥ</s> — 'Due to the mild, medium, or intense [nature of practice], even from that there is further distinction.' (1.22)

children.text: mṛdumadhyādhimātratvāt tato+api viśeṣaḥ/ nigadavyākhyātena bhāṣyeṇa vyākhyātam iti //1.22//
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛdumadhyādhimātratvāt tato 'pi viśeṣaḥ</s> — 'Due to the mild, medium, or intense [nature], even from that there is further distinction.' This has been explained by the <s>Bhāṣya</s> in the manner of a running gloss (<s>nigadavyākhyāna</s>). (1.22)

children.text: īśvarapraṇidhānād vā //1.23//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 1.23:] <s>Īśvarapraṇidhānād vā</s> — 'Or, from devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord).' (1.23)

children.text:
sūtrāntaraṃ pātayituṃ vimṛśati --- kim etasmād eveti/ na vāśabdaḥ saṃśayanivartakaḥ/
	    īśvarapraṇidhānād vā/ vyācaṣṭe --- praṇidhānād bhaktiviśeṣān mānasād vācikāt kāyikād
	    vāvarjito+abhimukhīkṛtas tam anugṛhṇāti/ abhidhyānam anāgatārthecchā --- idam
	    asyābhimatam astv iti/ tanmātreṇa na vyāpārāntareṇa/ śeṣaṃ sugamam //1.23//
children.translated_text: In order to introduce the next <s>sūtra</s>, he deliberates: 'Is it only from this [means]...' The particle 'vā' (or) does not resolve a doubt [but offers an alternative]. '<s>Īśvarapraṇidhānād vā</s>' — 'Or, from devotion to <s>Īśvara</s>.' He explains: 'From <s>praṇidhāna</s>' — a special form of devotion (<s>bhaktiviśeṣa</s>), whether mental, verbal, or bodily — '[<s>Īśvara</s>], won over and made favorable, blesses him.' '<s>Abhidhyāna</s>' (benevolent attention) is the wish regarding a future aim: 'May this [desired object] belong to him.' By that alone — not by any other activity. The rest is easy to understand. (1.23)

children.text: kleśakarmavipākāśayair aparāmṛṣṭaḥ puruṣaviśeṣa īśvaraḥ //1.24//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 1.24:] <s>Kleśakarmavipākāśayair aparāmṛṣṭaḥ puruṣaviśeṣa īśvaraḥ</s> — '<s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) is a special <s>puruṣa</s> (Self) untouched by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>karma</s> (action), <s>vipāka</s> (fruition), and <s>āśayas</s> (latent deposits).' (1.24)

children.text:
nanu cetnācetanābhyām eva vyūḍhaṃ nānyena viśvam/ īśvaraś ced acetanas tarhi pradhānaṃ
	    pradhānavikārāṇām api pradhānam adhyapātāt tathā ca na tasyāvarjanam acetanatvād atha
	    cetanas tathāpi citiśakter audāsīnyād asaṃsāritayā cāsmitādivirahāt kuta āvarjanam/
	    kutaś cābhidhyānam ity āśayavān āha --- atha pradhāneti/ atra sūtreṇottaram āha ---
	    kleśakarmavipākāśayair aparāmṛṣṭaḥ puruṣaviśeṣa īśvaraḥ/ avidyādayaḥ kleśāḥ kliśnanti
	    khalv amī puruṣaṃ

sāṃsārikaṃ vividhaduḥkhaprahāreṇeti/ kuśalākuśalānīti
	    dharmādharmās teṣāṃ ca karmajatvād upacārāt karmatvam/ vipāko jātyāyurbhogāḥ/
	    vipākānuguṇā vāsanās tāś cittabhūmāv āśerata ity āśayāḥ/ na hi karabhajātinirvartakaṃ
	    karma prāgbhavīyakarabhabhogabhāvitāṃ bhāvanāṃ na yāvad abhivyanakti tāvat karabhocitāya
	    bhogāya kalpate/ tasmād bhavati karabhajātyanubhavajanmā bhāvanā karabhavipākānuguṇeti/
	    nanv amī kleśādayo buddhidharmā na kathaṃcid api puruṣaṃ parāmṛśanti, tasmāt
	    puruṣagrahaṇād eva tadaparāmarśasiddheḥ kṛtaṃ kleśakarmetyādinety ata āha --- te ca
	    manasi vartamānāḥ sāṃsārike puruṣe vyapadiśyante/ kasmāt, sa hi tatphalasya bhoktā
	    cetayiteti/ tasmāt puruṣatvād īśvarasyāpi tatsaṃbandhaḥ prāpta iti tatpratiṣedha
	    upapadyata ity āha --- yo hy anena buddhisthenāpi puruṣamātrasādhāraṇena
	    bhogenāparāmṛṣṭaḥ sa puruṣaviśeṣa īśvaraḥ/ viśiṣyata iti viśeṣaḥ puruṣāntarād
	    vyavacchidyate/ viśeṣapadasya vyāvartyaṃ darśayitukāmaḥ paricodanāpūrvaṃ pariharati ---
	    kaivalyaṃ prāptās tarhīti/ prakṛtilayānāṃ prākṛto bandhaḥ/ vaikāriko bandho videhānām/
	    dakṣiṇādibandho divyādivyaviṣayabhogabhājām/ tāny amūni trīṇi bandhanāni/
	    prakṛtibhāvanāsaṃskṛtamanaso hi dehapātānantaram eva prakṛtilayatām āpannā itītareṣāṃ
	    pūrvā bandhakoṭiḥ prajñāyate, tenottarakoṭividhānamātram iha tu pūrvāparakoṭiniṣedha
	    iti/ saṃkṣipya viśeṣaṃ darśayati --- sa tu sadaiva muktaḥ sadaiveśvara iti/
	    jñānakriyāśaktisaṃpad aiśvaryam/
children.translated_text: who is in <s>saṃsāra</s>, by striking him with manifold suffering. This is the meaning. <s>Dharma</s> (virtue) and <s>adharma</s> (vice) — being produced by <s>karma</s>, they are called '<s>karma</s>' by metonymy. <s>Vipāka</s> (fruition) is birth (<s>jāti</s>), lifespan (<s>āyus</s>), and enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>). <s>Vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) that follow the pattern of <s>vipāka</s> — those that rest (<s>āśerate</s>) in the ground of the mind are called <s>āśayas</s> (latent deposits). For the <s>karma</s> that brings about birth as a camel does not become suitable for camel-appropriate enjoyment until it first manifests the impression (<s>bhāvanā</s>) conditioned by camel-enjoyment from a previous birth. Therefore, the impression born from the experience of camel-birth follows the pattern of the camel-<s>vipāka</s>. Now, these <s>kleśas</s> and the rest are properties of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and do not in any way touch the <s>puruṣa</s>. Therefore, by the very mention of '<s>puruṣa</s>,' the fact that he is untouched by them is established — so what is the need for mentioning '<s>kleśa</s>, <s>karma</s>,' etc.? To this he replies: 'And these, existing in the mind, are predicated of the <s>puruṣa</s> who is in <s>saṃsāra</s>.' Why? 'Because he is the experiencer of their fruit, being conscious.' Therefore, since <s>Īśvara</s> too is a <s>puruṣa</s>, the connection with those [<s>kleśas</s>, etc.] is to be expected — hence the negation [of that connection] is justified. Thus he says: 'For he who is untouched by this experience — which, though common to all <s>puruṣas</s> merely, is a thief of the intellect — is a special <s>puruṣa</s>, [namely] <s>Īśvara</s>.' 'Special' (<s>viśeṣa</s>) means he is distinguished — set apart from other <s>puruṣas</s>. Wishing to show what the word 'special' excludes, he resolves [an objection] preceded by a challenge: 'Then those who have attained <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) [would also be Īśvara]...' Those who are dissolved into <s>Prakṛti</s> have a <s>prākṛta</s> (natural) bondage. Those who are bodiless (<s>videha</s>) have a <s>vaikārika</s> (derivative) bondage. Those who enjoy divine and non-divine objects of experience have a <s>dakṣiṇādi</s> (merit-based) bondage. These are the three kinds of bondage. For those whose minds have been conditioned by contemplation of <s>Prakṛti</s>, immediately after death they attain the state of being dissolved into <s>Prakṛti</s> — thus the earlier limit of bondage of the others is known; hence only the later limit is mentioned here, while [for <s>Īśvara</s>] both the earlier and later limits are negated. He shows the distinguishing feature in summary: 'But He is eternally liberated, eternally the Lord.' The wealth (<s>saṃpad</s>) of the powers of knowledge and action is lordship (<s>aiśvarya</s>).

children.text:
atra pṛcchati --- yo+asāv iti/ jñānakriye
	    hi na cicchakter apariṇāminyāḥ saṃbhavata iti rajastamorahitaviśuddhacittasattvāśraye
	    vaktavye/ na ceśvarasya sadā muktasyāvidyāprabhavacittasattvasamutkarṣeṇa saha
	    svasvāmibhāvaḥ saṃbandhaḥ saṃbhavatīty ata uktaṃ --- prakṛṣṭasattvopādānād iti/
	    neśvarasya pṛthagjanasyevāvidyānibandhanaś cittasattvena svasvāmibhāvaḥ/ kiṃ tu
	    tāpatrayaparītān pretyabhāvamahārṇavāj jantūn uddhariṣyāmi jñānadharmopadeśena/ na ca
	    jñānakriyāsāmarthyātiśayasaṃpattim antareṇa tadupadeśaḥ/ na ceyam
	    apahatarajastamomalaviśuddhasattvopādānaṃ vinety ālocya sattvaprakarṣam upādatte
	    bhagavān aparāmṛṣṭo 'py avidyayā/ avidyābhimānī cāvidyāyās tattvam avidvān bhavati na
	    punar avidyām avidyātvena sevamānaḥ/ na khalu śailūṣo rāmatvam āropya tās tāś ceṣṭā
	    darśayan bhrānto bhavati/ tad idam āhāryam asya rūpaṃ na tāttvikam iti/ syād etat/
	    uddidhīrṣayā bhagavatā sattvam upādeyaṃ tadupādānena ca taduddidhīrṣā, asyā api
	    prākṛtatvāt tathā cānyonyāśraya ity ata uktam --- śāśvatika iti/ bhaved etad evaṃ
	    yadīdaṃprathamatā sargasya bhaved anādau tu sargasaṃhāraprabandhe
	    sargāntarasamutpannasaṃjihīrṣāvadhisamaye pūrṇe mayā sattvaprakarṣa upādeya iti
	    praṇidhānaṃ kṛtvā bhagavāñ jagat saṃjahāra/ tadā ceśvaracittasattvaṃ praṇidhānavāsitaṃ
	    pradhānasāmyam upagatam api paripūrṇo mahāpralayāvadhau praṇidhānavāsanāvaśāt
	    tathaiveśvaracittasattvabhāvena pariṇamate/ yathā caitraḥ śvaḥ prātar evotthātavyaṃ
	    mayeti praṇidhāya suptas tadaivottiṣṭhati praṇidhānasaṃskārāt/ tasmād anāditvād
	    īśvarapraṇidhānasattvopādānayoḥ śāśvatikatvena nānyonyāśrayaḥ/ na ceśvarasya
	    cittasattvaṃ mahāpralaye+api na prakṛtisāmyam upaitīti vācyam/ yasya hi na kadācid api
	    pradhānasāmyaṃ na tat prādhānikaṃ nāpi citiśaktir ajñatvād ity arthāntaram aprāmāṇikam
	    āpadyeta/ tac cāyuktaṃ, prakṛtipuruṣavyatirekeṇārthāntarābhāvāt/ so+ayam īdṛśa īśvarasya
	    śāśvatika utkarṣaḥ/ sa kiṃ sanimittaḥ sapramāṇaka āhosvin nirnimitto niṣpramāṇaka iti/
	    uttaraṃ --- tasya śāstraṃ nimittam/ śrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇāni śāstram/ codayati ---
	    śāstraṃ punaḥ kiṃnimittam/ pratyakṣānumānapūrvaṃ hi śāstram/ na ceśvarasya
	    sattvaprakarṣe kasyacit pratyakṣam anumānaṃ vāsti/ na ceśvarapratyakṣaprabhavaṃ śāstram
	    iti yuktam/ kalpayitvāpi hy ayaṃ brūyād ātmaiśvaryaprakāśanāyeti bhāvaḥ/ pariharati ---
	    prakṛṣṭasattvanimittam/
children.translated_text: Here he asks: 'He who is that,' etc. For knowledge and action cannot belong to the <s>citi-śakti</s> (power of consciousness), which is incapable of transformation; hence it must be said that they reside in the pure <s>sattva</s> of the mind (<s>cittasattva</s>) free from <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>. And since <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is ever liberated, the relation of ownership (<s>svasvāmibhāva</s>) between him and the excellence of <s>cittasattva</s> born from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is impossible — hence it is said: 'through the adoption of supremely pure <s>sattva</s>.' <s>Īśvara</s>'s relation of ownership with <s>cittasattva</s> is not, like that of an ordinary person, bound by <s>avidyā</s>. Rather, [he reflects:] 'I shall rescue beings afflicted by the threefold suffering from the great ocean of transmigration through the teaching of the <s>dharma</s> of knowledge.' And that teaching is not possible without the attainment of a supreme excellence of the capacity for knowledge and action. And this [excellence] is not possible without the adoption of pure <s>sattva</s> whose impurities of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> have been removed — reflecting thus, the Lord adopts the excellence of <s>sattva</s>, even though he is untouched by <s>avidyā</s>. One who identifies with <s>avidyā</s> becomes ignorant of the true nature of <s>avidyā</s>, but not one who employs <s>avidyā</s> knowing it as <s>avidyā</s>. Indeed, an actor who assumes the role of <s>Rāma</s> and displays those various actions does not become deluded. Thus, this form of his is assumed, not intrinsic. One might object: the Lord must adopt <s>sattva</s> out of the desire to rescue, and through adopting it [arises] the desire to rescue — and since this too is material, there is mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>). Hence it is said: 'eternal,' etc. This would be so if creation had a first beginning; but in the beginningless succession of creation and dissolution, when the period culminating in the desire to withdraw, which arose from a previous creation, is completed, the Lord, having made the resolve 'I must adopt the excellence of <s>sattva</s>,' dissolved the world. Then the <s>cittasattva</s> of <s>Īśvara</s>, perfumed by that resolve, even though it has entered the equilibrium of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primary matter), when the period of the great dissolution is complete, transforms once again into the state of <s>Īśvara</s>'s <s>cittasattva</s> by the force of the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) of the resolve. Just as <s>Caitra</s>, having resolved 'I must wake up early tomorrow morning,' falls asleep but wakes up at that very time due to the <s>saṃskāra</s> (impression) of the resolve. Therefore, because of the beginninglessness of <s>Īśvara</s>'s resolve and his adoption of <s>sattva</s>, their being eternal means there is no mutual dependence. Nor should it be said that <s>Īśvara</s>'s <s>cittasattva</s> does not enter the equilibrium of <s>Prakṛti</s> even during the great dissolution. For what never enters the equilibrium of <s>Pradhāna</s> is neither a product of <s>Pradhāna</s> nor the <s>citi-śakti</s> [itself] — being ignorant, it would be an absurd third category. And that is untenable, since there is no entity apart from <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. This is the nature of the eternal excellence of <s>Īśvara</s>. Is it with a cause and a means of valid cognition, or is it causeless and without a means of valid cognition? The answer: scripture is its cause. <s>Śruti</s> (revealed texts), <s>Smṛti</s> (remembered tradition), <s>Itihāsa</s> (epics), and <s>Purāṇas</s> (ancient lore) are scripture. He raises an objection: what is the cause of scripture, in turn? For scripture is preceded by perception and inference. And no one has perception or inference regarding the excellence of <s>sattva</s> of <s>Īśvara</s>. Nor is it fitting [to say] that scripture originates from the perception of <s>Īśvara</s>. For even if one granted that, he might speak merely to display his own sovereignty — such is the purport. He resolves: 'caused by supremely pure <s>sattva</s>.'

children.text:
ayam abhisaṃdhiḥ --- mantrāyurvedeṣu tāvad
	    īśvarapraṇīteṣu pravṛttisāmarthyād arthāvyabhicāraviniścayāt prāmāṇyaṃ siddham/ na
	    cauṣadhibhedānāṃ tatsaṃyogaviśeṣāṇāṃ ca mantrāṇāṃ ca tattadvarṇāvāpoddhāreṇa sahasreṇāpi
	    puruṣāyuṣair laukikapramāṇavyavahārī śaktaḥ kartum anvayavyatirekau/ na cāgamād
	    anvayavyatirekau tābhyāṃ cāgamas tatsaṃtānayor anāditvād iti pratipādayituṃ yuktam/
	    mahāpralaye tatsaṃtānayor vicchedāt/ na ca tadbhāve pramāṇābhāvaḥ/ abhinnaṃ
	    pradhānavikāro jagad iti hi pratipādayiṣyate/ sadṛśapariṇāmasya ca visadṛśapariṇāmatā
	    dṛṣṭā/ yathā kṣīrekṣurasāder dadhiguḍādirūpam/ visadṛśapariṇāmasya pūrvaṃ
	    sadṛśapariṇāmatā ca dṛṣṭā/ tad iha pradhānenāpi mahadahaṃkārādirūpavisadṛśapariṇāmena
	    satā bhāvyaṃ kadācit sadṛśapariṇāmenāpi/ sadṛśapariṇāmaś cāsya sāmyāvasthā/ sa ca
	    mahāpralayaḥ/ tasmān mantrāyurvedapraṇayanāt tāvad bhagavato
	    vigalitarajastamomalāvaraṇatayā paritaḥ pradyotamānaṃ buddhisattvam āstheyam/ tathā
	    cābhyudayaniḥśreyasopadeśaparo+api vedarāśir īśvarapraṇītas tadbuddhisattvaprakarṣād eva
	    bhavitum arhati/ na ca sattvotkarṣe rajastamaḥprabhavau vibhramavipralambhau
	    saṃbhavataḥ/ tat siddhaṃ prakṛṣṭasattvanimittaṃ śāstram iti/ syād etat/
	    prakarṣakāryatayā prakarṣaṃ bodhayac chāstraṃ śeṣavad anumānaṃ bhaven na tv āgama ity
	    ata āha --- etayor iti/ na kāryatvena bodhayaty api tv anādivācyavācakabhāvasaṃbandhena
	    bodhayatīty arthaḥ/ īśvarasya hi buddhisattve prakarṣo vartate, śāstram api
	    tadvācakatvena tatra vartata iti/ upasaṃharati --- etasmād
	    īśvarabuddhisattvaprakarṣavācakāc chāstrād etad bhavati jñāyate viṣayeṇa viṣayiṇo
	    lakṣaṇāt sadaiveśvaraḥ sadaiva mukta iti/ tad evaṃ puruṣāntarād vyavacchidyeśvarāntarād
	    api vyavacchinatti --- tac ca tasyeti/ atiśayavinirmuktim āha --- na tāvad iti/ kutaḥ
	    --- yad eveti/ kasmāt sarvātiśayavinirmuktaṃ tadaiśvaryam ity ata āha --- tasmād
	    yatreti/ atiśayaniṣṭhām aprāptānām aupacārikam aiśvaryam ity arthaḥ/
children.translated_text: The purport is this: with respect to <s>mantras</s> and <s>Āyurveda</s> (medical science) at least, which are authored by <s>Īśvara</s>, their authoritativeness (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) is established through the efficacy of their operation and the ascertainment that their objects do not deviate. And no practitioner of worldly means of valid cognition, even with a thousand human lifetimes, is capable of establishing the agreement and difference (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) of the varieties of herbs, their specific combinations, and the <s>mantras</s>, through the inclusion and exclusion of their respective syllables. Nor is it fitting to maintain that agreement and difference [derive] from tradition, and tradition from agreement and difference — because of the beginninglessness of both lineages. [This is] because both those lineages are interrupted during the great dissolution. Nor is there an absence of a means of valid cognition in [the existence of] that. For it will be demonstrated that the world is an undifferentiated transformation of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primary matter). And it is observed that what undergoes similar transformation [later] undergoes dissimilar transformation — as milk, sugarcane juice, etc. take the form of curd, sugar, etc. And it is observed that what undergoes dissimilar transformation previously underwent similar transformation. Thus here too, <s>Pradhāna</s>, which has undergone dissimilar transformation in the form of <s>Mahat</s> (great principle), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), etc., must sometimes undergo similar transformation as well. And its similar transformation is the state of equilibrium (<s>sāmyāvasthā</s>). And that is the great dissolution. Therefore, from the composition of <s>mantras</s> and <s>Āyurveda</s> at least, the <s>buddhisattva</s> (intellective purity) of the Lord, from which the impurity and covering of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> have been removed, shining forth on all sides, must be acknowledged. And likewise, the mass of the <s>Vedas</s>, directed toward [teaching] worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>), being authored by <s>Īśvara</s>, is fitting to have arisen precisely from the excellence of his <s>buddhisattva</s>. And in the excellence of <s>sattva</s>, delusion and deception, which arise from <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, are not possible. Thus it is established that scripture is caused by supremely pure <s>sattva</s>. One might object: scripture, informing of the excellence as an effect [of sattva], would be an inference, like the remainder [of inferential arguments], not an <s>āgama</s> (verbal testimony). Hence he says: 'of these two,' etc. It does not inform [of it] by way of being an effect, but rather by the beginningless relation of signifier and signified — such is the meaning. For the excellence resides in the <s>buddhisattva</s> of <s>Īśvara</s>, and scripture also, as its signifier, is present there. He concludes: 'From this scripture, which signifies the excellence of <s>Īśvara</s>'s <s>buddhisattva</s>, this becomes known — from the characteristic of the possessor [being known] through [its] object — that <s>Īśvara</s> is ever [existent], ever liberated.' Thus, having distinguished [<s>Īśvara</s>] from other <s>puruṣas</s> (selves), he also distinguishes him from any other [putative] <s>Īśvara</s>: 'And that of his,' etc. He states freedom from superiority: 'Not so,' etc. Why? 'Because that very,' etc. Why is that sovereignty free from all superiority? Hence he says: 'Therefore, where,' etc. The sovereignty of those who have not reached the culmination of superiority is figurative — such is the meaning.

children.text:
sāmyavinirmuktim āha --- na ca tatsamānam iti/ prākāmyam avihatecchatā tadvighātān
	    ūnatvam (tadvighātād ūnatvam) anūnatve vā dvayor api prākāmyavighātaḥ kāryānutpatter
	    utpattau vā viruddhadharmasamāliṅgitam ekadā kāryam upalabhyetety āśayavān āha ---
	    dvayoś ceti/ aviruddhābhiprāyatve vā pratyekam īśvaratve kṛtam anyair ekenaiveśanāyāḥ
	    kṛtatvāt/ saṃbhūyakāritve vā na kaścid īśvaraḥ pariṣadvan nityeśanāyogināṃ ca
	    paryāyāyogāt kalpanāgauravaprasaṅgāc ceti draṣṭavyam/ tasmāt sarvam avadātam //1.24//
children.translated_text: He states freedom from equality: 'Nor is there one equal to that,' etc. '<s>Prākāmya</s>' (irresistible will) is the state of having unobstructed desire. From the obstruction of that, there is deficiency; or, if there is no deficiency [in either], then for both there is obstruction of their <s>prākāmya</s>, since an effect would either not arise, or if arising, would be apprehended as embraced by contradictory properties at once — with this intention he says: 'and of two,' etc. Or, if both have non-contradictory intentions, then since the sovereignty could be accomplished by one alone, there is no need for the other. Or, if they act in concert, then no one is [truly] <s>Īśvara</s> — like a council. And since it is impossible for those who are eternally sovereign to take turns, and since there would be the undesirable consequence of excessive postulation — thus it should be understood. Therefore, everything is clear. (1.24)

Now, the universe is constituted by the conscious and the unconscious alone, not by anything else. If <s>Īśvara</s> is unconscious, then he would be <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) — indeed the chief among the products of <s>Pradhāna</s> — and being within [<s>Pradhāna</s>], he could not be won over, since he would be unconscious. But if he is conscious, even so — since the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>) is indifferent and not subject to <s>saṃsāra</s>, and since it lacks <s>asmitā</s> (egoism), etc. — whence could he be won over? And whence could there be benevolent attention (<s>abhidhyāna</s>)? With this intent he says: 'Now, <s>Pradhāna</s>...' Here he replies with the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Īśvara</s> is a special <s>puruṣa</s> untouched by <s>kleśas</s>, <s>karma</s>, <s>vipāka</s>, and <s>āśayas</s>.' <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the rest are the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — they indeed afflict the <s>puruṣa</s>

children.text: tatra niratiśayaṃ sarvajñabījam //1.25//
children.translated_text: Therein, the seed of omniscience is unsurpassed. (1.25)

children.text:
evam asya kriyājñānaśaktau śāstraṃ pramāṇam abhidhāya jñānaśaktāv anumānaṃ pramāṇayati
	    --- kiṃ ca --- tatra niratiśayaṃ sarvajñabījam/ vyācaṣṭe --- yad idam iti/
	    buddhisattvāvarakatamopagamatāratamyena yad idam atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ pratyekaṃ ca
	    samuccayena ca vartamānānām atīndriyāṇāṃ grahaṇaṃ, tasya viśeṣaṇam alpaṃ bahv iti
	    sarvajñabījaṃ kāraṇam/ kaścit kiṃcid evātītādi gṛhṇāti kaścid bahu kaścid bahutaraṃ
	    kaścid bahutamam iti grāhyāpekṣayā grahaṇasyālpatvaṃ bahutvaṃ kṛtam/ etad vivardhamānaṃ
	    yatra niṣkrāntam atiśayāt sa sarvajña iti/ tad anena prameyamātraṃ kathitam/ atra
	    pramāṇayati --- asti kāṣṭhāprāptiḥ sarvajñabījasyeti/ sādhyanirdeśaḥ/ niratiśayatvaṃ
	    kāṣṭhā/ yataḥ param atiśayavattā nāstīti/ tena nāvadhimātreṇa siddhasādhanam/
	    sātiśayatvād iti hetuḥ/ yad yat sātiśayaṃ tat tat sarvaṃ niratiśayaṃ, yathā
	    kuvalāmalakabilveṣu sātiśayaṃ mahattvam ātmani niratiśayam iti vyāptiṃ darśayati ---
	    parimāṇavat/ na ca garimādibhir guṇair vyabhicāra iti sāṃpratam/ na khalv
	    avayavagarimātiśayī garimāvayavinaḥ kiṃ

tvā paramāṇubhya āntyāvayavibhyo
	    yāvantaḥ kecana teṣāṃ pratyekavartino garimṇaḥ samāhṛtya garimā vardhamānābhimānaḥ/
	    jñānaṃ tu na pratijñeyaṃ samāpyata ity ekadvibahuviṣayatayā yuktaṃ sātiśayam iti na
	    vyabhicāraḥ/ upasaṃharati --- yatra kāṣṭheti/ nanu santi bahavas tīrthakarā
	    buddhārhatakapilarṣiprabhṛtayas tat kasmāt ta eva sarvajñā na bhavanty asmād anumānād
	    ity ata āha --- sāmānyeti/ kutas tarhi tadviśeṣapratipattir ity ata āha --- tasyeti/
	    buddhādipraṇīta āgamābhāso na tv āgamaḥ,
	    sarvapramāṇabādhitakṣaṇikanairātmyādimārgopadeśakatvena vipralambhakatvād iti bhāvaḥ/
	    tena śrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇalakṣaṇād āgamata āgacchanti buddhim ārohanti asmād
	    abhyudayaniḥśreyasopāyā ity āgamaḥ, tasmāt saṃjñādiviśeṣapratipattiḥ/ saṃjñāviśeṣaḥ
	    śiveśvarādiḥ śrutyādiṣu prasiddhaḥ/ ādipadena ṣaḍaṅgatādaśāvyayate saṃgṛhīte/ yathoktaṃ
	    vāyupurāṇe ---
children.translated_text: The heaviness of all things collectively, from atoms to the final composite parts — each having its own individual weight, and the mass increasing [proportionally with size]. But knowledge should not be [similarly] conceived ...

Having thus established scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) as the authority for His powers of action and knowledge, he now validates inference as the authority for the power of knowledge — 'moreover' — 'in Him is the unsurpassed seed of omniscience.' He explains —

children.text:
"sarvajñatā tṛptir anādibodhaḥ svatantratā nityam aluptaśaktiḥ/ anantaśaktiś ca vibhor
	    vidhijñāḥ ṣaḍ āhur aṅgāni maheśvarasya"//

vāyupurāṇam
	    12.31
children.translated_text: [Reference to] <s>Vāyupurāṇa</s> 12.31.

'Omniscience, contentment, beginningless awareness, independence, eternally undiminished power, and infinite power — the knowers of the sacred ordinances declare these six to be the attributes of <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord).'

children.text: tathā ---
children.translated_text: Likewise —

children.text:
"jñānaṃ vairāgyam aiśvaryaṃ tapaḥ satyaṃ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ/ sraṣṭṛtvam ātmasaṃbodho hy
	    adhiṣṭhātṛtvam eva ca// avyayāni daśaitāni nityaṃ tiṣṭhanti śaṃkare"
vāyupurāṇam 10.60
children.translated_text: [Reference to] <s>Vāyupurāṇa</s> 10.60.

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: Thus.

'Knowledge, dispassion, sovereignty, austerity, truth, patience, steadfastness, creatorship, self-awareness, and the power of governance — these ten imperishable [qualities] always abide in <s>Śaṃ[kara]</s> (Śiva) ...'

children.text:
syād etat, nityatṛptasya bhagavato vairāgyātiśayasaṃpannasya svārthe tṛṣṇāsaṃbhavāt
	    kāruṇikasya ca sukhaikatānajanasarjanaparasya duḥkhabahulajīvalokajananānupapatter
	    aprayojanasya ca prekṣāvataḥ pravṛttyanupapatteḥ kriyāśaktiśālino+api na jagatkriyety
	    ata āha --- tasyātmānugrahābhāve+apīti/ bhūtānāṃ prāṇinām anugrahaḥ prayojanaṃ,
	    śabdādyupabhogavivekakhyātirūpakāryakaraṇāt kila caritārthaṃ cittaṃ nivartate/ tataḥ
	    puruṣaḥ kevalī bhavati/ atas tatprayojanāya kāruṇiko vivekakhyātyupāyaṃ kathayati/
	    tenācaritārthatvāc cittasya jantūnīśvaraḥ puṇyāpuṇyasahāyaḥ sukhaduḥkhe bhāvayann api
	    nākāruṇikaḥ/ vivekakhyātyupāyakathanāya

bhūtānugrahaṃ dvāram āha ---
	    jñānadharmopadeśeneti/ jñānaṃ ca dharmaś ca jñānadharmau tayor upadeśena
	    jñānadharmasamuccayāl labdhavivekakhyātiparipākāt kalpapralaye brahmaṇo dināvasāne yatra
	    satyalokavarjaṃ jagad astameti/ mahāpralaye sasatyalokasya brahmaṇo+api nidhane
	    saṃsāriṇaḥ svakāraṇagāmino 'tas tadā maraṇaduḥkhabhājaḥ, kalpety upalakṣaṇam anyadāpi
	    svārjitakarmapākavaśena janmamaraṇādibhājaḥ puruṣānuddhariṣyāmīti kaivalyaṃ prāpya
	    puruṣā uddhṛtā bhavantīty arthaḥ/ etac ca karuṇāprayuktasya jñānadharmopadeśanaṃ
	    kāpilānām api siddham ity āha --- tathā coktaṃ pañcaśikhācāryeṇa --- ādividvān kapila
	    iti/ ādividvān iti pañcaśikhācāryavacanam ādimuktasvasaṃtānādiguruviṣayaṃ na tv
	    anādimuktaparamaguruviṣayam/ ādimukteṣu kadācin mukteṣu vidvatsu kapilo+asmākam
	    ādividvān muktaḥ sa eva ca gurur iti/ kapilasyāpi jāyamānasya maheśvarānugrahād eva
	    jñānaprāptiḥ śrūyata iti/ kapilo nāma viṣṇor avatāraviśeṣaḥ prasiddhaḥ/ svayaṃbhūs tu
	    hiraṇyagarbhaḥ/ tasyāpi sāṃkhyayogaprāptir vede śrūyata iti/ sa eveśvara ādividvān
	    kapilo viṣṇur na svayaṃbhūr iti bhāvaḥ/ svāyaṃbhuvānāṃ tv īśvara iti bhāvaḥ //1.25//
children.translated_text: He states the door of beneficence toward beings — 'by the teaching of knowledge and <s>dharma</s>' — knowledge and <s>dharma</s> are <s>jñānadharma</s>; by the teaching of both, from the combination of knowledge and <s>dharma</s>, having obtained discrimination-knowledge (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) ...

One might object: since the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Lord), being eternally content and endowed with the highest dispassion, has no possibility of desire for his own sake, and since he is compassionate and intent on creating beings disposed solely to happiness — how is it [consistent with] beings whose lives are filled with suffering?

children.text: pūrveṣām api guruḥ kālenānavacchedāt //1.26//
children.translated_text: [Yogasūtra 1.26:] He is the teacher even of the ancients, since He is not limited by time.

children.text:
saṃprati bhagavato brahmādibhyo viśeṣam āha --- sa eṣa iti/ pātanikā --- sa eṣa iti/
	    sūtram --- pūrveṣām api guruḥ kālenānavacchedāt/ vyācaṣṭe --- pūrve hīti/ kālas tu
	    śatavarṣādir avacchedārthenāvacchedena prayojanena nopāvartate na vartate/ prakarṣasya
	    gatiḥ prāptiḥ/ pratyetavya āgamāt //1.26//
children.translated_text: Now he states the distinction of the <s>Bhagavān</s> from <s>Brahmā</s> and others — 'He is this' — <s>Pātañjala</s> [gloss]: 'He is this.' The sūtra: 'He is the teacher even of the ancients, since He is not limited by time.' He explains —

children.text: tasya vācakaḥ praṇavaḥ //1.27//
children.translated_text: [Yogasūtra 1.27:] His designator (<s>vācaka</s>) is <s>Praṇava</s> (the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>).

children.text:
tad anena prabandhena bhagavān īśvaro darśitaḥ/ saṃprati tatpraṇidhānaṃ darśayituṃ
	    tasya vācakam āha --- tasya vācakaḥ praṇavaḥ/ vyācaṣṭe --- vācya iti/ tatra pareṣāṃ
	    mataṃ vimarśadvāreṇopanyasyati --- kim asyeti/ vācakatvaṃ pratipādakatvam ity arthaḥ/
	    pare hi paśyanti yadi svābhāvikaḥ śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandhaḥ saṃketenāsmāc chabdād ayam
	    arthaḥ pratyetavya ityevamātmakenābhivyajyeta tato yatra nāsti sa saṃbandhas tatra
	    saṃketaśatenāpi na vyajyeta/ na hi pradīpavyaṅgyo ghaṭo yatra nāsti tatra
	    pradīpasahasreṇāpi śakyo vyaṅktum/ kṛtasaṃketas tu karabhaśabdo vāraṇe vāraṇapratipādako
	    dṛṣṭaḥ/ tataḥ saṃketakṛtam eva vācakatvam iti/ vimṛśyābhimatam avadhārayati ---
	    sthito+asyeti/ ayam abhiprāyaḥ --- sarva eva śabdāḥ sarvākārārthābhidhānasamarthā iti/
	    sthita evaiṣāṃ sarvākārair arthaiḥ svābhāvikaḥ saṃbandhaḥ/ īśvarasaṃketas tu prakāśakaś
	    ca niyāmakaś ca/ tasyeśvarasaṃketāsaṃketakṛtaś cāsya vācakāpabhraṃśavibhāgaḥ/ tad idam
	    āha --- saṃketas tv īśvarasyeti/ nidarśanam āha --- yatheti/ nanu śabdasya prādhānikasya
	    mahāpralayasamaye pradhānabhāvam upagatasya śaktir api pralīnā, tato
	    mahadādikrameṇotpannasyāvācakasyaiva māheśvareṇa saṃketena na śakyā vācakaśaktir
	    abhivyañjayituṃ vinaṣṭaśaktitvād ity ata āha --- sargāntareṣv apīti/ yady api saha
	    śaktyā pradhānasāmyam upagataḥ śabdas tathāpi punar āvirbhavaṃs tacchaktiyukta
	    evāvirbhavati varṣātipātasamadhigatamṛdbhāva ivodbhijjo meghavisṛṣṭavāridhārāvasekāt/
	    tena pūrvasaṃbandhasaṃketānusāreṇa saṃketaḥ kriyate bhagavateti/ tasmāt saṃpratipatteḥ
	    sadṛśavyavahāraparamparāyā nityatayā nityaḥ śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandho na kūṭasthanitya ity
	    āgamikāḥ pratijānate, na punar āgamanirapekṣāḥ sargāntareṣv api tādṛśa eva saṃketa iti
	    pratipattum īśata iti bhāvaḥ //1.27//
children.translated_text: By this sequence, the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Īśvara</s> has been demonstrated. Now, to show the practice of devotion to Him, he introduces His designator — 'His designator is <s>Praṇava</s>.' He explains — 'designator' (<s>vācaka</s>). There, he presents the view of others by way of critical examination — 'Is this [the relation]?' etc. Designator-hood (<s>vācakatva</s>) means the capacity to convey meaning — such is the sense. For others hold: if the relation between word and meaning is natural (<s>svābhāvika</s>), [then the convention] 'from this word, this meaning is to be understood' — a convention of such nature — would [merely] reveal [it]. Then, where that relation does not exist, even a hundred conventions could not reveal it. For a pot, which is revealed by a lamp, cannot be revealed by a thousand lamps where [the pot] does not exist. Yet the word '<s>karabha</s>' (young camel), through convention, is seen to denote an elephant (<s>vāraṇa</s>). Therefore, designator-hood is produced by convention alone — [so they say]. Having examined this, he establishes his own view — 'It is established that this [relation exists].' The purport is this: all words whatsoever are capable of denoting meanings of all forms. The natural relation of these [words] with meanings of all forms is well-established. But <s>Īśvara</s>'s convention is both illuminator and restrictor. And the distinction between a designator (<s>vācaka</s>) and a corrupted form (<s>apabhraṃśa</s>) is produced by <s>Īśvara</s>'s convention and non-convention. This he states — 'But the convention is <s>Īśvara</s>'s.' He gives an illustration — 'just as.' [Objection:] But at the time of the great dissolution (<s>mahāpralaya</s>), when the word, being a product of <s>Prakṛti</s>, has returned to its primal state, its power too is dissolved. Therefore, for a word that has arisen again through the sequence of <s>mahat</s> (intellect) and the rest, and which is [now] without designating power — that designating power cannot be revealed by <s>Maheśvara</s>'s convention, since its power has been destroyed. Hence he says — 'in other creations too.' Although the word has returned to equilibrium with <s>Prakṛti</s> along with its power, nevertheless, when it re-manifests, it re-manifests endowed with that very power — like a sprouting plant that had attained the state of earth during the prolonged rains, [re-emerging] from the irrigation of water-streams released by clouds. Therefore, the convention is made in accordance with the prior relation and convention — [thus states] the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Hence, those who follow scripture (<s>āgamikāḥ</s>) maintain that the relation between word and meaning is eternal through the eternity of the unbroken succession of similar usages — not eternal in the sense of immutable (<s>kūṭasthanitya</s>). But they are not able, independently of scripture, to ascertain that in other creation-cycles too the convention is exactly the same — such is the purport. //1.27//

children.text: tajjapas tadarthabhāvanam //1.28//
children.translated_text: 'Its repetition (<s>japa</s>) is the meditation on its meaning (<s>tadarthabhāvana</s>).' //1.28//

children.text:
vācakam ākhyāya praṇidhānam āha --- tajjapas tadarthabhāvanam/ vyācaṣṭe ---
	    praṇavasyeti/ bhāvanaṃ punaḥ punaś citte niveśanam/ tataḥ kiṃ sidhyatīty ata āha ---
	    praṇavam iti/ ekasmin bhagavaty āramati cittam/ atraiva vaiyāsikīṃ gāthām udāharati ---
	    tathā ceti/ tata īśvaraḥ samādhitatphalalābhena tam anugṛhṇāti //1.28//
children.translated_text: Having stated the designator, he introduces the practice of devotion (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) — 'Its repetition is the meditation on its meaning.' He explains — 'of <s>Praṇava</s>.' <s>Bhāvana</s> (meditation) is the repeated placing [of the object] in the mind. Then what is accomplished by that? Hence he says — '<s>Praṇava</s> [meditation].' The mind delights in the one <s>Bhagavān</s> (Lord). Here itself he cites a verse from <s>Vyāsa</s> — 'And thus.' Then <s>Īśvara</s>, through the attainment of <s>samādhi</s> and its fruits, bestows grace upon him. //1.28//

children.text: tataḥ pratyakcetanādhigamo+apy antarāyābhāvaś ca //1.29//
children.translated_text: 'From that [arises] the attainment of the inner Self (<s>pratyakcetana</s>) and also the absence of obstacles.' //1.29//

children.text:
kiṃ cāparam asmāt --- tataḥ pratyakcetanādhigamo+apy antarāyābhāvaś ca/ pratīpaṃ
	    viparītam añcati vijānātīti pratyak sa cāsau cetanaś ceti pratyakcetano+avidyāvān
	    puruṣaḥ/ tad aneneśvarāc chāśvatikasattvotkarṣasaṃpannād vidyāvato nivartayati/ pratīcaś
	    cetanasyādhigamo jñānaṃ svarūpato 'sya bhavaty antarāyā vakṣyamāṇās tadabhāvaś ca/ asya
	    vivaraṇaṃ --- ye tāvad iti/ svam ātmā tasya rūpam/ rūpagrahaṇenāvidyāsamāropitān dharmān
	    niṣedhati/ nanv īśvarapraṇidhānam īśvaraviṣayaṃ katham iva pratyakcetanaṃ sākṣātkaroty
	    atiprasaṅgād ity ata āha --- yathaiveśvara iti/ śuddhaḥ
	    kūṭasthanityatayodayavyayarahitaḥ prasannaḥ kleśavarjitaḥ kevalo dharmādharmāpetaḥ/ ata
	    evānupasargaḥ/ upasargā jātyāyurbhogāḥ/ sādṛśyasya kiṃcid bhedādhiṣṭhānatvād īśvarād
	    bhinatti --- buddheḥ pratisaṃvedīti/ tad anena pratyaggrahaṇaṃ vyākhyātam/
	    atyantavidharmiṇor anyatarārthānucintanaṃ na taditarasya sākṣātkārāya kalpate/

sadṛśārthānucintanaṃ tu sadṛśāntarasākṣātkāropayogitām anubhavati
	    ekaśāstrābhyāsa iva tatsadṛśārthaśāstrāntarajñānopayogitām/ pratyāsattis tu svātmani
	    sākṣātkārahetur na parātmanīti sarvam avadātam //1.29//
children.translated_text: But the contemplation of something similar does serve for the direct realization of the similar other — just as the study of one <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) serves for the knowledge of another treatise of similar content. Proximity (<s>pratyāsatti</s>), however, is the cause of direct realization of one's own Self, not of another's self — thus everything is clear. //1.29//

And what else [results] from this? — 'From that, the attainment of the inner Self and also the absence of obstacles.' <s>Pratyak</s> means 'reverse' or 'inward'; one who cognizes (<s>añcati</s>) in a reverse [inward] manner is <s>pratyak</s>; and he is a conscious being (<s>cetana</s>) — thus <s>pratyakcetana</s> is the <s>Puruṣa</s> endowed with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). By this, he distinguishes [the individual self] from <s>Īśvara</s>, who is endowed with the eternal excellence of <s>sattva</s> and with <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge). The attainment (<s>adhigama</s>) of the inner conscious being is knowledge of its own nature. The obstacles, to be described, and their absence [also result from this]. The explanation of this — 'Those, indeed,' etc. 'Own' (<s>sva</s>) is the Self (<s>ātman</s>); 'its form' (<s>rūpa</s>) [is its essential nature]. By the word 'form,' he negates the properties superimposed [upon it] by <s>avidyā</s>. [Objection:] Now, <s>Īśvara-praṇidhāna</s> (devotion to the Lord), being directed toward <s>Īśvara</s>, how can it bring the inner Self (<s>pratyakcetana</s>) to direct realization? — this would be an overextension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>). Hence he says — 'Just as <s>Īśvara</s> [is].' 'Pure' (<s>śuddha</s>) — free from arising and decay by virtue of immutable eternity (<s>kūṭasthanitya</s>). 'Lucid' (<s>prasanna</s>) — free from <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). 'Isolated' (<s>kevala</s>) — devoid of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit). Hence, 'free from afflictions' (<s>anupasarga</s>). The afflictions (<s>upasargas</s>) are birth, lifespan, and enjoyment. Because similarity has some difference as its basis, he distinguishes [the individual self] from <s>Īśvara</s> — '[the individual self is] the experiencer through <s>buddhi</s> (intellect).' By this, the word 'inner' (<s>pratyak</s>) [in the sūtra] is explained. The contemplation of something utterly dissimilar to another does not serve for the direct realization of that other.

children.text:
vyādhistyānasaṃśayapramādālasyāviratibhrāntidarśanālabdhabhūmikatvānavasthitatvāni
	      cittavikṣepās te+antarāyāḥ //1.30//
children.translated_text: 'Disease (<s>vyādhi</s>), dullness (<s>styāna</s>), doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), negligence (<s>pramāda</s>), laziness (<s>ālasya</s>), non-abstinence (<s>avirati</s>), erroneous perception (<s>bhrāntidarśana</s>), failure to attain a stage (<s>alabdhabhūmikatva</s>), and instability (<s>anavasthitatva</s>) — these distractions of the mind are the obstacles.' //1.30//

children.text:
pṛcchati --- atha ka iti/ sāmānyenottaram --- ya iti/ viśeṣasaṃkhye pṛcchati --- ka
	    iti/ uttaraṃ vyādhītyādisūtram/ antarāyā nava/ etāś cittavṛttayo yogāntarāyā
	    yogavirodhinaś cittasya vikṣepakāś cittaṃ khalv amī vyādhyādayo yogād vikṣipanty
	    apanayantīti vikṣepāḥ/ yogapratipakṣatve hetum āha --- sahaita iti/
	    saṃśayabhrāntidarśane tāvad vṛttitayā vṛttinirodhapratipakṣau/ ye+api na vṛttayo
	    vyādhiprabhṛtayas te+api vṛttisāhacaryāt tatpratipakṣā ity arthaḥ/ padārthān vyācaṣṭe
	    --- vyādhir iti/ dhātavo vātapittaśleṣmāṇaḥ śarīradhāraṇāt/ aśitapītāhārapariṇāmaviśeṣo
	    rasaḥ/ karaṇānīndriyāṇi teṣāṃ vaiṣamyaṃ nyūnādhikabhāva iti/ akarmaṇyatā karmānarhatā/
	    saṃśaya ubhayakoṭispṛgvijñānam/ saty apy atadrūpapratiṣṭhatvena saṃśayaviparyāsayor
	    abhede, ubhayakoṭisparśāsparśarūpāvāntaraviśeṣavivakṣayātra

bhedenopanyāsaḥ/ abhāvanam akaraṇaṃ tatrāprayatna iti yāvat/ kāyasya gurutvaṃ kaphādinā,
	    cittasya gurutvaṃ tamasā/ gardhas tṛṣṇā/ madhumatyādayaḥ samādhibhūmayaḥ/ labdhabhūmer
	    yadi tāvataiva susthitaṃmanyasya samādhibhreṣaḥ syāt tatas tasyā api bhūmer apāyaḥ syāt/
	    yasmāt samādhipratilambhe tadavasthitaṃ syāt tasmāt tatra prayatitavyam iti //1.30//
children.translated_text: on account of the subsidiary distinction [between them] — namely, that [doubt] touches both alternatives while [error does] not. Non-cultivation (<s>abhāvana</s>) is non-performance — that is, non-effort in that regard. Heaviness of the body [arises] from <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and the like; heaviness of the mind [arises] from <s>tamas</s> (inertia). Craving (<s>gardha</s>) is thirst (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). <s>Madhumatī</s> and the others are stages of <s>samādhi</s>. If one who has attained a stage becomes complacent, thinking 'this much is sufficient,' and there is a fall from <s>samādhi</s>, then there would also be loss of that very stage. Since upon the attainment of <s>samādhi</s> one must remain established in it, therefore one must strive in that regard. //1.30//

He asks — 'Now, what [are the obstacles]?' The general answer — 'those which,' etc. He asks about their specific number — 'what [are they]?' The answer is the <s>sūtra</s> beginning with 'disease,' etc. The obstacles are nine. These mental modifications are obstacles to <s>yoga</s>, opposed to <s>yoga</s>, and are distractions of the mind — for these [conditions] such as disease and the rest scatter the mind away from <s>yoga</s>, remove it [from yoga] — hence they are called distractions (<s>vikṣepas</s>). He states the reason for their being opposed to <s>yoga</s> — 'together with these,' etc. Doubt and erroneous perception, being themselves <s>vṛttis</s> (modifications), are directly opposed to the cessation of <s>vṛttis</s>. Those that are not <s>vṛttis</s> — disease and the rest — are also opposed [to yoga] because of their co-occurrence with <s>vṛttis</s> — such is the meaning. He explains the terms — 'disease,' etc. The <s>dhātus</s> (bodily constituents) are <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm) — called [<s>dhātus</s>] because they sustain the body. <s>Rasa</s> (chyle) is the specific transformation of consumed food and drink. <s>Karaṇas</s> (instruments) are the sense organs; their imbalance (<s>vaiṣamya</s>) is their state of deficiency or excess. Unfitness for action (<s>akarmaṇyatā</s>) is the inability to perform action. Doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) is a cognition that touches both alternatives. Although there is no [essential] difference between doubt and error (<s>viparyāsa</s>), since both rest upon what is not the [true] nature [of the object], a distinct mention is made here

children.text: duḥkhadaurmanasyāṅgamejayatvaśvāsapraśvāsā vikṣepasahabhuvaḥ //1.31//
children.translated_text: 'Pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), despair (<s>daurmanasya</s>), trembling of the body (<s>aṅgamejayatva</s>), [faulty] inhalation (<s>śvāsa</s>), and exhalation (<s>praśvāsa</s>) are co-existent with the distractions.' //1.31//

children.text:
na kevalaṃ navāntarāyā duḥkhādayo+apy asya tatsahabhuvo bhavantīty āha --- duḥkhetyādi/
	    pratikūlavedanīyaṃ duḥkham ādhyātmikaṃ śārīraṃ vyādhivaśān mānasaṃ ca kāmādivaśāt/
	    ādhibhautikaṃ vyāghrādijanitam/ ādhidaivikaṃ grahapīḍādijanitam/ tac cedaṃ duḥkhaṃ
	    prāṇimātrasya pratikūlavedanīyatayā heyam ity āha --- yenābhihatā iti/ anicchataḥ prāṇo
	    yad bāhyaṃ vāyum ācāmati pibati praveśayatīti yāvat sa śvāsaḥ samādhyaṅgarecakavirodhī/
	    anicchato+api prāṇo yat kauṣṭhyaṃ vāyuṃ niścārayati niḥsārayati sa praśvāsaḥ
	    samādhyaṅgapūrakavirodhī //1.31//
children.translated_text: Not only are the nine obstacles [present], but pain and the rest are also their accompaniments — hence he says: 'Pain,' etc. Unfavorable sensation is pain (<s>duḥkha</s>) — <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self): bodily, arising from disease; and mental, arising from desire and the like. <s>Ādhibhautika</s> (pertaining to beings): caused by tigers and such. <s>Ādhidaivika</s> (pertaining to the divine): caused by planetary afflictions and the like. And this pain, being an unfavorable sensation for all living beings, is to be abandoned — hence he says: 'by which one is afflicted,' etc. <s>Śvāsa</s> (inhalation) is when, involuntarily, <s>prāṇa</s> (the vital breath) draws in — that is, inhales, takes in — the external air; this is opposed to <s>recaka</s> (the yogic practice of exhalation), which is a limb of <s>samādhi</s>. <s>Praśvāsa</s> (exhalation) is when, even involuntarily, <s>prāṇa</s> expels — that is, sends out — the internal air; this is opposed to <s>pūraka</s> (the yogic practice of inhalation), which is a limb of <s>samādhi</s>. //1.31//

children.text: tatpratiṣedhārtham ekatattvābhyāsaḥ //1.32//
children.translated_text: 'For the prevention of those, [there is] the practice of a single principle (<s>ekatattvābhyāsa</s>).' //1.32//

children.text:
uktārthopasaṃhārasūtram avatārayati --- athaita iti/ athoktārthānantaram upasaṃharann
	    idaṃ sūtram āheti saṃbandhaḥ/ niroddhavyatve hetur uktaḥ --- samādhipratipakṣā iti/ yady
	    apīśvarapraṇidhānād ity abhyāsamātram uktaṃ tathāpi vairāgyam iha tatsahakāritayā
	    grāhyam ity āha --- tābhyām uktalakṣaṇābhyām evābhyāsavairāgyābhyāṃ niroddhavyāḥ/ tatra
	    tayor abhyāsavairāgyayor madhye+abhyāsasyānantaroktasyeti/ tatpratiṣedhārtham ityādi/
	    ekaṃ tattvam īśvaraḥ prakṛtatvād iti/ vaināśikānāṃ

tat sarvam ekāgram eva
	    cittaṃ nāsti kiṃcid vikṣiptam iti tadupadeśānāṃ tadarthānāṃ ca pravṛttīnāṃ vaiyarthyam
	    ity āha --- yasya tv iti/ yasya mate pratyarthe+arpyamāṇa ekasminn anekasmin vā niyataṃ
	    yāvad arthāvabhāsam utpannaṃ tatraiva samāptam ananyagāmi/ arthāntaraṃ tāvat prathamaṃ
	    gṛhītvārthāntaram api paścāt kasmān na gṛhṇātīty ata āha --- kṣaṇikaṃ ca
	    kṣaṇasyābhedyatvena pūrvapaścādbhāvasyāpy abhāva iti bhāvaḥ/ asmanmate tv akṣaṇikaṃ
	    cittaṃ svaviṣaya ekasminn anekasmin vānavasthitaṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ
	    tattadviṣayopādānaparityāgābhyāṃ viṣayāniyataṃ vikṣiptam ato vikṣepapariṇāmam apanīya
	    śakyaikāgratādhātum iti tadupadeśapravṛttyor nānarthakatvam ity āha --- yadi punar idam
	    iti/ upasaṃharati --- ato neti/ vaināśikam utthāpayati --- yo+apīti/ mā bhūd ekasmin
	    kṣaṇike citta ekāgratādhānaprayatnaḥ/ cittasaṃtāne tv anādāv akṣaṇike vikṣepam
	    apanīyaikāgratādhāsyata ity arthaḥ/ tad etad vikalpya dūṣayati --- tasyeti/ tasya
	    darśana ekāgratā yadi pravāhacittasya cittasaṃtānasya vā dharmaḥ/ tatraikaṃ kramavad
	    utpādeṣu pratyayeṣv anugataṃ nāsti pravāhacittam/ kutaḥ, yad yāvad asti tasya sarvasya
	    kṣaṇikatvād akṣaṇikasya cāsattvād bhavatāṃ darśana iti bhāvaḥ/ dvitīyaṃ kalpaṃ gṛhṇāti
	    --- atheti/ sāṃvṛtasya pravāhasyāṃśaḥ pratyayaḥ paramārthasaṃs tasya pratyayasyaikāgratā
	    prayatnasādhyo dharmaḥ/ dūṣayati --- sa sarvaḥ sāṃvṛtapravāhāpekṣayā
	    sadṛśapratyayapravāhī vā visadṛśapratyayapravāhī vā/ ataḥ paramārthasattārūpeṇa
	    pratyarthaniyatatvād yadarthāvabhāsa utpannas tatra samāptatvād ekāgra eveti
	    vikṣiptacittānupapattiḥ, yad apanayenaikāgratādhīyata iti/ upasaṃharati --- tasmād iti/
children.translated_text: All that [mind] is solely one-pointed; there is no distracted <s>citta</s> (mind) whatsoever — thus the teachings concerning that [one-pointedness] and the activities directed toward that purpose would be futile — to this he says: 'yasya tv iti' (but for one whose...). In whose view, when applied to each object, whether one or many, [each cognition] is necessarily produced only for the duration of the appearance of that object and, being completed therein, does not proceed to anything else. Why then, having first grasped one object, does it not subsequently grasp another object as well? To this he says: 'kṣaṇikaṃ ca' — because it is momentary, since a moment is indivisible, there is no possibility even of a before and after — this is the purport. But in our view, the <s>citta</s> is non-momentary, and being unsettled in its own object, whether one or many, it is distracted (<s>vikṣipta</s>) because at every moment it is unfixed with respect to objects through the acquisition and abandonment of various objects. Therefore, by removing the transformation of distraction (<s>vikṣepa-pariṇāma</s>), one-pointedness (<s>ekāgratā</s>) can be established in it — hence the teaching and the activity directed toward it are not purposeless — to this he says: 'yadi punar idam iti.' He concludes: 'ato na' iti. He raises the Buddhist [objection]: 'yo 'pi' iti. Let there be no effort to establish one-pointedness in a single momentary <s>citta</s>; but in the beginningless, non-momentary stream of mind (<s>citta-saṃtāna</s>), one-pointedness will be established by removing distraction — this is the meaning. He takes up this alternative and refutes it: 'tasya' iti.
