If, in that [Buddhist] view, one-pointedness is a property either of the stream-mind (<s>pravāha-citta</s>) or of the mental continuum (<s>citta-saṃtāna</s>) — regarding the first, there is no single stream-mind persisting through sequentially arising cognitions (<s>pratyaya</s>), because everything that exists is momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>) according to you, and what is non-momentary has no existence — this is the purport. He takes up the second alternative: 'atha' iti. The conventional (<s>sāṃvṛta</s>) stream's component is a cognition that is ultimately real (<s>paramārtha-sat</s>), and one-pointedness is a property of that cognition achievable through effort. He refutes this: that [cognition], with respect to the conventional stream, is either a stream of similar cognitions or a stream of dissimilar cognitions. Therefore, since each is determined to its own object in its ultimately real form, and since, having arisen as the appearance of that object, it is completed therein, it is one-pointed by nature — hence the impossibility of a distracted mind, whose removal would allow one-pointedness to be established. He concludes: 'tasmāt' iti.

children.text:
ito+api cittam ekam anekārtham avasthitaṃ cety āha --- yadi ceti/ yathā
	    hi maitreṇādhītasya śāstrasya na caitraḥ smarati/ yathā vā maitreṇāpacitasya puṇyasya
	    pāpasya vā karmāśayasya phalaṃ tadasaṃbandhī caitro na bhuṅkte, evaṃ
	    pratyayāntaradṛṣṭasya pratyayāntaraṃ na smaret/ pratyayāntaropacitasya vā karmāśayasya
	    phalaṃ ca na pratyayāntaram upabhuñjītety arthaḥ/ nanu nātiprasajyete kāryakāraṇabhāve
	    satīti viśeṣaṇāc chrāddhavaiśvānarīyeṣṭyādāv akartṛmātṛpitṛputrādigāmiphaladarśanān
	    madhurarasabhāvitānāṃ vāmrabījādīnāṃ paramparayā phalamādhuryaniyamād ity ata āha ---
	    samādhīyamānam apy etad iti/ ayam abhisaṃdhiḥ --- kaḥ khalv ekasaṃtānavartināṃ
	    pratyayānāṃ saṃtānāntaravartibhyaḥ pratyayebhyo viśeṣo yenaikasaṃtānavartinā
	    pratyayenānubhūtasyopacitasya ca karmāśayasya tatsaṃtānavarty eva pratyayaḥ smartā
	    bhoktā ca syān nānyasaṃtānavartī/ na hi saṃtāno nāma kaścid asti vastusan/ ya enaṃ
	    saṃtānaṃ saṃtānāntaravartibhyo bhindyāt/ na ca kālpaniko bhedaḥ kriyāyām upapadyate/ na
	    khalu kalpitāgnibhāvo māṇavakaḥ pacati/ na ca kāryakāraṇabhāvasaṃbandho 'pi vāstavaḥ/
	    sahabhuvoḥ savyetaraviṣāṇayor ivābhāvād asahabhuvor api pratyutpannāśrayatvāyogāt/ na hy
	    atītānāgatau vyāsajjya pratyutpannaṃ vartitum arhataḥ/ tasmāt saṃtānena vā
	    kāryakāraṇabhāvena vā svābhāvikenānupahitāḥ paramārthasantaḥ pratyayāḥ
	    parasparāsaṃsparśitvena svasaṃtānavartibhyaḥ parasaṃtānavartibhyo vā pratyayāntarebhyo
	    na bhidyante/ so+ayaṃ gomayaṃ ca pāyasaṃ cādhikṛtya pravṛtto nyāyo gomayaṃ pāyasaṃ
	    gavyatvād ubhayasiddhapāyasavad iti/ tam ākṣipati nyāyābhāsatvena tato+apy adhikatvād
	    iti/ na cātra kṛtanāśākṛtābhyāgamaṃ codyam/ yataś cittam eva karmaṇāṃ kartṛ tad eva
	    tajjanitābhyāṃ sukhaduḥkhābhyāṃ yujyate/ sukhaduḥkhe ca citicchāyāpannaṃ cittaṃ bhuṅkta
	    iti puruṣe bhogābhimānaś citicittayor abhedagrahād iti/ svapratyayaṃ pratītya
	    samutpannānāṃ svabhāva evaiṣāṃ tādṛśo yat ta eva smaranti phalaṃ copabhuñjate na tv
	    anye/ na ca svabhāvā niyogaparyanuyogāv arhanti evaṃ bhavata maivaṃ bhūteti vā kasmān
	    naivam iti ceti/ yaḥ pūrvokte na parituṣyati taṃ pratyāha --- kiṃ ca svātmeti/
	    udayavyayadharmāṇām
children.translated_text: From this also [it follows that] the <s>citta</s> is one, apprehends many objects, and is enduring — to this he says: 'yadi ca' iti. For just as <s>Caitra</s> does not remember the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) studied by <s>Maitra</s>, or just as <s>Caitra</s>, who is unconnected with the merit or demerit accumulated by <s>Maitra</s>, does not experience the fruit of that <s>karmāśaya</s> (latent karmic impression) — so too, one cognition would not remember what was perceived by another cognition, nor would one cognition experience the fruit of the <s>karmāśaya</s> accumulated by another cognition — this is the meaning. [Objection:] Is there not an over-extension [of this argument], since when a cause-effect relation obtains, we see that the fruit accrues to someone other than the agent, as in the <s>Śrāddha</s>, <s>Vaiśvānarī</s> sacrifice, etc., where the fruit reaches the non-agent — mother, father, son, and others — and since seeds of mango etc. that have been imbued with sweet flavor invariably produce sweet fruit through a succession [of causes]? To this he says: 'samādhīyamānam apy etad' iti. The intent is this: what indeed is the difference between cognitions belonging to one continuum (<s>saṃtāna</s>) and cognitions belonging to another continuum, such that a cognition within the same continuum would be the rememberer and experiencer of what was experienced and accumulated by [another cognition in] that continuum, and not a cognition belonging to another continuum? For a continuum (<s>saṃtāna</s>) is not anything really existing that could distinguish this continuum from cognitions belonging to other continua. Nor can a merely imagined distinction operate in actual activity — for a boy who is merely imagined to be fire does not cook. Nor is the cause-effect relation itself ultimately real, since for things existing simultaneously, like the right and left horns [of a cow], it is absent, and for non-simultaneous things too, the dependence on a present substratum is untenable — for the past and the future cannot engage with the present. Therefore, cognitions that are ultimately real, unmodified by either continuum or cause-effect relation or inherent nature, being mutually untouching, do not differ from other cognitions whether in their own continuum or in another's continuum. This is the reasoning deployed regarding cow-dung and rice-pudding: 'cow-dung is rice-pudding, because it is bovine, like rice-pudding which is accepted by both [parties].' He dismisses this as a mere semblance of reasoning (<s>nyāyābhāsa</s>), since [the actual consequence] goes even further than that. Nor is the objection of destruction of what is done and arrival of what is not done [applicable] here, since the <s>citta</s> alone is the agent of <s>karmas</s> (actions), and it alone is connected with the pleasure and pain born from them; and the <s>citta</s> that has assumed the reflection of pure consciousness (<s>citi-chāyā</s>) experiences [pleasure and pain] — while the attribution of experience to <s>puruṣa</s> (the Self) is due to the failure to distinguish between consciousness (<s>citi</s>) and mind (<s>citta</s>). [The Buddhist says:] those [cognitions] that arise dependently from their own [preceding] cognition — it is simply their nature that they themselves remember and experience the fruit, and not others. And natures do not admit of the demand 'why is it so and not otherwise?' He addresses one who is not satisfied with what was stated before: 'kiṃ ca svātma' iti. Of experiences and memories of experiences, which have the nature of arising and perishing,

children.text:
anubhavānām anubhavasmṛtīnāṃ ca nānātve+api tadāśrayam
	    abhinnaṃ cittam aham iti pratyayaḥ pratisaṃdadhānaḥ katham atyantabhinnān pratyayān
	    ālambeta/ nanu grahaṇasmaraṇarūpakāraṇabhedāt
	    pārokṣyāpārokṣyarūpaviruddhadharmasaṃsargād vā na pratyabhijñānaṃ nāmaikaḥ pratyayo
	    yataḥ pratyayinaś cittasyaikatā syād ity ata āha --- svānubhaveti/ nanu
	    kāraṇabhedaviruddhadharmasaṃsargāv evātra bādhakāv uktāv ity ata āha --- na ca
	    pratyakṣasyeti/ pratyakṣānusārata eva sāmagryabhedaḥ pārokṣyāpārokṣyadharmāvirodhaś
	    copapādito nyāyakaṇikāyām/ akṣaṇikasya cārthakriyā nyāyakaṇikābrahmatattvasamīkṣābhyām
	    upapāditeti sarvam avadātam //1.32//
children.translated_text: even though they are diverse, the cognition 'I' (<s>aham iti pratyayaḥ</s>), which reconnects them to a single undifferentiated <s>citta</s> as their substratum — how could it apprehend cognitions that are utterly distinct [from one another]? [Objection:] Since there is a difference of causes in the form of perception and memory, or since there is a conjunction of contradictory properties in the form of directness and indirectness, recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) is not a single cognition, from which the unity of the <s>citta</s> as its object could be established — to this he says: 'svānubhava' iti. [Objection:] But the very difference of causes and the conjunction of contradictory properties have been stated as invalidating [the argument] — to this he says: 'na ca pratyakṣasya' iti. Following direct perception itself, the non-difference of the causal complex and the non-contradiction of the properties of directness and indirectness have been established in the <s>Nyāyakaṇikā</s>. And the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) of a non-momentary entity has been established in the <s>Nyāyakaṇikā</s> and the <s>Brahmatattvasamīkṣā</s> — thus everything is clear. //1.32//

He introduces the <s>sūtra</s> that summarizes the stated topics — 'Now this,' etc. 'Now' — after the stated topics, he summarizes with this <s>sūtra</s> — such is the connection. The reason for [the need to] cease [the distractions] has been stated — 'because they are opposed to <s>samādhi</s>.' Although through [the mention of] <s>Īśvara-praṇidhāna</s> only practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) was stated, dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) should also be understood here as its cooperant — hence he says: 'By those two, of the described characteristics — by practice and dispassion alone — [the distractions] are to be ceased.' Among those two, practice and dispassion, practice was just mentioned — [hence]: 'For the prevention of those,' etc. The single principle (<s>ekatattva</s>) is <s>Īśvara</s>, because He is the topic under discussion. The <s>Vaināśikas</s> (annihilationists) —

children.text:
maitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣāṇāṃ sukhaduḥkhapuṇyāpuṇyaviṣayāṇāṃ bhāvanātaś
	      cittaprasādanam //1.33//
children.translated_text: Through the cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) of <s>maitrī</s> (friendliness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>muditā</s> (joy), and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) toward those who are happy, suffering, virtuous, and non-virtuous [respectively], [comes] the clarification of the mind (<s>citta-prasādana</s>). //1.33//

children.text:
aparikarmitamanaso+asūyādimataḥ samādhitadupāyasaṃpattyanutpādāc cittaprasādanopāyān
	    asūyādivirodhinaḥ pratipādayitum upakramate --- yasya cittasyāvasthitasyedam iti/
	    maitrīkaruṇetyādiprasādanāntam/ sukhiteṣu maitrīṃ sauhārdaṃ bhāvayata īrṣyākāluṣyaṃ
	    nivartate cittasya/ duḥkhiteṣu ca karuṇām ātmanīva parasmin duḥkhaprahāṇecchāṃ
	    bhāvayataḥ parāpakāracikīrṣākāluṣyaṃ cetaso nivartate/ puṇyaśīleṣu prāṇiṣu muditāṃ
	    harṣaṃ bhāvayato+asūyākāluṣyaṃ cetaso nivartate/ apuṇyaśīleṣu copekṣāṃ mādhyasthyaṃ
	    bhāvayato+amarṣakāluṣyaṃ

cetaso nivartate/ tataś cāsya
	    rājasatāmasadharmanivṛttau sāttvikaḥ śuklo dharma upajāyate/ sattvotkarṣasaṃpannaḥ
	    saṃbhavati vṛttinirodhapakṣe/ tasya prasādasvābhāvyāc cittaṃ prasīdati/ prasannaṃ ca
	    vakṣyamāṇebhya upāyebhya ekāgraṃ sthitipadaṃ labhate/ asatyāṃ punar maitryādibhāvanāyāṃ
	    na ta upāyāḥ sthityai kalpanta iti //1.33//
children.translated_text: is removed from the mind. Thereupon, with the cessation of <s>rājasa</s> (passionate) and <s>tāmasa</s> (dark) properties, the <s>sāttvika</s> (luminous), pure <s>dharma</s> arises. Endowed with the predominance of <s>sattva</s>, [the yogin] becomes capable of the cessation of mental modifications (<s>vṛtti-nirodha</s>). Due to the natural tendency toward clarity (<s>prasāda</s>) of that [sattva-predominant mind], the <s>citta</s> becomes clear. And the clarified [mind], through the means to be described hereafter, attains one-pointedness (<s>ekāgratā</s>) — a stable state (<s>sthiti-pada</s>). However, in the absence of the cultivation of <s>maitrī</s> and the rest, those means are not effective for [achieving] stability. //1.33//

Since for one whose mind is unpurified and afflicted by envy and the like, the attainment of <s>samādhi</s> and its means does not arise, he undertakes to teach the means of mental clarification (<s>citta-prasādana</s>) that are opposed to envy and the rest — [this is indicated by] 'yasya cittasyāvasthitasya idam iti,' [continuing through] 'maitrī-karuṇā' etc. up to 'prasādana.' By cultivating <s>maitrī</s> (friendliness), that is, goodwill (<s>sauhārda</s>), toward the happy, the impurity of jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) in the mind is removed. And by cultivating <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) toward the suffering — the wish to remove another's pain as if it were one's own — the impurity of the desire to harm others (<s>parāpakāra-cikīrṣā</s>) is removed from the mind. By cultivating <s>muditā</s> (joy), that is, delight (<s>harṣa</s>), toward beings of virtuous conduct, the impurity of envy (<s>asūyā</s>) is removed from the mind. And by cultivating <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), that is, impartiality (<s>mādhyasthya</s>), toward those of non-virtuous conduct, the impurity of intolerance (<s>amarṣa</s>)

children.text: pracchardanavidhāraṇābhyāṃ vā prāṇasya //1.34//
children.translated_text: Or, by expulsion (<s>pracchardana</s>) and retention (<s>vidhāraṇa</s>) of <s>prāṇa</s> (breath). //1.34//

children.text:
tān idānīṃ sthityupāyān āha --- pracchardanavidhāraṇābhyāṃ vā prāṇasya/ vāśabdo
	    vakṣyamāṇopāyāntarāpekṣo vikalpārthaḥ, na maitryādibhāvanāpekṣayā tayā saha samuccayāt/
	    pracchardanaṃ vivṛṇoti --- kauṣṭhyasyeti/ prayatnaviśeṣād yogaśāstravihitād yena
	    kauṣṭhyo vāyur nāsikāpuṭābhyāṃ śanai recyate/ vidhāraṇaṃ vivṛṇoti --- vidhāraṇaṃ
	    prāṇāyāmaḥ/ recitasya prāṇasya kauṣṭhyasya vāyor yad āyāmo bahir eva sthāpanaṃ na tu
	    sahasā praveśanam/ tad etābhyāṃ pracchardanavidhāraṇābhyāṃ vāyor laghukṛtaśarīrasya
	    manaḥ sthitipadaṃ labhate/ atra cottarasūtragatāt sthitinibandhanītipadāt sthitigrahaṇam
	    ākṛṣya saṃpādayed ity arthaprāptena saṃbandhanīyam //1.34//
children.translated_text: He now states those means of steadiness — 'Or by exhalation and retention of <s>prāṇa</s> (breath).' The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) indicates an alternative in relation to the other means to be mentioned hereafter, not a combination with the cultivation of <s>maitrī</s> (friendliness) and the like, since it is combined with that [already]. He explains exhalation — 'of the abdominal [breath]': by a specific effort prescribed in the <s>Yogaśāstra</s> (science of Yoga), by which the abdominal air is gently expelled through the two nostrils. He explains retention — 'retention is <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control)': the extension of the exhaled <s>prāṇa</s>, the abdominal air — that is, holding it outside and not allowing it to re-enter suddenly. Thus, by these two — exhalation and retention — the mind of one whose body has been made light attains the state of steadiness. And here, from the phrase '<s>sthitinibandhanī</s>' (binding to steadiness) occurring in the next <s>sūtra</s>, the word '<s>sthiti</s>' (steadiness) should be drawn in and connected [with this sūtra] — this is understood from the meaning. (1.34)

children.text: viṣayavatī vā pravṛttir utpannā manasaḥ sthitinibandhanī //1.35//
children.translated_text: Or a sensory activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) that has arisen, being related to objects, binds the mind to steadiness. (1.35)

children.text:
sthityupāyāntaram āha --- viṣayavatī vā pravṛttir utpannā manasaḥ sthitinibandhanī/
	    vyācaṣṭe --- nāsikāgre dhārayata iti/ dhāraṇādhyānasamādhīn kurvatas tajjayādyā
	    divyagandhasaṃvittatsākṣātkāraḥ/ evam anyāsv api pravṛttiṣu yojyam/ etac cāgamāt
	    pratyetavyaṃ nopapattitaḥ/ syād etat kim etādṛgbhir vṛttibhiḥ kaivalyaṃ
	    pratyanupayoginībhir ity ata āha --- etā vṛttayo+alpenaiva kālenotpannāś cittam
	    īśvaraviṣayāyāṃ vā vivekakhyātiviṣayāyāṃ

vā sthitau nibadhnanti/ nanv
	    anyaviṣayā vṛttiḥ katham anyatra sthitiṃ nibadhnātīty ata āha --- saṃśayaṃ vidhamanti
	    apasārayanti ata eva samādhiprajñāyām iti/ vṛttyantarāṇām apy āgamasiddhānāṃ
	    viṣayavattvam atidiśati --- eteneti/ nanv āgamādibhir avagateṣv artheṣu kutaḥ saṃśaya
	    ity ata āha --- yady api hīti/ śraddhāmūlo hi yoga upadiṣṭārthaikadeśapratyakṣīkaraṇe ca
	    śraddhātiśayo jāyate/ tanmūlāś ca dhyānādayo+asyāpratyūhaṃ bhavantīty arthaḥ //1.35//
children.translated_text: One might ask: how does a <s>vṛtti</s> (modification) directed to one object bind [the mind] to steadiness in another? Hence he says — 'they dispel' — they remove doubt, and hence [they lead to] the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s>. He extends the quality of being related to objects to the other [vṛttis] as well, which are established by scripture — 'by this,' etc. One might ask: when the objects are known through scripture and the like, whence [comes] doubt? Hence he says — 'for indeed,' etc. For <s>yoga</s> is rooted in faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), and when a portion of the taught content is made perceptible, an excess of faith arises. Rooted in that [faith], meditation and the rest proceed for him without obstruction — such is the meaning. (1.35)

He states another means of steadiness — 'Or a sensory activity that has arisen, being related to objects, binds the mind to steadiness.' He explains — 'while concentrating on the tip of the nose': for one who performs <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) [on that point], the mastery over them [results in] the direct perception of divine fragrance — that is its realization. The same should be applied to the other [sensory] activities as well. And this is to be understood from scripture (<s>āgama</s>), not from reasoning alone. One might ask: what use are such <s>vṛttis</s> (modifications) that are not conducive to <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation)? Hence he says — 'These <s>vṛttis</s>, having arisen in only a short time, bind the mind to steadiness, whether directed toward <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) or toward <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative discernment).'

children.text: viśokā vā jyotiṣmatī //1.36//
children.translated_text: Or [the mind attains steadiness through a state that is] sorrowless and luminous. (1.36)

children.text:
viśokā vā jyotiṣmatī/ vigataśokā duḥkharahitā jyotiṣmatī jyotir asyā astīti jyotiṣmatī
	    prakāśarūpā/ hṛdayapuṇḍarīka iti/ udarorasor madhye yat padmam adhomukhaṃ tiṣṭhaty
	    aṣṭadalaṃ recakaprāṇāyāmena tad ūrdhvamukhaṃ kṛtvā tatra cittaṃ dhārayet/ tanmadhye
	    sūryamaṇḍalam akāro jāgaritasthānaṃ tasyopari candramaṇḍalam ukāraḥ svapnasthānam/
	    tasyopari vahnimaṇḍalaṃ makāraḥ suṣuptisthānam/ tasyopari paravyomātmakaṃ brahmanādaṃ
	    turīyasthānam ardhamātram udāharanti brahmavādinaḥ/ tatra karṇikāyām ūrdhvamukhī
	    sūryādimaṇḍalamadhyagā brahmanāḍī/ tato+apy ūrdhvaṃ pravṛttā suṣumnā nāma nāḍī/

tayā khalu bāhyāny api sūryādīni maṇḍalāni protāni/ sa hi cittasthānam/
	    tasyāṃ dhārayato yoginaś cittasaṃvid upajāyate/ upapattipūrvakaṃ buddhisaṃvida ākāram
	    ādarśayati --- buddhisattvaṃ hīti/ ākāśakalpam iti vyāpitām āha/ sūryādīnāṃ prabhās
	    tāsāṃ rūpaṃ tadākāreṇa vikalpate nānārūpā bhavati/ manaś cātra buddhir abhimataṃ na tu
	    mahattattvam/ tasya ca suṣumnāsthasya vaikārikāhaṃkārajanmanaḥ sattvabahulatayā
	    jyotīrūpatā vivakṣitā/ tattadviṣayagocaratayā ca vyāpitvam api siddham/ asmitākārye
	    manasi samāpattiṃ darśayitvāsmitāsamāpatteḥ svarūpam āha --- tatheti/ śāntam
	    apagatarajastamastaraṅgam/ anantaṃ vyāpi/ asmitāmātraṃ na punar nānāprabhārūpam/
	    āgamāntareṇa svamataṃ samīkaroti --- yatredam uktaṃ pañcaśikhena tam aṇuṃ
	    duradhigamatvād ātmānam ahaṃkārāspadam anuvidyānucintyāsmītyevaṃ tāvat saṃjānīta iti/
	    syād etat/ nānāprabhārūpā bhavatu jyotiṣmatī katham asmitāmātrarūpā jyotiṣmatīty ata āha
	    --- eṣā dvayīti/ vidhūtarajastamomalāsmitaiva sattvamayī jyotir iti bhāvaḥ/ dvividhāyā
	    api jyotiṣmatyāḥ phalam āha --- yayeti //1.36//
children.translated_text: Through that [<s>Suṣumnā</s>], indeed, even the external discs of the sun and the like are strung together. For that is the seat of the mind. For the <s>yogin</s> who concentrates there, awareness of the mind arises. He shows the form of mental awareness with supporting reasoning — 'for the <s>sattva</s> of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect)': 'like space' indicates its pervasiveness. The radiances of the sun and the like — their forms — take on different configurations through that [buddhi], becoming manifold in form. And 'mind' here means <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) as intended, not the <s>mahat</s> principle. And since it [the mind], situated in the <s>Suṣumnā</s>, is born from the <s>vaikārika</s> (modifying) <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle), its luminous nature is intended due to the predominance of <s>sattva</s>. And its pervasiveness is also established through its capacity to apprehend various objects. Having shown <s>samāpatti</s> (meditative absorption) with respect to the mind as the product of <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness), he states the essential nature of <s>asmitā-samāpatti</s> — 'thus': peaceful — free from the waves of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>; infinite — pervasive; consisting of <s>asmitā</s> alone — not of manifold radiant forms. He reconciles his own view with another scripture — 'where this was stated by <s>Pañcaśikha</s>: having found that subtle Self, difficult to perceive due to its subtlety, the abode of <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, having contemplated it, one first knows "I am" thus.' One might ask: let <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> be of manifold radiant forms — how is it of the form of <s>asmitā</s> alone? Hence he says — 'this is twofold.' The very <s>asmitā</s>, free from the impurities of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, consisting of <s>sattva</s>, is itself light — such is the purport. He states the fruit of the twofold <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> — 'by which.' (1.36)

Or [through a state that is] sorrowless and luminous — '<s>viśokā</s>' means free from sorrow, devoid of suffering; '<s>jyotiṣmatī</s>' means 'that which possesses light,' that is, of the nature of radiance. 'In the lotus of the heart': in the middle between the abdomen and the chest, there is a lotus facing downward with eight petals. By <s>recaka-prāṇāyāma</s> (exhalation breath-control), one turns it upward and concentrates the mind there. In its center is the solar disc, the letter 'a,' the waking state; above that is the lunar disc, the letter 'u,' the dream state; above that is the disc of fire, the letter 'm,' the state of deep sleep. Above that, the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> declare the <s>brahmanāda</s> (sound of Brahman), of the nature of supreme space, the fourth state (<s>turīya</s>), the half-measure (<s>ardhamātra</s>). There, in the pericarp, facing upward, passing through the center of the solar and other discs, is the <s>Brahmanāḍī</s>. Rising further above from that is the <s>nāḍī</s> called <s>Suṣumnā</s>.

children.text: vītarāgaviṣayaṃ vā cittam //1.37//
children.translated_text: Or [the mind attains steadiness when] directed toward one who is free from attachment (<s>vītarāga</s>). (1.37)

children.text:
vītarāgaviṣayaṃ vā cittam/ vītarāgāḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaprabhṛtayas teṣāṃ cittaṃ tad
	    evālambanaṃ tenoparaktam iti //1.37//
children.translated_text: Or [the mind attains steadiness when] directed toward one who is free from attachment. The <s>vītarāgas</s> (those free from attachment) are <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> and others; their mind — that very [mind] is the support (<s>ālambana</s>); colored by it — thus. (1.37)

children.text: svapnanidrājñānālambanaṃ vā //1.38//
children.translated_text: Or [the mind attains steadiness when] supported by the knowledge [arising from] dream and sleep. (1.38)

children.text:
svapnanidrājñānālambanaṃ vā/ yadā khalv ayaṃ svapne viviktavanasaṃniveśavartinīm
	    utkīrṇām

iva candramaṇḍalāt komalamṛṇālaśakalānukāribhir aṅgapratyaṅgair
	    upapannām abhijātacandrakāntamaṇimayīm atisurabhimālatīmallikāmālāhāriṇīṃ manoharāṃ
	    bhagavato maheśvarasya pratimām ārādhayann eva prabuddhaḥ prasannamanās tadā tām eva
	    svapnajñānālambanībhūtām anucintayatas tasya tadekākāramanasas tatraiva cittaṃ
	    sthitipadaṃ labhate/ nidrā ceha sāttvikī grahītavyā/ yasyāḥ prabuddhasya sukham aham
	    asvāpsam iti pratyavamarśo bhavati/ ekāgraṃ hi tasyāṃ mano bhavati/ tāvanmātreṇa coktam
	    --- etad eva brahmavido brahmaṇo rūpam udāharanti suptāvastheti/ jñānaṃ ca jñeyarahitaṃ
	    na śakyaṃ gocarayitum iti jñeyam api gocarīkriyate //1.38//
children.translated_text: from the lunar disc, endowed with limbs and minor limbs resembling tender lotus-stalk fibers, made of the finest moonstone, adorned with garlands of exceedingly fragrant <s>mālatī</s> and <s>mallikā</s> flowers, an enchanting image of the <s>Bhagavān Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord), dwelling in a secluded forest hermitage — and having been worshipping [that image], he awakens with a tranquil mind. Then, for one who contemplates that very dream-knowledge as the support, whose mind takes on exclusively that form, the mind attains the state of steadiness in that very [object]. And sleep here should be understood as <s>sāttvika</s> (of the nature of purity) — [that sleep] upon waking from which one has the recollection 'I slept happily.' For the mind in that [state] becomes one-pointed. And to that extent it has been stated — 'This very form of <s>Brahman</s> the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> declare to be the state of deep sleep.' And knowledge devoid of a knowable [object] cannot be made into a support; therefore, the knowable too is made into a support. (1.38)
Or [the mind attains steadiness when] supported by the knowledge [arising from] dream and sleep. When indeed, in a dream, [a yogin perceives] as if carved out

children.text: yathābhimatadhyānād vā //1.39//
children.translated_text: Or by meditation on whatever is agreeable [to the practitioner]. (1.39)

children.text: yathābhimatadhyānād vā/ kiṃ bahunā yad evābhimataṃ tattaddevatārūpam iti //1.39//
children.translated_text: Or by meditation on whatever is agreeable. In short — whatever is agreeable, that deity's form and the like. (1.39)

children.text: paramāṇuparamamahattvānto+asya vaśīkāraḥ //1.40//
children.translated_text: His mastery extends from the minutest atom to the greatest magnitude. (1.40)

children.text:
kathaṃ punaḥ sthitipadasātmībhāvo+avagantavya ity ata āha ---
	    paramāṇuparamamahattvānto+asya vaśīkāraḥ/ vyācaṣṭe --- sūkṣma iti/ uktam arthaṃ
	    piṇḍīkṛtya vaśīkārapadārtham āha --- evaṃ tām ubhayīm iti/ vaśīkārasyāvantaraphalam āha
	    --- tadvaśīkārād iti //1.40//
children.translated_text: How then is one to understand that the state of steadiness has become one's own nature? Hence he says — 'His mastery extends from the minutest atom to the greatest magnitude.' He explains — 'the subtle,' etc. Having condensed the stated meaning, he states the meaning of the term <s>vaśīkāra</s> (mastery) — 'thus, that twofold,' etc. He states the subsidiary result of mastery — 'from that mastery,' etc. (1.40)

children.text:
kṣīṇavṛtter abhijātasyeva maṇer grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyeṣu tatsthatadañjanatā
	      samāpattiḥ //1.41//
children.translated_text: For one whose <s>vṛttis</s> (modifications) have dwindled, like a precious jewel of fine quality, there is <s>samāpatti</s> (coalescence) — the state of being colored by and imbued with [the nature of] the knower (<s>grahītṛ</s>), the act of knowing (<s>grahaṇa</s>), and the knowable object (<s>grāhya</s>). (1.41)

children.text:
tad evaṃ cittasthiter upāyā darśitāḥ/ labdhasthitikasya cittasya vaśīkāro+api darśitaḥ/
	    saṃprati labdhasthitikasya cetasaḥ kiṃviṣayaḥ kiṃrūpaś ca saṃprajñāto bhavatīti pṛcchati
	    --- atheti/ atrottaraṃ sūtram avatārayati --- tad ucyata iti/ sūtraṃ paṭhati ---

kṣīṇavṛtter ityādi samāpattyantam/ tad vyācaṣṭe --- kṣīṇeti/
	    abhyāsavairāgyābhyāṃ kṣīṇarājasatāmasapramāṇādivṛtteś cittasya/ tasya vyākhyānaṃ ---
	    pratyastamitapratyayasyeti/ tad anena cittasattvasya svabhāvasvacchasya rajastamobhyām
	    anabhibhava uktaḥ/ dṛṣṭāntaṃ spaṣṭayati --- yatheti/ upāśraya upādhir japākusumādir
	    uparaktas tacchāyāpannaḥ/ upāśrayasya yad ātmīyaṃ rūpaṃ lohitanīlādi tad evākāras tena
	    lakṣito nirbhāsate/ dārṣṭāntike yojayati --- tathā grāhyeti/ grāhyaṃ ca tadālambanaṃ ca
	    tenoparaktaṃ tadanuviddhaṃ, tad anena grahītṛgrahaṇābhyāṃ vyavacchinatti/ ātmīyam
	    antaḥkaraṇarūpam apidhāya grāhyasamāpannaṃ grāhyatām iva prāptam iti yāvat/ ato
	    grāhyasvarūpākāreṇa nirbhāsate/ grāhyoparāgam eva sūkṣmasthūlatābhyāṃ vibhajate ---
	    bhūtasūkṣmeti/ viśvabhedaś cetanācetanasvabhāvo gavādir ghaṭādiś ca draṣṭavyaḥ/ tad
	    anena vitarkavicārānugatau samādhī darśitau/ tathā grahaṇeṣv apīndriyeṣv iti/ gṛhyanta
	    ebhir arthā iti grahaṇānīndriyāṇi/ etad eva spaṣṭayati --- grahaṇālambaneti/ grahaṇaṃ
	    cālambanaṃ ca tad iti grahaṇālambanaṃ tenoparaktam anuviddham ātmīyam antaḥkaraṇarūpam
	    apidhāya grahaṇam iva bahiṣkaraṇam ivāpannam iti/ tad anenānandānugatam
	    uktvāsmitānugatam āha --- tathā grahītṛpuruṣeti/ asmitāspadaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Of one whose modifications have waned' — and so on up to <s>samāpatti</s> (cognitive absorption). He explains that: 'waned' — [meaning] of the mind whose <s>rājasa</s> (active) and <s>tāmasa</s> (inert) modifications such as valid cognition, etc., have waned through <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice) and <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion). The explanation of that: 'whose cognitions have set.' By this, the non-overpowering of the <s>sattva</s> (purity) of the mind, which is naturally clear, by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, is stated. He clarifies the analogy: 'just as' — the support (<s>upāśraya</s>) is the conditioning factor (<s>upādhi</s>), such as a hibiscus flower, etc.; 'colored' means having assumed its hue. Whatever is the intrinsic form of the support — red, blue, etc. — that very form is the appearance by which [the crystal] is characterized and shines. He applies this to the illustrated case: 'so too, the graspable (<s>grāhya</s>).' The graspable, which is also the support, is 'colored' by it — pervaded by it. By this, he distinguishes [it] from the grasper (<s>grahītṛ</s>) and the instrument of grasping (<s>grahaṇa</s>). Concealing its own inner-organ nature, it has become as if graspable — meaning it has arrived at the state of graspability. Therefore, it shines in the form and appearance of the graspable. He divides the coloring by the graspable into subtle and gross: 'the subtle elements (<s>bhūtasūkṣma</s>)' — the variety of the universe, which is of conscious and unconscious nature, should be understood as [including] cows, etc., and pots, etc. By this, the <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) accompanied by <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation) and <s>vicāra</s> (reflection) are indicated. 'So too, in the case of the instruments of grasping (<s>grahaṇa</s>), i.e., the sense organs' — things are grasped by these, therefore the sense organs are 'instruments of grasping.' He clarifies just this: 'with the instrument of grasping as support' — having the instrument of grasping as its support, colored by it, pervaded by it, concealing its own inner-organ nature, it has become as if the instrument of grasping, as if an external organ. By this, having stated [the <s>samādhi</s>] accompanied by <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), he states [the one] accompanied by <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness): 'so too, the grasper, <s>puruṣa</s>.' The seat of <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness)

children.text:
hi grahītā
	    puruṣa iti bhāvaḥ/ puruṣatvāviśeṣād anenaiva mukto+api puruṣaḥ śukaprahlādādiḥ
	    samādhiviṣayatayā saṃgrahītavya ity āha --- tathā mukteti/ upasaṃharaṃs
	    tatsthatadañjanatāpadaṃ vyācaṣṭe --- tad evam iti/ teṣu grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyeṣu sthitasya
	    dhāritasya dhyānaparipākavaśād apahatarajastamomalasya cittasattvasya yā
	    tatsthatadañjanatā tadākāratā sā samāpattiḥ saṃprajñātalakṣaṇo yoga ucyate/ tatra ca
	    grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyeṣv iti sautraḥ pāṭhakramo 'rthakramavirodhān nādartavyaḥ/ evaṃ
	    bhāṣye+api prathamaṃ bhūtasūkṣmopanyāso+apy anādaraṇīya iti sarvaṃ ramaṇīyam //1.41//
children.translated_text: is indeed the grasper, the <s>puruṣa</s> — such is the purport. Since there is no distinction in <s>puruṣa</s>-hood, even a liberated <s>puruṣa</s> — such as <s>Śuka</s>, <s>Prahlāda</s>, and others — must be included within the scope of <s>samādhi</s> as its object. Hence he says: 'so too, the liberated.' Concluding, he explains the term 'abiding in that, colored by that' (<s>tatsthatadañjanatā</s>): 'thus.' 'Abiding in' — established in, sustained in those — the graspable, the instrument of grasping, and the grasper. Of the <s>sattva</s> of the mind, whose impurities of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> have been removed through the ripening of meditation, the 'abiding in that, colored by that' — the assuming of their form — that is <s>samāpatti</s> (cognitive absorption), which is called <s>Yoga</s> characterized as <s>saṃprajñāta</s> (with discernment). And therein, the order of enumeration in the <s>sūtra</s> — 'in the graspable, the instrument of grasping, and the grasper' — being contrary to the order of meaning, should not be attended to. Likewise in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, the initial mention of the subtle elements should also not be regarded [as establishing order]. Thus everything is satisfactory. (1.41)

Thus, the means of mental steadiness have been shown. The mastery of the mind that has attained steadiness has also been shown. Now, for the mind that has attained steadiness, he asks — what is the object and what is the form of <s>saṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi]? — 'Now,' etc. He introduces the answering <s>sūtra</s> — 'That is stated,' etc. He recites the <s>sūtra</s> —

children.text: tatra śabdārthajñānavikalpaiḥ saṃkīrṇā savitarkā samāpattiḥ //1.42//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 1.42:] <s>Tatra śabdārthajñānavikalpaiḥ saṃkīrṇā savitarkā samāpattiḥ</s> — 'Among those, the <s>savitarkā</s> (deliberative) cognitive absorption is that which is mixed with conceptual alternatives (<s>vikalpas</s>) of word, meaning, and knowledge.' (1.42)

children.text:
sāmānyataḥ samāpattir uktā/ seyam avāntarabhedāc caturvidhā bhavati/ tadyathā savitarkā
	    nirvitarkā savicārā nirvicārā ceti/ tatra savitarkāyāḥ samāpatter lakṣaṇam āha ---
	    tatretyādi/ tāsu samāpattiṣu madhye savitarkā samāpattiḥ pratipattavyā/ kīdṛśī śabdaś
	    cārthaś ca jñānaṃ ca teṣāṃ vikalpāḥ/ vastuto bhinnānām api śabdādīnām itaretarādhyāsād
	    vikalpo+apy ekasmin bhedam ādarśayati bhinneṣu cābhedam/ tena śabdārthajñānavikalpaiḥ
	    saṃkīrṇā vyāmiśrety arthaḥ/ tadyathā gaur iti śabda iti/ gaur ity upāttayor
	    arthajñānayoḥ śabdābhedavikalpo darśitaḥ/ gaur ity artha iti/ gaur ity upāttayoḥ
	    śabdajñānayor arthābhedavikalpaḥ/ gaur iti jñānam iti/ gaur ity upāttayoḥ śabdārthayor
	    jñānābhedavikalpaḥ/ tad evam avinirbhāgena (avinirbhāgeṇa) vibhaktānām api
	    śabdārthajñānānāṃ grahaṇaṃ loke dṛṣṭaṃ draṣṭavyam/ yady avibhāgena grahaṇaṃ kutas tarhi
	    vibhāga ity ata āha --- vibhajyamānāś cānvayavyatirekābhyāṃ parīkṣakair

anye śabdadharmā dhvanipariṇāmamātrasya śabdasyodāttādayo dharmā anye+arthasya
	    jaḍatvamūrtatvādayaḥ, anye prakāśamūrtivirahādayo jñānasya dharmā iti/ tasmād eteṣāṃ
	    vibhaktaḥ panthāḥ svarūpabhedonnayanamārgaḥ/ tatra vikalpate gavādyarthe samāpannasyeti/
	    tad anena yogino+aparaṃ pratyakṣam uktam/ śeṣaṃ sugamam //1.42//
children.translated_text: the properties of word are different — for word, which is merely a modification of sound, has properties such as high-pitched, etc. Different are [the properties] of the object — insentience, materiality, etc. And different are the properties of knowledge — luminosity, formlessness, and so on. Therefore, the path of these is distinct — the method of bringing out their difference in essential nature. 'Therein, one who has attained cognitive absorption regarding the object such as a cow, etc., engages in conceptual construction.' By this, another [i.e., yogic] perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) of the <s>yogin</s> is indicated. The rest is easy to understand. (1.42)

<s>Samāpatti</s> (cognitive absorption) has been stated in general. This, through its sub-varieties, is fourfold — namely: <s>savitarkā</s> (deliberative), <s>nirvitarkā</s> (non-deliberative), <s>savicārā</s> (reflective), and <s>nirvicārā</s> (non-reflective). Of those, he states the definition of <s>savitarkā samāpatti</s>: 'among those,' etc. Among those cognitive absorptions, the <s>savitarkā samāpatti</s> is to be understood. Of what kind? 'Word, meaning, and knowledge' — the conceptual alternatives (<s>vikalpas</s>) of these. Even though word, meaning, and knowledge are actually different, through the mutual superimposition of word, etc., upon each other, the <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) displays difference in what is actually one, and non-difference in what is actually different. 'Mixed with the conceptual alternatives of word, meaning, and knowledge' — means intermingled. This is the meaning. For example: 'cow is a word' — here the conceptual construction of non-difference of the word from the meaning and knowledge that have been apprehended in [the expression] 'cow' is shown. 'Cow is a thing' — here the conceptual construction of non-difference of the meaning from the word and knowledge apprehended in 'cow.' 'Cow is a cognition' — here the conceptual construction of non-difference of the knowledge from the word and meaning apprehended in 'cow.' Thus, the apprehension of word, meaning, and knowledge without discrimination — even though they are distinct — is seen and should be recognized in ordinary experience. If they are apprehended without discrimination, then whence comes discrimination? To this he replies: 'But when analyzed through [the methods of] agreement (<s>anvaya</s>) and difference (<s>vyatireka</s>) by investigators,'

children.text: smṛtipariśuddhau svarūpaśūnyevārthamātranirbhāsā nirvitarkā //1.43//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 1.43:] <s>Smṛtipariśuddhau svarūpaśūnyevārthamātranirbhāsā nirvitarkā</s> — 'When memory is purified, [the mind,] as if empty of its own form, shining forth as the object alone — that is the <s>nirvitarkā</s> (non-deliberative) [cognitive absorption].' (1.43)

children.text:
sūtraṃ yojayituṃ prathamatas tāvan nirvitarkāṃ vyācaṣṭe --- yadā punar iti/ pariśuddhir
	    apanayaḥ/ śabdasaṃketasmaraṇapūrve khalv āgamānumāne pravartete/ saṃketaś cāyaṃ gaur iti
	    śabdārthajñānānām itaretarādhyāsātmā/ tataś cāgamānumānajñānavikalpau bhavataḥ/ tena
	    tatpūrvā samādhiprajñā savitarkā/ yadā punar arthamātrapravaṇena cetasārthamātrādṛtena
	    tadabhyāsān nāntarīyakatām upagatā saṃketasmṛtis tyaktā, tattyāge ca
	    śrutānumānajñānavikalpau tanmūlau tyaktau, tadā tacchūnyāyāṃ samādhiprajñāyāṃ
	    svarūpamātreṇāvasthito+arthas tatsvarūpamātratayaiva na tu vikalpitenākāreṇa
	    paricchidyate/ sā nirvitarkā samāpattir iti/ tad yogināṃ paraṃ pratyakṣam
	    asadāropagandhasyāpy abhāvāt/ syād etat pareṇa pratyakṣeṇārthatattvaṃ gṛhītvā yogina
	    upadiśanty upapādayanti ca/ kathaṃ cātadviṣayābhyām āgamaparārthānumānābhyāṃ so+artha
	    upadiśyata upapādyate ca/ tasmād āgamānumāne tadviṣaye te ca vikalpāv iti param api
	    pratyakṣaṃ vikalpa evety ata āha --- tac ca śruteti/ yadi hi savitarkam iva
	    śrutānumānasahabhūtaṃ tadanuṣaktaṃ syād bhavet saṃkīrṇaṃ tayos tu bījam evaitat tato hi
	    śrutānumāne prabhavataḥ/ na ca yad yasya kāraṇaṃ tat tadviṣayaṃ bhavati/ na hi
	    dhūmajñānaṃ vahnijñānakāraṇam iti vahniviṣayam/ tasmād avikalpena pratyakṣeṇa gṛhītvā
	    vikalpyopadiśanti copapādayanti ca/ upasaṃharati --- tasmād iti/ vyākhyeyaṃ sūtraṃ
	    yojayati ---

nirvitarkāyā iti/ smṛtipariśuddhāv ityādi sūtram/
	    śabdasaṃketaś ca śrutaṃ cānumānaṃ ca teṣāṃ jñānam eva vikalpas tasmāt smṛtis tasyāḥ
	    pariśuddhir apagamas tasyām/ tatra ca saṃketasmṛtipariśuddhir hetuḥ/
	    śrutānumānasmṛtipariśuddhiś ca hetumatī/ anumānaśabdaś ca karmasādhano+anumeyavācakaḥ/
	    svam ivetīvakāro bhinnakramas tyaktvetipadānantaraṃ draṣṭavyaḥ/ viṣayavipratipattiṃ
	    nirākaroti --- tasyā eketi/ ekāṃ buddhim upakramata ārabhata ity ekabuddhyupakramaḥ/ tad
	    anena paramāṇavo nānātmāno na nirvitarkaviṣayā ity uktaṃ bhavati/ yogyatve+api teṣāṃ
	    paramasūkṣmāṇāṃ nānābhūtānāṃ
	    mahattvaikārthasamavetaikatvanirbhāsapratyayaviṣayatvāyogāt/ astu tarhi paramārthasatsu
	    paramāṇuṣu sāṃvṛtaḥ pratibhāsadharmaḥ sthaulyam ity ata āha --- arthātmeti/ nāsati
	    bādhake sthūlam anubhavasiddhaṃ śakyāpahnavam iti bhāvaḥ/ tatra ye paśyanti
	    dvyaṇukādikrameṇa goghaṭādaya upajāyanta iti tān pratyāha --- aṇupracayeti/ aṇūnāṃ
	    pracayaḥ sthūlarūpapariṇāmaḥ, sa ca viśiṣyate+anyasmāt pariṇāmāntarāt sa evātmā svarūpaṃ
	    yasya sa tathoktaḥ/ gavādir bhogāyatanam/ ghaṭādir viṣayaḥ/ tac caitad ubhayam api
	    lokyata iti lokaḥ/ nanv eṣa bhūtasūkṣmebhyo bhinno+abhinno vā syād bhinnaś cet kathaṃ
	    tadāśrayaḥ kathaṃ ca tadākāraḥ/ na hi ghaṭaḥ paṭād anyas tadākāras tadāśrayo vā/
	    abhinnaś cet tadvad eva sūkṣmo+asādhāraṇaś ca syād ata āha --- sa ceti/ ayam abhiprāyaḥ
	    --- naikāntataḥ paramāṇubhyo bhinno ghaṭādir abhinno vā, bhinnatve gavāśvavad
	    dharmadharmibhāvānupapatteḥ/ abhinnatve dharmirūpavad eva
children.translated_text: On <s>nirvitarkā</s> (beyond deliberation). The <s>sūtra</s> is: 'Upon the purification of memory,' etc. The verbal convention, what is heard [from scripture], and inference — the knowledge of these is indeed <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction); from that [arises] memory; the purification of that [memory] is its departure — upon that [departure, nirvitarka samāpatti arises]. And therein, the purification of the memory of verbal conventions is the cause; the purification of the memory of what is heard and inferred is the effect. And the word '<s>anumāna</s>' (inference) here, construed as a <s>karmasādhana</s> (objective compound), denotes the inferable [object]. The particle 'iva' (as if) in 'as its own' is to be read out of order, placed after the word 'having abandoned.' He removes the dispute about the object: 'Of that, one,' etc. 'Initiating one cognition' means beginning, undertaking one cognition. By this, it is said that atoms (<s>paramāṇus</s>), being of diverse nature, are not the object of <s>nirvitarka</s> [samāpatti]. Even though they are suitable [objects], because those supremely subtle entities, being of diverse natures, cannot be the object of a cognition that manifests as a unity, being the [appearance of] magnitude, having a single purpose, and being co-inherent. Then let grossness be a merely conventional, apparent property while atoms exist in ultimate reality — hence he says: 'whose nature is the object,' etc. The purport is: in the absence of a sublator, the gross [object], established through experience, cannot be denied. Against those who hold that cows, pots, and so forth arise through the successive aggregation of dyads and the like, he responds: 'accumulation of atoms,' etc. The accumulation of atoms is the transformation into a gross form, and it is distinguished from another transformation — that alone is the essential nature (<s>ātman</s>) of which [the whole] is so described. Cows and the like are the locus of enjoyment. Pots and the like are the objects. Both of these constitute the world, because they are perceived. But would this [whole] be different from or identical with the subtle elements? If different, how is it their substrate, how does it have their form? For a pot is not something other than a cloth while having its form and being its substrate. If identical, it would be subtle and uncommon just like them — hence he says: 'and that,' etc. The purport is this: a pot and the like is not absolutely different from atoms nor absolutely identical;  if different, the relation of property and property-bearer would not hold, as between a cow and a horse; if identical, just like the property-bearer [being subtle],

tadanupapatteḥ/
	    tasmāt kathaṃcid bhinnaḥ kathaṃcid abhinnaś cāstheyas tathā ca sarvam upapadyate/

	    kiṃ tadātmabhūto dharmo nityo nety āha --- dharmāntarasya kapālāder udaya iti/
	    tasyāvayavinaḥ paramāṇubhyo vyāvṛttaṃ rūpam ādarśayati --- sa eṣa iti/ paramāṇusādhyāyāḥ
	    kriyāyā anyā kriyā madhūdakādidhāraṇalakṣaṇā taddharmaka iti/ na kevalam anubhavād api
	    tu vyavahārato+api tannibandhanatvāl lokayātrāyā ity āha --- teneti/ syād etad asati
	    bādhake+anubhavo 'vayavinaṃ vyavasthāpayet/ asti ca bādhakaṃ yat sat tat sarvam
	    anavayavaṃ yathā vijñānam/ sac ca goghaṭādīti svabhāvahetuḥ/ sattvaṃ hi
	    viruddhadharmasaṃsargarahitatvena vyāptaṃ, tadviruddhaś ca viruddhadharmasaṃsargaḥ
	    sāvayava upalabhyamāno vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhyā sattvam api nivartayati/ asti cāvayavini
	    taddeśatvātaddeśatvāvṛtatvānāvṛtatvaraktatvāraktatvacalatvācalatvalakṣaṇo
	    viruddhadharmasaṃsarga ity ata āha --- yasya punar iti/ ayam abhiprāyaḥ ---
	    anubhavasiddhaṃ sattvaṃ hetuḥ kriyate yat kila pāṃśulapāduko hāliko+api pratipadyate/
	    anyad vānubhavasiddhāt/ tatrānyad asiddhatvād ahetuḥ/ anubhavasiddhaṃ tu ghaṭādīnāṃ
	    sattvam arthakriyākāritvarūpaṃ na sthūlād anyat/ so+ayaṃ hetuḥ sthūlatvam apākurvann
	    ātmānam eva vyāhanti/ nanu na sthūlatvam eva sattvam api tv asato vyāvṛttiḥ/
	    asthaulyavyāvṛttiś ca sthaulyaṃ, vyāvartyabhedāc ca vyāvṛttayo bhidyante/ ataḥ
	    sthaulyābhāve+api na sattvavyāhatiḥ/ anyatvāt/ bhavatu vā vyāvṛttibhedād
	    avasāyaviṣayabhedaḥ/ yatpūrvakās tv avasāyās tasyānubhavasyāvikalpasya pramāṇasya ko
	    viṣaya iti nirūpayatu bhavān rūpaparamāṇavo nirantarotpādā agṛhītaparamasūkṣmatattvā iti
	    cet, hantaite gandharasasparśaparamāṇubhir antaritā na nirantarāḥ/ tasmād antarālāgraha
	    ekaghanavanapratyayavat paramāṇvālambanaḥ sann ayaṃ vikalpo mithyeti tatprabhavavikalpā
	    na pāramparyeṇāpi vastupratibaddhā iti kutas tadavasitasya
	    sattvasyānavayavatvasādhakatvam/ tasmād avikalpasya pratyakṣasya prāmāṇyam
children.translated_text: that too would be untenable. Therefore, [the whole] should be maintained as somehow different and somehow identical, and thus everything is explained. The genitive case in 'of the subtle elements' indicates a kind of difference; 'being their essential nature' indicates non-difference. By the manifest effect — characterized by [direct] experience and by [conventional] usage — the [cause], which is disputed, is inferred. And since the form of the cause is established when the cause is non-different, he says: 'eye-salve that is its own revealer,' etc. Is that property, being the essential nature of those [elements], eternal or not? He says: 'The arising of another property such as a potsherd,' etc. He shows the form of the whole as distinct from atoms: 'This very one,' etc. The activity that is to be accomplished from atoms — another activity, characterized by holding honey, water, etc. — that [whole] possesses that property. Not only from experience, but also from conventional usage, because worldly activity depends on it — hence he says: 'by that,' etc. One might say: in the absence of a sublator, experience would establish the whole. And there is a sublator: whatever exists is entirely partless, like consciousness; and cows, pots, etc. exist — [this would be] a natural reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>). For existence is pervaded by the absence of contact with contradictory properties, and contact with contradictory properties, being contrary to that, when apprehended in something with parts, would negate even its existence through the apprehension of what contradicts the pervader. And in a whole, there is contact with contradictory properties characterized by being-in-that-place and not-being-in-that-place, being-covered and not-being-covered, being-red and not-being-red, being-moving and not-being-moving — hence he says: 'But for one who,' etc. The purport is this: existence established through experience is made the reason — which even a peasant wearing straw sandals, even a ploughman, understands. Or [it is] something other than what is established through experience. There, the other [option], being unestablished, is not a reason. But the existence of pots and the like, established through experience, having the form of causal efficacy, is not different from the gross [thing]. This very reason, in removing grossness, would contradict itself. Now [one might say], existence is not grossness itself but rather the exclusion from non-existence; and grossness is the exclusion from non-grossness, and exclusions differ because the things excluded from differ; hence, even in the absence of grossness, there is no contradiction of existence, because they are different. Or let there be difference in the objects of ascertainment due to the difference of exclusions; but what is the object of the experience — the non-conceptual, valid cognition — that precedes those ascertainments? Let the gentleman determine: are [they] form-atoms, arising without interruption, whose supremely subtle true nature is not grasped? In that case — alas! — these are interspersed with smell-atoms, taste-atoms, and touch-atoms, and are not uninterrupted. Therefore, the non-apprehension of the interstices — like the cognition of a single dense forest — this <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) resting on atoms is false; and the conceptual constructions arising from it are not connected to reality even indirectly. How then can the existence ascertained through them have the capacity to prove partlessness? Therefore, the authority of non-conceptual, direct perception

children.text:
icchatā tadanubhūyamānasthaulyasyaiva sattvam avikalpāvaseyam akāmenāpy abhyupeyam/
	    tathā ca tadbādhamānaṃ sattvam ātmānam evāpabādheta/ paramasūkṣmāḥ paramāṇavo
	    vijātīyaparamāṇvanantaritā anubhavaviṣayā iti vyāhatam aṅgīkaraṇam/ tad idam uktaṃ ---
	    yasya punar avastukaḥ sa pracayaviśeṣo nirvikalpaviṣayaḥ/ santu tarhi sūkṣmāḥ paramāṇavo
	    nirvikalpaviṣayā ity ata āha --- sūkṣmaṃ ca kāraṇam anupalabhyam avikalpasyeti/
	    tasyāvayavyabhāvād dhetor atadrūpapratiṣṭhaṃ mithyājñānam iti lakṣaṇena sarvam evaṃ
	    (eva) prāptaṃ mithyājñānaṃ yat sthaulyālambanaṃ yac ca tadadhiṣṭhānasattvālambanam ity
	    arthaḥ/ nanv etāvatāpi na jñānam ātmani mithyā bhavati tasyāvayavitvenāprakāśād ity ata
	    āha --- prāyeṇeti/ nanu kim etāvatāpīty ata āha --- tadā ceti/ sattvādijñānaṃ cen mithyā
	    tadā sattvādihetukam anavayavitvādijñānam api mithyaiva tasyāpi hi
	    nirvikalpagocarasthūlam evāvaseyatayā viṣayaḥ, sa ca nāstīti tātparyārthaḥ/ viṣayābhāva
	    eva kuta ity ata āha --- yad yad iti/ virodhaś ca pariṇāmavaicitryeṇa bhedābhedena
	    coktopapattyanusāreṇoddhartavya iti sarvaṃ ramaṇīyam //1.43//
children.translated_text: [must be accepted by] one who desires [to establish partlessness]; the very existence of that grossness being experienced must be determinable by non-conceptual [perception], and must be accepted even unwillingly. And thus, the existence that would sublate it would sublate itself. [The claim that] supremely subtle atoms, interspersed by atoms of other kinds, are the object of experience — this is a self-contradictory acceptance. Thus it has been stated: 'But for one who [holds that] that accumulation-as-distinct [from atoms] is unreal, the object of non-conceptual [perception] [is the gross thing itself].' 'Then let the subtle atoms be the object of non-conceptual [perception]' — to this he says: 'And the subtle cause is unperceivable, by non-conceptual [cognition],' etc. Because the whole does not exist [on the opponent's view], by the logical mark — 'false cognition is that which rests on what is not of that nature' — everything that has grossness as its object, and everything that has the existence underlying that [grossness] as its object, is all equally obtained as false cognition — such is the meaning. But even with all this, cognition is not false with respect to the self, since [the self] is not manifested as having parts — hence he says: 'for the most part,' etc. But what follows from even this? Hence he says: 'And then,' etc. If cognition of <s>sattva</s> (existence) and the like is false, then cognition of partlessness and the like, which is caused by <s>sattva</s> and the like, is also false; for even that has as its object the gross [thing] alone as what is to be determined by non-conceptual [cognition], and that [gross thing] does not exist — such is the essential meaning. Why does the object not exist? Hence he says: 'Whatever,' etc. And the contradiction is to be resolved through the variety of transformation, through difference-and-identity, following the explanation given above — thus everything is delightful. (1.43)

In order to connect the <s>sūtra</s>, he first explains the <s>nirvitarkā</s>: 'But when...' 'Purification' means removal. Indeed, scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and inference (<s>anumāna</s>) operate preceded by the recollection of verbal conventions (<s>śabdasaṃketa</s>). And this convention is the mutual superimposition of word, meaning, and knowledge [implied in] 'cow.' From this, the conceptual constructions of scriptural and inferential knowledge arise. Therefore, <s>samādhi</s>-wisdom (<s>samādhiprajñā</s>) preceded by those [constructions] is <s>savitarkā</s>. But when, through the practice of a mind inclined toward the object alone, attentive only to the object alone, the recollection of conventions — having become an inseparable [accompaniment] of that practice — is abandoned, and upon its abandonment the conceptual constructions of scriptural and inferential knowledge, which are rooted in it, are [also] abandoned — then, in that <s>samādhi</s>-wisdom which is empty of those [constructions], the object, established in its own form alone, is discerned only as that very own form, not through a conceptualized appearance. This is the <s>nirvitarkā samāpatti</s>. That is the supreme perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) of <s>yogins</s>, because there is the complete absence of even a trace of false superimposition. One might object: having grasped the reality of the object through the supreme perception, [<s>yogins</s>] instruct and demonstrate [it to others]. But how can that object be instructed and demonstrated by scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and inference for others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>), which do not have that [object] as their domain? Therefore, scripture and inference have it as their domain, and those conceptual constructions [are involved] — thus even the supreme perception would be nothing but conceptual construction. To this he replies: 'And that — based on scripture,' etc. For if, like the <s>savitarka</s> [absorption], it were accompanied by and attached to scripture and inference, then it would indeed be mixed [with conceptual construction]. But this [<s>nirvitarkā</s>] is only the seed of those — for from it, scripture and inference originate. And it is not the case that whatever is the cause of something has that thing as its object. For the cognition of smoke is the cause of the cognition of fire, but it does not have fire as its object. Therefore, having grasped [the object] through perception free from conceptual construction, they conceptually construct, instruct, and demonstrate [it to others]. He concludes: 'therefore.' He connects the <s>sūtra</s> to be explained —

children.text: etayaiva savicārā nirvicārā ca sūkṣmaviṣayā vyākhyātā //1.44//
children.translated_text: By this very [explanation], <s>savicārā</s> (with reflection) and <s>nirvicārā</s> (beyond reflection) [samāpattis], which have subtle objects, are explained. (1.44)

children.text:
etayaiva savicārā nirvicārā ca sūkṣmaviṣayā vyākhyātā/ abhivyakto ghaṭādir dharmo yais
	    te tathoktāḥ/ ghaṭādidharmopagṛhītā iti yāvat/ deśa uparyadhaḥpārśvādiḥ/ kālo
	    vartamānaḥ/ nimittaṃ pārthivasya paramāṇor gandhatanmātrapradhānebhyaḥ pañcatanmātrebhya
	    utpattiḥ/ evam āpyasya paramāṇor gandhatanmātravarjitebhyo rasatanmātrapradhānebhyaś
	    caturbhyaḥ/ evaṃ taijasasya gandharasatanmātrarahitebhyo rūpatanmātrapradhānebhyas
	    tribhyaḥ/ evaṃ vāyavīyasya gandhāditanmātrarahitābhyāṃ sparśapradhānābhyāṃ
	    sparśaśabdatanmātrābhyām/ evaṃ nābhasasya śabdaṇām

(śabdatanmātrād
	    evaikasmāt/ tad idaṃ nimittaṃ bhūtasūkṣmāṇām/) eteṣāṃ deśakālanimittānām anubhavaḥ,
	    tenāvacchinneṣu nānanubhūtaviśeṣaṇā viśeṣye buddhir upajāyata ity arthaḥ/ nanu
	    savitarkayā saha kiṃ sārūpyaṃ savicārāyā ity ata āha --- tan nāpīti/ pārthivo hi
	    paramāṇuḥ pañcatanmātrapracayātmaikabuddhinirgrāhyaḥ/ evam āpyādayo+api
	    catustridvyekatanmātrātmāna ekabuddhinirgrāhyā vedvyatavyāḥ (veditavyāḥ)/ udito
	    vartamāno dharmas tena viśiṣṭam/ etāvatā cātra saṃketasmṛtyāgamānumānavikalpānuvedhaḥ
	    sūcitaḥ/ na hi pratyakṣeṇa sthūle dṛśyamāne paramāṇavaḥ prakāśante/ api tv
	    āgamānumānābhyām/ tasmād upapannam asyāḥ saṃkīrṇatvam iti/ nirvicārām āha --- yā punar
	    iti/ sarvathā sarveṇa nīlapītādinā prakāreṇa/ sarvata iti sārvavibhaktikas tasiḥ/
	    sarvair deśakālanimittānubhavair ity arthaḥ/ tad anena svarūpeṇa kālānavacchedaḥ
	    paramāṇūnām iti darśitam/ nāpi tadārabdhadharmadvāreṇety āha --- śāntā atītā uditā
	    vartamānā avyapadeśyā bhaviṣyanto dharmās tair anavacchinneṣu/ anavacchinnā dharmaiḥ
	    paramāṇavaḥ kim asaṃbaddhā eva tair ity ata āha --- sarvadharmānupātiṣv iti/ katamena
	    saṃbandhena dharmān anupatanti paramāṇava ity ata āha --- sarvadharmātmakeṣu/ kathaṃcid
	    bhedaḥ kathaṃcid abhedo dharmāṇāṃ paramāṇubhya ity arthaḥ/ kasmāt punar iyaṃ samāpattir
	    etadviṣayety ata āha --- evaṃsvarūpaṃ hīti/ vastutattvagrāhiṇī nātattve pravartata ity
	    arthaḥ/ viṣayam abhidhāyāsyāḥ svarūpam āha --- prajñā ceti/ saṃkalayya
	    svarūpabhedopayogiviṣayam āha --- tatreti/ upasaṃharati --- evam iti/ ubhayor ātmanaś ca
	    nirvicārāyāś ceti //1.44//
children.translated_text: (from the sound-<s>tanmātra</s> alone, from a single [subtle element]; this is the cause of the subtle elements.) The experience of these — space, time, and cause — is such that in objects delimited by them, no cognition of an attribute not previously experienced arises in the qualified object — such is the meaning. Now, what is the similarity of <s>savicārā</s> [samāpatti] with <s>savitarkā</s>? Hence he says — 'that is not so either.' For a terrestrial atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>) is the aggregate of five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) and is graspable by a single cognition. Likewise, the aqueous and other [atoms] too, having four, three, two, or one <s>tanmātra</s> as their nature, should be understood as graspable by a single cognition. An arisen, present property — [the object is] qualified by that. And by this much, the intermixture of convention, memory, scripture, inference, and conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) is indicated here. For atoms are not manifest when a gross [object] is perceived directly; rather, [they are known] through scripture and inference. Therefore, the mixed nature of this [savicārā samāpatti] is established. He states <s>nirvicārā</s> — 'but that which,' etc. 'In every way' means by every mode such as blue, yellow, and so on. 'From every direction' — the suffix <s>tasi</s> takes all case-endings; the meaning is: by all experiences of space, time, and cause. By this, the non-delimitation of atoms by time in their own essential nature is shown. Nor [are they delimited] through their originated properties — hence he says: 'quiescent' means past; 'arisen' means present; 'indescribable' means future — properties; in [atoms] not delimited by them. Are atoms, not delimited by properties, simply unrelated to them? Hence he says — 'in those that follow all properties.' By what relation do atoms follow properties? Hence he says — 'in those whose nature is all properties.' There is in some respect difference and in some respect non-difference of properties from atoms — such is the meaning. Why is this <s>samāpatti</s> directed toward this [object]? Hence he says — 'for [it is] of such a nature.' [This samāpatti] grasps the true reality of things and does not operate upon what is unreal — such is the meaning. Having stated the object, he states its essential nature — 'and the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>),' etc. Having compiled the object useful for the distinction of essential nature, he says — 'therein,' etc. He concludes — 'thus': of both — of the self and of <s>nirvicārā</s>. (1.44)

By this very [explanation], <s>savicārā</s> (with reflection) and <s>nirvicārā</s> (beyond reflection) [samāpattis], which have subtle objects, are explained. Those by which the property such as a pot, etc. is manifested are so called — that is, they are apprehended through the properties of pots and the like. 'Place' (<s>deśa</s>) means above, below, to the side, etc. 'Time' (<s>kāla</s>) means the present. 'Cause' (<s>nimitta</s>) means: the earthly atom arises from the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) with smell-<s>tanmātra</s> predominating; likewise the watery atom from the four [<s>tanmātras</s>] excluding smell-<s>tanmātra</s>, with taste-<s>tanmātra</s> predominating; likewise the fiery atom from the three [<s>tanmātras</s>] excluding smell and taste <s>tanmātras</s>, with form-<s>tanmātra</s> predominating; likewise the aerial atom from the two — touch-<s>tanmātra</s> and sound-<s>tanmātra</s> — excluding smell and the rest, with touch [predominating]; likewise the ethereal [atom] from sound-<s>tanmātra</s> alone.

children.text: sūkṣmaviṣayatvaṃ cāliṅgaparyavasānam //1.45//
children.translated_text: And the domain of subtle objects extends up to the Unmanifest (<s>aliṅga</s>). (1.45)

children.text:
kiṃ bhūtasūkṣma eva grāhyaviṣayā samāpattiḥ samāpyate/ na/ kiṃ tu --- sūkṣmaviṣayatvaṃ
	    cāliṅgaparyavasānam/ pārthivasya paramāṇoḥ saṃbandhinī yā gandhatanmātratā sā samāpatteḥ
	    sūkṣmo viṣayaḥ/ evam uttaratrāpi yojyam/ liṅgamātraṃ mahattattvaṃ tad dhi layaṃ gacchati
	    pradhāna iti/ aliṅgaṃ pradhānaṃ tad dhi na kvacil layaṃ gacchatīty arthaḥ/
	    aliṅgaparyavasānatvam āha --- na cāliṅgāt param iti/ codayati --- nanu puruṣo+api sūkṣmo
	    nāliṅgam evety arthaḥ/ pariharati --- satyam iti/ upādānatayā saukṣmyam aliṅga eva
	    nānyatrety arthaḥ/ tatra puruṣārthanimittatvān mahadahaṃkārādeḥ puruṣo+api kāraṇam
	    aliṅgavad iti/ kuta evaṃlakṣaṇam aliṅgasyaiva saukṣmyam ity āśayavān pṛcchati --- kiṃ tv
	    iti/ uttaram āha --- liṅgasyeti/ satyaṃ kāraṇaṃ na tūpādānam/ yathā hi pradhānaṃ
	    mahadādibhāvena pariṇamate na tathā puruṣas taddhetur apīty arthaḥ/ upasaṃharati ---
	    ataḥ pradhāna eva saukṣmyaṃ niratiśayaṃ vyākhyātam //1.45//
children.translated_text: Does <s>samāpatti</s> (meditative absorption) reach its completion with subtle elements alone as its graspable object? No. Rather — 'the domain of subtle objects extends up to the Unmanifest.' The <s>gandha-tanmātratā</s> (nature of the smell-subtle-element) related to a terrestrial atom is the subtle object of <s>samāpatti</s>. The same should be applied to the subsequent [elements] as well. <s>Liṅgamātra</s> (the 'mere-sign') is the <s>mahat-tattva</s> (Great Principle); for it undergoes dissolution into <s>pradhāna</s> (the Primal Cause). The Unmanifest (<s>aliṅga</s>)

children.text: tā eva sabījaḥ samādhiḥ //1.46//
children.translated_text: — these alone [constitute] <s>sabīja samādhi</s> (samādhi with seed). (1.46)

children.text:
catasṛṇām api samāpattīnāṃ grāhyaviṣayāṇāṃ saṃprajñātatvam āha --- tā eva sabījaḥ
	    samādhiḥ/ evakāro bhinnakramaḥ sabīja ity asyānantaraṃ draṣṭavyaḥ/ tataś catasraḥ
	    samāpattayo grāhyaviṣayāḥ sabījatayā niyamyante/ sabījatā tv aniyatā
	    grahītṛgrahaṇagocarāyām api samāpattau vikalpāvikalpabhedenāniṣiddhā vyavatiṣṭhate/ tena
	    grāhye catasraḥ

samāpattayo grahītṛgrahaṇayoś catasra ity aṣṭau siddhā
	    bhavantīti/ nigadavyākhyātaṃ bhāṣyam //1.46//
children.translated_text: — [thus] four <s>samāpattis</s> concerning the knower and the act of knowing — making eight in total, are established. The <s>bhāṣya</s> (commentary) is explained by direct statement (<s>nigada</s>). (1.46)

He states that all four <s>samāpattis</s>, whose objects are the graspable, have the nature of <s>saṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi] — 'These alone [constitute] <s>sabīja samādhi</s>.' The particle 'eva' (alone) is to be seen as displaced in sequence and should be read immediately after '<s>sabīja</s>' (with seed). Thus the four <s>samāpattis</s> whose objects are the graspable are restricted to being '<s>sabīja</s>' (with seed). But the quality of being with seed is not restricted [only to these], since <s>samāpatti</s> directed toward the knower (<s>grahītṛ</s>) and the act of knowing (<s>grahaṇa</s>) also [involves] conceptual and non-conceptual

children.text: nirvicāravaiśāradye+adhyātmaprasādaḥ //1.47//
children.translated_text: Upon the clarity of <s>nirvicārā</s> [samāpatti], there arises inner luminosity (<s>adhyātmaprasāda</s>). (1.47)

children.text:
catasṛṣv api samāpattiṣu grāhyaviṣayāsu nirvicārāyāḥ śobhanatvam āha ---
	    nirvicāravaiśāradye+adhyātmaprasādaḥ/ vaiśāradyapadārtham āha --- aśuddhīti/
	    rajastamasor upacayo 'śuddhiḥ saivāvaraṇalakṣaṇo malas tasmād apetasya prakāśātmanaḥ
	    prakāśasvabhāvasya buddhisattvasyāta evānabhibhūta iti/ syād etad grāhyaviṣayā cet
	    samāpattiḥ katham ātmaviṣayaḥ prasāda ity ata āha --- bhūtārthaviṣaya iti/ nātmaviṣayaḥ
	    kiṃ tu tadādhāra ity arthaḥ/ kramānanurodhī yugapad ity arthaḥ/ atraiva pāramarṣīṃ
	    gāthām udāharati --- tathā ceti/ jñānālokaprakarṣeṇātmānaṃ sarveṣām upari paśyan
	    duḥkhatrayaparītāñ śocato janāñ jānāti //1.47//
children.translated_text: Among all four <s>samāpattis</s> whose objects are the graspable, he states the excellence of <s>nirvicārā</s> — 'Upon the clarity of <s>nirvicārā</s>, there arises inner luminosity.' He explains the meaning of the word <s>vaiśāradya</s> (clarity) — 'impurity': the accumulation of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> is impurity; that very [impurity] is the defilement characterized as a covering. Of the <s>buddhi-sattva</s> (intellect-in-its-pure-aspect), whose essential nature is luminosity — [the sattva] that has departed from that [impurity], which is of the nature of light — hence, not overcome [by impurity]

children.text: ṛtaṃbharā tatra prajñā //1.48//
children.translated_text: Therein, the wisdom is truth-bearing (<s>ṛtaṃbharā</s>). (1.48)

children.text:
atraiva yogijanaprasiddhānvarthasaṃjñākathanena yogisaṃmatim āha --- ṛtaṃbharā tatra
	    prajñā/ sugamaṃ bhāṣyam/ āgameneti vedavihitaṃ śravaṇam uktam/ anumāneneti mananam/
	    dhyānaṃ cintā/ tatrābhyāsaḥ paunaḥpunyenānuṣṭhānam/ tasmin rasa ādaraḥ/ tad anena
	    nididhyāsanam uktam //1.48//
children.translated_text: Here, by stating the well-known meaningful designation current among <s>yogins</s>, he declares the consensus of <s>yogins</s> — 'Therein, the wisdom is truth-bearing.' The <s>bhāṣya</s> is clear. 'By scripture (<s>āgama</s>)' refers to hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) as prescribed by the <s>Veda</s>. 'By inference' refers to reflection (<s>manana</s>). Meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) is contemplation (<s>cintā</s>). Therein, practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) is repeated performance. The relish (<s>rasa</s>) in that is devotion (<s>ādara</s>). By this, sustained meditation (<s>nididhyāsana</s>) is stated. (1.48)

children.text: śrutānumānaprajñābhyām anyaviṣayā viśeṣārthatvāt //1.49//
children.translated_text: [This wisdom] has a different object from the wisdoms [derived from] scripture and inference, because it pertains to particulars (<s>viśeṣa</s>). (1.49)

children.text:
syād etat/ āgamānumānagṛhītārthaviṣayā bhāvanā prakarṣalabdhajanmā
	    nirvicārāgamānumānaviṣayam eva gocarayet/ na khalv anyaviṣayānubhavajanmā saṃskāraḥ
	    śakto+anyatra jñānaṃ janayitum atiprasaṅgāt/ tasmān nirvicārā ced ṛtaṃbharāgamānumānayor
	    api tatprasaṅga ity ata āha --- śrutānumānetyādi/ buddhisattvaṃ hi prakāśasvabhāvaṃ
	    sarvārthadarśanasamartham api tamasāvṛtaṃ yatraiva rajasodghāṭyate tatraiva gṛhṇāti/
	    yadā tv abhyāsavairāgyābhyām apāstarajastamomalam anavadyavaiśāradyam udyotate
	    tadāsyātipatitasamastamānameyasīmnaḥ prakāśānantye sati kiṃ nāma yan na gocara iti
	    bhāvaḥ/ vyācaṣṭe --- śrutam āgama[vi]jñānaṃ (āgamavijñānaṃ) tatsāmānyaviṣayam/ kasmāt/
	    na hy āgamena śakyo viśeṣo+abhidhātum/ kuto yasmād ānantyād vyabhicārāc ca na viśeṣeṇa
	    kṛtasaṃketaḥ śabdaḥ/ yasmād asya viśeṣeṇa saha vācyavācakasaṃbandhaḥ pratīyeta/ na ca
	    vākyārtho+apīdṛśo viśeṣaḥ saṃbhavati/ anumāne+api liṅgaliṅgisaṃbandhagrahaṇādhīnajanmani
	    gatir eṣaivety āha --- tathānumānam iti/ yatra prāptir ity atra yatratatraśabdayoḥ
	    sthānaparivartanena vyāpyavyāpakabhāvo 'vagamayitavyaḥ/ ato+atrānumānena
	    sāmānyenopasaṃhāraḥ/ upasaṃharati --- tasmād iti/ astu tarhi saṃbandhagrahānapekṣaṃ
	    lokapratyakṣaṃ na tatsāmānyaviṣayam ity ata āha --- na cāsyetyādi/ mā bhūt
	    saṃbandhagrahādhīnaṃ lokapratyakṣam/ indriyādhīnaṃ tu bhavaty eva/ na cendriyāṇām asminn
	    asti yogyatety arthaḥ/ nanu ca yady āgamānumānapratyakṣāgocaro viśeṣas

tarhi nāsti pramāṇavirahād ity ata āha --- na ceti/ na hi pramāṇaṃ vyāpakaṃ kāraṇaṃ vā
	    prameyasya yena tannivṛttau nivarteta/ no khalu kalāvataś candrasya
	    parabhāgavartihariṇasadbhāvaṃ prati na saṃdihate prāmāṇikā ity arthaḥ/ iti tasmāt
	    samādhiprajñānirgrāhya eveti/ atra ca vivādādhyāsitāḥ paramāṇava ātmānaś ca
	    prātisvikaviśeṣaśālino dravyatve sati parasparaṃ vyāvartamānatvād ye dravyatve sati
	    parasparaṃ vyāvartante te prātisvikaviśeṣaśālino yathā khaṇḍamuṇḍādaya ity
	    anumānenāgamena ca ṛtaṃbharaprajñopadeśapareṇa yady api viśeṣo nirūpyate tadanirūpaṇe
	    saṃśayaḥ syān nyāyaprāptatvāt tathāpy adūraviprakarṣeṇa tatsattvaṃ kathaṃcid gocarayataḥ
	    śrutānumāne na tu sākṣāc cārtham iva samuccayādipadāni liṅgasaṃkhyāyogitayā/ tasmāt
	    siddhaṃ śrutānumānaprajñābhyām anyaviṣayeti //1.49//
children.translated_text: Then it does not exist, due to the absence of a means of knowledge — to this he says: 'nor' (<s>na ca</s>). For a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is not the pervader or the cause of the object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>), such that upon the cessation of the former the latter would cease. Indeed, an authoritative person does not doubt the existence of the hare on the far side of the moon merely because the moon has digits — this is the meaning. Therefore, [the particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>)] is graspable only by <s>samādhi</s>-wisdom (<s>samādhiprajñā</s>). And here, the atoms (<s>paramāṇus</s>) and the selves (<s>ātmans</s>) that are the subject of dispute — they possess individual particularities (<s>viśeṣas</s>), because while being substances they are mutually distinct; whatever, while being substances, are mutually distinct, possess individual particularities — like <s>Khaṇḍa</s>, <s>Muṇḍa</s>, and others. Thus, even though the <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular) is ascertained through inference and through scripture that aims at teaching the <s>ṛtaṃbharā prajñā</s> (truth-bearing wisdom), and though in its non-ascertainment there would be doubt — since it is established by reasoning — nevertheless, scripture and inference, which make the existence of that [particular] an object of cognition only remotely and indirectly, [do so] but not directly as [they cognize] an object. The terms of conjunction and similar [grammatical forms] are [to be understood] through [their] gender and number usage. Therefore, it is established that [<s>ṛtaṃbharā prajñā</s>] has a different domain from the wisdoms born of scripture and inference. (1.49)

One might think: contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) whose object is what has been grasped through scripture and inference, having been born from the intensity [of practice], would bring within its scope only what falls within the domain of <s>nirvicārā</s>, scripture, and inference. For surely an impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) born from the experience of one object is not capable of generating knowledge of another object — that would lead to absurd over-extension. Therefore, if <s>nirvicārā</s> [samāpatti] were truth-bearing, the same would apply to scripture and inference too. Hence he says — 'from those of scripture and inference'

children.text: tajjaḥ saṃskāro+anyasaṃskārapratibandhī //1.50//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 1.50:] <s>Tajjaḥ saṃskāro 'nyasaṃskārapratibandhī</s> — 'The <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) born from that [<s>samādhi</s>] obstructs other <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions).' (1.50)

children.text:
syād etat/ bhavatu paramārthaviṣayaḥ saṃprajñāto yathoktopāyābhyāsād anādinā tu
	    vyutthānasaṃskāreṇa nirūḍhanibiḍatayā pratibandhanīyā samādhiprajñā sā
	    vātyāvartamadhyavartipradīpaparamāṇur iveti śaṅkām apanetuṃ sūtram avatārayati ---
	    samādhiprajñeti/ sūtraṃ paṭhati --- tajjaḥ saṃskāro+anyasaṃskārapratibandhī/ tad iti
	    nirvicārāṃ samāpattiṃ parāmṛśati/ anyeti vyutthānam āha/ bhūtārthapakṣapāto hi dhiyāṃ
	    svabhāvas tāvad eveyam anavasthitā bhrāmyati na yāvat tattvaṃ pratilabhate/
	    tatpratilambhe tatra sthitapadā satī saṃskārabuddhiḥ
	    saṃskārabuddhicakrakrameṇāvartamānānādim

apy atattvasaṃskārabuddhikramaṃ
	    bādhata eveti/ tathā ca bāhyā apy āhuḥ ---
children.translated_text: overrides even the beginningless cycle of <s>saṃskāras</s> and cognitions of non-reality (<s>atattva</s>). And thus even the external [philosophers] say:

One might object: granted that <s>saṃprajñāta</s> (cognitive <s>samādhi</s>) has ultimate reality as its object through the practice of the means described; but the <s>samādhi</s>-wisdom, being obstructed by the beginningless <s>vyutthāna</s>-<s>saṃskāra</s> (impression of the emergent state) due to its deeply rooted density, would be like a lamp-flame or an atom situated in the middle of a whirlwind — to remove this doubt, he introduces the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>samādhiprajñā</s>,' etc. He reads the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>tajjaḥ saṃskāro 'nyasaṃskārapratibandhī</s>.' The word 'that' (<s>tad</s>) refers to <s>nirvicārā samāpatti</s> (non-reflective cognitive absorption). The word 'other' (<s>anya</s>) denotes <s>vyutthāna</s> (the emergent state). For it is the nature of cognitions to incline toward real objects; the mind wanders unstably only so long as it has not attained reality (<s>tattva</s>). Upon attaining reality, having become established therein, the <s>saṃskāra</s>-cognition cycle (<s>saṃskāra-buddhi-cakra</s>), revolving in succession,

children.text:
"nirupadravabhūtārthasvabhāvasya viparyayaiḥ/ na bādho+anādimattve 'pi buddhes
	    tatpakṣapātataḥ" iti//
children.translated_text: 'For one whose nature is unafflicted real objects, there is no obstruction by erroneous cognitions (<s>viparyayas</s>), even though they are beginningless — because cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) inclines toward that [reality].'

children.text:
syād etat samādhiprajñāto+astu vyutthānajasya saṃskārasya nirodhaḥ/ samādhijas tu
	    saṃskārātiśayaḥ samādhiprajñāprasavahetur asty avikala iti tadavasthaiva cittasya
	    sādhikārateti codayati --- katham asāv iti/ pariharati --- na ta iti/ cittasya hi
	    kāryadvayaṃ śabdādyupabhhogo vivekakhyātiś ceti/ tatra kleśakarmāśayasahitaṃ
	    śabdādyupabhoge vartate/ prajñāprabhavasaṃskāronmūlitanikhilakleśakarmāśayasya tu
	    cetaso+avasitaprāyādhikārabhāvasya vivekakhyātimātram avaśiṣyate kāryam/ tasmāt
	    samādhisaṃskārāś cittasya na bhogādhikārahetavaḥ pratyuta tatparipanthina iti/ svakāryād
	    bhogalakṣaṇād avasādayanti asamarthaṃ kurvantīty arthaḥ/ kasmāt khyātiparyavasānaṃ hi
	    cittaceṣṭitaṃ, tāvad vibhogāya (dhi bhogāya) cittaṃ ceṣṭate na yāvad vivekakhyātim
	    anubhavati/ saṃjātavivekakhyātinas tu kleśanivṛttau na bhogādhikāra ity arthaḥ //1.50//
children.translated_text: One might object: let the <s>saṃskāra</s> born of the emergent state be suppressed by <s>samādhi</s>-wisdom; but the <s>saṃskāra</s> born of <s>samādhi</s>, being an undiminished cause for the production of <s>samādhi</s>-wisdom, remains completely intact — so the mind's state of having further purpose (<s>sādhikāratā</s>) persists. He raises this objection: 'how can that...' He resolves it: 'not so,' etc. For the mind has a twofold function (<s>kārya</s>): the experience of sound and other [objects], and discriminative discernment (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>). Of these, it engages in the experience of sound and other [objects] when accompanied by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>karma</s> (actions), and <s>āśayas</s> (latent deposits). But for the mind whose entire stock of <s>kleśas</s>, <s>karmas</s>, and <s>āśayas</s> has been uprooted by the <s>saṃskāras</s> born of wisdom — whose scope of purpose is nearly exhausted — only discriminative discernment (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) remains as its function. Therefore, the <s>saṃskāras</s> of <s>samādhi</s> are not causes of the mind's authority over enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>); rather, they are antagonistic to it. 'They bring down from their own function characterized by enjoyment' — means they render [the mind] incapable, this is the meaning. Why? Because the activity of the mind culminates in discriminative discernment (<s>khyāti</s>); the mind strives toward enjoyment only so long as it has not experienced <s>vivekakhyāti</s>. But for one in whom <s>vivekakhyāti</s> has arisen, upon the cessation of <s>kleśas</s>, there is no further authority over enjoyment — this is the meaning. (1.50)

children.text: tasyāpi nirodhe sarvanirodhān nirbījaḥ samādhiḥ //1.51//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 1.51:] <s>Tasyāpi nirodhe sarvanirodhān nirbījaḥ samādhiḥ</s> — 'Upon the cessation of even that [<s>saṃskāra</s>], from the cessation of all [modifications], there arises <s>nirbīja samādhi</s> (seedless concentration).' (1.51)

children.text: iti śrīpatañjaliviracitayogasūtreṣu prathamaḥ samādhipādaḥ //1//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter, the <s>Samādhipāda</s> (Chapter on Concentration), of the <s>Yogasūtras</s> composed by the venerable <s>Patañjali</s>. (1)

children.text:
tad atra bhogādhikārapraśāntiḥ prayojanaṃ prajñāsaṃskārāṇām ity uktam/ pṛcchati --- kiṃ
	    ceti/ kiṃ cāsya bhavati prajñāsaṃskāravac cittaṃ prajñāsaṃskārapravāhajanakatayā
	    tathaiva sādhikāram ity adhikārāpanuttaye+anyad api kiṃcid apekṣaṇīyam astīty arthaḥ/
	    sūtreṇottaram āha --- tasyāpi nirodhe sarvanirodhān nirbījaḥ samādhiḥ/ pareṇa vairāgyeṇa
	    jñānaprasādamātralakṣaṇena saṃskāropajananadvārā tasyāpi prajñākṛtasaṃskārasya nirodhe,
	    na kevalaṃ prajñāyā ity apiśabdārthaḥ/ sarvasyotpadyamānasya saṃskāraprajñāpravāhasya
	    nirodhāt kāraṇābhāvena

kāryānutpādāt so+ayaṃ nirbījaḥ samādhir bhavati/
	    vyācaṣṭe --- sa nirbījaḥ samādhiḥ samādhiprajñāvirodhinaḥ parasmād vairāgyād
	    upajāyamānaḥ svakāraṇadvāreṇa na kevalaṃ samādhiprajñāvirodhī prajñākṛtānām apy asau
	    saṃskārāṇāṃ paripanthī bhavati/ nanu vairāgyajaṃ vijñānaṃ sadvijñānaṃ prajñāmātraṃ
	    bādhatāṃ saṃskāraṃ tv avijñānarūpaṃ kathaṃ bādhate/ dṛṣṭā hi jāgrato+api
	    svapnadṛṣṭārthasmṛtir ity āśayavān pṛcchati --- kasmād iti/ uttaraṃ --- nirodhaja iti/
	    nirudhyate+anena prajñeti nirodhaḥ paraṃ vairāgyam/ tato jāto nirodhajaḥ saṃskāraḥ/
	    saṃskārād eva dīrghakālanairantaryasatkārāsevitaparavairāgyajanmanaḥ prajñāsaṃskārabādho
	    na tu vijñānād ity arthaḥ/ syād etat/ nirodhajasaṃskārasadbhāve kiṃ pramāṇaṃ sa hi
	    pratyakṣeṇa vānubhūyeta smṛtyā vā kāryeṇānumīyeta/ na ca sarvavṛttinirodhe pratyakṣam
	    asti yoginaḥ/ nāpi smṛtiḥ/ tasya vṛttimātranirodhatayā smṛtijanakatvāsaṃbhavād ity ata
	    āha --- nirodheti/ nirodhe sthitiś cittasya niruddhāvasthety arthaḥ/ tasyāḥ kālakramo
	    muhūrtārdhayāmayāmāhorātrādis tadanubhavena/ etad uktaṃ bhavati ---
	    vairāgyābhyāsaprakarṣānurodhī nirodhaprakarṣo muhūrtārdhayāmādivyāpitayānubhūyate
	    yoginā/ na ca vairāgyakṣaṇāḥ kramaniyatatayā parasparam asaṃbhavantas
	    tattatkālavyāpitayā sātiśayaṃ nirodhaṃ kartum īśata iti tattadvairāgyakṣaṇapracayajanyaḥ
	    sthāyī saṃskārapracaya eṣitavya iti bhāvaḥ/ nanūcchidyantāṃ prajñāsaṃskārāḥ/
