	    nirodhasaṃskārās tu kutaḥ samucchidyante/ anucchede vā sādhikāratvam evety ata āha ---
	    vyutthāneti/ vyutthānaṃ ca tasya nirodhasamādhiś ca saṃprajñātas tatprabhavāḥ saṃskārāḥ
	    kaivalyabhāgīyā nirodhajāḥ saṃskārā ity arthaḥ/ vyutthānaprajñāsaṃskārāś citte pralīnā
	    iti bhavati cittaṃ vyutthānaprajñāsaṃskāravat/ nirodhasaṃskāras tu pratyudita evāste
	    citte/ nirodhasaṃskāre saty api cittam anadhikāravat/ puruṣārthajanakaṃ cittaṃ hi
	    sādhikāraṃ śabdādyupabhogavivekakhyātī ca tathā puruṣārthaḥ/ saṃskāraśeṣatāyāṃ tu na
	    buddheḥ pratisaṃvedī puruṣa iti nāsau puruṣārthaḥ/
children.translated_text: the effect does not arise; this is <s>nirbīja samādhi</s> (seedless concentration). He explains: 'that <s>nirbīja samādhi</s>...' This <s>nirbīja samādhi</s>, arising from the supreme <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) that opposes <s>samādhi</s>-wisdom, through its own cause, not only opposes <s>samādhi</s>-wisdom but also becomes an adversary of the <s>saṃskāras</s> produced by wisdom. [Objection:] The cognition born of <s>vairāgya</s>, being a valid cognition and mere wisdom, may override [other] wisdom — but how can it override a <s>saṃskāra</s>, which is of the nature of non-cognition? For even in the waking state, the memory of objects seen in dreams is observed — with this intention he asks: 'why?' The answer: 'born of cessation' (<s>nirodhaja</s>). That by which wisdom is suppressed (<s>nirudhyate</s>) is <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) — [meaning] the supreme <s>vairāgya</s>. Born from that is the <s>nirodhaja saṃskāra</s> (impression born of cessation). The obstruction of the <s>saṃskāras</s> of wisdom is from the <s>saṃskāra</s> alone — born of the supreme <s>vairāgya</s> that has been cultivated over a long time, without interruption, and with devotion — not from cognition [directly]; this is the meaning. One might object: what is the proof for the existence of the <s>nirodhaja saṃskāra</s>? For it would be experienced either through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), or inferred through memory or through its effect. But in the cessation of all <s>vṛttis</s> (modifications), there is no perception for the <s>yogin</s>. Nor is there memory, since the cessation of all modifications makes it impossible for it to generate memory. To this he says: 'cessation,' etc. The mind's stability in cessation is what is meant by the 'state of cessation' (<s>niruddhāvasthā</s>). Its temporal duration — a <s>muhūrta</s> (48 minutes), half a <s>yāma</s> (watch), a <s>yāma</s>, a day-and-night, etc. — [is known] through the experience of that. The purport is this: the intensity of cessation, which accords with the intensity of <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) and <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice), is experienced by the <s>yogin</s> as pervading [durations of] a <s>muhūrta</s>, half a <s>yāma</s>, and so on. And the moments of <s>vairāgya</s>, being regulated by sequence and thus not occurring simultaneously, cannot by themselves produce cessation of increasing degree pervading those respective durations — therefore, a stable accumulation of <s>saṃskāras</s> generated by the accumulation of those respective moments of <s>vairāgya</s> must be postulated; this is the import. [Objection:] Let the <s>saṃskāras</s> of wisdom be destroyed. But whence are the <s>saṃskāras</s> of cessation destroyed? Or, if they are not destroyed, there would be a continued state of purposive function. To this he says: '<s>vyutthāna</s>,' etc. <s>Vyutthāna</s> (emergence) and <s>nirodhasamādhi</s> (cessation-concentration) are both <s>saṃprajñāta</s> (cognitive); the <s>saṃskāras</s> born from those [belong to the realm of emergence], while the <s>saṃskāras</s> born of cessation (<s>nirodhaja</s>) are conducive to <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) — this is the meaning. The <s>saṃskāras</s> of emergent wisdom are dissolved in the mind, so the mind possesses <s>saṃskāras</s> of emergent wisdom. But the <s>saṃskāra</s> of cessation stands forth manifestly in the mind. Even when the <s>saṃskāra</s> of cessation is present, the mind is devoid of further purpose (<s>anadhikāra</s>). For the mind that generates the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> has purposive function — and the experience of sound and other objects as well as <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative discernment) constitute that purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>. But when only <s>saṃskāras</s> remain, <s>puruṣa</s> is not the experiencer of cognition, and so that is not the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text:
videhaprakṛtilayānāṃ na
	    nirodhabhāgitayā sādhikāraṃ cittam/ api tu kleśavāsitatayety āśayavān āha --- yasmād
	    iti/ śeṣaṃ sugamam //1.51//
children.translated_text: For the <s>videhas</s> (the bodiless) and the <s>prakṛtilayas</s> (those merged in <s>Prakṛti</s>), the mind does not have purposive function through the cessation-portion; rather, [it has purposive function] through being tinged by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — with this intention he says: 'since,' etc. The rest is easy to understand. (1.51)

Now, it has been stated here that the purpose of the <s>saṃskāras</s> of wisdom is the cessation of the mind's authority over enjoyment. He asks: 'what further,' etc. What further happens to the mind that possesses <s>saṃskāras</s> of wisdom? Since it still has a purposive function as the generator of the flow of <s>saṃskāras</s> of wisdom, is there something else required for the removal of [its] purposive function? — this is the meaning. He answers with the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>tasyāpi nirodhe sarvanirodhān nirbījaḥ samādhiḥ</s>.' Through the supreme <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), characterized merely by the clarity of knowledge (<s>jñānaprasāda</s>), by means of generating [counteracting] <s>saṃskāras</s>, upon the cessation of even that <s>saṃskāra</s> produced by wisdom — not only of wisdom [itself], this is the meaning of the word 'even' (<s>api</s>). From the cessation of all — that is, the flow of <s>saṃskāras</s> and wisdom that is being produced — due to the absence of the cause,

children.text:
yogasyoddeśanirdeśau tadarthaṃ vṛttilakṣaṇam/ yogopāyāḥ prabhedāś ca pāde+asminn
	    upavarṇitāḥ //1//
children.translated_text: The definition and description of <s>Yoga</s>, the nature of <s>vṛttis</s> (modifications) for that purpose, the means of <s>Yoga</s> and its varieties — these have been described in this chapter. (1)

children.text:
iti śrīvācaspatimiśraviracitāyāṃ pātañjalayogasūtrabhāṣyavyākhyāyāṃ prathamaḥ
	    samādhipādaḥ //1//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter, the <s>Samādhipāda</s> (Chapter on Concentration), of the commentary on the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on <s>Patañjali's</s> <s>Yogasūtras</s>, composed by the venerable <s>Vācaspatimiśra</s>. (1)

children.text: tatra dvitīyaḥ sādhanapādaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, the second chapter: the <s>Sādhanapāda</s> (Chapter on Practice).

children.text: tapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni kriyāyogaḥ //2.1//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 2.1:] <s>Tapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni kriyāyogaḥ</s> — '<s>Tapas</s> (austerity), <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), and <s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s> (devotion to God) constitute <s>Kriyāyoga</s> (yoga of action).' (2.1)

children.text:
nanu prathamapādenaiva sopāyaḥ sāvāntaraprabhedaḥ saphalo yoga uktas tat kim aparam
	  avaśiṣyate yadarthaṃ dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ prārabhyetety ata āha --- uddiṣṭa iti/
	  abhyāsavairāgye hi yogopāyau prathame pāda uktau/ na ca tau vyutthitacittasya drāg ity
	  eva saṃbhavata iti dvitīyapādopadeśyān upāyān apekṣate sattvaśuddhyartham/ tato hi
	  viśuddhasattvaḥ kṛtarakṣāsaṃvidhāno+abhyāsavairāgye pratyahaṃ bhāvayati/ samāhitatvam
	  avikṣiptatvam/ kathaṃ vyutthānacitto+apy upadekṣyamāṇair upāyair yuktaḥ san yogī syād
	  ity arthaḥ/ tatra vakṣyamāṇeṣu niyameṣv ākṛṣya prāthamikaṃ pratyupayuktataratayā
	  prathamataḥ kriyāyogam upadiśati sūtrakāraḥ --- tapaḥsvādhyāyetyādi/ kriyaiva yogaḥ
	  kriyāyogo yogasādhanatvāt/ ata eva viṣṇupurāṇe khāṇḍikyakeśidhvajasaṃvāde ---
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Yoga</s> with its means, sub-varieties, and fruits has already been described in the first chapter. What then remains, for the sake of which a second chapter should be undertaken? To this he replies: 'having been indicated.' For <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice) and <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), the means of <s>Yoga</s>, were stated in the first chapter. But these are not immediately possible for one whose mind is in the emergent state (<s>vyutthāna</s>). Therefore, it requires the means to be taught in the second chapter for the purpose of purifying <s>sattva</s>. For indeed, one whose <s>sattva</s> is purified, having made protective arrangements, cultivates <s>abhyāsa</s> and <s>vairāgya</s> daily — [attaining] composure and non-distraction. The meaning is: how can one whose mind is in the emergent state become a <s>yogin</s> when equipped with the means to be taught? There, drawing from the <s>niyamas</s> (observances) to be described, [and] because of its greater immediate usefulness as a preliminary, the author of the <s>sūtras</s> first teaches <s>kriyāyoga</s> (the yoga of action): 'austerity, self-study,' etc. Action itself is <s>Yoga</s> — <s>kriyāyoga</s> — because it is a means to <s>Yoga</s>. For this very reason, in the <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s>, in the dialogue between <s>Khāṇḍikya</s> and <s>Keśidhvaja</s>:

children.text: "yogayuk prathamaṃ yogī yuñjamāno+abhidhīyate"
viṣṇupurāṇam 6.7.33
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> 6.7.33
'The <s>yogin</s> who is first engaged in <s>Yoga</s> is called "one who is yoking."'

children.text:
ity upakramya tapaḥsvādhyāyādayo darśitāḥ/ vyatirekamukhena (vyatirekamukheṇa) tapasa
	  upāyatvam āha --- nātapasvina iti/ tapaso+avāntaravyāpāram upāyatopayoginaṃ darśayati
	  --- anādīti/ anādibhyāṃ karmakleśavāsanābhyāṃ citrāta eva pratyupasthitam upanataṃ
	  viṣayajālaṃ yasyāṃ sā tathoktā/ aśuddhī rajastamaḥsamudreko nāntareṇa tapaḥ saṃbhedam
	  āpadyate/ sāndrasya nitāntaviralatā saṃbhedaḥ/ nanūpādīyamānam api tapo
	  dhātuvaiṣamyahetutayā yogapratipakṣa iti kathaṃ tadupāya ity ata āha --- tac ceti/
	  tāvanmātram eva tapaś caraṇīyaṃ na yāvatā dhātuvaiṣamyam āpadyata ity arthaḥ/

praṇavādayaḥ puruṣasūktarudramaṇḍalabrāhmaṇādayo vaidikāḥ, paurāṇikāś ca
	  brahmapārāyaṇādayaḥ/ paramagurur bhagavān īśvaras tasmin/ yatredam uktam ---
children.translated_text: <s>Praṇava</s> (the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>) and others [constitute self-study]; Vedic [texts include] the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, <s>Rudra</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and the like; and Purāṇic [texts include] the <s>Brahmapārāyaṇa</s> and the like. The supreme teacher is the <s>Bhagavān</s>, <s>Īśvara</s> — devotion to Him [is <s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s>]. As it has been said:

— having thus introduced the topic, austerity (<s>tapas</s>), self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), and the rest were shown. He states the instrumentality of austerity through the method of exclusion (<s>vyatireka</s>): 'not for one without austerity.' He shows the subsidiary function of austerity, useful as a means: 'beginningless' — the impurity (<s>aśuddhi</s>) that is the predominance of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, in which a web of sense-objects has been presented and offered from the beginningless [impressions of] <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśa</s>-<s>vāsanās</s> (affliction-impressions), is so described. That impurity does not undergo attenuation (<s>saṃbheda</s>) without austerity. 'Attenuation' means the extreme rarefaction of what is dense. But doesn't austerity, even when undertaken, being a cause of elemental imbalance (<s>dhātuvaiṣamya</s>), oppose <s>Yoga</s>? How then can it be its means? To this he replies: 'And that' — austerity should be practiced only to the extent that it does not produce elemental imbalance. This is the meaning.

children.text:
"kāmato+akāmato vāpi yat karomi śubhāśubham/ tat sarvaṃ tvayi saṃnyastaṃ tvatprayuktaḥ
	  karomy aham" iti/
children.translated_text: 'Whether willingly or unwillingly, whatever I do, good or bad — all that is surrendered to you; impelled by you, I act.' Thus.

children.text: tatphalasaṃnyāso vā phalānabhisaṃdhānena kāryakaraṇam/ yatredam uktam ---
children.translated_text: Or, the surrender of [its] fruit — performing action without attachment to the result. As it has been said:

children.text:
"karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana/ mā karmaphalahetur bhūr mā te saṅgo+astv
	  akarmaṇi"
bhagavadgītā 2.47
children.translated_text: <s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 2.47
'Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits; do not be the cause of the fruit of action, nor let your attachment be to inaction.'

children.text: samādhibhāvanārthaḥ kleśatanūkaraṇārthaś ca //2.2//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 2.2:] <s>Samādhibhāvanārthaḥ kleśatanūkaraṇārthaś ca</s> — '[<s>Kriyāyoga</s>] is for the purpose of cultivating <s>samādhi</s> and for the purpose of attenuating the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).' (2.2)

children.text:
tasya prayojanābhidhānāya sūtram avatārayati --- sa hīti/ sūtraṃ ---
	  samādhibhāvanārthaḥ kleśatanūkaraṇārthaś ca/ nanu kriyāyoga eva cet kleśān pratanūkaroti
	  kṛtaṃ tarhi prasaṃkhyānenety ata āha --- pratanūkṛtān iti/ kriyāyogasya
	  pratanūkaraṇamātre vyāpāro na tu vandhyatve kleśānāṃ prasaṃkhyānasya tu tadvandhyatve/
	  dagdhabījakalpān iti vandhyatvena dagdhakalamabījasārūpyam uktam/ syād etat/
	  prasaṃkhyānam eva cet kleśān aprasavadharmiṇaḥ kariṣyati, kṛtam eṣāṃ pratanūkaraṇenety
	  ata āha --- teṣām iti/ kleśānām atānave hi balavadvirodhigrastā sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātir
	  udetum eva notsahate/ prāg eva tadvandhyabhāvaṃ kartuṃ praviralīkṛteṣu tu kleśeṣu
	  durbaleṣu tadvirodhiny api vairāgyābhyāsābhyām upajāyate/ upajātā ca tair
	  aparāmṛṣṭānabhibhūtā naiva yāvat parāmṛśyata iti/ sattvapuruṣānyatāmātrakhyātiḥ sūkṣmā
	  prajñātīndriyatayā sūkṣmo+asyā viṣaya iti sūkṣmā prajñā pratiprasavāya pravilayāya
	  kalpiṣyate/ kutaḥ, samāptādhikārā yataḥ samāpto+adhikāraḥ kāryārambhaṇaṃ guṇānāṃ yayā
	  hetubhūtayā sā tathokteti //2.2//
children.translated_text: In order to state its purpose, he introduces the <s>sūtra</s>: 'For indeed' — the <s>sūtra</s>: 'For the purpose of cultivating <s>samādhi</s> and for the purpose of attenuating the <s>kleśas</s>.' Now, if <s>kriyāyoga</s> alone attenuates the <s>kleśas</s>, then what need is there for <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (discernment-meditation)? To this he replies: 'attenuated.' The operation of <s>kriyāyoga</s> is limited to mere attenuation, not to rendering the <s>kleśas</s> barren; but the operation of <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> is to render them barren. 'Like burnt seeds' — their barrenness is expressed through the simile of burnt husk-seeds. One might say: if <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> alone will render the <s>kleśas</s> incapable of producing [effects], what need is there for their attenuation? To this he replies: 'of those' — for when the <s>kleśas</s> are not attenuated, the discernment of the otherness of <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> (<s>sattvapuruṣānyatākhyāti</s>), being seized by its powerful adversary, is simply unable to arise, let alone render them barren. But when the <s>kleśas</s> have been made thin and weak through attenuation, the [discernment], though opposed by them, arises through <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) and <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice). And having arisen, not being seized or overpowered by them, it [continues] unimpeded. The discernment of mere otherness of <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> — this subtle <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), whose object is subtle because it transcends the senses — this subtle wisdom will be designated as [leading to] <s>pratiprasava</s> (dissolution [of the <s>guṇas</s>]). Why? Because its operation is complete — since the operation of the <s>guṇas</s>, which is their activity, is complete when it serves as a cause [for this discernment]. (2.2)

children.text: avidyāsmitārāgadveṣābhiniveśāḥ kleśāḥ //2.3//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 2.3:] <s>Avidyāsmitārāgadveṣābhiniveśāḥ kleśāḥ</s> — 'The <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are: <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>asmitā</s> (egoism), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life).' (2.3)

children.text:
pṛcchati --- atheti/ avidyeti sūtreṇa parihāraḥ/ avidyāsmitārāgadveṣābhiniveśāḥ kleśāḥ/
	  vyācaṣṭe --- pañca viparyayā iti/ avidyā tāvad viparyaya eva/ asmitādayo 'py
	  avidyopādānās tadavinirbhāgavartina iti viparyayāḥ/ tataś cāvidyāsamucchede teṣām api
	  samucchedo yukta iti bhāvaḥ/ teṣām ucchettavyatāhetuṃ saṃsārakāraṇatvam āha --- te
	  spandamānāḥ samudācaranto guṇānām adhikāraṃ draḍhayanti balavantaṃ kurvanty ata eva
	  pariṇāmam avasthāpayanti avyaktamahadahaṃkāraparamparayā hi kāryakāraṇasrota unnamayanty
	  udbhāvayanti/ yadarthaṃ sarvam etat kurvanti tad darśayati --- paraspareti/ karmaṇāṃ
	  vipāko jātyāyurbhogalakṣaṇaḥ puruṣārthas tam amī kleśā abhinirharanti niṣpādayanti/ kiṃ
	  pratyekaṃ nety āha --- parasparānugraheti/ karmabhiḥ kleśāḥ kleśaiś ca karmāṇīti //2.3//
children.translated_text: He asks: 'now' — the <s>sūtra</s> replies: '<s>avidyā</s>, <s>asmitā</s>, <s>rāga</s>, <s>dveṣa</s>, and <s>abhiniveśa</s> are the <s>kleśas</s>.' He explains: 'the five errors (<s>viparyayas</s>).' <s>Avidyā</s> is indeed error itself. <s>Asmitā</s> and the rest, having <s>avidyā</s> as their material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) and operating inseparably from it, are [also] errors. Therefore, upon the eradication of <s>avidyā</s>, their eradication too is appropriate — such is the purport. He states the reason for their being subject to eradication — namely, their being the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>: 'They, when active, when operating, strengthen the operation of the <s>guṇas</s>' — that is, make it powerful. For that very reason, 'they establish transformation' — for through the series of the Unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), the Great (<s>mahat</s>), the Ego-sense (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), they raise up, bring forth the stream of cause and effect. He shows the purpose for which they do all this: 'mutually' — the fruition of <s>karmas</s> (actions), characterized by birth (<s>jāti</s>), lifespan (<s>āyus</s>), and enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>), [serves] the purpose of the <s>puruṣa</s> — these <s>kleśas</s> bring it about, accomplish it. Is it individually or not? He says: 'through mutual support' — <s>karmas</s> [support] <s>kleśas</s>, and <s>kleśas</s> [support] <s>karmas</s>. (2.3)

children.text: avidyā kṣetram uttareṣāṃ prasuptatanuvicchinnodārāṇām //2.4//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 2.4:] <s>Avidyā kṣetram uttareṣāṃ prasuptatanuvicchinnodārāṇām</s> — '<s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the field of the subsequent [afflictions], whether dormant (<s>prasupta</s>), attenuated (<s>tanu</s>), interrupted (<s>vicchinna</s>), or fully active (<s>udāra</s>).' (2.4)

children.text:
heyānāṃ kleśānām avidyāmūlatvaṃ darśayati --- avidyā kṣetram uttareṣāṃ
	  prasuptatanuvicchinnodārāṇām/ tatra kā prasuptir iti/ svocitām arthakriyām akurvatāṃ
	  kleśānāṃ sadbhāve na pramāṇam astīty abhiprāyaḥ pṛcchataḥ/ uttaraṃ --- cetasīti/ mā
	  nāmārthakriyāṃ kārṣuḥ kleśā videhaprakṛtilayānāṃ bījabhāvaṃ prāptās tu te śaktimātreṇa
	  santi kṣīra iva dadhi/ na hi vivekakhyāter anyad asti kāraṇaṃ tadvandhyatāyām/ ato
	  videhaprakṛtilayā vivekakhyātivirahiṇaḥ

prasuptakleśā na yāvat
	  tadavadhikālaṃ prāpnuvanti/ tatprāptau tu punarāvṛttāḥ santaḥ kleśās teṣu teṣu viṣayeṣu
	  saṃmukhībhavanti/ śaktimātreṇa pratiṣṭhā yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ/ tad anenotpattiśaktir uktā/
	  bījabhāvopagama iti ca kāryaśaktir iti/ nanu vivekakhyātimato+api kleśāḥ kasmān na
	  prasuptā ity ata āha --- prasaṃkhyānavata iti/ caramadeho na tasya dehāntaram utpatsyate
	  yadapekṣayāsya dehaḥ pūrva ity arthaḥ/ nānyatra videhādiṣv ity arthaḥ/ nanu sato
	  nātyantavināśa iti kim iti tadīyayogarddhibalena viṣayasaṃmukhībhāve na kleśāḥ
	  prabudhyanta ity ata āha --- satām iti/ santu kleśā dagdhas tv eṣāṃ prasaṃkhyānāgninā
	  bījabhāva ity arthaḥ/ kleśapratipakṣaḥ kriyāyogas tasya bhāvanam anuṣṭhānaṃ tenopahatās
	  tanavaḥ/ athavā samyagjñānam avidyāyāḥ pratipakṣo bhedadarśanam asmitāyā mādhyasthyaṃ
	  rāgadveṣayor anubandhabuddhinivṛttir abhiniveśasyeti/ vicchittim āha --- tatheti/
	  kleśānām anyatamena samudācaratābhibhavād vātyantaviṣayasevayā vā vicchidya vicchidya
	  tena tenātmanā samudācaranty āvirbhavanti vājīkaraṇādyupayogena vābhibhāvakadaurbalyena
	  veti/ vīpsayā vicchedasamudācārayoḥ paunaḥpunyaṃ darśayatā yathoktāt prasuptād bheda
	  uktaḥ/ rāgeṇa vā samudācaratā vijātīyaḥ krodho+abhibhūyate sajātīyena vā
	  viṣayāntaravartinā rāgeṇaiva viṣayāntaravartī rāgo+abhibhūyata ity āha --- rāgeti/
	  bhaviṣyadvṛttes trayī gatir yathāyogaṃ veditavyety āha ---
children.translated_text: have dormant <s>kleśas</s> and do not reach the time-limit set by that [<s>vivekakhyāti</s>]. But upon reaching that [limit], having returned [to embodied existence], the <s>kleśas</s> confront them with respect to various objects. Those whose existence is through mere potency are so described. By this, the power to arise is stated. And the phrase 'reaching the seed-state' states the power to produce effects. Now, even for one possessing <s>vivekakhyāti</s>, why are the <s>kleśas</s> not dormant? To this he replies: 'for the one possessing <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (discernment-meditation).' 'Of last body' means: no other body will arise for him in relation to which his [present] body would be 'previous' — such is the meaning. 'Not elsewhere, such as in the <s>videhas</s>, etc.' — such is the meaning. Now, [according to the principle that] 'there is no absolute annihilation of what exists,' why do the <s>kleśas</s> not awaken when confronted with objects through the power of his yogic attainments (<s>ṛddhi</s>)? To this he replies: 'of existing [<s>kleśas</s>]' — let the <s>kleśas</s> exist; but their seed-state has been burned by the fire of <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>. This is the meaning. The practice of <s>kriyāyoga</s>, which is the antidote to the <s>kleśas</s> — those [<s>kleśas</s>] impaired by its cultivation are 'attenuated' (<s>tanu</s>). Alternatively, right knowledge is the antidote of <s>avidyā</s>; the vision of difference [is the antidote] of <s>asmitā</s>; equanimity (<s>mādhyasthya</s>) [is the antidote] of <s>rāga</s> and <s>dveṣa</s>; and the cessation of the belief in continuation [is the antidote] of <s>abhiniveśa</s>. He states 'interruption' (<s>vicchinna</s>): 'thus.' The <s>kleśas</s>, being overpowered by the operation of one among them, or being interrupted again and again through excessive indulgence in sense-objects, operate and manifest in one or another form. Or, through the use of aphrodisiacs, etc., or through the weakness of the overpowering [affliction], [they re-emerge]. By the repetition [of the verb], the recurrence of interruption and operation is shown — thereby indicating the difference from dormancy as described above. Or, <s>krodha</s> (anger) — being of a different kind — is overpowered by <s>rāga</s> (attachment) in operation; or <s>rāga</s> directed at one object is overpowered by <s>rāga</s> directed at another object — being of the same kind. Thus he says: '<s>rāga</s>.' He says that the three courses of future modification should be understood as appropriate —

children.text:
sa hīti/
	  bhaviṣyadvṛttikleśamātraparāmarśi sarvanāma na caitrarāgaparāmarśi tasya vicchinnatvād
	  eveti/ udāram āha --- viṣaya iti/ nanūdāra eva puruṣān kliśnātīti bhavatu kleśo+anye tv
	  akliśnantaḥ kathaṃ kleśā ity ata āha --- sarva evaita iti/ kleśaviṣayatvaṃ
	  kleśapadavācyatvaṃ nātikrāmanty udāratām āpadyamānāḥ/ ata eva te+api heyā iti bhāvaḥ/
	  kleśatvenaikatāṃ manyamānaś codayati --- kas tarhīti/ kleśatvena samānatve+api
	  yathoktāvasthābhedād viśeṣa iti pariharati --- ucyate satyam iti/ syād etat/ avidyāto
	  bhavantu kleśāḥ, tathāpy avidyānivṛttau kasmān nivartante/ na khalu paṭaḥ
	  kuvindanivṛttau nivartata ity ata āha --- sarva eveti/ bhedā iva bhedās
	  tadavinirbhāgavartina iti yāvat/ pṛcchati --- kasmāt/ uttaraṃ --- sarveṣv iti/ tad eva
	  sphuṭayati --- yad iti/ ākāryate samāropyate/ śeṣaṃ sugamam/
children.translated_text: 'For he,' etc. The pronoun 'all' (<s>sarvanāman</s>) refers only to the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) in terms of future modifications; it does not refer to the attachment of <s>Caitra</s> [specifically], because that [particular attachment] has been cut off. He states the active [state]: 'object,' etc. [Objection:] Only the active [kleśa] afflicts persons, so let that be a <s>kleśa</s>; but the others, not afflicting, how are they <s>kleśas</s>? Hence he says: 'All these indeed,' etc. They do not transcend being the domain of <s>kleśa</s>, being denotable by the word <s>kleśa</s>, even when attaining the active state. Hence they too are to be abandoned — such is the purport. One who considers them unified as <s>kleśas</s> raises an objection: 'What then?' etc. Even though they are the same in being <s>kleśas</s>, there is a distinction due to the difference of states as described — he resolves thus: 'It is said, truly,' etc. One might say: let the <s>kleśas</s> arise from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); even so, why do they cease upon the cessation of <s>avidyā</s>? A cloth does not cease upon the cessation of the weaver — hence he says: 'All indeed,' etc. The divisions are, as it were, divisions — they exist inseparably within it — such is the import. He asks: 'Why?' The answer: 'In all,' etc. He clarifies that very thing: 'That which,' etc. 'Is imposed' means is superimposed. The rest is easy to understand.

He shows that <s>avidyā</s> is the root of the <s>kleśas</s> to be abandoned: '<s>Avidyā</s> is the field of the subsequent [afflictions], whether dormant, attenuated, interrupted, or fully active.' Therein: 'What is dormancy (<s>prasupta</s>)?' — the questioner's intent is: there is no means of valid cognition for the existence of <s>kleśas</s> that are not performing their appropriate function. The answer: 'in the mind.' Let it be that the <s>kleśas</s> do not perform their function for those who are bodiless (<s>videha</s>) and merged in <s>Prakṛti</s> (<s>prakṛtilaya</s>); still, having reached the seed-state, they exist through their mere potency — like curd in milk. For there is no other cause for their barrenness than <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative discernment). Therefore, the <s>videha</s> and <s>prakṛtilaya</s>, being devoid of <s>vivekakhyāti</s>,

children.text:
"prasuptās tattvalīnānāṃ tanvavasthāś ca yoginām/ vicchinnodārarūpāś ca kleśā
	  viṣayasaṅginām" iti saṃgrahaḥ //2.4//
children.translated_text: "Dormant [in those absorbed into the principles], in an attenuated state [in yogins], and in the cut-off and active forms [in those attached to sense objects] — such are the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) [in those attached to] objects" — this is the summary. (2.4)

children.text: anityāśuciduḥkhānātmasu nityaśucisukhātmakhyātir avidyā //2.5//
children.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the perception of the eternal, the pure, the pleasant, and the self in what is non-eternal, impure, painful, and non-self. (2.5)

children.text:
anityāśuciduḥkhānātmasu nityaśucisukhātmakhyātir avidyā/ anityatvopayogiviśeṣaṇaṃ ---
	  kārya iti/ kecit kila bhūtāni nityatvenābhimanyamānās tadrūpam abhīpsavas

tāny evopāsate/ evaṃ dhūmādimārgān upāsate candrasūryatārakādyulokān nityān
	  abhimanyamānās tatprāptaye/ evaṃ divaukaso devān amṛtān abhimanyamānās tabhāvāya somaṃ
	  pibanti/ āmnāyate hi --- "apāma somam amṛtā abhūma"
children.translated_text: worship those very [elements]. Likewise, they worship the paths of smoke and the like, regarding the worlds above — of the moon, sun, stars, etc. — as eternal, for the purpose of attaining them. Likewise, regarding the celestial gods as immortal, they drink <s>Soma</s> in order to attain that state. For it is recorded: 'We have drunk the <s>Soma</s>; we have become immortal.'

children.text: taittirīyasaṃhitā 3.2.5.4
children.translated_text: <s>Taittirīyasaṃhitā</s> 3.2.5.4

children.text:
iti/
	  seyam anityeṣu nityakhyātir avidyā/ tathāśucau paramabībhatse kāye/ ardhokta eva
	  kāyabībhatsatāyāṃ vaiyāsikīṃ gāthāṃ paṭhati --- sthānād iti/ mātur udaraṃ
	  mūtrādyupahataṃ sthānaṃ, pitror lohitaretasīṃ bījam/ aśitapītāhārarasādibhāva
	  upaṣṭambhas tena śarīraṃ dhāryate/ niḥsyandaḥ prasvedaḥ/ nidhanaṃ ca śrotriyaśarīram apy
	  apavitrayati tatsparśe snānavidhānāt/ nanu yadi śarīram aśuci kṛtaṃ tarhi
	  mṛjjalādikṣālanenety ata āha --- ādheyaśaucatvād iti/ svabhāvenāśucer api śarīrasya
	  śaucam ādheyaṃ sugandhiteva kāminīnām aṅgarāgādibhiḥ/ ardhoktaṃ pūrayati --- ity
	  uktebhyo hetubhyo+aśucau śarīra iti/ śucikhyātim āha --- naveti/ hāvaḥ śṛṅgārajā līlā/
	  kasya strīkāyasya paramabībhatsasya kena mandatamasādṛśyena śaśāṅkalekhādinā saṃbandhaḥ/
	  etenāśucau strīkāye śucikhyātipradarśanena/ apuṇye hiṃsādau saṃsāramocakādīnāṃ
	  puṇyapratyayaḥ/ evam arjanarakṣaṇādiduḥkhabahulatayānarthe dhanādāv arthapratyayā
	  vyākhyātāḥ sarveṣāṃ jugupsitatvenāśucitvāt/ tathā duḥkha iti/ sugamam/ tathānātmanīti/
	  sugamam/ tathaitad atroktaṃ pañcaśikhena/
children.translated_text: This is <s>avidyā</s> — the perception of the eternal in what is non-eternal. Likewise, [the perception of purity] in the body, which is supremely disgusting. He recites <s>Vyāsa</s>'s verse, [the illustration of] the body's disgusting nature being half-stated already: 'From the place,' etc. The womb of the mother, contaminated by urine and the like, is the 'place'; the seed is the blood and semen of the parents. The 'sustenance' is the transformation of the essence of food and drink consumed — by that the body is sustained. The 'exudation' is perspiration. And 'death' — even the body of a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s> causes impurity, since bathing is prescribed upon contact with it. Now, if the body is impure, then it could be purified by washing with water and clay — hence he says: 'because purity is [only] superimposed.' The purity of the body, which is impure by nature, is [merely] superimposed — like the fragrance of courtesans [applied] with cosmetics and the like. He completes what was half-stated: 'Thus, from the stated reasons, the body is impure.' He states the perception of purity: 'new,' etc. '<s>Hāva</s>' is the coquetry born of amorous sentiment. What connection does the body of a woman, supremely disgusting, have with the faint likeness [of beauty], such as the sliver of the moon and the like? By this, the perception of purity in the impure body of a woman is illustrated. The notion of merit in what is non-meritorious, such as violence and the like, including those who [claim to] liberate from <s>saṃsāra</s>; likewise, the notion of value (<s>artha</s>) in what is valueless, such as wealth and the like, which abounds in the suffering of acquisition, preservation, and the rest — all these are explained, because all are objects of disgust, hence impure. 'Likewise, in suffering,' etc. — easy to understand. 'Likewise, in the non-self,' etc. — easy to understand. And this is stated here by <s>Pañcaśikha</s>:

children.text:
vyaktaṃ cetanaṃ putradārapaśvādi/
	  avyaktam acetanaṃ śayyāsanāśanādi/ sa sarvo+apratibuddho mūḍhaḥ/ catvāri padāni sthānāny
	  asyā iti catuṣpadā/ nanv anyāpi diṅmohālātacakrādiviṣayānantapadāvidyā tat kim ucyate
	  catuṣpadety ata āha --- mūlam asyeti/ santu nāmānyā apy avidyāḥ saṃsārabījaṃ tu
	  catuṣpadaiveti/ nanv avidyeti nañsamāsaḥ pūrvapadārthapradhāno vā syād yathāmakṣikam
	  iti/ uttarapadārthapradhāno vā yathārājapuruṣa iti/ anyapadārthapradhāno vā yathāmakṣiko
	  deśa iti/ tatra pūrvapadārthapradhānatve vidyāyāḥ prasajyapratiṣedho gamyeta/ na cāsyāḥ
	  kleśādikāraṇatvam/ uttarapadārthapradhānatve vā vidyaiva kasyacid abhāvena viśiṣṭā
	  gamyeta/ sā ca kleśādiparipanthinī na tu tadbījam/ na hi pradhānopaghātī pradhānaguṇo
	  yuktaḥ/ tadanupaghātāya guṇe tv anyāyyakalpanā/ tasmād vidyāsvarūpānupaghātāya
	  naño+anyathākaraṇam apy āhāro vā niṣedhyasyeti/ anyapadārthapradhānatve tv
	  avidyamānavidyā buddhir vaktavyā/ na cāsau vidyāyā abhāvamātreṇa kleśādibījam/
	  vivekakhyātipūrvakanirodhasaṃpannāyā api tathātvaprasaṅgāt/ tasmāt sarvathaivāvidyāyā na
	  kleśādimūlatety ata āha --- tasyāś ceti/ vastuno bhāvo vastusatattvaṃ vastutvam iti
	  yāvat/ tad anena na prasajyapratiṣedhaḥ/ nāpi vidyaivāvidyā, na tadabhāvaviśiṣṭā buddhir
	  api tu vidyāviruddhaṃ viparyayajñānam avidyety uktam/ lokādhīnāvadhāraṇo hi śabdārthayoḥ
	  saṃbandhaḥ/ loke cottarapadārthapradhānasyāpi naña uttarapadābhidheyopamardakasya
	  tallakṣitatadviruddhaparatayā tatra tatropalabdher ihāpi tadviruddhe vṛttir iti bhāvaḥ/
	  dṛṣṭāntaṃ vibhajate --- yathā nāmitra iti/ na mitrābhāvo nāpi mitramātram ity
	  asyānantaraṃ vastvantaraṃ kiṃ tu tadviruddhaḥ sapatna iti vaktavyam/ tathāgoṣpadam iti
	  na goṣpadābhāvo na goṣpadamātraṃ kiṃ tu deśa eva vipulo goṣpadaviruddhas tābhyām
	  abhāvagoṣpadābhyām anyad vastvantaram/ dārṣṭāntike yojayati --- evam iti //2.5//
children.translated_text: The manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) and sentient — sons, wife, cattle, and the like; the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) and insentient — bed, seat, food, and the like. All such a person, unawakened, is deluded. '[<s>Avidyā</s>] having four feet' — [it has] four stations. But other <s>avidyās</s> [too] — such as confusion of direction, the firebrand-circle illusion, and the like — are <s>avidyā</s> with countless feet; so why is it said to have four feet? Hence he says: 'The root of this,' etc. Let there be other <s>avidyās</s> by name; but the seed of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) is only the four-footed one. Now, '<s>avidyā</s>' is a negative compound (<s>nañsamāsa</s>): is it one in which the first member is primary, as in '<s>amakṣika</s>' (fly-free)? Or one in which the last member is primary, as in '<s>rājapuruṣa</s>' (king's man)? Or one in which some other meaning is primary, as in '<s>amakṣika deśa</s>' (a region free of flies)? If the first member is primary, a mere negation (<s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>) of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) would be understood. And that [mere absence] cannot be the cause of <s>kleśas</s> and the like. Or if the last member is primary, <s>vidyā</s> itself, qualified by the absence of something, would be understood. And that is opposed to <s>kleśas</s> and the like, not their seed. For it is not reasonable that what destroys the principal should be a quality of the principal. And postulating an irregularity for the purpose of not destroying the nature of <s>vidyā</s> would be unreasonable. Therefore, the negative particle is [to be understood as expressing] the alteration [of vidyā], or as what is prohibited — namely, the [false knowledge]. If the other meaning is primary, then <s>avidyā</s> would be a cognition in which <s>vidyā</s> is absent. And that [mere absence of vidyā] alone cannot be the seed of <s>kleśas</s> and the like, since even one who has attained cessation preceded by <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative discernment) would likewise be so [afflicted]. Therefore, in every way, <s>avidyā</s> cannot be the root of <s>kleśas</s> and the like — hence he says: 'And of that,' etc. 'The being of an entity' (<s>vastutvam</s>) means the real nature of the entity, its thingness. By this, it is not a mere negation (<s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>); nor is <s>avidyā</s> just <s>vidyā</s> [itself], nor a cognition qualified by the absence of that [vidyā]; but rather, <s>avidyā</s> is erroneous knowledge contrary to <s>vidyā</s> — thus it is stated. For the connection between word and meaning depends on convention. And in the world, even when the negative particle is one in which the last member is primary, because it is observed here and there to have the sense of what is contrary to the thing denoted by the last member, the usage here too is in [the sense of] what is contrary to that — such is the purport. He analyzes the example: 'Just as "non-friend",' etc. [It is] not the absence of a friend, nor a mere friend — following this, it must be said: some other entity, namely an enemy, which is contrary to that [friend]. 'Likewise, "non-hoofprint"' — not the absence of a hoofprint, nor a mere hoofprint, but rather: an extensive space contrary to a hoofprint — some other entity different from both, namely the absence and the hoofprint. He applies it to the illustrated meaning: 'Thus,' etc. (2.5)

<s>Avidyā</s> is the perception of the eternal, the pure, the pleasant, and the self in what is non-eternal, impure, painful, and non-self. The qualifying attribute serving [the illustration of] non-eternality: 'effect,' etc. Some, regarding the elements as eternal and desiring that nature,

children.text: dṛgdarśanaśaktyor ekātmatevāsmitā //2.6//
children.translated_text: <s>Asmitā</s> (egoism) is, as it were, the identity of the power of seeing and the power of sight. (2.6)

children.text:
avidyām uktvā tasyāḥ kāryam asmitāṃ rāgādivārṣiṣṭhām āha --- dṛgdarśanaśaktyor
	  ekātmatevāsmitā/ dṛk ca darśanaṃ ca te eva śaktī tayor ātmānātmanor anātmany
	  ātmajñānalakṣaṇāvidyāpāditā yaikātmateva na tu paramārthata ekātmatā sāsmitā/
	  dṛgdarśanayor iti vaktavye tayor bhoktṛbhogyayor yogyatālakṣaṇaṃ saṃbandhaṃ darśayituṃ
	  śaktigrahaṇam/ sūtraṃ vivṛṇoti --- puruṣa iti/ nanv anayor abhedapratīter abheda eva
	  kasmān na bhavati kutaś caikatvaṃ kliśnāti puruṣam ity ata āha --- bhoktṛbhogyeti/
	  bhogyaśaktir buddhir bhoktṛśaktiḥ puruṣas tayor atyantavibhaktayoḥ kuto
	  'tyantavibhaktatvam ity ata āha --- atyantāsaṃkīrṇayoḥ/ apariṇāmitvādidharmakaḥ puruṣaḥ
	  pariṇāmitvādidharmikā buddhir ity asaṃkīrṇatā/ tad anena pratīyamāno+apy abhedo na
	  pāramārthika ity uktam/ avibhāgeti kleśatvam uktam/ anvayaṃ darśayitvā vyatirekam āha
	  --- svarūpeti/ pratilambho vivekakhyātiḥ/ parasyāpy etat saṃmatam ity āha --- tad uktaṃ
	  (tathā coktaṃ) pañcaśikhena buddhita iti/ ākāraḥ svarūpaṃ sadā viśuddhiḥ, śīlam
	  audāsīnyaṃ, vidyā caitanyaṃ, buddhir aviśuddhānudāsīnā jaḍā ceti tatrātmabuddhir avidyā/
	  mohaḥ pūrvāvidyājanitaḥ saṃskāras tamo vāvidyāyās tāmasatvād iti //2.6//
children.translated_text: Having stated <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), he states its effect, <s>asmitā</s> (egoism), which is the eldest [sibling] of <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and the rest: '<s>Asmitā</s> is, as it were, the identity of the power of seeing and the power of sight.' Seeing (<s>dṛk</s>) and sight (<s>darśana</s>) — these are the two powers; the identity of these two — of the self and the non-self — as it were (<s>iva</s>), brought about by <s>avidyā</s> in the form of knowledge of the self in what is not the self — is <s>asmitā</s>, but not identity in ultimate reality. Instead of saying 'of seeing and sight,' the word 'power' (<s>śakti</s>) is used to show the relation characterized by fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) between those two, the enjoyer and the enjoyed. He elaborates the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Puruṣa</s>,' etc. Now, since there is a perception of non-difference between these two, why should there not indeed be non-difference? And how does the unity afflict <s>Puruṣa</s>? Hence he says: 'the power of the enjoyed,' etc. The power of the enjoyed is <s>buddhi</s> (intellect); the power of the enjoyer is <s>Puruṣa</s>. Of these two, which are utterly distinct — whence is this utter distinctness? Hence he says: 'absolutely unmixed.' <s>Puruṣa</s> has the properties of being non-transforming, etc.; <s>buddhi</s> has the properties of being transforming, etc. — hence they are unmixed. By this, it is stated that the non-difference that is perceived is not ultimate. 'Non-discrimination,' etc. states its nature as a <s>kleśa</s>. Having shown the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), he shows the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>): 'Of its own nature,' etc. 'Attainment' is <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative discernment). That this is agreed upon by the other [authority] too, he says: 'Thus it is stated by <s>Pañcaśikha</s>: "From buddhi,"' etc. 'Form' (<s>ākāra</s>) means essential nature; 'perpetual purity' [is its nature]; 'disposition' (<s>śīla</s>) means indifference; '<s>vidyā</s>' means consciousness. <s>Buddhi</s> is impure, non-indifferent, and inert — therein, the notion of self is <s>avidyā</s>. 'Delusion' is the <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) born from prior <s>avidyā</s>, or <s>tamas</s> (darkness), because <s>avidyā</s> is of the nature of <s>tamas</s>. (2.6)

children.text: sukhānuśayī rāgaḥ //2.7//
children.translated_text: <s>Rāga</s> (attachment) is that which accompanies pleasure as a latent tendency. (2.7)

children.text:
vivekadarśane rāgādīnāṃ vinivṛtter avidyāpāditāsmitā rāgādīnāṃ nidānam ity
	  asmitānantaraṃ rāgādīṃl lakṣayati --- sukhānuśayī rāgaḥ/ anabhijñasya smṛter abhāvāt
	  sukhābhijñasyety uktam/ smaryamāṇe sukhe rāgaḥ sukhānusmṛtipūrvakaḥ/ anubhūyamāne tu
	  sukhe nānusmṛtim apekṣate/ tatsādhane tu smaryamāṇe dṛśyamāne vā sukhānusmṛtipūrva eva
	  rāgaḥ/ dṛśyamānam api hi sukhasādhanaṃ tajjātīyasya sukhahetutāṃ smṛtvā tajjātīyatayā
	  vāsya
sukhahetutvam anumāyecchati/ anuśayipadārtham āha --- ya iti //2.7//
children.translated_text: infers its pleasure-causing nature by [recognizing] its type, and desires it. He explains the meaning of the term '<s>anuśayin</s>' (following upon) — 'that which,' etc. //2.7//

Since, upon the vision of discrimination, attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest are eradicated, and since <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness) produced by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the root cause of attachment and the rest, after <s>asmitā</s> he defines attachment and the rest — '<s>Rāga</s> (attachment) follows upon pleasure (<s>sukha</s>).' 'Of one who has experienced [pleasure]' — because for one who has not experienced it, there is no memory [of it]; hence [the sūtra says] 'of one who has experienced pleasure.' When pleasure is being remembered, attachment is preceded by the recollection of pleasure. But when pleasure is being directly experienced, [attachment] does not require recollection. However, when the means to pleasure is either remembered or perceived, attachment is indeed preceded by the recollection of pleasure. For even when the means to pleasure is directly perceived, one either remembers that things of that type are causes of pleasure, or

children.text: duḥkhānuśayī dveṣaḥ //2.8//
children.translated_text: '<s>Dveṣa</s> (aversion) follows upon pain (<s>duḥkha</s>).' //2.8//

children.text:
duḥkhānuśayī dveṣaḥ/ duḥkhābhijñasyeti pūrvavad vyākhyeyam/ anuśayipadārtham āha ---
	  yaḥ pratigha iti/ pratihantīti pratighaḥ/ etad eva paryāyair vivṛṇoti --- manyur iti //2.8//
children.translated_text: 'Aversion follows upon pain.' 'Of one who has experienced pain' — this should be explained as before [i.e., as in the case of attachment]. He explains the meaning of the term '<s>anuśayin</s>' — 'that which is <s>pratigha</s> (hostility).' '<s>Pratigha</s>' is that which strikes back (<s>pratihanti</s>). He elaborates this very [meaning] with synonyms — '<s>manyu</s>' (anger), etc. //2.8//

children.text: svarasavāhī viduṣo+api tathā rūḍho+abhiniveśaḥ //2.9//
children.translated_text: '<s>Abhiniveśa</s> (the will-to-live), flowing by its own momentum (<s>svarasavāhin</s>), is firmly established (<s>rūḍha</s>) even in the wise (<s>viduṣa</s>).' //2.9//

children.text:
svarasavāhī viduṣo+api tathā rūḍho+abhiniveśaḥ/ abhiniveśapadārthaṃ vyācaṣṭe ---
	  sarvasya pāṇina iti/ iyam ātmāśīr ātmani prārthanā mā na bhūvaṃ mābhāvī bhūvaṃ bhūyāsaṃ
	  jīvyāsam iti/ na cānanubhūtamaraṇadharmakasya, ananubhūto maraṇadharmo yena jantunā na
	  tasyaiṣā bhavaty ātmāśīr abhiniveśo maraṇabhayam/ prasaṅgato janmāntaraṃ pratyācakṣāṇaṃ
	  nāstikaṃ nirākaroti --- etayā ceti/ pratyuditasya śarīrasya dhriyamāṇatvāt
	  pūrvajanmānubhavaḥ pratīyate/ nikāyaviśiṣṭābhir apūrvābhir dehendriyabuddhivedanābhir
	  abhisaṃbandho janma tasyānubhavaḥ prāptiḥ sā pratīyate katham ity ata āha --- sa cāyam
	  abhiniveśaḥ/ ardhoktāv evāsya kleśatvam āha --- kleśa iti/ ayam ahitakarmādinā jantūn
	  kliśnāti duḥkhākarotīti kleśaḥ/ vaktum upakrāntaṃ parisamāpayati --- svarasavāhīti/
	  svabhāvena vāsanārūpeṇa vahanaśīlo na punar āgantukaḥ/ kṛmer api jātamātrasya
	  duḥkhabahulasya nikṛṣṭatamacaitanyasyānāgantukatve hetum āha --- pratyakṣānumānāgamaiḥ
	  pratyudite janmany asaṃbhāvito 'saṃpādito maraṇatrāsa ucchedadṛṣṭyātmakaḥ
	  pūrvajanmānubhūtaṃ maraṇaduḥkham anumāpayati/ ayam abhisaṃdhiḥ --- jātamātra eva hi
	  bālako

mārakavastudarśanād vepamānaḥ kampaviśeṣād anumitamaraṇapratyāsattis
	  tato bibhyad upalabhyate/ duḥkhād duḥkhahetoś ca bhayaṃ dṛṣṭam/ na cāsmiñ janmany anena
	  maraṇam anubhūtam anumitaṃ śrutaṃ vā, prāg evāsya duḥkhatvaṃ taddhetutvaṃ vāvagamyeta,
	  tasmāt tasya tathābhūtasya smṛtiḥ pariśiṣyate/ na ceyaṃ saṃskārād ṛte/ na cāyaṃ
	  saṃskāro+anubhavaṃ vinā/ na cāsmiñ janmany anubhava iti prāgbhavīyaḥ pariśiṣyata ity
	  āsīt pūrvajanmasaṃbandha iti/ tathāpadaṃ yathāpadam ākāṅkṣatīty arthaprāpte yathāpade
	  sati yādṛśo vākyārtho bhavati tādṛśaṃ darśayati --- yathā cāyam iti/ atyantamūḍheṣu
	  mandatamacaitanyeṣu/ vidvattāṃ darśayati --- vijñātapūrvāparāntasya/ antaḥ koṭiḥ/
	  puruṣasya hi pūrvā koṭiḥ saṃsāra uttarā ca kaivalyaṃ saiva vijñātā śrutānumānābhyāṃ yena
	  sa tathoktaḥ/ so+ayaṃ maraṇatrāsa ā kṛmer ā ca viduṣo rūḍhaḥ prasiddha iti/ nanv aviduṣo
	  bhavatu maraṇatrāso viduṣas tu na saṃbhavati vidyayonmūlitatvāt/ anunmūlane vā syād
	  atyantasattvam ity āśayavān pṛcchati --- kasmād iti/ uttaram āha --- samānā hīti/ na
	  saṃprajñātavān vidvān api tu śrutānumitaviveka iti bhāvaḥ //2.9//
children.translated_text: trembles upon seeing a death-causing object; by a particular trembling, one infers the proximity of death, and from that [the infant] is observed to be afraid. Fear is [normally] observed to arise from suffering and from the cause of suffering. But this creature has not experienced, inferred, or heard about death in this birth — much less could it have understood its suffering-nature or its causal nature. Therefore, the memory of that [prior death-experience] alone remains. And this [memory] cannot exist without a <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression). And this <s>saṃskāra</s> cannot exist without [prior] experience. And there is no such experience in this birth — therefore a prior-birth [experience] alone remains; hence there was a prior-birth connection. The word '<s>tathā</s>' (thus/similarly) [in the sūtra] calls for '<s>yathā</s>' (just as); and when the '<s>yathā</s>'-clause is supplied, he shows what kind of sentence-meaning results — 'And just as this,' etc. 'In the utterly deluded, of the most feeble consciousness.' He shows the learned [quality] — 'of one who has known the prior and latter ends.' 'End' (<s>anta</s>) means limit. For <s>Puruṣa</s>, the prior limit is <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) and the latter limit is <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation); one who has known both through scripture and inference is so called. This fear of death is established (<s>rūḍha</s>) from the worm up to the wise — such is the meaning. [Objection:] Let there be fear of death for the ignorant, but not for the wise, since it has been uprooted by knowledge. Or if not uprooted, it would exist eternally. With this in mind, he asks — 'why?' etc. The answer — 'for the same [nature],' etc. The wise [here] is not one who has attained <s>saṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi], but rather one with discrimination known through scripture and inference — such is the purport. //2.9//

'<s>Abhiniveśa</s>, flowing by its own momentum, is firmly established even in the wise.' He explains the meaning of the term '<s>abhiniveśa</s>' — 'of every living being,' etc. This is the self-blessing (<s>ātmāśīḥ</s>), the prayer regarding oneself: 'May I not cease to exist! May I not become non-existent! May I continue to be! May I live!' And this [self-blessing] cannot belong to one who has not experienced the nature of death — for a being who has not experienced the nature of death does not have this self-blessing, this <s>abhiniveśa</s> [which is] the fear of death (<s>maraṇabhaya</s>). Incidentally, he refutes the materialist (<s>nāstika</s>) who denies other births — 'and by this,' etc. The experience of prior births is inferred from the fact that the arisen body is sustained. Birth (<s>janma</s>) is the connection with particular [sets of] body, sense organs, intellect, and sensations; the experience of that — its attainment — is inferred. How? Hence he says — 'and this <s>abhiniveśa</s>.' Having stated half [the explanation], he declares its <s>kleśa</s>-nature — '<s>kleśa</s>,' etc. This [abhiniveśa] afflicts beings through harmful actions and the like, causing suffering — hence [it is] a <s>kleśa</s>. He concludes what was begun to be stated — 'flowing by its own momentum' — flowing by its own nature in the form of <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression), not adventitious. Even for a worm, just born, full of suffering, of the most inferior consciousness — he gives the reason for its non-adventitious nature — 'by perception, inference, and scripture': the fear of death in this birth, which is not established, not produced, by perception, inference, or scripture — being of the nature of the annihilationist view (<s>ucchedadṛṣṭi</s>) — infers [i.e., leads one to infer] the suffering of death experienced in a prior birth. The purport is this: even a newborn infant

children.text: te pratiprasavaheyāḥ sūkṣmāḥ //2.10//
children.translated_text: 'These, in their subtle (<s>sūkṣma</s>) [form], are to be abandoned by involution (<s>pratiprasava</s>).' //2.10//

children.text:
tad evaṃ kleśā lakṣitās teṣāṃ ca heyānāṃ prasuptatanuvicchinnodārarūpatayā
	  catasro+avasthā darśitāḥ/ kasmāt punaḥ pañcamī kleśāvasthā dagdhabījabhāvatayā sūkṣmā na
	  sūtrakāreṇa kathitety ata āha --- te pratiprasavaheyāḥ sūkṣmāḥ/ yat kila
	  puruṣaprayatnagocaras tad upadiśyate/ na ca sūkṣmāvasthāhānaṃ prayatnagocaraḥ kiṃ tu
	  pratiprasavena kāryasya cittasyāsmitālakṣaṇakāraṇabhāvāpattyā hātavyeti/ vyācaṣṭe --- ta
	  iti/ sugamam //2.10//
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>kleśas</s> have been defined, and their four states — dormant (<s>prasupta</s>), attenuated (<s>tanu</s>), interrupted (<s>vicchinna</s>), and active (<s>udāra</s>) — have been shown. Why then does the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the sūtras) not mention a fifth state of the <s>kleśas</s> — the subtle one, of burnt-seed nature? Hence he says — 'These, in their subtle form, are to be abandoned by involution.' What is within the scope of human effort is taught [by the sūtrakāra]. The abandonment of the subtle state is not within the scope of effort; rather, [it is] to be abandoned through <s>pratiprasava</s> (involution) — by the reversion of the effect, the mind, into its cause, the <s>asmitā</s>-characterized state. He explains — 'those,' etc. Easy to understand. //2.10//

children.text: dhyānaheyās tadvṛttayaḥ //2.11//
children.translated_text: 'Their modifications (<s>vṛttis</s>) are to be abandoned by meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>).' //2.11//

children.text:
atha kriyāyogatanūkṛtānāṃ kleśānāṃ kiṃviṣayāt puruṣaprayatnād dhānam ity ata āha ---
	  sthitānāṃ tu bījabhāvopagatānām iti vandhyebhyo vyavacchinatti/ sūtraṃ paṭhati ---

dhyānaheyās tadvṛttayaḥ/ vyācaṣṭe --- kleśānām iti/ kriyāyogatanūkṛtā api hi
	  pratiprasavahetubhāvena kāryataḥ svarūpataś ca śakyā ucchettum iti sthūlā uktāḥ/
	  puruṣaprayatnasya prasaṃkhyānagocarasyāvadhim āha --- yāvad iti/ sūkṣmīkṛtā iti vivṛṇoti
	  --- dagdheti/ atraiva dṛṣṭāntam āha --- yathā vastrāṇām iti/ yatnena kṣālanādinopāyena
	  kṣārasaṃyogādinā/ sthūlasūkṣmamātratayā dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikayoḥ sāmyaṃ na punaḥ
	  prayatnāpaneyatayā pratiprasavaheyeṣu tadasaṃbhavāt/ svalpaḥ pratipakṣa ucchedahetur
	  yāsāṃ tās tathoktāḥ/ mahān pratipakṣa ucchedahetur yāsāṃ tās tathoktāḥ/ pratiprasavasya
	  cādhastāt prasaṃkhyānam ity avaratayā svalpatvam uktam //2.11//
children.translated_text: 'Their modifications are to be abandoned by meditation.' He explains — 'of the <s>kleśas</s>,' etc. Even <s>kleśas</s> attenuated by <s>kriyāyoga</s> can be cut off both in their effects and in their essential nature through the cause of <s>pratiprasava</s> (involution) — hence they are called 'gross.' He states the limit of personal effort, which has <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (discernment) as its scope — 'up to,' etc. He elaborates 'made subtle' (<s>sūkṣmīkṛtā</s>) — 'burnt,' etc. He gives an illustration — 'just as garments,' etc. 'By effort' means by washing and similar methods, through combination with alkali and the like. The similarity between the illustration and the illustrated is only in terms of gross and subtle degrees, not in terms of removability by effort — since for those [kleśas] to be abandoned by <s>pratiprasava</s>, that [removability by effort] is impossible. 'Those whose cause of destruction is a small counteragent' are so called; 'those whose cause of destruction is a great counteragent' are so called. And since <s>pratiprasava</s> is below <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> [in rank], 'smallness' is stated by way of inferiority. //2.11//

Now, for the <s>kleśas</s> that have been attenuated by <s>kriyāyoga</s> (the yoga of action), through what kind of personal effort directed to what object are they to be abandoned? Hence he says — 'But of those established in seed-state' — distinguishing them from the barren [i.e., those of burnt-seed nature]. He recites the <s>sūtra</s> —

children.text: kleśamūlaḥ karmāśayo dṛṣṭādṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ //2.12//
children.translated_text: 'The repository of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāśaya</s>), rooted in the <s>kleśas</s>, is to be experienced in seen [present] or unseen [future] births.' //2.12//

children.text:
syād etaj jātyāyurbhogahetavaḥ puruṣaṃ kliśnantaḥ kleśāḥ karmāśayaś ca tathā, na tv
	  avidyādayas tat katham avidyādayaḥ kleśā ity ata āha --- kleśamūlaḥ karmāśayo
	  dṛṣṭādṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ/ kleśā mūlaṃ yasyotpāde ca kāryakaraṇe ca sa tathoktaḥ/ etad
	  uktaṃ bhavati --- avidyādimūlo hi karmāśayo jātyāyurbhogahetur ity avidyādayo 'pi
	  taddhetavo+ataḥ kleśā iti/ vyācaṣṭe --- tatreti/ āśerate sāṃsārikāḥ puruṣā asminn ity
	  āśayaḥ karmaṇām āśayo dharmādharmau/ kāmāt kāmyakarmapravṛttau svargādihetur dharmo
	  bhavati/ evaṃ lobhāt paradravyāpahārādāv adharmaḥ/ mohād adharme hiṃsādau dharmabuddheḥ
	  pravartamānasyādharma eva/ na tv asti mohajo dharmaḥ/ asti krodhajo dharmaḥ/ tadyathā
	  dhruvasya janakāpamānajanmanaḥ krodhāt tajjigīṣayā cittena karmāśayena
	  puṇyenāntarikṣalokavāsinām uparisthānam/ adharmas tu krodhajo brahmavadhādijanmā
	  prasiddha

eva bhūtānām/ tasya dvaividhyam āha --- sa dṛṣṭajanmeti/
	  dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyam āha --- tīvrasaṃvegeneti/ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ dṛṣṭāntāv āha --- yathā
	  nandīśvara iti/ tatra nārakāṇām iti/ yena karmāśayena kumbhīpākādayo narakabhedāḥ
	  prāpyante tatkāriṇo nārakās teṣāṃ nāsti dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ karmāśayaḥ/ na hi
	  manuṣyaśarīreṇa tatpariṇāmabhedena vā sā tādṛśī vatsarasahasrādinirantaropabhogyā vedanā
	  saṃbhavatīti/ śeṣaṃ sugamam //2.12//
children.translated_text: indeed among beings. He states its twofold [classification] — 'that [is to be experienced] in the seen [present] birth,' etc. He explains what is to be experienced in the present birth (<s>dṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s>) — 'with intense impulse,' etc. He gives illustrations in due order — 'as <s>Nandīśvara</s>,' etc. 'Therein, of those in hell' — the <s>karmāśaya</s> by which the divisions of hell such as <s>Kumbhīpāka</s> and the rest are reached — those who perform such [actions] are the hell-beings; they do not have a <s>karmāśaya</s> to be experienced in the present birth. For with a human body, or with a particular modification thereof, such suffering — to be experienced uninterruptedly for thousands of years — is not possible. The rest is easy to understand. //2.12//

One might think: birth (<s>jāti</s>), lifespan (<s>āyus</s>), and enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) — [these], afflicting <s>Puruṣa</s>, are <s>kleśas</s>; and <s>karmāśaya</s> likewise [afflicts]. But then, how are <s>avidyā</s> and the rest specifically <s>kleśas</s>? Hence he says — 'The repository of <s>karma</s>, rooted in the <s>kleśas</s>, is to be experienced in seen or unseen births.' The <s>kleśas</s> are the root of the <s>karmāśaya</s>, both in its arising and in its coming to fruition — [hence] it is so called. This amounts to saying: since <s>karmāśaya</s>, rooted in <s>avidyā</s> and the rest, is the cause of birth, lifespan, and enjoyment, <s>avidyā</s> and the rest are also causes thereof — hence [they are called] <s>kleśas</s>. He explains — 'therein,' etc. '<s>Āśaya</s>' (repository) is that in which <s>saṃsāric</s> (transmigrating) beings rest — the repository of <s>karmas</s>, i.e., <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit). From desire (<s>kāma</s>), engagement in optional (<s>kāmya</s>) rites produces <s>dharma</s> leading to heaven and the like. Likewise from greed (<s>lobha</s>), theft of others' property and the like produces <s>adharma</s>. From delusion (<s>moha</s>), when one engages in harmful acts like violence, thinking them to be <s>dharma</s> — that is <s>adharma</s> alone. But there is no <s>dharma</s> born from delusion. There is, however, <s>dharma</s> born from anger (<s>krodha</s>) — as in the case of <s>Dhruva</s>, whose anger, born from the insult by his father <s>Janaka</s>, with the aspiration to conquer [his rivals], through the mental <s>karmāśaya</s> of merit, [led to] a station above the inhabitants of the intermediate world. But <s>adharma</s> born from anger, such as that arising from the slaying of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the like, is well known

children.text: sati mūle tadvipāko jātyāyurbhogāḥ //2.13//
children.translated_text: 'When the root (<s>mūla</s>) exists, the fruition (<s>vipāka</s>) of that [<s>karmāśaya</s> consists of] birth (<s>jāti</s>), lifespan (<s>āyus</s>), and enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>).' //2.13//

children.text:
syād etad avidyāmūlatve karmāśayasya vidyotpāde saty avidyāvināśān mā nāma
	  karmāśayāntaraṃ caiṣīt/ prācāṃ tu karmāśayānām anādibhavaparamparāsaṃcitānām
	  asaṃkhyātānām aniyatavipākakālānāṃ bhogena kṣapayitum aśakyatvād aśakyocchedaḥ saṃsāraḥ
	  syād ity ata āha --- sati mūle tadvipāko jātyāyurbhogāḥ/ etad uktaṃ bhavati ---
	  sukhaduḥkhaphalo hi karmāśayas tādarthyena tannāntarīyakatayā janmāyuṣī api prasūte/
	  sukhaduḥkhe ca rāgadveṣānuṣakte tadavinirbhāgavartinī tadabhāve na bhavataḥ/ na cāsti
	  saṃbhavo na ca tatra yas tuṣyati vodvijate vā tac ca tasya sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ veti/ tad
	  iyam ātmabhūmiḥ kleśasalilāvasiktā karmaphalaprasavakṣetram ity asti kleśānāṃ
	  phalopajanane+api karmāśayasahakāriteti kleśasamucchede sahakārivaikalyāt sann apy
	  ananto+apy aniyatavipākakālo+api prasaṃkhyānadagdhabījabhāvo na phalāya kalpata iti/
	  uktam arthaṃ bhāṣyam eva dyotayati

--- satsv iti/ atraiva dṛṣṭāntam āha ---
	  yathā tuṣeti/ satuṣā api dagdhabījabhāvāḥ svedādibhiḥ/ dārṣṭāntike yojayati --- tatheti/
	  nanu na kleśāḥ śakyā apanetuṃ na hi satām apanaya ity ata āha --- na
	  prasaṃkhyānadagdhakleśabījabhāva iti/ vipākasya traividhyam āha --- sa ceti/ vipacyate
	  sādhyate karmabhir iti vipākaḥ/ karmaikatvaṃ dhruvaṃ kṛtvā janmaikatvānekatvagocarā
	  prathamā vicāraṇā/ dvitīyā tu karmānekatvaṃ dhruvaṃ kṛtvā janmaikatvānekatvagocarā/ tad
	  evaṃ catvāro vikalpāḥ/ tatra prathamaṃ vikalpam apākaroti --- na tāvad ekaṃ karmaikasya
	  janmanaḥ kāraṇam/ pṛcchati --- kasmād iti/ uttaram --- anādikālaikaikajanmapracitasyāta
	  evāsaṃkhyeyasyaikaikajanmakṣapitād ekaikasmāt karmaṇo 'vaśiṣṭasya karmaṇaḥ sāṃpratikasya
	  ca phalakramānigamād anāśvāso lokasya prasaktaḥ sa cāniṣṭa iti/ etad uktaṃ bhavati ---
	  karmakṣayasya viralatvāt tadutpattibāhulyāc cānyonyasaṃpīḍitāḥ karmāśayā
	  nirantarotpattayo nirucchvāsāḥ svavipākaṃ pratīti na phalakramaḥ śakyo 'vadhārayituṃ
	  prekṣāvatety anāśvāsaḥ puṇyānuṣṭhānaṃ prati prasakta iti/ dvitīyaṃ vikalpaṃ nirākaroti
	  --- na caikaṃ karmānekasya janmanaḥ kāraṇam/ pṛcchati --- kasmād iti/ uttaram ---
	  anekasmiñ janmany āhitam ekaikam eva karmānekasya janmalakṣaṇasya vipākasya nimittam ity
	  avaśiṣṭasya vipākakālābhāvaḥ prasaktaḥ sa cāpy aniṣṭaḥ karmavaiphalyena
	  tadananuṣṭhānaprasaṅgāt/ yadaikajanmasamucchedye karmaṇy ekasmin phalakramāniyamād
	  anāśvāsas tadā kaiva kathā bahujanmasamuccedye karmaṇy ekasmiṃs tatra hy avasarābhāvād
	  vipākakālābhāva eva sāṃpratikasyeti
children.translated_text: 'When they exist' — and here he gives an illustration: 'Just as husked [rice]' — even husked [rice grains], when their seeds have been burned by steaming and the like [cannot sprout]. He applies it to the illustrated case: 'Similarly.' Now, [one might object:] the <s>kleśas</s> cannot be removed, for there is no removal of what exists — therefore he says: 'Not for one whose <s>kleśa</s>-seeds have been burned by <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (discernment).' He states the threefold nature of <s>vipāka</s> (fruition): 'And that.' <s>Vipāka</s> means what is brought about, accomplished by <s>karmas</s>. The first inquiry, taking the oneness of <s>karma</s> as fixed, concerns whether birth is one or many. The second, taking the multiplicity of <s>karma</s> as fixed, concerns whether birth is one or many. Thus there are four alternatives. Among these, he refutes the first alternative: 'A single <s>karma</s> is not the cause of a single birth.' He asks: 'Why?' The answer: because the <s>karma</s> accumulated in each single birth since beginningless time, being therefore innumerable, with each single birth exhausting [only some] — from the remaining <s>karma</s> and the present [<s>karma</s>], since the sequence of fruition cannot be ascertained, there would follow a lack of assurance for people, and that is undesirable. What is being said is this: because the exhaustion of <s>karma</s> is rare and its production is abundant, the <s>karmāśayas</s>, pressing upon one another, arising without interruption and without respite, [rush] toward their own fruition — thus the sequence of fruition cannot be determined by the discerning, and there follows a lack of assurance regarding the performance of meritorious acts. He refutes the second alternative: 'Nor is a single <s>karma</s> the cause of multiple births.' He asks: 'Why?' The answer: if each single <s>karma</s> deposited across many births were the cause of fruition characterized as multiple births, then there would follow an absence of time for fruition of the remaining [<s>karma</s>], and that too is undesirable, because it would entail the fruitlessness of <s>karma</s> and consequently the failure to perform it. When there is a lack of assurance due to the indeterminacy of the sequence of fruition regarding a single <s>karma</s> that is to be eradicated in one lifetime, what need even to speak of a single <s>karma</s> to be eradicated over many lifetimes? For in that case, due to the absence of opportunity, there would simply be no time for the fruition of the present [<s>karma</s>] —

children.text:
bhāvaḥ/ tṛtīyaṃ vikalpaṃ nirākaroti ---
	  na cānekaṃ karmānekasya janmanaḥ kāraṇam/ tatra hetum āha --- tad anekaṃ janma yugapan
	  na saṃbhavaty ayogina iti krameṇa vācyam/ yadi hi karmasahasraṃ yugapaj janmasahasraṃ
	  prasuvīta tata eva karmasahasraprakṣayād avaśiṣṭasya vipākakālaḥ phalakramaniyamaś ca
	  syātām/ na hy asti janmanāṃ yaugapadyam/ evam eva prathamapakṣoktaṃ dūṣaṇam ity arthaḥ/
	  tad evaṃ pakṣatraye nirākṛte pāriśeṣyād anekaṃ karmaikasya janmanaḥ kāraṇam iti pakṣo
	  vyavatiṣṭhata ity āha --- tasmāj janmeti/ janma ca prāyaṇaṃ ca janmaprāyaṇe tayor
	  antaraṃ madhyaṃ tasmin vicitrasukhaduḥkhaphalopahāreṇa vicitraḥ, yad atyantam udbhūtam
	  anantaram eva phalaṃ dāsyati tat pradhānaṃ, yat tu kiṃcid vilambena tad upasarjanaṃ,
	  prāyaṇaṃ maraṇaṃ tenābhivyaktaḥ svakāryārambhaṇābhimukham upanīta ekapraghaṭṭakena
	  yugapat saṃmūrchito janmādilakṣaṇe kārye kartavya ekalolībhāvam āpanna ekam eva janma
	  karoti nānekam/ tac ca janma manuṣyādibhāvas tenaiva karmaṇā labdhāyuṣkaṃ kālabhedān
	  niyatajīvitaṃ bhavati/ tasminn āyuṣi tenaiva karmaṇā bhogaḥ sukhaduḥkhasākṣātkāraḥ
	  svasaṃbandhitayā saṃpadyata iti/ tasmād asau karmāśayo jātyāyurbhogahetutvāt trivipāko
	  'bhidhīyate/ autsargikam upasaṃharati --- ata ekabhavikaḥ karmāśaya ukta iti/ eko bhava
	  ekabhavaḥ/ "pūrvakāla-"
children.translated_text: this is the meaning. He refutes the third alternative: 'Nor is multiple <s>karma</s> the cause of multiple births.' There he states the reason: 'Those multiple births cannot occur simultaneously for a non-<s>yogin</s>' — [this] is to be stated as [occurring] in sequence. For if a thousand <s>karmas</s> were to simultaneously produce a thousand births, then by the exhaustion of those thousand <s>karmas</s>, there would be a time for the fruition of the remaining [<s>karma</s>] and a fixed sequence of fruition. But there is no simultaneity of births — thus the same objection stated in the first alternative [applies here too], this is the meaning. Thus, with three alternatives refuted, by the method of elimination, the alternative that multiple <s>karmas</s> are the cause of a single birth stands firm — therefore he says: 'Hence, birth.' Both birth and death [constitute] the birth-and-death [pair]; the interval between them is the middle, which is varied by the offering of diverse fruits of pleasure and pain. That [<s>karma</s>] which has most prominently arisen and will give its fruit immediately is the principal one; that which [gives fruit] with some delay is the subordinate one. Death — by that [moment], made manifest, brought to face the commencement of its own effect, coalesced simultaneously in one surge, having attained a state of fusion, produces one single birth, not many. And that birth — [i.e.,] the state of being human and so forth — by that very <s>karma</s> has a lifespan obtained, a life determined by divisions of time. During that lifespan, by that very <s>karma</s>, <s>bhoga</s> (experience) — the direct realization of pleasure and pain — is accomplished as belonging to oneself. Therefore, that <s>karmāśaya</s>, because it causes <s>jāti</s> (birth), <s>āyus</s> (lifespan), and <s>bhoga</s> (experience), is called 'having threefold fruition.' He concludes with the general rule: 'Therefore, the <s>karmāśaya</s> is said to pertain to a single existence.' One existence is <s>ekabhava</s> —

'<s>Aikabhavika</s>' [is formed as]: one who has a single existence — the <s>matvarthīya</s> suffix <s>ṭhan</s> [is added]. In some readings it is '<s>aikabhavika</s>'; there the suffix <s>ṭhak</s> is applied to the word <s>ekabhava</s> in the sense of existence. The meaning is: whose coming-into-being is delimited by a single birth. Thus, having stated the threefold fruition of the general case pertaining to a single existence, he distinguishes the threefold fruition of <s>karma</s> that is to be experienced in the present life (<s>dṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s>) — 'Visible [in this life].' For <s>Nandīśvara</s>, whose lifespan was delimited to eight years,

manuṣyajanmanas tīvrasaṃvegādhimātropāyajanmā puṇyabheda āyurbhogahetutvād

children.translated_text: whose meritorious distinction, born of intense fervor and the highest means, [applied to] a human birth — is of twofold fruition (<s>dvivipāka</s>), being the cause of lifespan and experience. But for <s>Nahuṣa</s>, since his lifespan was ordained by the very same <s>karma</s> that caused <s>Agastya</s>'s attainment of <s>Indra</s>'s seat through the demerit of the heel-blow conflict, his demeritorious distinction is the cause of experience alone. Now, [one might ask:] just as the <s>karmāśaya</s> pertains to a single existence, so too do the <s>kleśa</s>-<s>vāsanās</s> (affliction-traces) and the <s>karmavipākānubhava</s>-<s>vāsanās</s> (traces of karmic fruition experience) favorable to experience — and thus a human being who has obtained an animal birth would not enjoy what is proper to that species? Therefore he says: 'The <s>kleśas</s>.' 'Coalesced' means having attained a state of fusion. He states the essential nature of <s>vāsanā</s> (residual trace) as distinguished from <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit): 'Those <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions).' He prepares the ground for occasionally overriding the general rule of pertaining to a single existence: 'But that which.' By the word 'but' he distinguishes [this] from <s>vāsanā</s>. This rule of pertaining to a single existence applies only to <s>dṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s> (karma experienced in the present life), which has determinate fruition, but not to <s>adṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s> (karma experienced in a future unseen life). Of what kind? Of indeterminate fruition. He asks for the reason: 'Why?' He states the reason: 'For that which.' He states the first course: 'Of what has been done.' He states the second: 'The principal.' He states the third: 'The determined.' Among these, he analyzes the first: 'There, of what has been done.' Apart from the <s>karmas</s> of the renunciant, which are neither white nor black, there are only three [kinds of] <s>karmas</s>: black, black-and-white, and white. Here, the white <s>karmāśaya</s>, accomplished through <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), and the like, when it has arisen, destroys the black [<s>karma</s>] that has not yet given its fruit, and without distinction also [destroys] the black portion of the mixed [<s>karma</s>] —

children.translated_text: — thus it should be understood. At this very point, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Lord) cites the sacred tradition — 'where this,' etc. 'Two by two indeed the actions — the dark, the dark-and-white — it removes': this is the syntactic connection. The distributive repetition indicates abundance. Of whom? Hence he says — 'of the sinful person.' Who removes them? Hence he says — 'a single mass of meritorious [karma].' Because the collective [effect] is accomplished by the collective [cause]. By this, the white <s>karmāśaya</s> (repository of action) is stated as the third kind. What is stated amounts to this: such is the white <s>karmāśaya</s>, accomplished by means free from harming others and the like, that even being single, it removes the dark and the dark-and-white <s>karmāśayas</s> that are completely opposed [to it], though they be numerous. Therefore, 'desire it!' — the <s>ātmanepada</s> ending is Vedic usage. The rest is clear. And here it is solely the arising of white <s>karma</s> that has such great power that it causes the absence of the others, not [that this arises] from the suffering born of self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) and the like. For it is not that [white karma] opposes all suffering whatsoever, but rather it opposes the suffering that is its own effect. Nor is the suffering born from self-study and the like its effect — for if it were its effect, the injunction of self-study and the like would be purposeless, since that [suffering] would arise by its own force. Or, if [that suffering] did not arise, even the Kumbhīpāka [hell] and the like could be enjoined [as meritorious]. But without such an injunction, that [suffering] would not arise — thus everything is consistent. He distinguishes the second course — the subordination: in a principal rite like the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the subsidiary element such as animal slaughter comes along with the principal. Now, the slaughter and the like have two effects: because they are enjoined as subsidiaries of the principal [rite], they contribute to [the principal]; 'one should not harm any being'

children.translated_text: is sufficient for the destruction [of that subsidiary demerit]. He asks — 'why?' The answer for the meritorious one — 'for I have much other meritorious principal <s>karma</s> established in an auxiliary capacity, from the consecration fee (<s>dīkṣaṇīya</s>) through to the final sacrificial gift (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>). Where this admixture [of demerit] is small — even in heaven, the fruit [of such a person], born from mixed merit, from heaven [eventually falls]'

One might object: given that the <s>karmāśaya</s> (repository of karma) has <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) as its root, when <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) arises and <s>avidyā</s> is destroyed, let it be that no new <s>karmāśaya</s> is sought. But since the prior <s>karmāśayas</s>, accumulated through a beginningless succession of existences, innumerable and of undetermined time of fruition, cannot be exhausted through experience, <s>saṃsāra</s> would be impossible to eradicate — therefore he states: 'When the root exists, its fruition is <s>jāti</s> (birth), <s>āyus</s> (lifespan), and <s>bhoga</s> (experience).' [YS 2.13] What is being said is this: the <s>karmāśaya</s>, whose fruit is pleasure and pain, by serving that purpose and being inseparable from it, also produces birth and lifespan. And pleasure and pain are accompanied by <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), which abide inseparably within them — in their absence, those [attachment and aversion] do not arise. For there is no possibility, nor is there anyone who rejoices or is distressed there, nor is that his pleasure or pain. Therefore, this ground of the self, irrigated by the waters of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), is the field for the production of the fruits of <s>karma</s> — thus the <s>kleśas</s> serve as auxiliary causes of the <s>karmāśaya</s> even in the generation of fruit. Therefore, upon the complete eradication of the <s>kleśas</s>, due to the deficiency of the auxiliary cause, even though [the <s>karmāśaya</s>] exists, even though it is endless, even though the time of its fruition is undetermined, having become like a seed burned by <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (discernment), it is not capable of producing fruit. The <s>bhāṣya</s> itself illuminates the stated meaning —

Now, let birth, lifespan, and experience caused by demerit be the fruits of pain and be things to be abandoned, since they are experienced as adverse. But why

Now, of what are fruitions the root, such that they too must be abandoned? Hence he says — 'They have pleasure and pain as their results, due to being caused by merit and demerit.' children.translated_text: He raises an objection — 'that which in enjoyments' and so on. We do not maintain that pleasure in sense objects constitutes happiness; rather, for persons who are satiated (or: in a state of satiation), <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) itself — the torment of minds afflicted by longing for this or that object — is a great suffering. And this [craving] does not subside without enjoyment; nor is its subsidence free from being pervaded by <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and the rest — thus it does not constitute <s>pariṇāma-duḥkhatā</s> (suffering from change): this is the meaning. From satisfaction, because of the destruction of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) as the cause, there is the quiescence of the sense organs, i.e., their non-engagement with objects — this is the meaning. He clarifies this very point through the negative method (<s>vyatireka</s>) — 'that which from restlessness' and so on. He refutes [the objection] — 'nor of the sense organs' and so on. The suffix 'an' is used in the causal sense. True, the destruction of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is blameless happiness, but its cause is not the habitual practice of enjoyment, but rather [the destruction] of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> itself, which is opposed to it. As they say —
