tāpaduḥkhatāṃ pṛcchati --- atha keti/ uttaraṃ ---
	  sarvasyeti/ sarvajanaprasiddhatvena tatsvarūpaprapañcam akṛtvā tāpaduḥkhatāpi
	  pariṇāmaduḥkhatāsamatayā prapañciteti/ saṃskāraduḥkhatāṃ pṛcchati --- keti/ uttaraṃ ---
	  sukheti/ sukhānubhavo hi saṃskāram ādhatte/ sa ca sukhasmaraṇaṃ tac ca rāgaṃ sa ca
	  manaḥkāyavacanaceṣṭāṃ sā ca puṇyāpuṇye tato vipākānubhavas tato vāsanety evam anāditeti/
	  atra ca sukhaduḥkhasaṃskārātiśayāt tatsmaraṇaṃ tasmāc ca rāgadveṣau tābhyāṃ karmāṇi
	  karmabhyo vipāka iti yojanā/ tad evaṃ duḥkhasrotaḥ prasṛtaṃ yoginam eva kliśnāti netaraṃ
	  pṛthagjanam ity āha --- evam idam anādīti/ itaraṃ tu triparvāṇas tāpā anuplavanta iti
	  saṃbandhaḥ/ ādhibhautikādhidaivikayos tāpayor bāhyatvenaikatvaṃ vivakṣitam/ citte vṛttir
	  asyā ity avidyā cittavṛttis tayā hātavya eva buddhīndriyaśarīrādau dārāpatyādau
	  cāhaṃkāramamakārānupātinam iti/ tad atra na samyagdarśanād anyat paritrāṇam astīty āha
	  --- tad evam iti/
children.translated_text: He inquires about <s>tāpa-duḥkhatā</s> (suffering from affliction) — 'now, what?' and so on. The reply — 'of all' and so on. Because it is well-known to all people, without elaborating its essential nature, <s>tāpa-duḥkhatā</s> is also elaborated in the same manner as <s>pariṇāma-duḥkhatā</s>. He inquires about <s>saṃskāra-duḥkhatā</s> (suffering from latent impressions) — 'what?' and so on. The reply — 'pleasure' and so on. For the experience of pleasure deposits a <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression); that [impression] produces the memory of pleasure; that [memory] produces <s>rāga</s> (attachment); that [attachment] produces activity of mind, body, and speech; that [activity] produces merit and demerit; from that arises the experience of fruition; from that arise <s>vāsanās</s> (latent tendencies) — thus this is beginningless. And here the construction is: from the preponderance of <s>saṃskāras</s> of pleasure and pain arises their memory; from that arise <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion); from those arise actions; from actions arises fruition. Thus this stream of suffering, having issued forth, afflicts only the <s>yogin</s>, not the ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) — so he says: 'thus this beginningless' and so on. But for the other [the ordinary person], the connection is: the three-fold afflictions overwhelm. The intention is to treat the two external afflictions — <s>ādhibhautika</s> (from beings) and <s>ādhidaivika</s> (from divine agencies) — as one, on account of their externality. <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is a mental modification (<s>cittavṛtti</s>), since it operates in the mind; through it, the sense of 'I' (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) and 'mine' (<s>mamakāra</s>) regarding the intellect, sense organs, body and the like, as well as wife, children and the like, is to be abandoned. Therefore, he says there is no protection other than right knowledge — 'thus indeed' and so on.

children.text:
tad evam aupādhikaṃ viṣayasukhasya pariṇāmataḥ
	  saṃskāratas tāpasaṃyogāc ca duḥkhatvam abhidhāya svābhāvikam ādarśayati ---
	  guṇavṛttivirodhāc ceti/ vyācaṣṭe --- prakhyāpravṛttisthitirūpā buddhirūpeṇa pariṇatā
	  guṇāḥ sattvarajastamāṃsi parasparānugrahatantrāḥ śāntaṃ sukhātmakaṃ ghoraṃ duḥkhātmakaṃ
	  mūḍhaṃ viṣādātmakam eva pratyayaṃ sukhopabhogarūpam api triguṇam ārabhante/ na ca so 'pi
	  tādṛśapratyayarūpo+asya pariṇāmaḥ sthira ity āha --- calaṃ ca guṇavṛttam iti
	  kṣiprapariṇāmi cittam uktam/ nanv ekaḥ pratyayaḥ kathaṃ
	  parasparaviruddhaśāntaghoramūḍhatvāny ekadā pratipadyata ity ata āha --- rūpātiśayā
	  vṛttyatiśayāś ca paraspareṇa virudhyante/ rūpāṇi aṣṭau bhāvā dharmādayo vṛttayaḥ
	  sukhādyās tad iha dharmeṇa vipacyamānenādharmas tādṛśo virudhyate/ evaṃ
	  jñānavairāgyaiśvaryaiḥ sukhādibhiś ca tādṛśāny eva tadviparītāni virudhyante/ sāmānyāni
	  tv asamudācaradrupāṇy atiśayaiḥ samudācaradbhiḥ sahāvirodhāt pravartanta iti/ nanu
	  gṛhṇīma etat tathāpi viṣayasukhasya kutaḥ svābhāvikī duḥkhatety ata āha --- evam eta
	  iti/ upādānābhedād upādānātmakatvāc copādeyasyāpy abheda ity arthaḥ/ tat kim idānīm
	  ātyantikam eva tādātmyaṃ tathā ca buddhivyapadeśabhedau na kalpete ity ata āha ---
	  guṇapradhāneti/ sāmānyātmanā guṇabhāvo 'tiśayātmanā ca prādhānyam/ tasmād upādhitaḥ
	  svabhāvataś ca duḥkham eva sarvaṃ vivekina iti/ duḥkhaṃ ca heyaṃ prekṣāvatā/ na ca
	  tannidānahānam antareṇa tad dheyaṃ bhavitum arhati/ na cāparijñātaṃ nidānaṃ śakyaṃ hātum
	  iti mūlanidānam asya darśayati --- tad asyeti/ duḥkhasamudāyasya prabhava utpattir yatas
	  tadbījam ity arthaḥ/ taducchedahetuṃ darśayati --- tasyāś ceti/ idānīm asya śāstrasya
	  sarvānugrahārthaṃ pravṛttasya tadvidhenaiva śāstreṇa sādṛśyaṃ darśayati ---
children.translated_text: Having thus declared the suffering-nature of pleasure in sense objects from the adventitious perspectives of change, latent impressions, and association with affliction, he shows its inherent [suffering-nature] — 'and because of the conflict of <s>guṇa</s>-activities' and so on. He explains: the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents) — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — having transformed into the form of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), whose nature is illumination (<s>prakhyā</s>), activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), and stability (<s>sthiti</s>), being mutually dependent on one another's support, produce a cognition that is tranquil (of the nature of pleasure), agitated (of the nature of pain), or deluded (of the nature of despondency) — even one whose form is the enjoyment of pleasure is [actually] constituted of the three <s>guṇas</s>. And that transformation in the form of such a cognition is not stable — so he says: 'and the activity of the <s>guṇas</s> is unstable,' meaning the mind is of rapidly changing nature. Now, how can a single cognition simultaneously assume the mutually contradictory states of being tranquil, agitated, and deluded? Therefore he says: the predominant forms and predominant activities conflict with one another. The 'forms' are the eight dispositions (<s>bhāvas</s>) such as <s>dharma</s> and the rest; the 'activities' are pleasure and the like. Here, when <s>dharma</s> is ripening, a corresponding <s>adharma</s> is opposed [to it]. Likewise, <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty), and pleasure and the like — their very opposites are opposed to them. But the generic [forms], being non-manifest, do not conflict with the predominant ones that are manifest, and so they continue to operate. Now, we accept this, but still, whence comes the inherent suffering-nature of pleasure in sense objects? Therefore he says: 'thus these' and so on. Because of the non-difference of the material cause, and because the effect has the nature of its material cause, the effect too is non-different — this is the meaning. Then is the identity absolute? And [if so,] the distinctions of intellect and designation would not be possible. Therefore he says: '<s>guṇa</s> and predominant' and so on. The state of being a [subordinate] <s>guṇa</s> [belongs to something] in its generic aspect, and predominance [belongs to it] in its specific aspect. Therefore, from the adventitious standpoint and from the standpoint of inherent nature, everything is nothing but suffering for the discriminating person. And suffering is to be avoided (<s>heya</s>) by the discerning. And that [suffering] cannot be [truly] avoided without the removal of its cause. And the cause cannot be removed without being fully understood. So he shows the root cause of this — 'of this, then' and so on. The origin, i.e., the arising, of the aggregate of suffering — that from which is its seed: this is the meaning. He shows the means for its eradication — 'and of that' and so on. Now he shows the similarity of this <s>śāstra</s> (treatise), which has been set forth for the benefit of all, with that very kind of treatise —

yatheti/ catvāro vyūhāḥ saṃkṣiptāvayavaracanā yasya tat tathoktam/ nanu duḥkhaṃ heyam
	  uktvā saṃsāraṃ heyam abhidadhataḥ kuto na virodha ity ata āha --- tatra duḥkhabahula
	  iti/ yatkṛtvāvidyā saṃsāraṃ karoti tad asyā avāntaravyāpāraṃ saṃsārahetum āha ---
	  pradhānapuruṣayor iti/ mokṣasvarūpam āha --- saṃyogasyeti/ mokṣopāyam āha --- hānopāya
	  iti/ kecit paśyanti, hātuḥ svarūpoccheda eva mokṣaḥ/ yathāhuḥ ---
children.translated_text: — 'as' and so on. That which has a condensed arrangement of parts in four divisions (<s>caturvyūha</s>) is so called. Now, having said that suffering is to be avoided, would there not be a contradiction in declaring <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) to be that which is to be avoided? Therefore he says: 'therein, abundant in suffering' and so on. That by doing which <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) produces <s>saṃsāra</s> — that intermediate operation of hers, the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, he states — 'of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self)' and so on. He states the essential nature of liberation — 'of the conjunction' and so on. He states the means of liberation — 'the means of abandonment' and so on. Some hold that liberation is the very destruction of the nature of the one who is to abandon. As they say —
The remainder is self-evident.

children.text: "pradīpasyeva nirvāṇaṃ vimokṣas tasya cetasaḥ" iti/
children.translated_text: "The liberation of that mind is like the extinguishing of a lamp."

children.text:
anye tu savāsanakleśasamucchedād viśuddhavijñānotpāda eva mokṣa ity ācakṣate tān
	  pratyāha --- tatreti/ tatra hānaṃ tāvad dūṣayati --- hāne tasyeti/ na hi prekṣāvān
	  kaścid ātmocchedāya yatate/ nanu dṛśyante tīvragadonmūlitasakalasukhāṃ duḥkhamayīm iva
	  mūrtim udvahantaḥ svocchedāya yatamānāḥ/ satyam/ kecid eva te, na tv evaṃ saṃsāriṇo
	  vividhavicitradevādyānandabhogabhāginas te 'pi ca mokṣamāṇā dṛśyante tasmād
	  apuruṣārthatvaprasakter na hātuḥ svarūpocchedo mokṣo+abhyupeyaḥ/ astu tarhi hātuḥ
	  svarūpam upādeyam ity ata āha --- upādāne ca hetuvādaḥ/ upādāne hi kāryatvenānityatve
	  sati mokṣatvād eva cyaveta/ amṛtatvaṃ hi mokṣaḥ/ nāpi viśuddho vijñānasaṃtāno bhavaty
	  amṛtaḥ/ saṃtānibhyo vyatiriktasya saṃtānasya vastusato'bhāvāt/ saṃtānināṃ cānityatvāt/
	  tasmāt tathā yatitavyaṃ yathā śāśvatavādo bhavati/ tathā ca puruṣārthatāpavargasyety āha
	  --- ubhayapratyākhyāna iti/ tasmāt svarūpāvasthānam evātmano mokṣa iti/ etad eva
	  samyagdarśanam //2.15//
children.translated_text: But others declare that liberation is the arising of pure consciousness upon the complete eradication of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) together with their latent tendencies (<s>vāsanās</s>). Against them he says: 'therein' and so on. Therein, he first refutes abandonment [as self-destruction] — 'in the abandonment of that' and so on. For no discerning person strives for the annihilation of the self. One might say: but we do see people who, with all happiness uprooted by severe disease, bearing a form that seems nothing but suffering, strive for self-destruction. True. But they are only some [exceptional cases]; the beings in <s>saṃsāra</s>, who partake of manifold and variegated enjoyments of bliss in divine and other states, are not seen seeking self-annihilation. Therefore, because of the consequent purposelessness [of liberation as self-annihilation], liberation should not be accepted as the destruction of the nature of the one who is to abandon. Let then the essential nature of the one who abandons be something to be attained — to this he says: 'and in the case of attainment, the argument of causation [applies].' For in the case of attainment, since [what is attained] would be an effect and therefore impermanent, it would fall away from being liberation. For liberation is immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>). Nor can a purified stream of consciousness be immortal, since a 'stream' (<s>saṃtāna</s>) as a real entity apart from the individual moments that constitute it does not exist, and since those individual moments are impermanent. Therefore one must strive in such a way that the eternalist position holds. And thus the purposefulness of <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) is [established] — so he says: 'the rejection of both' and so on. Therefore, liberation is nothing but the abiding in one's own essential nature (<s>svarūpāvasthāna</s>) of the Self. This alone is right knowledge (<s>samyagdarśana</s>). (2.15)

children.text: heyaṃ duḥkham anāgatam //2.16//
children.translated_text: The suffering that has not yet come is to be avoided (<s>heya</s>). (2.16)

children.text:
tad etac chāstraṃ caturvyūham ity abhidhīyate --- heyaṃ duḥkham anāgatam/ anāgatam ity
	  atītavartamāne

vyavacchinne/ tatropapattim āha --- duḥkham atītam iti/ nanu
	  vartamānam upabhujyamānaṃ na bhogenātivāhitam iti kasmān na heyam ity ata āha ---
	  vartamānaṃ ceti/ sugamam //2.16//
children.translated_text: excluded. On this point, he states the rationale — 'suffering that is past' and so on. Now, the present [suffering], being experienced, has not been exhausted through experience — so why is it not to be avoided? To this he says: 'and the present' and so on. [The rest is] easy to understand. (2.16)

That this treatise has a fourfold structure (<s>caturvyūha</s>) is thus stated — 'The suffering that has not yet come is to be avoided.' By [the word] 'not yet come' (<s>anāgata</s>), the past and present are

heyam uktaṃ tasya nidānam ucyate --- draṣṭṛdṛśyayoḥ saṃyogo heyahetuḥ/ draṣṭuḥ svarūpam
	  āha --- draṣṭeti/ citicchāyāpattir eva buddher buddhipratisaṃveditvam udāsīnasyāpi
	  puṃsaḥ/ nanv etāvatāpi buddhir evānena dṛśyeta, na dṛśyerañ śabdādayo+atyantavyavahitā
	  ity ata āha --- dṛśyā buddhisattveti/ indriyapraṇālikayā buddhau śabdādyākāreṇa
	  pariṇatāyāṃ dṛśyāyāṃ bhavanti śabdādayo+api dharmā dṛśyā ity arthaḥ/ nanu tadākārāpattyā
	  buddhiḥ śabdādyākārā bhavatu puṃsas tu buddhisaṃbandhe+abhyupagamyamāne pariṇāmitvam
	  asaṃbandhe vā kathaṃ teṣāṃ buddhisattvopārūḍhānām api śabdādīnāṃ dṛśyatvam/ na hi
	  dṛśināsaṃspṛṣṭaṃ dṛśyaṃ dṛṣṭam ity ata āha --- tad etad dṛśyam iti/ prapañcitam idam
	  asmābhiḥ prathamapāda eva yathā cityāsaṃpṛktam api buddhisattvam atyantasvacchatayā
	  citibimbodgrāhitayā samāpannacaitanyam iva śabdādy anubhavatīti/ ata eva ca
	  śabdādyākārapariṇatabuddhisattvopanītāñ śabdādīn bhuñjānaḥ svāmī bhavati draṣṭā tādṛśaṃ
	  cāsya buddhisattvaṃ svaṃ bhavati/ tad etad buddhisattvaṃ śabdādyākāravad dṛśyam
	  ayaskāntamaṇikalpaṃ puruṣasya svaṃ bhavati dṛśirūpasya svāminaḥ/ kasmāt,
	  anubhavakarmaviṣayatām āpannaṃ yataḥ/ anubhavo bhogaḥ puruṣasya karma kriyā tadviṣayatāṃ
	  bhujyamānatām āpannaṃ yasmād ataḥ svaṃ bhavati/ nanu svayaṃprakāśaṃ buddhisattvaṃ katham
	  anubhavaviṣaya ity ata āha --- anyasvarūpeṇeti/ yadi hi caitanyarūpaṃ vastuto

buddhisattvaṃ syād bhavet svayaṃprakāśaṃ kiṃ tu svaṃ caitanyād anyaj jaḍarūpaṃ tena
	  pratilabdhātmakaṃ tasmāt tadanubhavaviṣayaḥ/ nanu yasya hi yatra kiṃcid āyatate tat
	  tadadhīnam/ na ca buddhisattvasya puruṣam udāsīnaṃ prati kiṃcid āyatata iti kathaṃ
	  tattantram/ tathā ca na tasya karmety ata āha --- svatantram api parārthatvāt
	  puruṣārthatvāt paratantraṃ puruṣatantram/ nanv ayaṃ dṛgdarśanaśaktyoḥ saṃbandhaḥ
	  svābhāviko vā syān naimittiko vā/ svābhāvikatve saṃbandhinor nityatvād aśakyocchedaḥ
	  saṃbandhas tathā ca saṃsāranityatvam/ naimittikatve tu kleśakarmatadvāsanānām
	  antaḥkaraṇavṛttitayā saty antaḥkaraṇe bhāvād antaḥkaraṇasya ca tannimittatve
	  parasparāśrayaprasaṅgād anāditvasya ca sargādāv asaṃbhavād anutpāda eva saṃsārasya syāt/
	  yathoktam ---
children.translated_text: it would be self-luminous; but its own [nature] is inert (<s>jaḍa</s>), different from consciousness, and having obtained its selfhood through that [consciousness], it therefore becomes an object of its experience. Now, whatever has some dependence on something is governed by that. But <s>buddhi-sattva</s> has no dependence whatsoever on the indifferent <s>puruṣa</s> — so how is it subject to him? And thus it would not be his activity (<s>karma</s>) — to this he says: 'Though independent, because of being for the sake of another (<s>parārthatva</s>),' that is, because of being for the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> (<s>puruṣārthatva</s>), it is dependent on <s>puruṣa</s>, subject to <s>puruṣa</s>. Now, is this connection between the power of seeing (<s>dṛk</s>) and the power of what is seen (<s>darśana</s>) natural (<s>svābhāvika</s>) or occasioned (<s>naimittika</s>)? If natural, then since both relata are eternal, the connection would be impossible to sever, and thus <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) would be eternal. If occasioned, then since <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>karma</s> (actions), and their latent impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) exist as modifications of the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), and since the inner instrument depends on them as its cause, there would be the fallacy of mutual dependence (<s>parasparāśraya</s>); and since beginninglessness would be impossible at the commencement of creation, <s>saṃsāra</s> itself would never arise. As has been said —

The avoidable (<s>heya</s>) has been stated; now its cause is declared — 'The conjunction of the <s>draṣṭṛ</s> (Seer) and the <s>dṛśya</s> (Seen) is the cause of the avoidable.' He states the essential nature of the <s>draṣṭṛ</s> — '<s>draṣṭā</s>' etc. The descent of the reflection of <s>citi</s> (consciousness) upon <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is indeed <s>buddhi</s>'s capacity to be experienced — even for <s>puruṣa</s> who remains indifferent. But if by this much only <s>buddhi</s> alone would be seen by him, and sounds and other [objects] being extremely remote would not be seen — to this he says: 'Visible are the <s>buddhi-sattva</s>' etc. Through the channel of the <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs), when <s>buddhi</s> has undergone transformation into the form of sound and other [objects] and has become visible, then sounds and other properties also become visible — this is the meaning. But even granting that <s>buddhi</s> assumes the form of sound etc. through the imposition of those forms, if a connection of <s>puruṣa</s> with <s>buddhi</s> is admitted, then mutability [would follow]; or if no connection [is admitted], how can sounds and other [objects], even when mounted upon <s>buddhi-sattva</s>, be visible? For nothing untouched by the Seer can be seen as visible — to this he says: 'This visible' etc. This has been elaborated by us in the first <s>pāda</s> (chapter) itself — how <s>buddhi-sattva</s>, though not actually united with <s>citi</s> (consciousness), through its extreme transparency and its capacity to receive the reflection of <s>citi</s>, as if having attained sentience, experiences sound and other [objects]. And precisely for this reason, the <s>draṣṭṛ</s> (Seer), enjoying sounds and other [objects] presented through <s>buddhi-sattva</s> transformed into the forms of sound etc., becomes the master, and such <s>buddhi-sattva</s> becomes his own [property]. This <s>buddhi-sattva</s>, visible as having the forms of sound etc., like a lodestone, becomes the property of <s>puruṣa</s>, the master whose nature is seeing. Why? Because it has attained the status of being the object of experience-activity. Experience is <s>bhoga</s> (enjoyment); the activity (<s>karma</s>) of <s>puruṣa</s> — it has attained the status of being its object, the state of being enjoyed, and therefore it becomes his own [property]. But if <s>buddhi-sattva</s> is self-luminous, how can it be an object of experience? To this he says: 'With a nature other [than consciousness]' etc. If <s>buddhi-sattva</s> were in reality of the nature of consciousness,

children.text:
"pumān akartā yeṣāṃ tu teṣām api guṇaiḥ kriyā/ katham ādau bhavet tatra karma tāvan na
	  vidyate// mithyājñānaṃ na tatrāsti rāgadveṣādayo+api vā/ manovṛttir hi sarveṣāṃ na
	  cotpannaṃ manas tadā//"
children.translated_text: 'For <s>puruṣa</s> is not the agent; yet for those [principles], action is through the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents). How could action arise at the beginning? For there is no <s>karma</s> then; nor is there false knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>), nor attachment (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and the rest. For the mental modification (<s>manovṛtti</s>) [is the basis] of all these, and mind (<s>manas</s>) had not yet arisen then.'

children.text:
iti śaṅkām apanayati --- tayor dṛgdarśanaśaktyor anādir arthakṛtaḥ saṃyogo heyahetuḥ/
	  satyam/ na svābhāvikaḥ saṃbandho naimittikas tu/ na caivam ādimān
	  anādinimittaprabhavatayā tasyāpy anāditvāt/ kleśakarmatadvāsanāsaṃtānaś cāyam anādiḥ
	  pratisargāvasthāyāṃ ca sahāntaḥkaraṇena pradhānasāmyam upagato+api sargādau punas tādṛg
	  eva prādurbhavati varṣāpāya ivodbhijjabhedo mṛdbhāvam upagato+api punar varṣāsu
	  pūrvarūpa ity asakṛd āveditam/ prāgbhāvitayā saṃyogasyāvidyā kāraṇaṃ sthitihetutayā
	  puruṣārthaḥ kāraṇaṃ tadvaśena tasya sthites tad idam uktam arthakṛta iti/ tathā coktaṃ
	  pañcaśikhena tatsaṃyogo buddhisaṃyogaḥ sa eva hetur duḥkhasya, tasya vivarjanāt syād
	  ayam ātyantiko duḥkhapratīkāraḥ/ arthāt tadaparivarjane duḥkham ity uktaṃ bhavati/
	  tatraivātyantaprasiddhaṃ nidarśanam āha --- tadyatheti/ pādatrāṇam upānat/

syād etat/ guṇasaṃyogas tāpahetur ity ucyamāne guṇānāṃ tāpakatvam abhyupetam/ na ca
	  tapikriyāyā asty āder iva kartṛstho bhāvo yena tapyam anyan nāpekṣeta/ na cāsyās
	  tapyatayā puruṣaḥ karma tasyāpariṇāmitayā kriyājanitaphalaśālitvāyogāt/ tasmāt tapes
	  tapyavyāptasya tannivṛttau nivṛttim avagacchāmo jvalanaviraheṇeva dhūmābhāvam ity ata
	  āha --- atrāpi tāpakasyeti/ guṇānām eva tapyatāpakabhāvas tatra mṛdutvāt pādatalavat
	  sattvaṃ tapyaṃ rajas tu tīvratayā tāpakam/ pṛcchati --- kasmāt sattvam eva tapyaṃ na tu
	  puruṣaḥ/ uttaram --- tapikriyāyā iti/ tat kim idānīṃ puruṣo na tapyate/ tathā
	  cācetanasyāstu sattvasya tāpaḥ kiṃ naś chinnam ity ata āha --- darśitaviṣayatvāt sattve
	  tu tapyamāne tadākārānurodhī puruṣo+apy anutapyata iti/ darśitaviṣayatvam anutāpahetus
	  tac ca prāg vyākhyātam //2.17//
children.translated_text: One might object: when it is said that conjunction with the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents) is the cause of affliction (<s>tāpa</s>), the capacity of the <s>guṇas</s> to cause affliction is admitted. But the action of afflicting does not have an agent-inherent nature like 'beginning' by which it could do without something to be afflicted. Nor is <s>puruṣa</s> the object of this [affliction], since due to his immutability there is the impossibility of his possessing results generated by action. Therefore we understand that the cessation of affliction, which pervades the afflicted, ceases upon the cessation of that — like the absence of smoke upon the absence of fire — to this he says: 'Here too, the afflicter' etc. The afflicted-afflicter relationship belongs to the <s>guṇas</s> themselves; therein, <s>sattva</s>, being soft like the sole of the foot, is the afflicted, while <s>rajas</s>, due to its intensity, is the afflicter. He asks: why is <s>sattva</s> alone the afflicted and not <s>puruṣa</s>? The answer: 'Of the action of afflicting' etc. Then what — does <s>puruṣa</s> not suffer at all? And in that case, let the non-sentient <s>sattva</s> have its affliction — what loss is ours? To this he says: 'Because of having been shown objects, when <s>sattva</s> is afflicted, <s>puruṣa</s> too, conforming to its form, suffers sympathetically.' The having-been-shown-objects is the cause of sympathetic suffering, and that has been explained earlier. (2.17)

He removes this doubt — 'The conjunction of the two, the power of seeing and the power of what is seen, is beginningless (<s>anādi</s>), purposeful (<s>arthakṛta</s>), and is the cause of the avoidable.' True — the connection is not natural but occasioned. Yet it does not thereby have a beginning, because its cause is beginningless. The continuum of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>karma</s> (actions), and their <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) is beginningless, and even having merged along with the inner instrument into the equilibrium of <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) during dissolution, at the commencement of creation it manifests again in exactly the same form — just as varieties of plants, having merged into the state of earth during the cessation of rains, resume their former form again in the rains — this has been stated repeatedly. As a prior condition, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the cause of the conjunction; as the cause of its persistence, the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> is the cause, since it persists by virtue of that — this is what is stated by 'purposeful' (<s>arthakṛta</s>). And thus <s>Pañcaśikha</s> has said: 'That conjunction is the conjunction with <s>buddhi</s>; that alone is the cause of suffering; through its abandonment, this would be the absolute remedy for suffering.' By implication, non-abandonment of that results in suffering — this is what is stated. Therein he gives a well-known illustration — 'Just as' etc. <s>Pādatrāṇa</s> means sandal (shoe).

children.text: prakāśakriyāsthitiśīlaṃ bhūtendriyātmakaṃ bhogāpavargārthaṃ dṛśyam //2.18//
children.translated_text: The <s>dṛśya</s> (Seen) has the nature of illumination (<s>prakāśa</s>), activity (<s>kriyā</s>), and stability (<s>sthiti</s>); consists of the <s>bhūtas</s> (elements) and <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs); and serves the purpose of <s>bhoga</s> (experience) and <s>apavarga</s> (liberation). (2.18)

children.text:
prakāśakriyāsthitiśīlaṃ bhūtendriyātmakaṃ bhogāpavargārthaṃ dṛśyam/ vyācaṣṭe ---
	  prakāśeti/ sattvasya hi bhāgaḥ prakāśas tāmasena bhāgena dainyena vā rājasena vā
	  duḥkhenānurajyate/ evaṃ rājasādiṣv api draṣṭavyam/ tad idam uktam ---
	  parasparoparaktapravibhāgā iti/ puruṣeṇa saha saṃyogaviyogadharmāṇaḥ/ yathāmnāyate
	  ---
children.translated_text: 'The <s>dṛśya</s> (Seen) has the nature of illumination, activity, and stability; consists of the elements and sense organs; and serves the purpose of experience and liberation.' He explains — '<s>prakāśa</s>' etc. For <s>prakāśa</s> (illumination) is the aspect of <s>sattva</s>; it is colored by the <s>tāmasic</s> aspect, namely depression, or by the <s>rājasic</s> [aspect], namely suffering. The same should be understood for <s>rajas</s> and the others as well. This is what is stated — 'Mutually colored in their divisions' etc. [The <s>guṇas</s>] have the properties of conjunction and disjunction with <s>puruṣa</s>. As the scripture declares —

children.text:
"ajām ekāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇāṃ bahvīḥ prajāḥ sṛjamānāṃ sarūpāḥ/ ajo hy eko
	  juṣamāṇo+anuśete jahāty enāṃ bhuktabhogām ajo+anyaḥ"
taittirīyāraṇyakam 6.10

children.translated_text: Thus.

'The one unborn [<s>prakṛti</s>], red, white, and black, producing many offspring of like form — one unborn [<s>puruṣa</s>] lies with her delighting [in her]; another unborn [<s>puruṣa</s>] abandons her after her enjoyments have been consumed.'

children.text:
itaretaropāśrayeṇopārjitā mūrtiḥ pṛthivyādirūpā yais te tathoktāḥ/ syād etat sattvena
	  śāntapratyaye janayitavye rajastamasor api sattvāṅgatvena tatra hetubhāvād asti
	  sāmarthyam iti yadāpi ca rajastamasor aṅgitvaṃ tadāpi śānta eva pratyaya

udīyeta na ghoro mūḍho vā sattvaprādhānya ivety ata āha --- parasparāṅgāṅgitve+apy
	  asaṃbhinnaśaktipravibhāgāḥ/ bhavatu śānte pratyaye janayitavye rajastamasor aṅgabhāvas
	  tathāpi naiṣāṃ śaktayaḥ saṃkīryante kāryāsaṃkaronneyo hi śaktīnām asaṃkaraḥ/ asaṃkīrṇena
	  ca samudācaratā rūpeṇa śāntaghoramūḍharūpāṇi kāryāṇi dṛśyanta iti siddhaṃ śaktīnām
	  asaṃbheda iti/ syād etat/ asaṃbhedaś cec chaktīnāṃ na saṃbhūyakāritvaṃ guṇānām/ na jātu
	  bhinnaśaktīnāṃ saṃbhūyakāritvaṃ dṛṣṭam/ na hi tantumṛtpiṇḍavīraṇādīni ghaṭādīn saṃbhūya
	  kurvata ity ata āha --- tulyajātīyātulyajātīyaśaktibhedānupātinaḥ/ yady api tulyajātīya
	  upādānaśaktir nānyatra sahakāriśaktis tv atulyajātīye/ paṭe tu janayitavye na vīraṇānām
	  asti sahakāriśaktir apīti na tais tantūnāṃ saṃbhūyakāriteti bhāvaḥ/
	  tulyajātīyātulyajātīyeṣu śakyeṣu ye śaktibhedās tān anupatituṃ śīlaṃ yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ/
	  pradhānavelāyām iti/ divyaśarīre janayitavye sattvaguṇaḥ pradhānam/ aṅge rajastamasī/
	  evaṃ manuṣyaśarīre janayitavye rajaḥ pradhānam aṅge sattvatamasī/ evaṃ tiryakśarīre
	  janayitavye tamaḥ pradhānam aṅge sattvarajasī/ tenaite guṇāḥ pradhānatvavelāyām
	  upadarśitasaṃnidhānāḥ kāryopajananaṃ pratyudbhūtavṛttaya ity arthaḥ/ pradhānaśabdaś ca
	  bhāvapradhānaḥ/ yathā "dvyekayor dvivacanaikavacane"
children.translated_text: — a fierce or deluded [cognition] would arise, not [just] a tranquil one, as in the case of <s>sattva</s>'s predominance — to this he says: 'Even in their mutual subsidiary-principal relationship, the divisions of their powers remain undivided.' Granted that <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> serve as subsidiaries when a tranquil cognition is to be produced, nevertheless their powers are not confused — for the non-confusion of powers is inferred from the non-confusion of effects. And since they operate in an unconfused form, effects of the nature of tranquil, fierce, and deluded are observed — thus the non-blending of powers is established. One might object: if the powers are unblended, then the <s>guṇas</s> cannot act collectively. Collective causation by things with distinct powers is never observed — for threads, clay lumps, and <s>vīraṇa</s> grass do not collectively produce pots and the like — to this he says: 'Following the distinctions of powers in things of the same and different classes.' Although the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) power belongs to the same class, the auxiliary (<s>sahakāri</s>) power [operates] in what is of a different class. But in producing cloth, <s>vīraṇa</s> grass does not even have auxiliary power — hence there is no collective causation of threads with those [materials] — this is the purport. Those whose nature it is to follow the power-distinctions in things of the same and different classes are so called. 'At the time of predominance' — when a divine body is to be produced, <s>sattva-guṇa</s> is predominant, with <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> as subsidiaries. Similarly, when a human body is to be produced, <s>rajas</s> is predominant, with <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s> as subsidiaries. Likewise, when an animal body is to be produced, <s>tamas</s> is predominant, with <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> as subsidiaries. Thus these <s>guṇas</s>, at the time of their predominance, having manifested their presence, are those whose functions have arisen for the generation of effects — this is the meaning. And the word '<s>pradhāna</s>' here carries the sense of predominance in state. Just as [in the rule] 'For two and one, the dual and singular [are used]' —

children.text: pāṇinisūtram 1.4.22
children.translated_text: <s>Pāṇini</s>'s <s>sūtra</s> 1.4.22

children.text:
ity atra
	  dvitvaikatvayor iti/ anyathā dvyekeṣv iti syāt/ nanu tadā pradhānam udbhūtatayā śakyam
	  astīti vaktum anudbhūtānāṃ tu tadaṅgānāṃ sadbhāve kiṃ pramāṇam ity ata āha ---
	  guṇatve+api ceti/ yady api nodbhūtās tathāpi guṇānām avivekitvāt saṃbhūyakāritvāc ca
	  vyāpāramātreṇa sahakāritayā pradhāne+antarṇītaṃ sad anumitam astitvaṃ yeṣāṃ te
	  tathoktāḥ/ nanu santu guṇāḥ saṃbhūyakāriṇaḥ samarthāḥ kasmāt punaḥ kurvanti na hi
	  samartham ity eva kāryaṃ janayati/ mā bhūd asya kāryopajananaṃ prati virāma ity ata āha
	  --- puruṣārthakartavyatayeti/ tato nirvartitanikhilapuruṣārthānāṃ guṇānāṃ uparamaḥ
	  kāryānārambhaṇam ity uktaṃ bhavati/ nanu puruṣasyānupakurvataḥ kathaṃ puruṣārthena
	  prayujyata ity ata āha --- saṃnidhimātreti/ nanu dharmādharmalakṣaṇam eva nimittaṃ
	  prayojakaṃ
children.translated_text: — here [it means] 'of duality and unity'; otherwise it would read 'in twos and ones.' Now, the predominant [<s>guṇa</s>] can be said to exist as manifest, but what is the proof for the existence of the subsidiary [<s>guṇas</s>] that are unmanifest? To this he says: 'Even in the state of being subsidiary' etc. Although they are not manifest, nevertheless, since the <s>guṇas</s> are inseparable and act collectively, their existence is inferred as contained within the predominant [<s>guṇa</s>] through mere operation as auxiliaries — those [<s>guṇas</s>] are so called. But let the <s>guṇas</s> be capable collective agents — why then do they act at all? For something's being capable does not by itself generate an effect. Lest there be no cessation of their production of effects — to this he says: 'Because of the task for <s>puruṣa</s> being [accomplished].' Therefore, for the <s>guṇas</s> that have accomplished all purposes of <s>puruṣa</s>, cessation means not commencing [further] effects — this is what is stated. But since <s>puruṣa</s> does not contribute anything, how is he impelled by the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>? To this he says: 'By mere proximity' etc. But if the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>) that impels the <s>guṇas</s> is precisely <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>,

guṇānāṃ tat kim ucyate puruṣārthaprayuktā ity ata āha ---
	  pratyayam antareṇeti/ ekatamasya sattvasya rajasas tamaso vā pradhānasya svakārye
	  pravṛttasya vṛttim itare pratyayaṃ nimittaṃ dharmādikaṃ vinaivānuvartamānāḥ/ yathā ca
	  vakṣyati --- "nimittam aprayojakaṃ prakṛtīnāṃ varaṇabhedas tu tataḥ kṣetrikavat"
children.translated_text: then why is it said that they are impelled by the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>? To this he says: 'Without any occasion' etc. When one of the [<s>guṇas</s>] — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, or <s>tamas</s> — being predominant, has engaged in its own effect, the others follow its activity without any occasion such as <s>dharma</s> etc. as a cause. And as will be stated: 'The occasion does not impel the <s>prakṛtis</s> (natural potentials); rather, [it operates] by removing the obstacle, like a farmer [removing the dam for irrigation]' —

children.text: yogasūtram 4.3
children.translated_text: <s>Yogasūtra</s> 4.3

children.text:
iti/ ete guṇāḥ pradhānaśabdavācyā bhavantīti saṃbandhaḥ/ pradhīyata
	  ādhīyate viśvaṃ kāryam ebhir iti vyutpattyaitad dṛśyam ucyate/ tad evaṃ guṇānāṃ śīlam
	  abhidhāya tasya kāryam āha --- tad etad iti/ satkāryavādasiddhau yad yadātmakaṃ tat tena
	  rūpeṇa pariṇamata iti bhūtendriyātmakatvaṃ dīpayati --- bhūtabhāvenetyādinā/
	  bhogāpavargārtham iti sūtrāvayavam avatārayati --- tat tu nāprayojanam api tu prayojanam
	  urarīkṛtya pravartate/ bhogaṃ vivṛṇoti --- tatreti/ sukhaduḥkhe hi triguṇāyā buddheḥ
	  svarūpe tasyās tathātvena pariṇāmāt tathāpi guṇagatatayāvadhāraṇe na bhoga ity ata āha

	  buddhivartinau ca kathaṃ tadakāraṇe tadandhikaraṇe ca puruṣe vyapadiśyete ity ata āha
	  --- tāv etāv iti/ bhoktṛtvaṃ ca puruṣasyopapāditam agre
children.translated_text: Thus. These <s>guṇas</s> are denoted by the word '<s>pradhāna</s>' — this is the connection. By the etymology '<s>pradhīyate</s>,' [meaning] 'the entire world of effects is placed (<s>ādhīyate</s>) in these' — this <s>dṛśya</s> (Seen) is so called. Having thus described the nature (<s>śīla</s>) of the <s>guṇas</s>, he states their effect — 'This, this' etc. In establishing the doctrine of <s>satkāryavāda</s> (pre-existence of the effect in the cause), whatever has a particular nature transforms into that form — he illuminates the nature of consisting of elements and sense organs by 'in the form of elements' and so on. He introduces the <s>sūtra</s>-portion 'for the purpose of experience and liberation' — 'But that does not operate without purpose; rather, it operates having accepted a purpose.' He explains <s>bhoga</s> (experience) — 'Therein' etc. For pleasure and pain are the own nature of <s>buddhi</s> composed of the three <s>guṇas</s>, since it transforms into that form; yet if determined as merely belonging to the <s>guṇas</s>, it would not be experience — to this he says: 'Having attained non-distinction' etc. This has been analyzed repeatedly. He explains <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) — 'Of the experiencer' etc. <s>Apavarga</s> means 'that by which one is released.' He states the absence of any other purpose — 'Of the two' etc. And thus <s>Pañcaśikha</s> has said — 'But this indeed' etc. But since <s>bhoga</s> and <s>apavarga</s> are in reality produced by and situated in <s>buddhi</s>, how can they be attributed to <s>puruṣa</s> who is neither their cause nor their locus? To this he says: 'These two' etc. The experiencership of <s>puruṣa</s> has been established [earlier] and

children.text:
ca vakṣyate/
	  paramārthatas tu --- buddher eva puruṣārthāparisamāptir iti/ etena bhogāpavargayoḥ
	  puruṣasaṃbandhitvakathanamārgeṇa grahaṇādayo+api puruṣasaṃbandhino veditavyāḥ/ tatra
	  svarūpamātreṇārthajñānaṃ grahaṇaṃ, tatra smṛtir dhāraṇaṃ, tadgatānāṃ viśeṣāṇām ūhanam
	  ūhaḥ, samāropitānāṃ ca yuktyāpanayo+apohaḥ/ tābhyām evohāpohābhyāṃ tadavadhāraṇaṃ
	  tattvajñānam/ tattvāvadhāraṇapūrvaṃ hānopādānajñānam abhiniveśaḥ //2.18//
children.translated_text: will be stated [later]. But in ultimate reality — 'It is <s>buddhi</s> alone whose purpose for <s>puruṣa</s> is not yet fulfilled.' By this, through the method of declaring <s>bhoga</s> and <s>apavarga</s> as related to <s>puruṣa</s>, <s>grahaṇa</s> (apprehension) and the rest are also to be understood as related to <s>puruṣa</s>. Among these, the knowledge of an object by its mere essential nature is <s>grahaṇa</s> (apprehension); memory of that is <s>dhāraṇa</s> (retention); the reasoning about the particulars contained therein is <s>ūha</s> (conjecture); and the removal by reasoning of what has been superimposed is <s>apoha</s> (exclusion). By these two — <s>ūha</s> and <s>apoha</s> — the ascertainment of that [reality] is <s>tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality). The knowledge of what is to be abandoned and what is to be adopted, preceded by the ascertainment of reality, is <s>abhiniveśa</s> (determination). (2.18)

The form acquired through mutual dependence, having the nature of earth and the rest, by which they are so called. One might object: when <s>sattva</s> is to produce a tranquil cognition, since <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> also have causal efficacy there by serving as subsidiaries (<s>aṅga</s>) to <s>sattva</s>, they too have the capacity [to produce it]; and even when <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> are principal, the cognition would still be tranquil

children.text: viśeṣāviśeṣaliṅgamātrāliṅgāni guṇaparvāṇi //2.19//
children.translated_text: The <s>viśeṣas</s> (particularized), the <s>aviśeṣas</s> (unparticularized), the <s>liṅgamātra</s> (the merely indicated), and the <s>aliṅga</s> (the unindicated) are the stages (<s>parvans</s>) of the <s>guṇas</s>. (2.19)

children.text:
dṛśyānāṃ guṇānāṃ svarūpabhedāvadhāraṇārtham idam ārabhyate ---
	  viśeṣāviśeṣaliṅgamātrāliṅgāni guṇaparvāṇi/ yeṣām aviśeṣāṇāṃ
	  śāntaghoramūḍhalakṣaṇaviśeṣarahitānāṃ ye viśeṣā vikārā eva na tu tattvāntaraprakṛtayas
	  teṣāṃ tān āha --- tatrākāśeti/ utpādakramānurūpa evopanyāsakramaḥ/
	  asmitālakṣaṇasyāviśeṣasya sattvapradhānasya buddhīndriyāṇi viśeṣāḥ/ rājasasya
	  karmendiyāṇi/ manas tūbhayātmakam ubhayapradhānasyeti mantavyam/ atra ca pañcatanmātrāṇi
	  buddhikāraṇakāny aviśeṣatvād asmitāvad iti/ vikārahetutvaṃ cāviśeṣatvaṃ tanmātreṣu
	  cāsmitāyāṃ cāviśiṣṭam/ saṃkalayya viśeṣān parigaṇayati --- guṇānām eṣa iti/ aviśeṣān api
	  gaṇayati --- ṣaḍ iti/ saṃkalayyodāharati --- tadyatheti/ viśiṣṭaṃ hy aparaṃ pareṇeti
	  gandha ātmanā pañcalakṣaṇo rasa ātmanā caturlakṣaṇo rūpam ātmanā trilakṣaṇaṃ

sparśa ātmanā dvilakṣaṇaḥ śabdaḥ śabdalakṣaṇa eveti/ kasya punar amī ṣaḍaviśeṣāḥ
	  kāryam ity ata āha --- ete sattāmātrasyātmana iti/ puruṣārthakriyākṣamaṃ sat tasya
	  bhāvaḥ sattā tanmātraṃ tan mahattattvam/ yāvatī kācit puruṣārthakriyā
	  śabdādibhogalakṣaṇā sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātilakṣaṇā vāsti sā sarvā mahati buddhau
	  samāpyata ity arthaḥ/ ātmana iti svarūpopadarśanena tucchatvaṃ niṣedhati/ prakṛter ayam
	  ādyaḥ pariṇāmo vāstavo na tu tadvivarta iti yāvat/ yat tatparaṃ viprakṛṣṭakālam
	  aviśeṣebhyas tadapekṣayā saṃnikṛṣṭakālebhyo liṅgamātraṃ mahattattvaṃ tasminn ete
	  ṣaḍaviśeṣāḥ sattāmātre mahaty ātmany avasthāya satkāryavādasiddher vivṛddhikāṣṭhām
	  anubhavanti prāpnuvanti/ ye punar aviśeṣāṇāṃ viśeṣapariṇāmās teṣāṃ ca
	  dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāḥ pariṇāmā iti/ seyam eṣāṃ vivṛddhikāṣṭhā pariṇāmakāṣṭheti/ tad evam
	  utpattikramam abhidhāya pralayakramam āha --- pratisaṃsṛjyamānāḥ pralīyamānāḥ svātmani
	  līnaviśeṣā aviśeṣās tasminn eva sattāmātre mahaty ātmany avasthāya vilīya sahaiva mahatā
	  te 'viśeṣā avyaktam anyatra layaṃ na gacchatīty aliṅgaṃ pratiyanti/ tasyaiva viśeṣaṇaṃ
	  niḥsattāsattaṃ sattā puruṣārthakriyākṣamatvam, asattā tucchatā niṣkrāntaṃ sattāyā
	  asattāyāś ca yat tat tathoktam/ etad uktaṃ bhavati --- sattvarajastamasāṃ sāmyāvasthā na
	  kvacit puruṣārtha upayujyata iti na satī nāpi gaganakamalinīva tucchasvabhāvā tena
	  nāsaty apīti/ syād etat/ avyaktāvasthāyām apy asti mahadādi tadātmanā, na hi sato vināśo
	  vināśe vā na punarutpādo na hy asata utpāda iti mahadādisadbhāvāt puruṣārthakriyā
	  pravarteta tat kathaṃ niḥsattvam avyaktam ity ata āha --- niḥsadasad iti/ niṣkrāntaṃ
	  kāraṇaṃ sataḥ kāryāt/ yady api kāraṇāvasthāyāṃ sad eva śaktyātmanā kāryaṃ tathāpi
	  svocitām arthakriyām akurvad asad ity uktam/ na caitat kāraṇaṃ śaśaviṣāṇāyamānakāryam
	  ity āha --- nirasad iti/ niṣkrāntam asatas tuccharūpāt kāryāt tathā sati hi
	  vyomāravindam ivāsmān na
children.translated_text: Touch has two characteristics by its own nature; sound has the characteristic of sound alone. Now, of what are these six <s>aviśeṣas</s> (non-specific categories) the effect? Hence he says — 'these, of the essence of mere being (<s>sattāmātra</s>).' That which is capable of serving the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> is 'existent' (<s>sat</s>); its nature is 'existence' (<s>sattā</s>); 'mere' (<s>mātra</s>) that — this is the <s>mahat-tattva</s> (Great Principle). Whatever purposive activity for <s>Puruṣa</s> there may be — whether characterized as the enjoyment of sound and the like, or characterized as the discriminative discernment of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>sattvapuruṣānyatākhyāti</s>) — all of that is accomplished in the <s>mahat</s>, the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), such is the meaning. By saying 'of the self,' he negates its being unreal through indicating its essential nature. This is the first real transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) of <s>Prakṛti</s>, not a mere apparent transformation (<s>vivarta</s>) of it — such is the purport. That which is distant in time from the <s>aviśeṣas</s> — the <s>liṅgamātra</s> (mere sign), the <s>mahat-tattva</s>, which is proximate in time relative to them — in that, these six <s>aviśeṣas</s>, having subsisted in the <s>mahat</s> as mere being, their own self, reach the pinnacle of development, as established by the <s>satkāryavāda</s> (doctrine of pre-existent effect). Now, the transformations of the <s>aviśeṣas</s> into <s>viśeṣas</s> (specific categories) — and of those, the transformations in terms of property, character, and state (<s>dharmalakṣaṇāvasthā</s>) — this is the pinnacle of their development, the limit of transformation. Having thus stated the order of origination, he states the order of dissolution — 'those being dissolved': the <s>aviśeṣas</s>, with their <s>viśeṣas</s> dissolved into themselves, having subsisted in and merged into that very <s>mahat</s> of mere being, their own self, together with the <s>mahat</s>, return to the <s>aliṅga</s> (the Unmanifest), not undergoing dissolution elsewhere. The qualification of that very [Unmanifest] is 'beyond existence and non-existence' — <s>sattā</s> is the capacity for purposive activity for <s>Puruṣa</s>; <s>asattā</s> is unreality; that which has gone beyond both existence and non-existence is so called. What is stated amounts to this: the state of equilibrium of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> is not employed for any purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, hence it is not 'existent'; nor is it of an unreal nature like a lotus in the sky, hence it is not 'non-existent' either. One might object: even in the state of the Unmanifest, the <s>mahat</s> and the rest exist in that form — for there is no destruction of what exists, nor upon destruction is there non-re-origination, nor is there origination of what does not exist — therefore, since the <s>mahat</s> and the rest exist [in the Unmanifest], purposive activity for <s>Puruṣa</s> should proceed; how then is the Unmanifest 'beyond existence'? Hence he says — 'beyond existent and non-existent': the cause has departed from the existent effect. Although in the causal state the effect exists in the form of potency, nevertheless, since it does not perform its appropriate purposive activity, it is called 'non-existent.' Nor is this cause [productive of] an effect that amounts to a hare's horn — hence he says — 'free from non-existence': departed from the non-existent, from an effect of an unreal nature; for if so, like a sky-lotus, from us no

children.text:
kāryam utpadyeteti bhāvaḥ/ pratisargam uktam
	  upasaṃharati --- eṣa teṣām iti/ eṣa ity anantaroktāt pūrvasya parāmarśaḥ/
	  liṅgamātrādyavasthāḥ puruṣārthakṛtatvād anityā aliṅgāvasthā tu puruṣārthenākṛtatvān
	  nityety atra hetum āha --- aliṅgāvasthāyām iti/ kasmāt punar na puruṣārtho hetur ity ata
	  āha --- nāliṅgāvasthāyām iti/ bhavatinā viṣayeṇa viṣayijñānam upalakṣayati/ etad uktaṃ
	  bhavati --- evaṃ hi puruṣārthatā kāraṇam aliṅgāvasthāyāṃ jñāyeta/ yady aliṅgāvasthā
	  śabdādyupabhogaṃ vā sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātiṃ vā puruṣārthaṃ nirvartayet tannirvartane hi
	  na sāmyāvasthā syāt/ tasmāt puruṣārthakāraṇatvam asyāṃ na jñāyata iti nāsyāḥ
	  puruṣārthatā hetuḥ/ upasaṃharati --- nāsāv iti/ itis tasmādarthe/ anityām avasthām āha
	  --- trayāṇāṃ liṅgamātrāviśeṣaviśeṣāṇām iti/ parvasvarūpaṃ darśayitvā guṇasvarūpam āha
	  --- guṇās tv iti/ nidarśanam āha --- yathā devadatta iti/ yatrātyantabhinnānāṃ gavām
	  upacayāpacayau devadattopacayāpacayahetū tatra kaiva kathā guṇebhyo bhinnābhinnānāṃ
	  vyaktīnām upajanāpāyayor ity arthaḥ/ nanu sargakramaḥ kim aniyato nety āha ---
	  liṅgamātram iti/ na khalu nyagrodhadhānā ahnāyaiva nyagrodhaśākhinaṃ
	  sāndraśādvaladalajaṭilaśākhākāṇḍanipītamārtaṇḍacaṇḍātapamaṇḍalam
children.translated_text: effect would arise — such is the purport. Having stated dissolution, he concludes — 'this of those,' etc. 'This' refers back to what was just stated. The states beginning with <s>liṅgamātra</s> are impermanent because they serve the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>; but the <s>aliṅga</s> state (the Unmanifest) is eternal because it does not serve the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> — here he states the reason: 'in the <s>aliṅga</s> state,' etc. Why is [service to] <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose not the cause [of the Unmanifest]? Hence he says — 'not in the <s>aliṅga</s> state,' etc. By 'the object exists,' he indicates object-based knowledge. What is stated amounts to this: the purposiveness would be known as the cause in the <s>aliṅga</s> state if that state were to accomplish a purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> such as the enjoyment of sound and the like, or the discriminative knowledge of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. For in accomplishing that, there would be no state of equilibrium. Therefore, purposive causation is not known in this [state], hence purposiveness is not its cause. He concludes — 'not that,' etc. The word 'thus' (<s>iti</s>) has the sense of 'therefore.' He states the impermanent state — 'of the three: <s>liṅgamātra</s>, <s>aviśeṣa</s>, and <s>viśeṣa</s>,' etc. Having shown the nature of the stages, he states the nature of the <s>guṇas</s> — 'but the <s>guṇas</s>,' etc. He gives an illustration — 'just as <s>Devadatta</s>,' etc. Where the increase and decrease of cows, which are completely different [from Devadatta], are the cause of <s>Devadatta</s>'s increase and decrease — then what need be said about the origination and dissolution of manifest entities (<s>vyaktis</s>) that are both different and non-different from the <s>guṇas</s>? Such is the meaning. Now, is the order of creation not fixed? Hence he says — '<s>liṅgamātra</s>,' etc. Surely the seeds of the banyan tree do not in a single day produce a banyan tree with dense canopy of leaves, matted aerial roots, and branches that drink in the fierce heat of the sun,

children.text:
ārabhante
	  kiṃ tu kṣitisalilatejaḥsaṃparkāt paramparayopajāyamānāṅkurapatrakāṇḍanālādikrameṇa/ evam
	  ihāpi yuktyāgamasiddhaḥ krama āstheya iti/ kathaṃ bhūtendriyāṇy aviśeṣasaṃsṛṣṭānīty ata
	  āha --- tathā coktaṃ purastād idam eva sūtraṃ prathamaṃ vyācakṣāṇaiḥ/ atha viśeṣāṇāṃ
	  kasmān na tattvāntarapariṇāma ukta ity ata āha --- na viśeṣebhya iti/ tat kim idānīm
	  apariṇāmina eva viśeṣās tathā ca nityāḥ prasajyerann ity ata āha --- teṣāṃ tv iti //2.19//
children.translated_text: rather, through contact with earth, water, and fire, [they produce] in succession, through the sequence of sprout, leaf, stalk, stem, and so on. Likewise here too, the order established by reasoning and scripture is to be followed. How are the gross elements and sense organs intermixed with the <s>aviśeṣas</s>? Hence he says — 'And thus it was stated earlier by those who first explained this very <s>sūtra</s>.' Now, why is a transformation into another category (<s>tattva</s>) of the <s>viśeṣas</s> not stated? Hence he says — 'not from the <s>viśeṣas</s>,' etc. Then are the <s>viśeṣas</s> simply non-transforming, and thus would they be eternal? Hence he says — 'but of those,' etc. (2.19)

For the purpose of ascertaining the distinctions in the essential nature of the <s>guṇas</s> that constitute the <s>dṛśya</s> (Seen), this [sūtra] is commenced — 'The <s>viśeṣas</s>, <s>aviśeṣas</s>, <s>liṅgamātra</s>, and <s>aliṅga</s> are the stages of the <s>guṇas</s>.' Those <s>aviśeṣas</s> (unparticularized), devoid of the distinguishing characteristics of tranquil, fierce, and deluded — their <s>viśeṣas</s> (particularized forms) are merely modifications, not <s>prakṛtis</s> (material causes) of further categories — of these he states them: '<s>Ākāśa</s>' etc. The order of presentation follows the order of production. The <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (cognitive sense organs) are the <s>viśeṣas</s> of the <s>aviśeṣa</s> characterized as <s>asmitā</s> (egoity), with <s>sattva</s> predominant. The <s>karmendriyas</s> (organs of action) [are the <s>viśeṣas</s>] of the <s>rājasic</s> [<s>asmitā</s>]. <s>Manas</s> (mind), being of both natures, should be understood as [the <s>viśeṣa</s>] of that in which both [<s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s>] predominate. And here, the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), being causes of <s>buddhi</s> and being <s>aviśeṣas</s> like <s>asmitā</s>, [are also unparticularized]. The property of being a cause of modification is the <s>aviśeṣatva</s> (unparticularized nature), and this is the same in the <s>tanmātras</s> and in <s>asmitā</s>. Collecting the <s>viśeṣas</s>, he enumerates — 'This of the <s>guṇas</s>' etc. He also enumerates the <s>aviśeṣas</s> — 'Six' etc. Collecting them, he illustrates — 'Namely' etc. For the latter is distinguished by the former — thus smell (<s>gandha</s>) has five characteristics by its own nature, taste (<s>rasa</s>) has four characteristics by its own nature, form (<s>rūpa</s>) has three characteristics by its own nature

children.translated_text: The Seer (<s>Draṣṭṛ</s>) is pure seeing (<s>dṛśi</s>) alone; though pure, [it] witnesses [through] the contents of the mind (<s>pratyaya</s>). (2.20)

	  sarvaviśeṣaṇarahitā dṛkśaktir na tarhi śabdādayo dṛśyeran/ na hi dṛśināsaṃspṛṣṭaṃ dṛśyaṃ
	  bhavatīty ata āha --- sa puruṣa iti/ buddhidarpaṇe puruṣapratibimbasaṃkrāntir eva
	  buddhipratisaṃveditvaṃ puṃsaḥ/ tathā ca dṛśicchāyāpannayā buddhyā saṃsṛṣṭāḥ śabdādayo
	  bhavanti dṛśyā ity arthaḥ/ syād etat/ pāramārthikam eva buddhicaitanyayoḥ kasmād aikyaṃ
	  nopeyate kim anayā tacchāyāpattyety ata āha --- sa buddher na sarūpa iti/ tathāsarūpasya
	  tacchāyāpattir api durghaṭety ata āha --- nātyantaṃ virūpa iti/ tatra sārūpyaṃ niṣedhati
	  --- na tāvad iti/ hetuṃ pṛcchati --- kasmāt/ sahetukaṃ vairūpye hetum āha --- jñāteti/
	  pariṇāminī buddhir yasmāt tasmād virūpā/ yadā khalv iyaṃ śabdādyākārā bhavati tadā jñāto
	  'syāḥ śabdādilakṣaṇo bhavati viṣayas tadanākāratve tv ajñātas tathā ca

kadācid eva tadākāratāṃ dadhatī pariṇāminīti/ prayogaś ca bhavati --- buddhiḥ pariṇāminī
	  jñātājñātaviṣayatvāc chrotrādivad iti/ tadvaidharmyaṃ puruṣasya tadviparītād dhetoḥ
	  sidhyatīty āha --- sadeti/ syād etat/ sadājñātaviṣayaś cet puruṣo na tarhi kevalī syād
	  ity āśayavān pṛcchati --- kasmād iti/ uttaram --- na hi buddhiś ca nāmeti/
	  buddhyagrahaṇayor asti sahasaṃbhavo nirodhāvasthāyām ata ukta virodhasūcanāya
	  puruṣaviṣayaś ceti/ tenādyaś cakāro buddhiṃ viṣayatvena samuccinoti/ pariśiṣṭau tu
	  virodhadyotakau cakārāv iti/ prayogas tu puruṣo+apariṇāmī
	  sadāsaṃprajñātavyutthānāvasthayor jñātaviṣayatvāt/ yas tu pariṇāmī nāsau sadājñātaviṣayo
	  yathā śrotrādir iti vyatirekī hetuḥ/ aparam api vaidharmyam āha --- kiṃ ca parārtheti/
	  buddhiḥ khalu kleśakarmavāsanādibhir viṣayendriyādibhiś ca saṃhatya puruṣārtham
	  abhinirvartayantī parārthā/ prayogaś ca parārthā buddhiḥ saṃhatyakāritvāc
	  chayanāsanābhyaṅgavad iti/ puruṣas tu na tathety āha --- svārthaḥ puruṣa iti/ sarvaṃ
	  puruṣāya kalpate/ puruṣas tu na kasmaicid ity arthaḥ/ vaidharmyāntaram āha --- sarveti/
	  sarvān arthāñ śāntaghoramūḍhāṃs tadākārapariṇatā buddhir adhyavasyati sattvarajastamasāṃ
	  caite pariṇāmā iti siddhā triguṇā buddhir iti/ na caivaṃ puruṣa ity āha --- guṇānām iti/
	  tatpratibimbitaḥ paśyati na tu tadākārapariṇata ity arthaḥ/ upasaṃharati --- ata iti/
	  astu tarhi virūpa iti/ nātyantaṃ virūpaḥ kasmād yataḥ śuddho+api
children.translated_text: [<s>Buddhi</s>] only sometimes assumes that form — it is transformable (<s>pariṇāmin</s>). And the inference is: <s>buddhi</s> is transformable, because it has objects that are [sometimes] known and [sometimes] unknown, like the ear and the rest. The dissimilarity of <s>puruṣa</s> is established from the opposite reason — hence he says: 'always.' One might say: if <s>puruṣa</s> always has a known object, then it could never be in the state of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation). With this intent he asks: 'Why?' The answer: 'For <s>buddhi</s> and non-apprehension are not [simultaneously possible]' — the co-existence of <s>buddhi</s> and non-apprehension is impossible in the state of cessation (<s>nirodha</s>). Hence the word 'ca' (and) was used [in the <s>sūtra</s>] to indicate the contradiction — '[<s>buddhi</s>] is also the object of <s>puruṣa</s>.' Therefore, the first 'ca' accumulates <s>buddhi</s> as [another] object; the remaining two 'ca'-s are indicators of contradiction. The inference is: <s>puruṣa</s> is non-transformable, because its object is always known in both the <s>asaṃprajñāta</s> and <s>vyutthāna</s> (emergent) states. But what is transformable does not always have a known object, like the ear, etc. — this is the dissimilar reason (<s>vyatirekī hetu</s>). He states yet another dissimilarity: 'moreover, for another's sake.' Indeed, <s>buddhi</s>, acting in combination with <s>kleśas</s>, <s>karma</s>, <s>vāsanās</s>, sense-objects, sense-organs, and the like, accomplishes the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> — hence it is 'for another's sake.' And the inference is: <s>buddhi</s> is for another's sake, because it acts in combination — like a bed, seat, or ointment. But <s>puruṣa</s> is not so — hence he says: '<s>puruṣa</s> is for its own sake.' Everything serves the <s>puruṣa</s>, but the <s>puruṣa</s> serves no one — such is the meaning. He states another dissimilarity: 'all' — <s>buddhi</s>, having transformed into the form of all objects — calm (<s>śānta</s>), terrifying (<s>ghora</s>), and deluded (<s>mūḍha</s>) — determines them. And since these are transformations of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, it is established that <s>buddhi</s> is constituted of the three <s>guṇas</s>. But <s>puruṣa</s> is not so — hence he says: 'of the <s>guṇas</s>.' It sees as reflected [in <s>buddhi</s>], but does not transform into their form — such is the meaning. He concludes: 'therefore.' 'Then let it be utterly dissimilar' — [one might say]. 'Not utterly dissimilar.' Why? Because, though pure,

children.translated_text: it 'looks upon' cognitions (<s>pratyayānupaśya</s>). And this is just as stated: 'conformity with the modifications, otherwise'

children.translated_text: <s>Yogasūtra</s> 1.4

children.text:
ity
	  atra/ tathā coktaṃ pañcaśikhenāpariṇāminī hi bhoktṛśaktir ātmā/ ata eva buddhāv
	  apratisaṃkramā ca pariṇāmini buddhirūpe 'rthe saṃkrānteva tadvṛttiṃ buddhivṛttim
	  anupatati/ nanv asaṃkrāntā kathaṃ saṃkrānteva kathaṃ vā vṛttiṃ vinānupatatīty ata āha
	  --- tasyāś ceti/ prāptaś caitanyopagraha uparāgo yena rūpeṇa tat tathā
	  prāptacaitanyopagrahaṃ rūpaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathoktā/ etad uktaṃ bhavati --- yathā nirmale
	  jale 'saṃkrānto+api candramāḥ saṃkrāntapratibimbatayā saṃkrānta iva, evam atrāpy
	  asaṃkrāntāpi saṃkrāntapratibimbā citiśaktiḥ saṃkrānteva/ tena buddhyātmatvam āpannā
	  buddhivṛttim anupatatīti/ tad anenānupaśya iti vyākhyātaṃ tām anukāreṇa paśyatīty
	  anupaśya iti //2.20//
children.translated_text: — there [at YS 1.4]. And so it has been said by <s>Pañcaśikha</s>: 'For the experiencer-power, the Self, is non-transformable.' For this very reason, 'non-migrating' [as applied to the power of consciousness] in <s>buddhi</s> — though it does not actually migrate into <s>buddhi</s>, which is a transformable object — it follows, as it were having migrated, the modification of <s>buddhi</s>. Now, if it has not migrated, how does it [appear] as if migrated? And how does it follow the modification without [actually participating in] the modification? To this he replies: 'And of that' — <s>buddhi</s>, whose form has acquired the coloring of consciousness (<s>caitanyopagraha</s>), is so described. What is meant is this: just as the moon, though not having migrated into clear water, [appears] as if migrated through the reflected image, so here too the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>), though not having migrated, being [present as] a reflected image that has migrated, [appears] as if migrated. Therefore, having assumed the nature of <s>buddhi</s>, it follows the modifications of <s>buddhi</s>. By this, the word '<s>anupaśya</s>' (one who looks upon) has been explained — it 'sees following' (<s>anupaśya</s>), that is, it sees by way of imitation. (2.20)

The seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) having been explained, this [sūtra] is commenced for the purpose of ascertaining the essential nature of the Seer — 'The Seer is pure seeing alone; though pure, it witnesses through the contents of the mind.' He explains — 'seeing alone (<s>dṛśimātra</s>)': attributes (<s>dharmas</s>) are qualifications; untouched by them. By this, the purport of the term 'alone' (<s>mātra</s>) is shown. One might think: if the power of seeing is devoid of all qualifications, then sound and the like would not be seen; for the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) cannot exist without being in contact with the seer (<s>dṛśi</s>). Hence he says — 'that <s>Puruṣa</s>,' etc. The reflection of <s>Puruṣa</s> transferred into the mirror of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) — this is what constitutes <s>Puruṣa</s>'s experience of what is presented by <s>buddhi</s>. And thus, sound and the like, conjoined with <s>buddhi</s> that has received the reflection of seeing, become 'seen' — such is the meaning. One might ask: why not accept a real identity between <s>buddhi</s> and consciousness? What is the need for this [notion of] receiving a reflection? Hence he says — 'he is not of the same form as <s>buddhi</s>,' etc. But even the receiving of a reflection by one that is not of the same form is difficult to establish — hence he says — 'nor is he entirely of a different form,' etc. Therein, he negates sameness of form — 'not so,' etc. He asks for the reason — 'why?' He states the reason for difference of form along with its ground — 'because it is known,' etc. <s>Buddhi</s> is subject to transformation; therefore it is of a different form [from <s>Puruṣa</s>]. For when this [<s>buddhi</s>] takes on the form of sound and the like, then its object characterized by sound and the like becomes known; but when it does not take on that form, [the object remains] unknown, and thus

children.text: tadartha eva dṛśyasyātmā //2.21//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 2.21:] <s>Tadartha eva dṛśyasyātmā</s> — 'The essential nature of the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) exists for the sake of that [seer] alone.' (2.21)

children.text:
draṣṭṛdṛśyayoḥ svarūpam uktvā svasvāmilakṣaṇasaṃbandhāṅgaṃ dṛśyasya draṣṭrarthatvam āha
	  --- tadartha eva dṛśyasyātmā/ vyācaṣṭe --- dṛśirūpasya puruṣasya bhoktuḥ karmarūpatāṃ
	  bhogyatām āpannaṃ dṛśyam iti tasmāt tadartha eva draṣṭrartha eva dṛśyasyātmā bhavati na
	  tu dṛśyārthaḥ/ nanu nātmātmārtha ity ata āha --- svarūpaṃ bhavatīti/ etad uktaṃ bhavati
	  --- sukhaduḥkhātmakaṃ dṛśyaṃ bhogyam/ sukhaduḥkhe cānukūlayitṛpratikūlayitṛṇī tattvena
	  tadarthe eva vyavatiṣṭhete/ viṣayā api hi śabdādayas tādātmyād eva cānukūlayitāraḥ
	  pratikūlayitāraś ca/ na cātmaivaiṣām anukūlanīyaḥ pratikūlanīyaś ca svātmani
	  vṛttivirodhād ataḥ pāriśeṣyāc citiśaktir evānukūlanīyā pratikūlanīyā ca/ tasmāt
	  tadartham eva dṛśyaṃ na tu dṛśyārtham/ ataś ca tadartha eva dṛśyasyātmā na dṛśyārtho yat
	  svarūpam asya yāvat puruṣārtham anuvartate/ nirvartite ca puruṣārthe nivartata ity āha
	  --- svarūpam iti/ svarūpaṃ tu dṛśyasya jaḍaṃ pararūpeṇātmarūpeṇa caitanyena
	  pratilabdhātmakam

anubhūtasvarūpaṃ bhogāpavargārthatāyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ puruṣeṇa
	  na dṛśyate/ bhogaḥ sukhādyākāraḥ śabdādyanubhavo 'pavargaḥ sattvapuruṣānyatānubhavas tac
	  caitad ubhayam apy ājānato jaḍāyā buddheḥ puruṣacchāyāpattyeti puruṣasyaiva/ tathā ca
	  puruṣabhogāpavargayoḥ kṛtayor dṛśyasya bhogāpavargārthatā samāpyata iti
	  bhogāpavargārthatāyāṃ kṛtāyām ity uktam/ atrāntare codayati --- svarūpahānād iti/
	  pariharati --- na tu vinaśyatīti //2.21//
children.translated_text: having its own form experienced [through consciousness]. When its purpose of experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) has been accomplished, it is not seen by that <s>puruṣa</s>. <s>Bhoga</s> (experience) is the experience of sound, etc., having the form of pleasure, etc. <s>Apavarga</s> (liberation) is the experience of the otherness of <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>. And both of these belong to the <s>puruṣa</s> alone, since they are [actually] the falling of the <s>puruṣa</s>'s reflection upon <s>buddhi</s>, which is insentient and which recognizes [objects] without knowing [itself]. And thus, when the <s>puruṣa</s>'s experience and liberation are both accomplished, the 'being for the sake of experience and liberation' of the seen is completed — hence it was said: 'when its purpose of experience and liberation has been accomplished.' In between, he raises an objection: 'from the destruction of its own form.' He resolves: 'but it does not perish.' (2.21)

Having stated the essential nature of the seer and the seen, he states [that] the seen exists for the seer's sake — an element of the property-owner relation (<s>svasvāmilakṣaṇasaṃbandha</s>): 'The essential nature of the seen exists for the sake of that [seer] alone.' He explains: 'The seen (<s>dṛśya</s>), having assumed the role of that which is to be experienced (<s>bhogyatā</s>) for the <s>puruṣa</s> who is the seer (<s>dṛśi</s>) — therefore the essential nature of the seen exists for the seer's sake alone, not for its own sake.' Now, [one might say:] a thing's self does not exist for its own sake. To this he replies: 'its essential nature is [for another].' What is meant is this: the seen, consisting of pleasure and pain, is what is to be experienced. And pleasure and pain, being what makes favorable and unfavorable, in their reality stand for that [seer's] sake alone. For even sense-objects such as sound, etc., by virtue of their identity [with pleasure and pain], are what make favorable and what make unfavorable. And it is not their own self that is to be favored or to be opposed — since activity toward one's own self would involve a contradiction. Therefore, by process of elimination, it is the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>) alone that is to be favored and to be opposed. Therefore, the seen exists for that [seer's] sake alone, not for the sake of the seen. And thus, the essential nature of the seen is 'for that sake alone' and not for its own sake — inasmuch as its own form continues [only] as long as the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> [continues]. And when the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> is accomplished, it ceases — hence he says: 'its own form.' The own form of the seen is insentient; having its self restored by the other's form — namely, consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) — [that is,] having obtained its self [through consciousness],

children.text: kṛtārthaṃ prati naṣṭam apy anaṣṭaṃ tadanyasādhāraṇatvāt //2.22//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 2.22:] <s>Kṛtārthaṃ prati naṣṭam apy anaṣṭaṃ tadanyasādhāraṇatvāt</s> — 'Though destroyed in relation to one whose purpose is accomplished, [the seen] is not [truly] destroyed, because it is common to others as well.' (2.22)

children.text:
nanv atyantānupalabhyaṃ kathaṃ na vinaśyatīty āśayavān pṛcchati --- kasmād iti/
	  sūtreṇottaram āha --- kṛtārthaṃ prati naṣṭam apy anaṣṭaṃ tadanyasādhāraṇatvāt/
	  kṛto+artho yasya puruṣasya sa tathā/ taṃ prati naṣṭam apy anaṣṭaṃ tad dṛśyaṃ kutaḥ
	  sarvān puruṣān kuśalān akuśalān prati sādhāraṇatvāt/ vyācaṣṭe --- kṛtārtham ekam iti/
	  nāśo 'darśanam/ anaṣṭaṃ tu dṛśyam anyapuruṣasādhāraṇatvāt/ tasmād dṛśyāt parasyātmanaś
	  caitanyaṃ rūpaṃ tena tad iha śrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇaprasiddham avyaktam anavayavam ekam
	  anāśrayaṃ vyāpi nityaṃ viśvakāryaśaktimat/ yady api kuśalena taṃ prati kṛtakāryaṃ na
	  dṛśyate tathāpy akuśalena dṛśyamānaṃ na nāsti/ na hi rūpam andhena na dṛśyata iti
	  cakṣuṣmatāpi dṛśyamānam abhāvaprāptaṃ bhavati/ na ca pradhānavad eka eva puruṣas
	  tannānātvasya janmamaraṇasukhaduḥkhopabhogamuktisaṃsāravyavasthayā siddheḥ/
	  ekatvaśrutīnāṃ ca pramāṇāntaravirodhāt kathaṃcid deśakālavibhāgābhāvena bhaktyāpy
	  upapatteḥ/ prakṛtyekatvapuruṣanānātvayoś ca śrutyaiva sākṣāt pratipādanāt/
children.translated_text: Now, [one might ask:] that which is absolutely unperceivable — how can it not perish? With this intent he asks: 'why?' The <s>sūtra</s> replies: 'Though destroyed in relation to one whose purpose is accomplished, [the seen] is not [truly] destroyed, because it is common to others as well.' One whose purpose (<s>artha</s>) is accomplished is so called. In relation to him, though destroyed — [i.e.,] unseen — the seen is not [truly] destroyed. Why? Because it is common to all <s>puruṣas</s>, both skilled [in liberation] and unskilled. He explains: 'for one whose purpose is accomplished.' 'Destruction' is non-perception. 'Not destroyed' — the seen [is not destroyed] because it is common to other <s>puruṣas</s>. Therefore, beyond the seen, the form of the Self is consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>). By that, it is here well established in <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Itihāsa</s>, and <s>Purāṇa</s> that the Unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is: without parts, one, without support, all-pervading, eternal, and possessing the power to produce the entire [world]. Although for the skilled one, it is not perceived since its purpose is accomplished in relation to him — nevertheless, being perceived by the unskilled, it does not cease to exist. For a visible form is not rendered non-existent simply because it is not seen by a blind person — since it is seen [perfectly well] by one with eyes. Nor is there only one <s>puruṣa</s>, like <s>Pradhāna</s> — for the plurality [of <s>puruṣas</s>] is established by the observed arrangements of birth, death, experience of pleasure and pain, liberation, and continued <s>saṃsāra</s>. And [the seemingly contradictory] <s>Śruti</s> texts proclaiming oneness can somehow be reconciled through the absence of spatial and temporal distinction, by devotional [interpretation]. Moreover, the oneness of <s>Prakṛti</s> and the plurality of <s>puruṣas</s> are directly taught by <s>Śruti</s> itself:

children.text:
"ajām ekāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇāṃ bahvīḥ prajāḥ sṛjamānāṃ sarūpāḥ/ ajo hy eko
	  juṣamāṇo+anuśete jahāty enāṃ bhuktabhogām ajo+anyaḥ"
taittirīyāraṇyakam 6.10
children.translated_text: <s>Taittirīyāraṇyaka</s> 6.10

children.text:
iti
	  śrutiḥ/
children.translated_text: Thus says the <s>Śruti</s>.

'The one unborn [<s>Prakṛti</s>], red, white, and black, producing many offspring of similar form — one unborn [<s>puruṣa</s>] enjoys her and lies with her; another unborn abandons her, whose enjoyments have been consumed.'

children.text:
asyā eva śruteś cānena sūtreṇārtho+anūdita iti/ yato dṛśyaṃ naṣṭam apy anaṣṭaṃ
	  puruṣāntaraṃ praty asti ato dṛgdarśanaśaktyor nityatvād anādiḥ saṃyogo vyākhyātaḥ/
	  atraivāgaminām anumatim āha --- tathā coktam iti/ dharmiṇāṃ guṇānām ātmabhir
	  anādisaṃyogād dharmamātrāṇāṃ mahadādīnām apy anādiḥ saṃyoga iti/ ekaikasya mahadādeḥ
	  saṃyogo+anādir apy anitya eva yady api tathāpi sarveṣāṃ mahadādīnāṃ nityaḥ
	  puruṣāntarāṇāṃ sādhāraṇatvād ata uktaṃ dharmamātrāṇām iti/ mātragrahaṇena vyāptiṃ
	  gamayati/ ata etad bhavati --- yady apy ekasya mahataḥ saṃyogo+atītatām āpannas tathāpi
	  mahadantarasya puruṣāntareṇa saṃyogo nātīta iti nitya uktaḥ //2.22//
children.translated_text: And the meaning of this very <s>Śruti</s> is reiterated by this <s>sūtra</s>. Since the seen, though destroyed [for one], is not [truly] destroyed because it exists for other <s>puruṣas</s>, and since the powers of seeing and the seen are eternal, the conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) is explained as beginningless. Here he states the agreement of the followers [of this tradition]: 'And so it has been said.' From the beginningless conjunction of the <s>guṇas</s> (<s>dharmiṇas</s>) with their own natures — [i.e., the selves] — the conjunction of the mere qualities (<s>dharmamātra</s>) — <s>Mahat</s>, etc. — is also beginningless. Although the conjunction of each individual <s>Mahat</s>, etc., with [a <s>puruṣa</s>] is beginningless yet impermanent, nevertheless, for all the <s>Mahat</s>, etc., [the conjunction is] eternal, because they are common to other <s>puruṣas</s> — hence it was said 'of the mere qualities.' By the word 'mere' (<s>mātra</s>), universality (<s>vyāpti</s>) is indicated. Therefore this follows: although the conjunction of one [particular] <s>Mahat</s> has come to an end [for one <s>puruṣa</s>], nevertheless the conjunction of another <s>Mahat</s> with another <s>puruṣa</s> has not come to an end — hence it is called eternal. (2.22)

children.text: svasvāmiśaktyoḥ svarūpopalabdhihetuḥ saṃyogaḥ //2.23//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 2.23:] <s>Svasvāmiśaktyoḥ svarūpopalabdhihetuḥ saṃyogaḥ</s> — 'Conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) is the cause of the apprehension of the own-natures of the powers of property (<s>sva</s>) and owner (<s>svāmin</s>).' (2.23)

children.text:
tad evaṃ tādarthye saṃyogakāraṇa ukte prāsaṅgike pradhānanityatve
	  saṃyogasāmānyanityatve hetau cokte saṃyogasya yat svarūpam asādhāraṇo viśeṣa iti yāvat
	  tadabhidhitsayedaṃ sūtraṃ pravavṛte --- svasvāmiśaktyoḥ svarūpopalabdhihetuḥ saṃyogaḥ/
	  yato dṛśyaṃ tadartham atas tajjanitam upakāraṃ bhajamānaḥ puruṣas tasya svāmī bhavati/
	  bhavati ca tad dṛśyam asya svaṃ sa cānayoḥ saṃyogaḥ śaktimātreṇa vyavasthitas
	  tatsvarūpopalabdhihetus tad etad bhāṣyam avadyotayati --- puruṣaḥ svāmī yogyatāmātreṇa
	  dṛśyena svena yogyatayaiva darśanārthaṃ saṃyuktaḥ/ śeṣaṃ sugamam/ syād etat/ draṣṭuḥ
	  svarūpopalabdhir apavṛjyate+anenety apavarga ukto na ca mokṣaḥ sādhanavāṃs tathā saty
	  ayaṃ mokṣatvād eva cyavetety ata āha --- darśanakāryāvasāno buddhiviśeṣeṇa saha
	  puruṣaviśeṣasya saṃyoga iti darśanaṃ viyogakāraṇam

uktam/ kathaṃ punar
	  darśanakāryāvasānatvaṃ saṃyogasyety ata āha --- darśanam iti/ tataḥ kim ity ata āha ---
	  adarśanam avidyā saṃyoganimittam ity uktam/ uktam arthaṃ spaṣṭayati --- nātreti/ nanu
	  darśanam adarśanaṃ virodhi nivartayatu bandhasya kuto nivṛttir ity ata āha ---
	  darśanasyeti/ buddhyādiviviktasyātmanaḥ svarūpāvasthānaṃ mokṣa ukto na tasya sādhanaṃ
	  darśanam api tv adarśananivṛtter ity arthaḥ/ asādhāraṇaṃ saṃyogahetum adarśanaviśeṣaṃ
	  grahītum adarśanamātraṃ vikalpayati --- kiṃ cedam iti/ paryudāsaṃ gṛhītvāha --- kiṃ
	  guṇānām adhikāraḥ kāryārambhaṇasāmarthyaṃ tato hi saṃyogaḥ saṃsārahetur upajāyate/
	  prasajyapratiṣedhaṃ gṛhītvā dvitīyaṃ vikalpam āha --- āhosvid iti/ darśito viṣayaḥ
	  śabdādiḥ sattvapuruṣānyatā ca yena cittena tasya tadviṣayasyānutpādaḥ/ etad eva
	  sphorayati --- svasmin dṛśye śabdādau sattvapuruṣānyatāyāṃ ceti/ tāvad eva pradhānaṃ
	  viceṣṭate na yāvad dvividhaṃ darśanam abhinirvartayati/ niṣpāditobhayadarśanaṃ tu
	  nivartata iti/ paryudāsa eva tṛtīyaṃ vikalpam āha --- kim arthavattā guṇānām/
	  satkāryavādasiddhau hi bhāvināv api bhogāpavargārthāv avyapadeśyatayā sta ity arthaḥ/
	  paryudāsa eva caturthaṃ vikalpam āha --- athāvidyā pratisargakāle svacittena saha
	  niruddhā pradhānasāmyam āgatā vāsanārūpeṇa svacittotpattibījam/ tena darśanād
	  anyāvidyāvāsanaivādarśanam uktā/ paryudāsa eva pañcamaṃ vikalpam āha --- kiṃ
	  sthitisaṃskārasya pradhānavartinaḥ sāmyapariṇāmaparamparāvahinaḥ kṣaye gatir
	  mahadādivikārārambhas taddhetuḥ saṃskāraḥ pradhānasya gatisaṃskāras tasyābhivyaktiḥ
children.translated_text: This has been stated. But how is it that <s>saṃyoga</s> ends with the accomplishment of seeing? Therefore he says — '<s>darśana</s>' etc. What follows from that? Therefore he says — '<s>adarśana</s> (non-seeing), which is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), has been stated as the cause of <s>saṃyoga</s>.' He clarifies the stated meaning — 'not here' etc. But one might object: let <s>darśana</s> remove <s>adarśana</s>, which is its opposite — from where then comes the cessation of bondage? Therefore he says — 'of <s>darśana</s>' etc. The abiding of the self (<s>ātman</s>) in its own nature, distinct from <s>buddhi</s> and the rest, has been called <s>mokṣa</s>; <s>darśana</s> is not its means, but rather [<s>mokṣa</s> comes] from the cessation of <s>adarśana</s> — this is the meaning. In order to grasp the specific form of <s>adarśana</s> as the distinctive cause of <s>saṃyoga</s>, he considers <s>adarśana</s> in general through alternatives — 'what is this?' etc. Taking it as an implicative negation (<s>paryudāsa</s>), he says — 'Is it the functioning (<s>adhikāra</s>) of the <s>guṇas</s>, the capacity to initiate action? For from that arises <s>saṃyoga</s>, which is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence).' Taking it as a simple negation (<s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>), he states the second alternative — 'or rather' etc. The demonstrated object (<s>viṣaya</s>) is sound and the like, and the otherness of <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>; the non-arising of that object in that <s>citta</s> (mind) by which [it was cognized]. He elaborates on this very point — 'in one's own seen (<s>dṛśya</s>), namely sound and the like, and in the otherness of <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>' etc. <s>Pradhāna</s> exerts itself only so long as it has not produced the twofold <s>darśana</s>; but having accomplished both kinds of seeing, it ceases. By implicative negation again, he states the third alternative — 'Is it the meaningfulness (<s>arthavattā</s>) of the <s>guṇas</s>?' For according to the established <s>satkāryavāda</s> (doctrine of pre-existent effect), even the future purposes of experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) would be inexpressible — this is the meaning. By implicative negation again, he states the fourth alternative — 'or is <s>avidyā</s>, at the time of dissolution (<s>pratisarga</s>), suppressed along with one's own <s>citta</s>, having reached the equilibrium of <s>pradhāna</s>, a seed for the production of one's own <s>citta</s> in the form of latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>)?' Therefore, <s>adarśana</s> is said to be the <s>vāsanā</s> of <s>avidyā</s> different from <s>darśana</s>. By implicative negation again, he states the fifth alternative — 'Is it the decay of the momentum-impression (<s>sthitisaṃskāra</s>) residing in <s>pradhāna</s>, flowing in a series of equilibrium-transformations? The movement — the initiation of modifications beginning with <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) and the rest — its cause is the impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>), the momentum-impression of <s>pradhāna</s>; its manifestation is

children.text:
kāryonmukhatvam/ tadubhayasaṃskārasadbhāve matāntarānumatim āha --- yatredam
	  uktam aikāntikatvaṃ vyāsedhadbhiḥ, pradhīyate janyate vikārajātam aneneti pradhānaṃ tac
	  cet sthityaiva varteta na kadācid gatyā tato vikārākaraṇān na pradhīyate tena kiṃcid ity
	  apradhānaṃ syāt/ atha gatyaiva varteta na kadācid api sthityā tatrāha --- tathā
	  gatyaiveti/ kvacit pāṭhaḥ "sthityai gatyai" iti/ tādarthye caturthī, evakāraś ca
	  draṣṭavyaḥ/ sthityai cen na varteta na kvacid vikāro vinaśyet/ tathā ca bhāvasya
	  sato+avināśino notpattir apīti vikāratvād eva cyaveta/ evaṃ ca na pradhīyate+atra kiṃcid
	  ity apradhānaṃ syāt tad ubhayathā sthityā gatyā cāsya vṛttiḥ pradhānavyavahāraṃ labhate
	  nānyathaikāntābhyupagame/ na kevalaṃ pradhāne kāraṇāntareṣv api
	  parabrahmatanmāyāparamāṇvādiṣu kalpiteṣu samānaś carco vicāraḥ/ tāny api hi sthityaiva
	  vartamānāni vikārākaraṇād akāraṇāni syuḥ, gatyaiva vartamānāni vikāranityatvād akāraṇāni
	  syur iti ca/ paryudāsa eva ṣaṣṭhaṃ vikalpam āha --- darśanaśaktir eveti/ yathā
	  prajāpativrate nekṣetodyantam ādityam ity anīkṣaṇapratyāsannaḥ saṃkalpo gṛhyata evam
	  ihāpi darśananiṣedhe tatpratyāsannā tanmūlā śaktir ucyate/ sā ca darśanaṃ
	  bhogādilakṣaṇaṃ prasotuṃ draṣṭāraṃ dṛśyena yojayatīti/ atraiva śrutim āha ---
	  pradhānasyeti/ syād etat/ ātmakhyāpanārthaṃ pradhānaṃ pravartata iti śrutir āha na tv
	  ātmadarśanaśakteḥ pravartata ity ata āha --- sarvabodhyabodhasamartha iti/ prāk
	  pravṛtteḥ pradhānasya nātmakhyāpanamātraṃ pravṛttau prayojakam asāmarthye tadayogāt
	  tasmāt sāmarthyaṃ pravṛtteḥ prayojakam iti śrutyārthād uktam ity arthaḥ/ darśanaśaktiḥ
	  pradhānāśrayety aṅgīkṛtya ṣaṣṭhaḥ kalpaḥ/ imām evobhayāśrayām āsthāya saptamaṃ vikalpam
	  āha --- ubhayasya puruṣasya ca dṛśyasya cādarśanaṃ darśanaśaktir dharma ity eke/
children.translated_text: the orientation toward producing effects. Regarding the existence of both types of impressions, he states the view accepted by another school — 'where this is said: by those who would deny absolute one-sidedness.' <s>Pradhāna</s> — so called because it produces, i.e., generates the entire class of modifications — if it were to exist only in a state of rest and never in activity, then since it would not produce any modifications, nothing would be produced by it, and it would be 'non-<s>pradhāna</s>' (not the primary cause). But if it were to exist only in activity and never in rest, to that he says — 'likewise, by activity alone' etc. In some readings the text is '<s>sthityai gatyai</s>' — the dative case indicates purpose, and the particle '<s>eva</s>' should be understood. If it did not exist for the sake of rest, no modification would ever perish. And thus, there would be no origination of what already exists as an imperishable entity — it would cease to be a modification by its very nature. And so nothing is produced here, hence it would be 'non-<s>pradhāna</s>.' Therefore, its functioning through both rest and activity obtains the designation '<s>pradhāna</s>'; not otherwise, by accepting only one side. Not only with regard to <s>pradhāna</s>, but also with regard to other postulated causes — <s>Parabrahman</s> (Supreme Brahman), its <s>Māyā</s> (illusion), <s>paramāṇu</s> (atoms), and the like — the same investigation and inquiry applies.
