For they too, if existing only in rest, would not be causes since they would not produce modifications; and if existing only in activity, would not be causes since modifications would be eternal — thus. By implicative negation again, he states the sixth alternative — 'the power of seeing (<s>darśanaśakti</s>) itself' etc. Just as in the <s>Prājāpatya</s> vow, 'one should not look at the rising sun' — the resolve close to non-looking is understood; similarly here too, when seeing is negated, what is referred to is the power proximate to it and rooted in it. And that [power], capable of producing seeing characterized by experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and the like, conjoins the seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>) with the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>). To this very point, he cites the scriptural passage — 'of <s>pradhāna</s>' etc. One might object: the scripture says that <s>pradhāna</s> operates for the purpose of manifesting the self — but not that it operates from the power of self-seeing. Therefore he says — 'capable of illuminating all that is to be known' etc. Prior to the activity of <s>pradhāna</s>, the mere manifestation of the self is not the motivating factor for its activity, because in the absence of capacity, that [activity] would be impossible. Therefore, capacity is the motivating factor for activity — this is what is meant by the purport of the scripture. Accepting that <s>darśanaśakti</s> (the power of seeing) resides in <s>pradhāna</s>, [this is] the sixth alternative. Accepting this very [power] as residing in both, he states the seventh alternative — 'the <s>adarśana</s> (non-seeing), which is the power of seeing, is a property of both — of <s>puruṣa</s> and of the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) — so say some.'

children.text:
syād etan mṛṣyāmahe dṛśyasyeti, tasya sarvaśaktyāśrayatvān na draṣṭur iti
	  punar mṛṣyāmaḥ/ na hi tadādhārā jñānaśaktis tatra jñānasyāsamavāyād anyathā
	  pariṇāmāpattir ity ata āha --- tatredam iti/ bhavatu dṛśyātmakaṃ tathāpi tasya jaḍatvena
	  tadgataśaktikāryaṃ darśanam api jaḍam iti na śakyaṃ taddharmatvena vijñātuṃ jaḍasya
	  svayam aprakāśatvād ato dṛśer ātmanaḥ pratyayaṃ caitanyacchāyāpattim apekṣya darśanaṃ
	  taddharmatvena bhavati jñāyate viṣayeṇa viṣayiṇo lakṣaṇāt/ nanv etāvatāpi
	  dṛśyadharmatvam asya jñānasya bhavati na tu puruṣadharmatvam apīty ata āha --- tathā
	  puruṣasyeti/ satyaṃ puruṣasyānātmabhūtam eva tathāpi dṛśyabuddhisattvasya yaḥ pratyayaś
	  caitanyacchāyāpattis tam apekṣya puruṣadharmatveneva na tu puruṣadharmatvena/ etad uktaṃ
	  bhavati --- caitanyabimbodgrāhitayā buddhicaitanyayor abhedād buddhidharmāś
	  caitanyadharmā iva cakāsatīti/ aṣṭamaṃ vikalpam āha --- darśanaṃ jñānam eva śabdādīnām
	  adarśanaṃ na tu sattvapuruṣānyatāyā iti kecit/ yathā cakṣū rūpe pramāṇam api rasādāv
	  apramāṇam ucyate/ etad uktaṃ bhavati --- sukhādyākāraśabdādijñānāni svasiddhyanuguṇatayā
	  draṣṭṛdṛśyasaṃyogam ākṣipantīti/ tad evaṃ vikalpya caturthaṃ vikalpaṃ svīkartum itareṣāṃ
	  vikalpānāṃ sāṃkhyaśāstragatānāṃ sarvapuruṣasādhāraṇyena bhogavaicitryābhāvaprasaṅgena
	  dūṣayati --- ity ete śāstragatā iti //2.23//
children.translated_text: One might say: we accept [that <s>darśanaśakti</s> resides] in the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>), since it is the locus of all powers; but we do not accept [that it resides] in the seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>). For the power of knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>) cannot reside there, since knowledge does not inhere (<s>samavāya</s>) in it — otherwise the consequence of [<s>puruṣa</s>] undergoing transformation would follow. Therefore he says — 'here, this' etc. Granted that [<s>darśana</s>] has the nature of the seen; nevertheless, since the seen is insentient (<s>jaḍa</s>), the seeing that is the effect of the power residing in it is also insentient. Therefore it cannot be cognized as its property, since what is insentient does not illuminate itself. Hence, seeing becomes its property only by depending on the reflection of consciousness (<s>caitanyacchāyāpatti</s>) — i.e., the cognition of the self (<s>dṛś</s>), the <s>ātman</s> — since the possessor is characterized by its object. But even so, this knowledge remains a property of the seen, not a property of <s>puruṣa</s> — therefore he says — 'likewise, of <s>puruṣa</s>' etc. True, it is indeed non-essential to <s>puruṣa</s>; nevertheless, the cognition of the seen <s>buddhi-sattva</s> — the reflection of consciousness (<s>caitanyacchāyāpatti</s>) — depending on that, it is as if a property of <s>puruṣa</s>, but not actually a property of <s>puruṣa</s>. What is thereby stated is this: because the reflection of consciousness is grasped [in <s>buddhi</s>], there is non-difference between <s>buddhi</s> and consciousness; therefore the properties of <s>buddhi</s> appear as though they were properties of consciousness. He states the eighth alternative — '<s>darśana</s>, which is knowledge itself, is <s>adarśana</s> with respect to sound and the like, but not with respect to the otherness of <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> — so say some.' Just as the eye, though a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) with respect to form, is said to be not a valid means with respect to taste and the like. What is thereby stated is this: cognitions of pleasure and the like, and cognitions of sound and the like, by their very nature of self-accomplishment, entail the conjunction of seer and seen. Having thus considered the alternatives, he adopts the fourth alternative and refutes the other alternatives — those found in <s>Sāṃkhya</s> scripture — on the ground that, being common to all <s>puruṣas</s>, they would lead to the absurd consequence of there being no variety in experience — 'thus these, found in scripture' etc. (2.23)

Thus, when the cause of <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) for the sake of that [<s>puruṣa</s>'s purpose] has been stated, and when the incidental eternality of <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter) and the cause in the form of the general eternality of <s>saṃyoga</s> have been stated, this <s>sūtra</s> was set forth with the intention of describing the essential nature of <s>saṃyoga</s>, that is, its distinctive characteristic — '<s>saṃyoga</s> is the cause of apprehending the true nature of the powers of the owned and the owner.' Since the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) exists for its [<s>puruṣa</s>'s] sake, therefore <s>puruṣa</s>, partaking of the benefit produced by it, becomes its owner. And that seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) becomes his own property, and the <s>saṃyoga</s> between these two is established through mere capacity (<s>śakti</s>) alone — it is the cause of apprehending the true nature of both. This is what the <s>bhāṣya</s> illuminates — '<s>Puruṣa</s>, the owner, is conjoined with the seen, his own, through mere fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) alone, for the purpose of seeing (<s>darśana</s>).' The rest is easy to understand. One might object: the realization of the <s>draṣṭṛ</s>'s (seer's) own nature is what is released by this, hence <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) is stated, but <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) does not have a means [of accomplishment]; if so, this would cease to be <s>mokṣa</s> by its very nature. Therefore he (<s>Vyāsa</s>) says — 'The <s>saṃyoga</s> of a particular <s>puruṣa</s> with a particular <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) ends with the accomplishment of seeing (<s>darśana</s>)' — thus <s>darśana</s> is the cause of separation (<s>viyoga</s>).

children.text: tasya hetur avidyā //2.24//
children.translated_text: Its cause is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). (2.24)

children.text:
caturthaṃ vikalpaṃ nirdhārayituṃ sūtram avatārayati --- yas tu pratyakcetanasya
	  svabuddhisaṃyoga iti/ pratīpam añcati prāpnotīti pratyag asādhāraṇas tu saṃyoga
	  ekaikasya puruṣasyaikaikayā buddhyā vaicitryahetuḥ/ sūtraṃ paṭhati --- tasyeti/ nanv
	  avidyā viparyayajñānaṃ tasya bhogāpavargayor iva svabuddhisaṃyogo hetuḥ/ asaṃyuktāyāṃ
	  buddhau tadanutpattes tat katham avidyā

saṃyogabhedasya hetur ity ata āha
	  --- viparyayajñānavāsaneti/ sargāntarīyāyā avidyāyāḥ svacittena saha niruddhāyā api
	  pradhāne+asti vāsanā tadvāsanāvāsitaṃ ca pradhānaṃ tattatpuruṣasaṃyoginīṃ tādṛśīm eva
	  buddhiṃ sṛjati/ evaṃ pūrvapūrvasargeṣv ity anāditvād adoṣaḥ/ ata eva pratisargāvasthāyāṃ
	  na puruṣo mucyata ity āha --- viparyayajñāneti/ yadā puruṣakhyātiṃ kāryaniṣṭhāṃ prāptā
	  tadā viparyayajñānavāsanāyā bandhakāraṇasyābhāvān na punar āvartata ity āha --- sā tv
	  iti/ atra kaścin nāstikaḥ kaivalyaṃ paṇḍakopākhyānenopahasati/ paṇḍakopākhyānam āha ---
	  mugdhayeti/ kimartham ity arthaśabdo nimittam upalakṣayati prayojanasyāpi nimittatvāt/
	  paṇḍakopākhyānena sāmyam āpādayati --- tathedaṃ vidyamānaṃ guṇapuruṣānyatājñānaṃ
	  cittanivṛttiṃ na karoti, paravairāgyeṇa jñānaprasādamātreṇa sasaṃskāraṃ niruddhaṃ
	  vinaṣṭaṃ kariṣyatīti kā pratyāśā/ yasmin saty eva yad bhavati tat tasya kāryam/ na tu
	  yasminn asatīti bhāvaḥ/ atraikadeśimatena parihāram āha --- tatreti/ īṣadaparisamāpta
	  ācārya ācāryadeśīyaḥ/ ācāryas tu vāyuprokte kṛtalakṣaṇaḥ ---
children.translated_text: As for the cause of the cessation of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), hence he says — 'the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) of erroneous knowledge (<s>viparyayajñāna</s>).' Even though <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) from a prior creation has been ceased along with one's own mind, its <s>vāsanā</s> persists in <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial nature). And <s>pradhāna</s>, imbued with that <s>vāsanā</s>, creates a <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) of exactly the same kind, conjoined with each respective <s>Puruṣa</s>. Thus, [tracing back] through prior and prior creations — since this is beginningless, there is no fault [of infinite regress]. For this very reason, <s>Puruṣa</s> is not liberated even in the state of dissolution (<s>pratisarga</s>) — hence he says: 'the <s>vāsanā</s> of erroneous knowledge,' etc. When [<s>buddhi</s>] has reached <s>Puruṣa-khyāti</s> (discernment of <s>Puruṣa</s>) established in its effect, then, due to the absence of the <s>vāsanā</s> of erroneous knowledge — the cause of bondage — [<s>Puruṣa</s>] does not return again — hence he says: 'but that,' etc. Here a certain materialist (<s>nāstika</s>) mocks <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) with the parable of the eunuch (<s>paṇḍaka</s>). He relates the parable — 'by the infatuated [woman],' etc. 'For what purpose' — the word 'purpose' (<s>artha</s>) indicates the cause, since the purpose too is a cause. He draws the parallel with the eunuch's parable — 'Likewise, the existing knowledge of the distinction between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> does not bring about the cessation of the mind; what hope is there that through supreme dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), through mere clarity of knowledge (<s>jñānaprasādamātra</s>), [the mind], along with its <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions), will be ceased and destroyed?' That which occurs when something exists is the effect of that [thing]; but not [when] that [thing] is absent — such is the purport. He gives a refutation based on a partial view — 'therein,' etc. An <s>ācāryadeśīya</s> (quasi-teacher) is one who is slightly incomplete as a teacher. But a [true] <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) is defined in the <s>Vāyupurāṇa</s> —

In order to determine the fourth alternative, he introduces the <s>sūtra</s> — 'but the conjunction of the inward-facing consciousness (<s>pratyakcetana</s>) with its own <s>buddhi</s>' etc. <s>Pratyak</s> means that which reaches or attains inwardly; the distinctive conjunction, that of each individual <s>puruṣa</s> with each individual <s>buddhi</s>, is the cause of variety [in experience]. He reads the <s>sūtra</s> — 'of that (<s>tasya</s>)' etc. But one might object: <s>avidyā</s> is erroneous knowledge (<s>viparyayajñāna</s>); how can it be the cause of one's own conjunction with <s>buddhi</s>, just as [it is the cause] of experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>)? For when <s>buddhi</s> is not conjoined, that [erroneous knowledge] does not arise. How then can <s>avidyā</s> [be the cause]?

children.text:
"ācinoti ca śāstrārtham ācāre sthāpayaty api/ svayam ācarate yasmād ācāryas tena
	  cocyate"
vāyupurāṇam 59.30
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyupurāṇa</s> 59.30.

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: Thus.
'He gathers the meaning of the <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures), establishes it in practice, and himself practices [it] — therefore he is called an <s>ācārya</s> (teacher).'

children.text:
bhogavivekakhyātirūpapariṇatabuddhinivṛttir eva mokṣaḥ/ na ca buddhisvarūpanivṛttiḥ/ sā
	  ca dharmameghāntavivekakhyātipratiṣṭhāyā anantaram eva bhavati saty api
	  buddhisvarūpamātrāvasthāna ity arthaḥ/ etad eva sphorayati --- adarśanasya
	  bandhakāraṇasyābhāvād buddhinivṛttiḥ/

tac cādarśanaṃ bandhakāraṇaṃ darśanān
	  nivartate/ darśananivṛttis tu paravairāgyasādhyā/ saty api buddhisvarūpāvasthāne mokṣa
	  iti bhāvaḥ/ ekadeśimatam upanyasya svamatam āha --- tatra cittanivṛttir eva mokṣaḥ/
	  nanūktaṃ darśane nivṛtte+acirāc cittasvarūpanivṛttir bhavatīti kathaṃ darśanakāryety ata
	  āha --- kimartham asthāne mativibhrama iti/ ayam abhisaṃdhiḥ --- yadi darśanasya sākṣāc
	  cittanivṛttau kāraṇabhāvam aṅgīkurvīmahi tata evam upālabhyemahi/ kiṃ tu vivekadarśanaṃ
	  prakarṣakāṣṭhāṃ prāptaṃ nirodhasamādhibhāvanāprakarṣakrameṇa
	  cittanivṛttimatpuruṣasvarūpāvasthānopayogīty ātiṣṭhāmahe tat katham upālabhyemahīti //2.24//
children.translated_text: And that non-seeing (<s>adarśana</s>), the cause of bondage, ceases from seeing (<s>darśana</s>). The cessation of seeing, however, is accomplished by supreme dispassion (<s>paravairāgya</s>). Even though the essential nature of <s>buddhi</s> persists, there is liberation — such is the purport. Having presented the partial view, he states his own view — 'therein, the cessation of the mind itself is liberation.' [Objection:] But it was said that shortly after the cessation of seeing, the cessation of the mind's essential nature occurs — how then is it [described as] the effect of seeing? Hence he says — 'Why this confusion of intellect regarding what is not the [proper] place?' The purport is this: if we were to accept that seeing (<s>darśana</s>) is directly the cause of the cessation of the mind, then indeed we would be open to this criticism. But we maintain that the vision of discrimination (<s>vivekadarśana</s>), having reached the extreme limit of perfection, through the progression of the cultivation of <s>nirodha-samādhi</s> (cessation-absorption), serves the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s abiding in its own nature accompanied by the cessation of the mind — so how could we be criticized? //2.24//

Liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) is precisely the cessation of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) as transformed into the form of enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) and discriminative discernment (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) — not the cessation of <s>buddhi</s>'s essential nature. And that [cessation] occurs immediately after the establishment of <s>vivekakhyāti</s> culminating in <s>dharmamegha</s> [samādhi], even though the mere essential nature of <s>buddhi</s> persists — such is the meaning. He elaborates this very point — 'From the absence of non-seeing (<s>adarśana</s>), the cause of bondage, [comes] the cessation of <s>buddhi</s>.'

children.text: tadabhāvāt saṃyogābhāvo hānaṃ tad dṛśeḥ kaivalyam //2.25//
children.translated_text: 'From the absence of that [ignorance], the absence of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) — that is abandonment (<s>hāna</s>); that is <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) of the Seer (<s>dṛś</s>).' //2.25//

children.text:
tad evaṃ vyūhadvayam uktvā tṛtīyavyūhābhidhānāya sūtram avatārayti --- heyaṃ duḥkham
	  iti/ tadabhāvāt saṃyogābhāvo hānaṃ tad dṛśeḥ kaivalyam/ vyācaṣṭe --- tasyeti/ asti hi
	  mahāpralaye+api saṃyogābhāvo+ata uktam ātyantika iti/ duḥkhoparamo hānam iti
	  puruṣārthatā darśitā/ śeṣam atirohitam //2.25//
children.translated_text: Having thus stated two arrangements (<s>vyūhas</s>), to state the third arrangement he introduces the <s>sūtra</s> — 'the suffering to be abandoned,' etc. 'From the absence of that, the absence of conjunction — that is abandonment; that is the <s>kaivalya</s> of the Seer.' He explains — 'of that,' etc. Even at the time of <s>mahāpralaya</s> (great dissolution) there is absence of conjunction — hence it is said 'absolute' (<s>ātyantika</s>). 'The cessation of suffering is abandonment' — by this, the purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s> is shown. The rest is clear. //2.25//

children.text: vivekakhyātir aviplavā hānopāyaḥ //2.26//
children.translated_text: 'Unfaltering (<s>aviplavā</s>) discriminative discernment (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) is the means of abandonment (<s>hānopāya</s>).' //2.26//

children.text:
hānopāyalakṣaṇaṃ caturthaṃ vyūham ākhyātuṃ sūtram avatārayati --- atheti/ vivekakhyātir
	  aviplavā hānopāyaḥ/ āgamānumānābhyām api vivekakhyātir asti/ na cāsau vyutthānaṃ
	  tatsaṃskāraṃ vā nivartayati tadvato+api tadanuvṛtter iti tannivṛttyartham aviplaveti/
	  viplavo mithyājñānaṃ tadrahitā/ etad uktaṃ bhavati --- śrutamayena jñānena vivekaṃ
	  gṛhītvā yuktimayena ca vyavasthāpya dīrghakālanairantaryasatkārāsevitāyā bhāvanāyāḥ
	  prakarṣaparyantaṃ

samadhigatā sākṣātkāravatī vivekakhyātir
	  nivartitasavāsanamithyājñānā nirviplavā hānopāya iti/ śeṣaṃ sugamaṃ bhāṣyam //2.26//
children.translated_text: — which has reached direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>), with erroneous knowledge and its <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) removed, unfaltering — that is the means of abandonment. The rest of the <s>bhāṣya</s> (commentary) is easy to understand. //2.26//

To state the fourth arrangement — the definition of the means of abandonment — he introduces the <s>sūtra</s> — 'now,' etc. 'Unfaltering discriminative discernment is the means of abandonment.' Discriminative discernment also exists through scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and inference (<s>anumāna</s>). But that [kind] does not remove <s>vyutthāna</s> (the outgoing state) or its <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions), since they persist even in one who possesses it. Hence, for their removal — 'unfaltering' (<s>aviplavā</s>). <s>Viplava</s> is erroneous knowledge; [<s>aviplavā</s> is] free from that. What is being said is: having grasped discrimination through knowledge born of hearing (<s>śrutamaya jñāna</s>), and having established it through knowledge born of reasoning (<s>yuktimaya</s>), the discriminative discernment attained at the ultimate limit of the perfection of meditation cultivated with long duration, uninterruptedness, and reverence —

children.text: tasya saptadhā prāntabhūmiḥ prajñā //2.27//
children.translated_text: 'Of that [<s>yogin</s>], the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is sevenfold, on the final stage (<s>prāntabhūmi</s>).' //2.27//

children.text:
vivekakhyātiniṣṭhāyāḥ svarūpam āha sūtreṇa --- tasya saptadhā prāntabhūmiḥ prajñā/
	  vyācaṣṭe --- tasyeti pratyuditakhyāter vartamānakhyāter yoginaḥ pratyāmnāyaḥ parāmarśaḥ/
	  aśuddhir evāvaraṇaṃ cittasattvasya tad eva malaṃ tasyāpagamāc cittasya
	  pratyayāntarānutpāde tāmasarājasavyutthānapratyayānutpāde nirviplavavivekakhyātiniṣṭhām
	  āpannasya saptaprakāraiva prajñā vivekino bhavati/ viṣayabhedāt prajñābhedaḥ/ prakṛṣṭo
	  'nto yāsāṃ bhūmīnām avasthānāṃ tās tathoktāḥ/ yataḥ paraṃ nāsti sa prakarṣaḥ/ prāntā
	  bhūmayo yasyāḥ prajñāyā vivekakhyāteḥ sā tathoktā/ tā eva saptaprakārāḥ prāntabhūmīr
	  udāharati --- tadyatheti/ tatra puruṣaprayatnaniṣpādyāsu catasṛṣu bhūmiṣu prathamām
	  udāharati --- parijñātaṃ heyam/ yāvat kila prādhānikaṃ tat sarvaṃ pariṇāmatāpasaṃskārair
	  guṇavṛttivirodhād duḥkham eveti heyaṃ tat parijñātam/ prāntatāṃ darśayati --- nāsya
	  punaḥ kiṃcid aparijñātaṃ parijñeyam asti/ dvitīyām āha --- kṣīṇā iti/ prāntatām āha ---
	  na punar iti/ tṛtīyām āha --- sākṣātkṛtaṃ pratyakṣeṇa niścitaṃ mayā saṃprajñātāvasthāyām
	  eva

nirodhasamādhisādhyaṃ hānaṃ, na punar asyāḥ paraṃ niścetavyam astīti
	  śeṣaḥ/ caturthīm āha --- bhāvito niṣpādito vivekakhyātirūpo hānopāyo nāsyāḥ paraṃ
	  bhāvanīyam astīti śeṣaḥ/ eṣā catuṣṭayī kāryā vimuktiḥ samāptiḥ, kāryatayā
	  prayatnavyāpyatā darśitā/ kvacit pāṭhaḥ kāryavimuktir iti/ kāryāntareṇa vimuktiḥ
	  prajñāyā ity arthaḥ/ prayatnaniṣpādyānuniṣpādanīyām aprayatnasādhyāṃ cittavimuktim āha
	  --- cittavimuktis tu trayī/ prathamām āha --- caritādhikārā buddhiḥ/
	  kṛtabhogāpavargakāryety arthaḥ/ dvitīyām āha --- guṇā iti/ prāntatām āha --- na caiṣām
	  iti/ tṛtīyām āha --- etasyām avasthāyām iti/ etasyām avasthāyāṃ jīvann eva puruṣaḥ
	  kuśalo mukta ity ucyate caramadehatvād ity āha --- etām iti/ anaupacārikaṃ muktam āha
	  --- pratiprasave pradhānalaye+api cittasya muktaḥ kuśala ity eva bhavati guṇātītatvād
	  iti //2.27//
children.translated_text: the abandonment (<s>hāna</s>) achievable through <s>nirodha-samādhi</s> [has been realized]' — nothing further remains to be determined — such is the remainder. He states the fourth — 'The means of abandonment (<s>hānopāya</s>), in the form of <s>vivekakhyāti</s>, has been cultivated (<s>bhāvita</s>), accomplished' — nothing further remains to be cultivated — such is the remainder. This fourfold [wisdom] is the liberation pertaining to the task (<s>kāryā vimukti</s>), the completion; by [calling it] 'pertaining to the task,' its accessibility to effort is shown. In some readings: '<s>kāryavimukti</s>' — liberation from the task, liberation of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) through the task's completion — such is the meaning. He states the liberation pertaining to the mind (<s>cittavimukti</s>), which is effortless and not to be further accomplished — 'the liberation of the mind is threefold.' He states the first — 'The intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) has completed its function (<s>caritādhikāra</s>)' — meaning: having accomplished the purposes of experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) — such is the meaning. He states the second — 'the <s>guṇas</s>,' etc. He shows its culmination-nature — 'and these [<s>guṇas</s>] do not,' etc. He states the third — 'in this very state,' etc. In this state, even while living, <s>Puruṣa</s>, the adept (<s>kuśala</s>), is said to be liberated — because this is [his] final body — hence he says — 'this,' etc. He states the non-figurative liberation — 'in <s>pratiprasava</s> (involution), when the mind dissolves into <s>pradhāna</s>, the adept is indeed liberated, because he has transcended the <s>guṇas</s>.' //2.27//

He states the essential nature of the culmination of <s>vivekakhyāti</s> through the <s>sūtra</s> — 'Of that [yogin], the wisdom is sevenfold, on the final stage.' He explains — 'of that' refers to the <s>yogin</s> whose <s>khyāti</s> (discernment) has arisen, whose discernment is presently active. The impurity itself is the covering of the <s>cittasattva</s> (mind-in-its-pure-aspect); that itself is the defilement. Upon its departure, when no other cognition arises in the mind — when no <s>tāmasa</s> (inert), <s>rājasa</s> (active), or <s>vyutthāna</s> (outgoing) cognitions arise — for one who has attained the establishment of unfaltering <s>vivekakhyāti</s>, the wisdom of the discriminating one is sevenfold. The difference in wisdom is due to the difference of objects. Those stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) whose culmination (<s>anta</s>) is supreme (<s>prakṛṣṭa</s>) are so called. That beyond which nothing further exists is the culmination. That wisdom (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) whose stages are at their culmination is so called. He illustrates those seven kinds of culminating stages — 'namely,' etc. Among those, of the four stages achievable by personal effort, he illustrates the first — 'The abandonable (<s>heya</s>) is fully known (<s>parijñāta</s>).' Whatever pertains to <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial nature) — all of that, through transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>), affliction (<s>tāpa</s>), and latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and through the opposition of the <s>guṇa</s>-activities, is nothing but suffering — hence it is abandonable and is fully known. He shows its culmination-nature — 'Nothing further remains unrecognized that needs to be recognized.' He states the second — 'The causes [of suffering] are attenuated (<s>kṣīṇā</s>).' He shows its culmination — 'not again,' etc. He states the third — 'Directly realized (<s>sākṣātkṛta</s>) — determined by direct perception: by me, in the state of <s>saṃprajñāta</s> itself,

children.text: yogāṅgānuṣṭhānād aśuddhikṣaye jñānadīptir ā vivekakhyāteḥ //2.28//
children.translated_text: 'From the practice of the limbs of <s>yoga</s> (<s>yogāṅga</s>), upon the destruction of impurity (<s>aśuddhi</s>), there arises the light of knowledge (<s>jñānadīpti</s>), [extending] up to <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative discernment).' //2.28//

children.text:
tad evaṃ caturo vyūhān uktvā tanmadhyapatitasya hānopāyasya vivekakhyāter godohanādivat
	  prāgasiddher asiddhasya copāyatvābhāvāt siddhyupāyān vaktum ārabhata ity āha ---
	  siddheti/ tatrābhidhāsyamānānāṃ sādhanānāṃ yena prakāreṇa vivekakhyātyupāyatvaṃ tad
	  darśayati sūtreṇa --- yogāṅgānuṣṭhāṇād aśuddhikṣaye jñānadīptir ā vivekakhyāteḥ/
	  yogāṅgāni hi yathāyogaṃ

dṛṣṭādṛṣṭadvāreṇāśuddhiṃ kṣiṇvanti/ pañcaparvaṇo
	  viparyayasyety upalakṣaṇaṃ puṇyāpuṇyayor api jātyāyurbhogahetutvenāśuddhirūpatvād iti/
	  śeṣaṃ sugamam/ nānāvidhasya kāraṇabhāvasya darśanād yogāṅgānuṣṭhānasya kīdṛśaṃ
	  kāraṇatvam ity ata āha --- yogāṅgānuṣṭhānam iti/ aśuddhyā viyojayati buddhisattvam ity
	  aśuddher viyogakāraṇam/ dṛṣṭāntam āha --- yathā paraśur iti/ paraśuś chedyaṃ vṛkṣaṃ
	  mūlena viyojayati/ aśuddhyā viyojayad buddhisattvaṃ vivekakhyātiṃ prāpayati yathā
	  dharmaḥ sukham/ tathā yogāṅgānuṣṭhānaṃ vivekakhyāteḥ prāptikāraṇaṃ nānyena prakāreṇety
	  āha --- vivekakhyātes tv iti/ nānyatheti pratiṣedhaśravaṇāt pṛcchati --- kati caitānīti/
	  uttaram --- navaiveti/ tāni darśayati kārikayā --- tadyathā --- utpattīti/
	  atrodāharaṇāny āha --- tatrotpattikāraṇam iti/ mano hi vijñānam
	  avyapadeśyāvasthāto+apanīya vartamānāvasthām āpādayad utpattikāraṇaṃ vijñānasya/
	  sthitikāraṇaṃ manasaḥ puruṣārthatā/ asmitāyā utpannaṃ manas tāvad avatiṣṭhate na yāvad
	  dvividhaṃ puruṣārtham abhinirvartayati/ atha nirvartitapuruṣārthadvayaṃ sthiter apaiti/
	  tasmāt svakāraṇād utpannasya manaso+anāgatapuruṣārthatā sthitikāraṇam/ dṛṣṭāntam āha ---
	  śarīrasyeveti/ pratyakṣajñānanimittam
children.translated_text: They destroy impurity through seen and unseen means. 'Of the five-branched <s>viparyaya</s> (error)' is indicative [of impurity in general], since merit and demerit also have the form of impurity by being causes of birth, lifespan, and experience. The rest is clear. Since many kinds of causation are observed, what kind of causation does the practice of the limbs of <s>yoga</s> (<s>yogāṅga</s>) have? Hence he says — 'the practice of the limbs of <s>yoga</s>.' It separates the <s>sattva</s> of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) from impurity, hence it is the cause of separation from impurity. He gives an illustration — 'just as an axe': the axe separates the tree to be cut from its root. By separating the <s>sattva</s> of <s>buddhi</s> from impurity, it brings it to <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative discernment), just as <s>dharma</s> (merit) [brings] happiness. Thus, the practice of the limbs of <s>yoga</s> is the cause of attaining <s>vivekakhyāti</s> and not in any other way — hence he says: 'but of <s>vivekakhyāti</s>,' etc. Hearing the negation 'not otherwise,' he asks — 'and how many are these?' The answer — 'nine indeed.' He shows them with a verse — 'namely: origination,' etc. Here he gives examples — 'there, the cause of origination,' etc. For the mind (<s>manas</s>), removing cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>) from the indescribable state and bringing it to the present state, is the cause of origination of cognition. The cause of the persistence of <s>manas</s> is [its serving] the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>. <s>Manas</s>, having arisen from <s>asmitā</s> (ego-sense), persists so long as it has not accomplished the twofold purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>. Then, having accomplished the twofold purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, it departs from persistence. Therefore, the yet-to-be-fulfilled purposiveness for <s>Puruṣa</s> is the cause of persistence of <s>manas</s> that has arisen from its own cause. He gives an illustration — 'just as of the body,' etc. The cause of perceptual knowledge

children.text:
indriyadvārā vā svato vā viṣayasya
	  saṃskriyābhivyaktis tasyāḥ kāraṇaṃ yathā rūpasyālokaḥ/ vikārakāraṇaṃ manaso
	  viṣayāntaram/ yathā hi mṛkaṇḍoḥ samāhitamanaso
	  vallakīvipañcyamānapañcamasvaraśravaṇasamanantaram unmīlitākṣasya
	  svarūpalāvaṇyayauvanasaṃpannām apsarasaṃ pramlocām īkṣamāṇasya samādhim apahāya tasyāṃ
	  saktaṃ mano babhūveti/ atraiva nidarśanam āha --- yathāgniḥ pākyasya taṇḍulādeḥ
	  kaṭhināvayavasaṃniveśasya praśithilāvayavasaṃyogalakṣaṇasya vikārasya kāraṇam/ sata eva
	  viṣayasya pratyayakāraṇaṃ dhūmajñānam agnijñānasyeti/ jñāyata iti jñānam agniś cāsau
	  jñānaṃ cety agnijñānaṃ tasya/ etad uktaṃ bhavati --- vartamānasyaivāgner jñeyasya
	  pratyayakāraṇatayā kāraṇam iti/ autsargikī nirapekṣāṇāṃ kāraṇānāṃ kāryakriyā prāptis
	  tasyāḥ kutaścid apavādo 'prāptiḥ/ yathā nimnopasarpaṇasvabhāvānām apāṃ pratibandhaḥ
	  setunā tathehāpi buddhisattvasya sukhaprakāśaśīlasya svābhāvikī
	  sukhavivekakhyātijanakatā prāptiḥ/ sā kutaścid adharmāt tamaso vā pratibandhān na
	  bhavati/ dharmād yogāṅgānuṣṭhānād vā tadapanaye tadapratibaddhavṛttisvabhāvata eva
	  tajjanakatayā tad āpnoti/ yathā vakṣyati --- "nimittam aprayojakaṃ prakṛtīnāṃ
	  varaṇabhedas tu tataḥ kṣetrikavat"
children.translated_text: — the manifestation of the object's modification either through the door of the senses or by itself — and the cause of that, just as light [is the cause] of [perceiving] form. The cause of transformation of <s>manas</s> is a different object. Just as when <s>Mṛkaṇḍu</s>, whose mind was concentrated, upon hearing the fifth note being played on the <s>vallakī</s> (<s>vīṇā</s>), opened his eyes and saw the <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymph) <s>Pramlocā</s>, endowed with beauty of form, grace, and youth — his mind, abandoning <s>samādhi</s>, became attached to her. Here he gives another illustration — 'just as fire is the cause of the transformation of what is to be cooked, such as rice grains, from the state of having firm molecular arrangement to the state characterized by loosened molecular bonds.' 'The cause of the cognition of something existing is the cognition of smoke for the cognition of fire' — 'that which is known' is <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge); fire is that, and it is knowledge too — hence '<s>agnijñāna</s>' (fire-knowledge); of that. What is stated amounts to this: the fire, which is the knowable presently existing, serves as a cause in the capacity of being the cause of the cognition [of itself]. The natural capacity of independent causes to produce their effects is [their] attainment; the obstruction of that from some [source] is non-attainment. Just as the natural tendency of water to flow downward is obstructed by a dam, so too here, the natural capacity of the <s>sattva</s> of <s>buddhi</s>, whose nature is happiness and luminosity, to generate happiness and <s>vivekakhyāti</s> is its attainment. That [capacity] does not [manifest] due to obstruction from <s>adharma</s> (demerit) or <s>tamas</s> (inertia). Through <s>dharma</s> or the practice of the limbs of <s>yoga</s>, upon the removal of that [obstruction], by its very nature of unobstructed activity, it generates that [discriminative discernment] and thus attains it. As will be stated: 'The incidental cause does not move the natural tendencies into activity, but merely removes the obstacles, like a farmer [removing a dam to let water flow]'

children.text: yogasūtram 4.3
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>Yogasūtra</s> 4.3]

children.text:
iti/ tad evaṃ
	  vivekakhyātilakṣaṇakāryāpekṣayā prāptikāraṇam uktam/ avāntarakāryāpekṣayā tu tad eva
	  viyogakāraṇam ity āha --- viyogakāraṇam iti/ anyatvakāraṇam āha --- anyatvakāraṇaṃ yathā
	  suvarṇakāraḥ suvarṇasya, kaṭakakuṇḍalakeyūrādibhyo bhinnābhinnasya bhedavivakṣayā
	  kaṭakādibhinnasyābhedavivakṣayā kaṭakādyabhinnasya suvarṇasya kuṇḍalād anyatvam/ tathā
	  ca kaṭakakārī suvarṇakāraḥ kuṇḍalād abhinnāt suvarṇād anyat kurvann anyatvakāraṇam/
	  agnir api pākyasyānyatvakāraṇaṃ yady api tathāpi dharmiṇo dharmayoḥ
	  pulākatvataṇḍulatvayor bhedāvivakṣayā dharmayor upajanāpāye+api dharmyanuvartata iti na
	  tasyānyatvaṃ śakyaṃ vaktum iti vikāramātrakāraṇatvam uktam iti na saṃkaraḥ/ na ca
	  saṃsthānabhedo dharmiṇo 'nyatvakāraṇam iti vyākhyeyam/ suvarṇakāra ity asyāsaṃgateḥ/
	  bāhyam anyatvakāraṇam upanyasyādhyātmikam udāharati --- evam ekasyeti/ avidyā
	  kamanīyeyaṃ kanyaketyādijñānam/ tanmohayogāt sa eva strīpratyayo
children.translated_text: Thus, the cause of attainment has been stated with respect to the effect characterized as <s>vivekakhyāti</s>. But with respect to the intermediate effect, that same [practice] is the cause of separation — hence he says: 'the cause of separation,' etc. He states the cause of otherness — 'the cause of otherness, just as a goldsmith of gold': gold, which is both different and non-different from bracelet, earring, armlet, and the like — when difference is intended, it is different from bracelet and the like; when non-difference is intended, it is non-different from bracelet and the like — the otherness of gold from an earring [is thus established]. And so the goldsmith who makes bracelets, producing something other than the earring from gold that is non-different from the earring, is the cause of otherness. Fire too is the cause of otherness of what is to be cooked; yet even so, when the two properties — being husk and being grain — of the substance [change], even though the two properties arise and perish, the substance persists — therefore its otherness cannot be said, and so only the causation of mere modification is stated; thus there is no confusion. Nor should it be explained that mere difference of shape is the cause of otherness of the substance — for that would be inconsistent with the goldsmith [example]. Having presented an external [example of] the cause of otherness, he illustrates an internal one — 'thus, of one [and the same],' etc. <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the knowledge 'this is a lovable maiden,' etc. Through the influence of that delusion, that very cognition of 'woman'

children.text:
mūḍho
	  viṣaṇṇo bhavati caitrasya maitrasya puṇyavato bata kalatraratnam etan na tu mama
	  bhāgyahīnasyeti/ evaṃ sapatnījanasya tasyāṃ dveṣaḥ strīpratyayasya duḥkhatve/ evaṃ
	  maitrasya tasyā bhartū rāgas tasyaiva strīpratyayasya sukhatve/ tattvajñānaṃ
	  tvaṅmāṃsamedo'sthimajjāsamūhaḥ strīkāyaḥ sthānabījādibhir aśucir iti vivekināṃ
	  mādhyasthye vairāgye kāraṇam iti/ dhṛtikāraṇaṃ śarīram indriyāṇāṃ vidhārakam indriyāṇi
	  ca śarīrasya sāmānyā karaṇavṛttir hi prāṇādyā vāyavaḥ pañca tadabhāve śarīrapātāt/ evaṃ
	  māṃsādikāyāṅgānām api parasparavidhāryavidhārakatvam/ evaṃ mahābhūtāni pṛthivyādīni
	  manuṣyavaruṇasūryagandhavahaśaśilokanivāsināṃ śarīrāṇāṃ, tāni ca parasparaṃ, pṛthivyāṃ
	  hi gandharasarūpasparśaśabdaguṇāyāṃ pañca mahābhūtāni parasparaṃ
	  vidhāryavidhārakabhāvenāvasthitāny apsu catvāri tejasi trīṇi dve ca mātariśvanīti/
	  tairyagyaunamānuṣadaivatādīni ca vidhāryavidhārakabhāvenāvasthitāni/ nanv
	  ādhārādheyabhāvarahitānāṃ kutas tattvam ity ata āha --- parasparārthatvād iti/
	  manuṣyaśarīraṃ hi paśupakṣimṛgasarīsṛpasthāvaraśarīropayogena dhriyate/ evaṃ
	  vyāghrādiśarīram api manuṣyapaśumṛgādiśarīropayogena/ evaṃ paśumṛgādiśarīram api
	  sthāvarādyupayogena/ evaṃ daivaśarīram api
	  manuṣyopahṛtacchāgamṛgakapiñjalamāṃsājyapuroḍāśasahakāraśākhāprastarādibhir ijyamānaṃ
	  tadupayogena/ evaṃ devatāpi varadānavṛṣṭyādibhir manuṣyādīni dhārayatīty asti
	  parasparārthatvam ity arthaḥ/ śeṣaṃ sugamam //2.28//
children.translated_text: — [the person becomes] deluded and despondent: 'Alas, this jewel of a wife belongs to <s>Caitra</s> [or] to fortunate <s>Maitra</s>, but not to unfortunate me.' Thus, the hatred of the co-wife's people toward her, when the cognition of 'woman' is [experienced as] painful. Likewise, the attachment of <s>Maitra</s>, her husband, when that very cognition of 'woman' is [experienced as] pleasant. But the knowledge of reality — 'the female body is a mass of skin, flesh, fat, bones, and marrow; it is impure due to its location, [reproductive] seed, and the like' — this, for the discerning, is the cause of equanimity and dispassion. The cause of sustenance: the body sustains the sense organs, and the sense organs sustain the body; the general function of the instruments — for the five <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) and the like are winds, and in their absence, the body would fall. Likewise, the limbs of the body such as flesh and the like mutually sustain one another. Similarly, the great elements — earth and the like — [sustain] the bodies of those dwelling in the worlds of humans, <s>Varuṇa</s>, the sun, the wind-god, and the moon; and they [sustain] each other — for in earth, which has the qualities of smell, taste, form, touch, and sound, five great elements abide in a relationship of mutual sustenance; in water, four; in fire, three; and two in air. And the animal, human, divine, and other [forms of life] also abide in a relationship of mutual sustenance. But if they lack the relationship of support and supported, whence is their reality? Hence he says — 'because of mutual purposiveness.' For the human body is sustained by the use of animals, birds, wild beasts, reptiles, and plants. Likewise, the body of a tiger and the like is sustained by the use of human, cattle, wild beast, and other bodies. Similarly, the body of cattle, wild beasts, and the like is sustained by the use of plants and the like. Likewise, the divine body too, being worshipped with goat-meat, deer-meat, quail-meat, ghee, sacred cakes (<s>puroḍāśa</s>), mango branches, sacrificial grass (<s>prastara</s>), and the like offered by humans, is sustained by that use. And the deities too sustain humans and the like through boons, rain, and the like — thus there is mutual purposiveness, such is the meaning. The rest is clear. (2.28)

Having thus stated the four arrangements (<s>vyūhas</s>), since <s>vivekakhyāti</s>, which falls within the means of abandonment, had not been previously established — like [the process of] milking a cow and the like — and since what has not been established cannot serve as a means, he begins to state the means of its establishment — hence he says: 'the established,' etc. He shows in what manner the means to be described serve as the means of <s>vivekakhyāti</s>, through the <s>sūtra</s> — 'From the practice of the limbs of <s>yoga</s>, upon the destruction of impurity, [there arises] the light of knowledge, up to <s>vivekakhyāti</s>.' For the limbs of <s>yoga</s>, each in its respective manner —

children.text: yamaniyamāsanaprāṇāyāmapratyāhāradhāraṇādhyānasamādhayo 'ṣṭāv aṅgāni //2.29//
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> (restraint), <s>niyama</s> (observance), <s>āsana</s> (posture), <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control), <s>pratyāhāra</s> (sense-withdrawal), <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) are the eight limbs. (2.29)

children.text:
saṃprati nyūnādhikasaṃkhyāvyavacchedārthaṃ yogāṅgāny avadhārayati --- tatra yogāṅgāny
	  avadhāryanta iti/ yamaniyamāsanaprāṇāyāmapratyāhāradhāraṇādhyānasamādhayo 'ṣṭāv aṅgāni/

abhyāsavairāgyaśraddhāvīryādayo 'pi yathāyogam eteṣv eva svarūpato
	  nāntarīyakatayā cāntarbhāvayitavyāḥ //2.29//
children.translated_text: <s>Abhyāsa</s> (practice), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), <s>śraddhā</s> (faith), <s>vīrya</s> (energy), and the like are also to be subsumed, as appropriate, within these very [eight limbs], either by their essential nature or as necessary concomitants. (2.29)

Now, for the purpose of excluding a lesser or greater number, he ascertains the limbs of <s>yoga</s> — 'there, the limbs of <s>yoga</s> are ascertained.' '<s>Yama</s>, <s>niyama</s>, <s>āsana</s>, <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, <s>pratyāhāra</s>, <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> are the eight limbs.'

children.text: ahiṃsāsatyāsteyabrahmacaryāparigrahā yamāḥ //2.30//
children.translated_text: Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), truthfulness (<s>satya</s>), non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>), celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), and non-possessiveness (<s>aparigraha</s>) are the <s>yamas</s> (restraints). (2.30)

children.text:
yamaniyamādyaṅgāny uddiśya yamanirdeśakaṃ sūtram avatārayati --- tatreti/
	  ahiṃsāsatyāsteyabrahmacaryāparigrahā yamāḥ/ yogāṅgam ahiṃsām āha --- sarvatheti/ īdṛśīm
	  ahiṃsāṃ stauti --- uttare ceti/ tanmūlā ity ahiṃsām aparipālya kṛtā apy akṛtakalpā
	  niṣphalatvād ity arthaḥ/ tatsiddhiparatayaivānuṣṭhānam/ ahiṃsā cen mūlam uttareṣāṃ
	  kathaṃ te+ahiṃsāsiddhiparā ity ata āha --- tatpratipādanāyeti/ siddhir jñānaṃ notpattir
	  ity arthaḥ/ syād etat/ ahiṃsājñānārthā yady uttare kṛtaṃ tair anyata eva tadavagamād ity
	  ata āha --- tadavadāteti/ yady uttare nānuṣṭhīyerann ahiṃsā malinā syād asatyādibhir ity
	  arthaḥ/ atraivāgamikānāṃ saṃmatim āha --- tathā ceti/ sugamam/ satyalakṣaṇam āha ---
	  yathārthe vāṅmanase iti/ yathāśabdaṃ sākāṅkṣaṃ pūrayati --- yathā dṛṣṭam iti/
	  pratisaṃbandhinaṃ tathāśabdaṃ pratikṣipati --- tathā vāṅmanaś ca vivakṣāyāṃ kartavyāyām
	  iti/ anyathā tu na satyam etat sopapattikam āha --- paratra puruṣe svabodhasaṃkrāntaye
	  svabodhasadṛśabodhajananāya vāg uktoccāritā, ataḥ sā yadi na vañcitā vañcikā yathā
	  droṇācāryeṇa svatanayāśvatthāmamaraṇam āyuṣman satyadhanāśvatthāmā hata iti pṛṣṭasya
	  yudhiṣṭhirasya prativacanaṃ hastinam abhisaṃdhāya satyaṃ hato+aśvatthāmeti,

tad idam uktasyottaraṃ na yudhiṣṭhirasya svabodhaṃ saṃkrāmayati --- svabodho hy asya
	  hastihananaviṣaya indriyajanmā, na cāsau saṃkrāntaḥ kiṃ tv anya eva tasya
	  tanayavadhabodho jāta iti/ bhrāntā vā bhrāntijā vā, bhrāntiś ca vivakṣāsamaye vā
	  jñeyārthāvadhāraṇasamaye vā/ pratipattyā vandhyā pratipattivandhyā yathārthān prati
	  mlecchabhāṣā pratipattivandhyā, niṣprayojanā vā syād iti yathānapekṣitābhidhānā vāk
	  tatra hi paratra svabodhasya saṃkrāntir apy asaṃkrāntir eva niṣprayojanatvād iti/
	  evaṃlakṣaṇam api satyaṃ parāpakāraphalaṃ satyābhāsaṃ na tu satyam ity āha --- eṣeti/
	  tadyathā satyatapasas taskaraiḥ sārthagamanaṃ pṛṣṭasya sārthagamanābhidhānam iti/
	  abhidhīyamānoccāryamāṇā/ śeṣaṃ sugamam/ abhāvasya bhāvādhīnanirūpaṇatayā steyalakṣaṇam
	  āha --- steyam aśāstrapūrvakam iti/ viśeṣeṇa sāmānyaṃ lakṣyata ity arthaḥ/
	  mānasavyāpārapūrvakatvād vācanikakāyikavyāpārayoḥ prādhānyān manovyāpāra
	  ukto+aspṛhārūpam iti/ brahmacaryasvarūpam āha --- gupteti/ saṃyatopastho+api hi
	  strīprekṣaṇatadālāpakandarpāyatanatadaṅgasparśanasakto na brahmacaryavān iti
	  tannirāsāyoktaṃ guptendriyasyeti/ indriyāntarāṇy api tatra lolupāni rakṣaṇīyānīti/
	  aparigrahasvarūpam āha --- viṣayāṇām iti/ tatra saṅgadoṣa ukto bhogābhyāsam anu
	  vivardhante rāgāḥ kauśalāni cendriyāṇām iti, hiṃsālakṣaṇaś ca doṣo nānupahatya bhūtāny
	  upabhogaḥ saṃbhavatīti/ aśāstrīyāṇām ayatnopanatānām api viṣayāṇāṃ
	  ninditapratigrahādirūpārjanadoṣadarśanāc chāstrīyāṇām apy upārjitānāṃ ca
	  rakṣaṇādidoṣadarśanād asvīkaraṇam aparigrahaḥ //2.30//
children.translated_text: — that utterance does not transfer <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s own cognition [to <s>Droṇa</s>]. For his own cognition, born from sense-perception, had the killing of the elephant as its object, and that [cognition] was not transferred; rather, a different cognition — of the death of his son — arose [in <s>Droṇa</s>]. Or [speech may be] deluded or born of delusion — delusion either at the time of the intention to speak or at the time of ascertaining the object to be communicated. Or [it may be] barren with respect to its [intended] cognition — i.e., fruitless for comprehension, like the language of barbarians (<s>mlecchas</s>) [which is] incomprehensible to [the intended hearers]. Or it might be purposeless — like an utterance made without regard [for the listener]. For therein, even if one's own cognition is transferred to another, it is as if not transferred, because it is purposeless. Even truthfulness having these characteristics, if its fruit is harm to others, is [only] an appearance of truth, not [real] truth — thus he says: 'this.' For example, the ascetic of truth (<s>satyatapas</s>), when asked by robbers about a caravan's route, declares the caravan's route — [this is] uttered and pronounced. The rest is easy to understand. Since non-existence is defined in dependence on existence, he states the definition of stealing (<s>steya</s>): 'stealing is [taking something] without scriptural authorization.' The universal is characterized by the particular — this is the meaning. Since verbal and bodily activities are preceded by mental activity, he states the mental activity as primary: 'in the form of non-covetousness.' He states the essential nature of celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>): 'of guarded [senses].' For even one who has controlled his sexual organ, if he is attached to gazing at women, conversing with them, the seat of desire, and touching their limbs — he is not a <s>brahmacārin</s>. Hence, to exclude that, it was said 'of one whose senses are guarded.' The other senses too, being eager in that [direction], are to be guarded. He states the essential nature of non-possessiveness (<s>aparigraha</s>): 'of sense-objects.' Therein, the fault of attachment is stated — 'through the habitual practice of enjoyments, desires increase, and the skills of the sense organs [grow].' And the fault characterized by violence [is stated] — 'enjoyment is not possible without harming living beings.' Due to seeing the fault of acquisition — in the form of accepting condemned gifts, etc. — even of objects that come unsought without scriptural authorization, and due to seeing the faults of guarding, etc., even of objects acquired with scriptural authorization — non-acceptance is <s>aparigraha</s>. (2.30)

Aiming at the limbs [of <s>Yoga</s>] beginning with <s>yama</s> (restraints) and <s>niyama</s> (observances), he introduces the <s>sūtra</s> that specifies the <s>yamas</s>: 'therein.' [<s>Sūtra</s> 2.30:] <s>Ahiṃsāsatyāsteyabrahmacaryāparigrahā yamāḥ</s> — 'Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), truthfulness (<s>satya</s>), non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>), celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), and non-possessiveness (<s>aparigraha</s>) are the <s>yamas</s> (restraints).' He states <s>ahiṃsā</s> as a limb of <s>Yoga</s>: 'in all ways.' He praises this kind of <s>ahiṃsā</s>: 'and the subsequent ones.' 'Rooted in it' means that the subsequent [<s>yamas</s>], even if practiced without safeguarding <s>ahiṃsā</s>, are as if not practiced, being fruitless — this is the meaning. Their practice is undertaken solely for the purpose of perfecting it [<s>ahiṃsā</s>]. If <s>ahiṃsā</s> is the root of the subsequent ones, how are they directed toward the perfection of <s>ahiṃsā</s>? To this he replies: 'for its elucidation.' 'Perfection' means knowledge, not [mere] production — this is the meaning. One might say: if the subsequent ones are for the sake of knowing <s>ahiṃsā</s>, they are done for another purpose since its understanding [can come] from elsewhere. To this he replies: 'its purity.' If the subsequent ones were not practiced, <s>ahiṃsā</s> would be impure — tainted by falsehood, etc. — this is the meaning. Here he states the agreement of the scriptural authorities: 'and so.' [This is] easy to understand. He states the definition of truthfulness (<s>satya</s>): 'speech and mind in accordance with the object (<s>artha</s>).' He completes the incomplete 'yathā' (as): 'as seen.' He rejects the correlative 'tathā' (so): 'so too, speech and mind should be employed when there is an intention to communicate.' Otherwise it is not truthfulness — this he states with reasoning: speech is uttered, pronounced, for the purpose of transferring one's own cognition to another person — i.e., for generating in them a cognition similar to one's own. Therefore, if that [speech] is not deceitful or deceptive — as, for example, [the reply of] <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> when asked by Teacher <s>Droṇa</s> about the death of his own son <s>Aśvatthāman</s>, [who said] 'O long-lived one, <s>Aśvatthāman</s> of true wealth is slain' — meaning the elephant [named <s>Aśvatthāman</s>], truthfully [saying] '<s>Aśvatthāman</s> is slain,'

children.text: jātideśakālasamayānavacchinnāḥ sārvabhaumā mahāvratam //2.31//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 2.31:] <s>Jātideśakālasamayānavacchinnāḥ sārvabhaumā mahāvratam</s> — 'When not limited by birth, place, time, or circumstance, [the <s>yamas</s>] are universal — [this is called] the great vow (<s>mahāvrata</s>).' (2.31)

children.text:
sāmānyata uktā yādṛśāḥ punar yoginām upādeyās tādṛśān vaktuṃ sūtram avatārayati --- te
	  tv iti/ jātideśakālasamayānavacchinnāḥ sārvabhaumā mahāvratam/ sarvāsu jātyādilakṣaṇāsu
	  bhūmiṣu viditāḥ sārvabhaumāḥ/ ahiṃsādaya ity anyatrāpy avaccheda ūhanīyaḥ/ sugamaṃ
	  bhāṣyam //2.31//
children.translated_text: In order to state the form in which they are to be adopted by <s>yogins</s> — [the <s>yamas</s>] having been stated in general — he introduces the <s>sūtra</s>: 'But these.' [<s>Sūtra</s>:] 'When not limited by birth, place, time, or circumstance, [they are] universal — the great vow.' 'Known across all stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) characterized by birth, etc.' means 'universal.' '<s>Ahiṃsā</s>, etc.' — the non-limitation should be extended to the others as well. The <s>Bhāṣya</s> is easy to understand. (2.31)

children.text: śaucasaṃtoṣatapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni niyamāḥ //2.32//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 2.32:] <s>Śaucasaṃtoṣatapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni niyamāḥ</s> — 'Purity (<s>śauca</s>), contentment (<s>saṃtoṣa</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), and devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> (<s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s>) are the <s>niyamas</s> (observances).' (2.32)

children.text:
śaucādiniyamān ācaṣṭe --- śaucasaṃtoṣatapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni niyamāḥ/ vyācaṣṭe
	  --- śaucam iti/ ādiśabdena gomayādayo gṛhyante/ gomūtrayāvakādi medhyaṃ
	  tasyābhyavaharaṇādi/ ādiśabdād grāsaparimāṇasaṃkhyāniyamādayo grāhyāḥ/
	  medhyābhyavaharaṇādijanitam iti vaktavye medhyābhyavaharaṇādi cety uktaṃ kārye
	  kāraṇopacārāt/ cittamalā madamānāsūyādayas tadapanayo manaḥśaucam/ prāṇatrāṇamātrahetor
	  abhyadhikasyānupāditsā saṃtoṣaḥ prāg eva svīkaraṇaparityāgād iti śeṣaḥ/

kāṣṭhamaunam iṅgitenāpi svābhiprāyāprakāśanam/ avacanamātram ākāramaunam/
	  parikṣīṇavitarkajāla iti vitarko vakṣyamāṇaḥ saṃśayaviparyayau veti/ etāvatā
	  śuddho+abhisaṃdhir uktaḥ/ ete ca yamaniyamā viṣṇupurāṇa uktāḥ ---
children.translated_text: 'Silence of the stick' (<s>kāṣṭhamauna</s>) is the non-disclosure of one's own intention even by gesture. Mere non-speaking is 'silence of form' (<s>ākāramauna</s>). 'One whose web of <s>vitarkas</s> (discursive thoughts) has withered' — '<s>vitarka</s>' here is to be described [later]; it means doubt and error. By this much, purity of intention is stated. And these <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> are stated in the <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s>:

He describes the <s>niyamas</s> beginning with purity: '<s>Śauca</s>, <s>saṃtoṣa</s>, <s>tapas</s>, <s>svādhyāya</s>, and <s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s> are the <s>niyamas</s>.' He explains: 'purity.' By the word 'ādi' (and others), cow-dung, etc., are understood. Cow-urine, barley-gruel, and the like are pure (<s>medhya</s>) — their consumption, etc. [constitutes external purity]. By the word 'ādi,' rules regarding the measure and number of morsels, etc., should also be understood. [The text says] 'medhyābhyavaharaṇādi ca' (and the consumption of pure things) instead of [the expected] 'medhyābhyavaharaṇādijanitam' (born from the consumption of pure things) — this is metonymy of cause for effect. The mental impurities (<s>cittamala</s>) — pride (<s>mada</s>), conceit (<s>māna</s>), envy (<s>asūyā</s>), etc. — their removal is mental purity. Contentment (<s>saṃtoṣa</s>) is the non-desire for anything more than what is needed for the mere preservation of life — let alone the renunciation of what has already been accepted. This is the remainder.

children.text:
"brahmacaryam ahiṃsāṃ ca satyāsteyāparigrahān/ seveta yogī niṣkāmo yogyatāṃ svamano
	  nayan// svādhyāyaśaucasaṃtoṣatapāṃsi niyatātmavān/ kurvīta brahmaṇi tathā parasmin
	  pravaṇaṃ manaḥ// ete yamāḥ saniyamāḥ pañca pañca prakīrtitāḥ/ viśiṣṭaphaladāḥ kāmyā
	  niṣkāmānāṃ (niṣkāmāṇāṃ) vimuktidāḥ"

viṣṇupurāṇam
	  6.7.36--38
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> 6.7.36–38

'The desireless <s>yogin</s> should observe celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), truthfulness (<s>satya</s>), non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>), and non-possessiveness (<s>aparigraha</s>), directing his mind toward fitness [for <s>Yoga</s>]. The self-controlled one should perform self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), purity (<s>śauca</s>), contentment (<s>saṃtoṣa</s>), and austerities (<s>tapas</s>), and likewise make the mind inclined toward the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. These <s>yamas</s> together with <s>niyamas</s>, five and five, are declared. They bestow distinguished fruits when desired; for the desireless, they bestow liberation.'

children.text: vitarkabādhane pratipakṣabhāvanam //2.33//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 2.33:] <s>Vitarkabādhane pratipakṣabhāvanam</s> — 'When [<s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s>] are disturbed by <s>vitarkas</s> (contrary thoughts), [one should cultivate] the opposite (<s>pratipakṣa</s>).' (2.33)

children.text:
"śreyāṃsi bahuvighnāni" ity eṣām apavādasaṃbhave tatpratīkāropadeśaparaṃ sūtram
	  avatārayati --- eteṣāṃ yamaniyamānām iti/ sūtraṃ --- vitarkabādhane pratipakṣabhāvanam/
	  vitarkāṇāṃ
bhāṣye nāsti tirohitam iva kiṃcana //2.33//
children.translated_text: — nothing is concealed in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. (2.33)

Since 'meritorious endeavors have many obstacles,' when there is the possibility of exceptions to these [<s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s>], he introduces the <s>sūtra</s> that teaches their antidote: 'of these <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s>.' The <s>sūtra</s>: 'When [they are] disturbed by <s>vitarkas</s>, [one should cultivate] the opposite.' The <s>vitarkas</s>

children.text:
vitarkā hiṃsādayaḥ kṛtakāritānumoditā lobhakrodhamohapūrvakā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā
	    duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam //2.34//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 2.34:] <s>Vitarkā hiṃsādayaḥ kṛtakāritānumoditā lobhakrodhamohapūrvakā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam</s> — 'The contrary thoughts — violence, etc. — whether done, caused to be done, or approved of; preceded by greed, anger, or delusion; mild, medium, or intense — [the reflection that] their fruit is endless suffering and ignorance: this is the cultivation of the opposite.' (2.34)

children.text:
tatra vitarkāṇāṃ svarūpaprakārakāraṇadharmaphalabhedān pratipakṣabhāvānāviṣayān
	  pratipakṣabhāvanāsvarūpābhidhitsayā sūtreṇāha --- vitarkā hiṃsādayaḥ kṛtakāritānumoditā
	  lobhakrodhamohapūrvakā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam/
	  vyācaṣṭe --- tatra hiṃseti/ prāṇabhṛdbhedasyāparisaṃkhyeyatvān niyamavikalpasamuccayāḥ
	  saṃbhavino hiṃsādiṣu/ tatrādharmatas tamaḥsamudreke sati
	  caturvidhaviparyayalakṣaṇasyājñānasyāpy udaya ity ajñānaphalatvam apy eteṣām iti/
	  duḥkhājñānānantaphalatvam eva hi pratipakṣabhāvanaṃ tadvaśād ebhyo nivṛtter iti/ tad eva
	  pratipakṣabhāvanaṃ sphorayati --- vadhyasya paśvāder vīryaṃ prayatnaṃ kāyavyāpārahetuṃ

prathamam ākṣipati yūpaniyojanena/ tena hi paśor aprāgalbhyaṃ bhavati/
	  śeṣam atisphuṭam //2.34//
children.translated_text: is first seized through binding [the animal] to the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>). For by that, the animal's boldness is [suppressed]. The rest is very clear. (2.34)

Therein, wishing to state the essential nature of the cultivation of the opposite — [covering] the varieties of the <s>vitarkas</s>' essential nature, mode, cause, properties, and fruits, which are the domain of <s>pratipakṣabhāvana</s> — he states [it] with the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>Vitarkas</s> — violence, etc. — done, caused to be done, or approved; preceded by greed, anger, or delusion; mild, medium, or intense — [the reflection that] their fruit is endless suffering and ignorance: this is the cultivation of the opposite.' He explains: 'therein, violence.' Since the varieties of living beings are innumerable, combinations, permutations, and aggregations are possible in violence, etc. Therein, through unrighteousness (<s>adharma</s>), when there is a preponderance of <s>tamas</s> (inertia), there is also the arising of ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) characterized by the fourfold error (<s>viparyaya</s>) — hence these [<s>vitarkas</s>] also have ignorance as their fruit. It is precisely [the reflection on] their having endless suffering and ignorance as their fruit that constitutes the cultivation of the opposite, since cessation from these [<s>vitarkas</s>] occurs through the force of that [reflection]. He makes explicit that very cultivation of the opposite: 'the energy of the victim — the animal, etc. — the effort that is the cause of bodily activity,'

children.text: ahiṃsāpratiṣṭhāyāṃ tatsaṃnidhau vairatyāgaḥ //2.35//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 2.35:] <s>Ahiṃsāpratiṣṭhāyāṃ tatsaṃnidhau vairatyāgaḥ</s> — 'When non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) is firmly established, in [the <s>yogin</s>'s] presence there is the abandonment of hostility.' (2.35)

children.text:
uktā yamaniyamās tadapavādakānāṃ ca vitarkāṇāṃ pratipakṣabhāvanāto hānir uktā, saṃpraty
	  apratyūhaṃ yamaniyamābhyāsāt tatsiddhiparijñānasūcakāni cihnāny upanyasyati
	  yatparijñānād yogī tatra tatra kṛtakṛtyaḥ kartavyeṣu pravartata ity āha (ti) --- yadeti
	  (pratipakṣeti)/ ahiṃsāpratiṣṭhāyāṃ tatsaṃnidhau vairatyāgaḥ/ śāśvatikavirodhā apy
	  aśvamahiṣamūṣakamārjārāhinakulādayo 'pi bhagavataḥ pratiṣṭhitāhiṃsasya saṃnidhānāt
	  taccittānukāriṇo vairaṃ parityajantīti //2.35//
children.translated_text: The <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> have been stated, and the abandonment of the <s>vitarkas</s> that would violate them through the cultivation of the opposite has been stated. Now he presents the signs indicating the attainment of perfection in each, through the unobstructed practice of <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> — knowing which, the <s>yogin</s> takes up the subsequent duties, having accomplished what was to be accomplished in each case. Thus he says: 'when.' 'When non-violence is firmly established, in his presence there is the abandonment of hostility.' Even beings that are eternally hostile to each other — such as horses and buffaloes, mice and cats, snakes and mongooses, and the like — due to the proximity of the blessed one who is firmly established in <s>ahiṃsā</s>, imitating his mental state, abandon their hostility. (2.35)

children.text: satyapratiṣṭhāyāṃ kriyāphalāśrayatvam //2.36//
children.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 2.36:] <s>Satyapratiṣṭhāyāṃ kriyāphalāśrayatvam</s> — 'When truthfulness (<s>satya</s>) is firmly established, actions and their fruits depend [upon his words].' (2.36)

children.text:
satyapratiṣṭhāyāṃ kriyāphalāśrayatvam/ kriyāsādhyau dharmādharmau kriyā tatphalaṃ ca
	  svarganarakādi te evāśrayatīty āśrayas tasya bhāvas tattvaṃ tad asya bhagavato vāco
	  bhavatīti/ kriyāśrayatvam āha --- dhārmika iti/ phalāśrayatvam āha --- svargam iti/
	  amoghāpratihatā //2.36//
children.translated_text: When established in truthfulness (<s>satya</s>), there is dependence of actions and their fruits [upon one's words]. <s>Dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) are accomplished through action; action and its fruit — heaven, hell, and so forth — depend upon [his words]; the state of being their support is the reality of the blessed one's speech. He states the dependence of action — 'the righteous one' etc. He states the dependence of the fruit — 'heaven' etc. [His words are] unfailing and unobstructed. (2.36)

children.text: asteyapratiṣṭhāyāṃ sarvaratnopasthānam //2.37//
children.translated_text: When established in non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>), all gems present themselves. (2.37)

children.text: asteyapratiṣṭhāyāṃ sarvaratnopasthānam/ subodham //2.37//
children.translated_text: When established in non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>), all gems present themselves. This is easy to understand. (2.37)

children.text: brahmacaryapratiṣṭhāyāṃ vīryalābhaḥ //2.38//
children.translated_text: When established in celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), there is the attainment of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>). (2.38)

children.text:
brahmacaryapratiṣṭhāyāṃ vīryalābhaḥ/ vīryaṃ sāmarthyaṃ yasya lābhād apratighān
	  apratighātān guṇān aṇimādīn utkarṣayaty upacinoti/ siddhaś ca tārādibhir (tarkādibhir)
	  aṣṭābhiḥ siddhibhir ūhādyaparanāmabhir upeto vineyeṣu śiṣyeṣu jñānaṃ yogatadaṅgaviṣayam
	  ādhātuṃ samartho bhavatīti //2.38//
children.translated_text: When established in celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), there is the attainment of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>). <s>Vīrya</s> is capacity, by the attainment of which one develops and accumulates unimpeded, unobstructed qualities such as <s>aṇimā</s> (atomization) and the rest. And being accomplished, endowed with eight <s>siddhis</s> (perfections) such as <s>tarka</s> (reasoning) and the rest, also known as <s>ūha</s> (inference) and by other names, one becomes capable of imparting knowledge concerning <s>yoga</s> and its limbs to the students who are to be instructed. (2.38)

children.text: aparigrahasthair ye janmakathaṃtāsaṃbodhaḥ //2.39//
children.translated_text: When established in non-possessiveness (<s>aparigraha</s>), there arises the understanding of the how and wherefore of births. (2.39)

children.text:
aparigrahasthair ye janmakathaṃtāsaṃbodhaḥ/ nikāyaviśiṣṭair dehendriyādibhir
	  abhisaṃbandho janma tasya kathaṃtā kiṃprakāratā tasyāḥ saṃbodhaḥ sākṣātkāraḥ
	  saprakārātīndriyaśāntoditāvyapadeśyajanmaparijñānam iti yāvat/ atītaṃ jijñāsate ---
	  ko+aham āsam iti/ tasyaiva prakārabhedam utpāde sthitau ca jijñāsate --- katham aham
	  āsam iti/ vartamānasya janmanaḥ svarūpaṃ jijñāsate --- kiṃ svid iti/ śarīraṃ bhautikaṃ
	  kiṃ bhūtānāṃ samūhamātram āhosvit tebhyo+anyad iti/ atrāpi kathaṃ svid ity
	  anuṣañjanīyam/ kvacit tu paṭhyata eva/ anāgataṃ jijñāsate --- ke vā bhaviṣyāma iti/
	  atrāpi kathaṃ svid ity anuṣaṅgaḥ/ evam asyeti/ pūrvānto+atītaḥ kālaḥ parānto bhaviṣyan
	  madhyo vartamānas teṣv ātmano bhāvaḥ śarīrādisaṃbandhas tasmiñ jijñāsā tataś ca jñānaṃ,
	  yo hi yad icchati sa tat karotīti nyāyāt //2.39//
children.translated_text: When established in non-possessiveness (<s>aparigraha</s>), there arises the understanding of the how and wherefore of births. Birth is the connection with a body, senses, and the like, distinguished by a particular class of beings; the 'how and wherefore' (<s>kathaṃtā</s>) is the manner thereof; 'understanding' (<s>saṃbodha</s>) is direct realization — that is, the complete knowledge of births in their various modes: past, arisen, and indeterminate, which are beyond the senses. One inquires about the past — 'who was I?' One inquires about the different modes of that very [past existence] in terms of origin and duration — 'how was I?' One inquires about the nature of the present birth — 'what is this?' Is the body, being material, merely an aggregate of elements, or something different from them? Here too, 'how is it?' should be connected. In some readings, it is indeed read [explicitly]. One inquires about the future — 'who shall we become?' Here too, 'how?' is to be connected. Thus, for this one — the prior end is past time, the latter end is the future, and the middle is the present; in these, the existence of the self is the connection with body and the like; regarding that there is inquiry, and from that, knowledge — for by the maxim 'whoever desires something accomplishes it.' (2.39)

children.text: śaucāt svāṅgajugupsā parair asaṃsargaḥ //2.40//
children.translated_text: From purity (<s>śauca</s>), there arises disgust toward one's own body and non-contact with others. (2.40)

children.text: śaucāt svāṅgajugupsā parair asaṃsargaḥ/ anena bāhyaśaucasiddhisūcakaṃ kathitam //2.40//
children.translated_text: From purity (<s>śauca</s>), there arises disgust toward one's own body and non-contact with others. By this, the indicator of the accomplishment of external purity (<s>bāhyaśauca</s>) has been stated. (2.40)

children.text: sattvaśuddhisaumanasyaikāgryendriyajayātmadarśanayogyatvāni ca //2.41//
children.translated_text: Purity of <s>sattva</s>, cheerfulness, one-pointedness, mastery over the senses, and fitness for the vision of the self — these also [arise from purity]. (2.41)

children.text:
āntaraśaucasiddhisūcakam āha --- kiṃ ceti/
	  sattvaśuddhisaumanasyaikāgryendriyajayātmadarśanayogyatvāni ca/ cittamalānām ākṣālane
	  cittasattvam amalaṃ prādurbhavati vaimalyāt saumanasyaṃ svacchatā svacchaṃ tadekāgraṃ
	  tato manastantrāṇām indriyāṇāṃ tajjayāj jayas tata ātmadarśanayogyatvaṃ buddhisattvasya
	  bhavatīti //2.41//
children.translated_text: He states the indicator of the accomplishment of internal purity (<s>āntaraśauca</s>) — 'and moreover' etc. Purity of <s>sattva</s>, cheerfulness, one-pointedness, mastery over the senses, and fitness for the vision of the self. When the impurities of the <s>citta</s> (mind) are washed away, the <s>sattva</s> of the <s>citta</s> manifests as pure; from that purity arises cheerfulness (<s>saumanasya</s>), i.e., clarity; that which is clear becomes one-pointed; from that comes mastery over the senses, which are dependent on the mind; and from that mastery comes the fitness of the <s>buddhi-sattva</s> for the vision of the self (<s>ātmadarśana</s>). (2.41)

children.text: saṃtoṣād anuttamaḥ sukhalābhaḥ //2.42//
children.translated_text: From contentment (<s>saṃtoṣa</s>), the attainment of unsurpassed happiness. (2.42)

children.text:
saṃtoṣād anuttamaḥ sukhalābhaḥ/ na vidyate+asmād uttama ity anuttmaḥ/ yathā coktaṃ
	  yayātinā pūrau yauvanam arpayatā ---
children.translated_text: From contentment (<s>saṃtoṣa</s>), the attainment of unsurpassed happiness. That which has no superior is 'unsurpassed' (<s>anuttama</s>). As was said by <s>Yayāti</s> when bestowing youth upon <s>Pūru</s> —

children.text:
"yā dustyajā durmatibhir yā na jīryati jīryatām/ tāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ saṃtyajan prājñaḥ
	  sukhenaivābhipūryate"
mahābhāratam ādiparva 85.14
children.translated_text: <s>Mahābhārata</s>, <s>Ādiparva</s> 85.14

children.text: iti//
children.translated_text: Thus.
'That [craving] which is hard to abandon by those of wicked mind, which does not age even as one ages — the wise one, abandoning that craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), is filled with happiness alone.'

children.text: tad etad darśayati --- yac ca kāmasukhaṃ loka ityādinā //2.42//
children.translated_text: He demonstrates this very point — with 'whatever sensory pleasure exists in the world' and so on. (2.42)

children.text: kāyendriyasiddhir aśuddhikṣayāt tapasaḥ //2.43//
children.translated_text: Perfection of the body and senses [arises] from <s>tapas</s> (austerity) through the destruction of impurity. (2.43)

children.text:
tapaḥsiddhisūcakam āha --- kāyendriyasiddhir aśuddhikṣayāt tapasaḥ/ aśuddhilakṣaṇam
	  āvaraṇaṃ tāmasam adharmādi/ aṇimādyā mahimā laghimā prāptiś ca/ sugamam //2.43//
children.translated_text: He states the indicator of the accomplishment of <s>tapas</s> (austerity) — 'Perfection of the body and senses from the destruction of impurity through <s>tapas</s>.' The impurity referred to is the <s>tāmasa</s> (dark) covering, consisting of <s>adharma</s> (demerit) and the like. [The perfections include] <s>aṇimā</s> (atomization), <s>mahimā</s> (magnification), <s>laghimā</s> (levitation), and <s>prāpti</s> (obtaining), and so forth. This is easy to understand. (2.43)

children.text: svādhyāyād iṣṭadevatāsaṃprayogaḥ //2.44//
children.translated_text: From self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), there is communion with the desired deity. (2.44)

children.text: svādhyāyasiddhisūcakam āha --- svādhyāyād iṣṭadevatāsaṃprayogaḥ/ sugamam //2.44//
children.translated_text: He states the indicator of the accomplishment of self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) — 'From self-study, communion with the desired deity.' This is easy to understand. (2.44)

children.text: samādhisiddhir īśvarapraṇidhānāt //2.45//
children.translated_text: The perfection of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) [comes] from devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). (2.45)

children.text:
samādhisiddhir īśvarapraṇidhānāt/ na ca vācyam īśvarapraṇidhānād eva cet saṃprajñātasya
	  samādher aṅginaḥ siddhiḥ kṛtaṃ saptabhir aṅgair iti/ īśvarapraṇidhānasiddhau dṛṣṭādṛṣṭāv
	  āntaravyāpāreṇa teṣām upayogāt/ saṃprajñātasiddhau ca saṃyogapṛthaktvena dadhna iva
	  kratvarthatā puruṣārthatā ca/ na caivam anantaraṅgatā dhāraṇādhyānasamādhīnāṃ
	  saṃprajñātasiddhau/ saṃprajñātasamānagocaratayāṅgāntarebhyo
	  'tadgocarebhyo+asyāntaraṅgatvapratīteḥ/ īśvarapraṇidhānam api īśvaragocaraṃ na
	  saṃprajñeyagocaram iti bahiraṅgam iti sarvam avadātam/ prajānātīti prajñāpadavyutpattir
	  darśitā //2.45//
children.translated_text: The perfection of <s>samādhi</s> [comes] from devotion to <s>Īśvara</s>. And one should not say: 'If the perfection of <s>saṃprajñāta samādhi</s> (cognitive absorption), which is the principal [practice], comes from devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> alone, then what is the use of the seven limbs?' Because in the accomplishment of devotion to <s>Īśvara</s>, those [limbs] are useful through their intermediate function in both seen and unseen [results]. And in the accomplishment of <s>saṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi], like curds [which serve both] the purpose of a sacrifice and the purpose of a person, there is a separate function of conjunction. And the inner limbs — <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>samādhi</s> — are not thus [merely auxiliary] in the accomplishment of <s>saṃprajñāta</s>, because their inner-limb status is understood from their sharing the same object as <s>saṃprajñāta</s>, unlike the other limbs which have different objects. Devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> too, having <s>Īśvara</s> as its object and not the objects of <s>saṃprajñāta</s>, is an outer limb — thus everything is clear. The etymological derivation of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) as 'one who knows distinctly' has been shown. (2.45)

children.text: sthirasukham āsanam //2.46//
children.translated_text: <s>Āsana</s> (posture) is that which is steady and comfortable. (2.46)

children.text:
uttarasūtram avatārayati --- uktāḥ saha siddhibhir yamaniyamāḥ/ āsanādīni vakṣyāmaḥ/
	  tatra --- sthirasukham āsanam/ sthiraṃ niścalaṃ yat sukhaṃ sukhāvahaṃ tad āsanam iti

sūtrārthaḥ/ āsyata āste vānenety āsanam/ tasya prabhedān āha --- tadyatheti/
	  padmāsanaṃ prasiddham/ sthitasyaikataraḥ pādo bhūnyasta ekataraś cākuñcitajānor upari
	  nyasta ity etad vīrāsanam/ pādatale vṛṣaṇasamīpe saṃpuṭīkṛtya tasyopari pāṇikacchapikāṃ
	  kuryāt tad bhadrāsanam/ savyam ākuñcitaṃ caraṇaṃ dakṣiṇajaṅghorvantare dakṣiṇaṃ
	  cākuñcitaṃ vāmajaṅghorvantare nikṣiped etat svastikam/ upaviśya śliṣṭāṅgulikau
	  śliṣṭagulphau bhūmiśliṣṭajaṅghorupādau prasārya daṇḍāsanam abhyaset/ yogapaṭṭakayogāt
	  sopāśrayam/ jānuprasāritabāhoḥ śayanaṃ paryaṅkaḥ/ krauñcaniṣadanādīni krauñcādīnāṃ
	  niṣaṇṇānāṃ saṃsthānadarśanāt pratyetavyāni/ pārṣṇyagrapādābhyāṃ dvayor ākuñcitayor
	  anyonyasaṃpīḍanaṃ samasaṃsthānaṃ, yena saṃsthānenāvasthitasya sthairyaṃ sukhaṃ ca
	  sidhyati tad āsanaṃ sthirasukham/ tad etad bhagavataḥ sūtrakārasya saṃmataṃ, tasya
	  vivaraṇaṃ yathāsukhaṃ ceti //2.46//
children.translated_text: This is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. <s>Āsana</s> [is so called because] one sits (<s>āsyate</s>) or remains (<s>āste</s>) in it. He describes its varieties — 'such as' etc. <s>Padmāsana</s> (lotus posture) is well known. Standing, one foot is placed on the ground and the other is placed upon the bent knee of the opposite [leg] — this is <s>vīrāsana</s> (hero posture). Placing the soles of the feet together near the scrotum and forming a tortoise shape with the hands above — that is <s>bhadrāsana</s> (auspicious posture). The left foot, bent, is placed between the right calf and thigh, and the right foot, bent, is placed between the left calf and thigh — this is <s>svastika</s> (auspicious cross posture). Sitting with interlocked fingers and joined ankles, with calves, thighs, and feet touching the ground, stretching out — one should practice <s>daṇḍāsana</s> (staff posture). With the use of a yoga strap, [it becomes] supported (<s>sopāśraya</s>). Lying down with arms extended over the knees is <s>paryaṅka</s> (couch posture). <s>Krauñcaniṣadana</s> (heron sitting) and others should be understood from observing the postures of herons and other [birds] when seated. With the heel and the tips of the toes of both bent [legs] pressing against each other in a symmetrical arrangement — whichever posture achieves both steadiness and comfort when one is established in it, that is the steady and comfortable <s>āsana</s>. This is the view approved by the blessed <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the sūtras), and its exposition is 'as is comfortable.' (2.46)

He introduces the following <s>sūtra</s> — 'The <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> together with their accomplishments have been stated. We shall now speak of <s>āsana</s> and the rest.' Among these — '<s>āsana</s> is that which is steady and comfortable.' That which is steady, i.e., motionless, and comfortable, i.e., conducive to ease — that is <s>āsana</s>.

children.text: prayatnaśaithilyānantasamāpattibhyām //2.47//
children.translated_text: [<s>Āsana</s> is perfected] by relaxation of effort and by <s>samāpatti</s> (absorption) on the infinite. (2.47)

children.text:
āsanasvarūpam uktvā tatsādhanam āha --- prayatnaśaithilyānantasamāpattibhyām/
	  sāṃsiddhiko hi prayatnaḥ śarīradhārako na yogāṅgasyopadeṣṭavyāsanasya kāraṇaṃ tasya
	  tatkāraṇatva upadeśavaiyarthyāt svarasata eva tatsiddheḥ/ tasmād
	  upadeṣṭavyasyāsanasyāyam asādhako virodhī ca svābhāvikaḥ prayatnas tasya ca
	  yādṛcchikāsanahetutayāsananiyamopahantṛtvāt/ tasmād upadiṣṭaniyamāsanam abhyasyatā
	  svābhāvikaprayatnaśaithilyāya prayatna āstheyo nānyathopadiṣṭam āsanaṃ sidhyatīti
	  svābhāvikaprayatnaśaithilyam āsanasiddhihetuḥ/ anante vā nāganāyake
	  sthirataraphaṇāsahasravidhṛtaviśvaṃbharāmaṇḍale samāpannaṃ cittam āsanaṃ
	  nirvartayatīti //2.47//
children.translated_text: Having stated the nature of <s>āsana</s>, he states its means of accomplishment — 'by relaxation of effort and by <s>samāpatti</s> on the infinite.' For the natural effort that sustains the body is not the cause of the <s>āsana</s> to be taught as a limb of <s>yoga</s>, since if it were the cause, teaching would be pointless, as [such āsana] would be accomplished spontaneously. Therefore, this natural effort is not the means of accomplishing the <s>āsana</s> to be taught, and is indeed opposed to it, since being the cause of haphazard posture, it would undermine the regulation of posture. Therefore, one who is practicing the regulated posture that has been taught should make an effort toward the relaxation of natural effort — otherwise the taught <s>āsana</s> would not be accomplished. Thus, the relaxation of natural effort is the cause of accomplishing <s>āsana</s>. Or, the mind absorbed in <s>Ananta</s>, the lord of serpents, whose thousands of supremely steady hoods uphold the orb of the earth — [such a mind] accomplishes the <s>āsana</s>. (2.47)

children.text: tato dvaṃdvānabhighātaḥ //2.48//
children.translated_text: From that, non-affliction by the pairs of opposites (<s>dvandva</s>). (2.48)

children.text:
āsanavijayasūcakam āha --- tato dvaṃdvānabhighātaḥ/ nigadavyākhyātaṃ bhāṣyam/ āsanam
	  apy uktaṃ viṣṇupurāṇe ---
children.translated_text: He states the indicator of mastery over <s>āsana</s> — 'From that, non-affliction by the pairs of opposites.' The <s>bhāṣya</s> is explained in a straightforward manner. <s>Āsana</s> has also been stated in the <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> —

children.text: "evaṃ bhadrāsanādīnāṃ samāsthāya guṇair yutam" iti
viṣṇupurāṇam 6.7.39
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> 6.7.39
'Thus, being established in <s>bhadrāsana</s> and the rest, endowed with [their] qualities.'

children.text: tasmin sati śvāsapraśvāsayor gativicchedaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ //2.49//
children.translated_text: When that [<s>āsana</s>] is [accomplished], <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) is the cessation of the movement of inhalation and exhalation. (2.49)

children.text:
āsanānantaraṃ tatpūrvakatāṃ prāṇāyāmasya darśayaṃs tallakṣaṇam āha --- tasmin sati
	  śvāsapraśvāsayor gativicchedaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ/ recakapūrakakumbhakeṣv asti śvāsapraśvāsayor
	  gativiccheda iti prāṇāyāmasāmānyalakṣaṇam etad iti/ tathā hi --- yatra bāhyo vāyur
	  ācamyāntardhāryate pūrake tatrāsti śvāsapraśvāsayor gativicchedaḥ/ yatrāpi kauṣṭhyo
	  vāyur virecya bahirdhāryate recake tatrāsti śvāsapraśvāsayor gativicchedaḥ/ evaṃ
	  kumbhake+apīti/ tad etad bhāṣyeṇocyate --- saty āsaneti //2.49//
children.translated_text: After <s>āsana</s> (posture), showing the precedence of that [āsana] for <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), he states its definition — 'When that [āsana] is [accomplished], the cessation of the movement of inhalation and exhalation is <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.' In <s>recaka</s> (exhalation), <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation), and <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention), there is a cessation of the movement of inhalation and exhalation — this is the general definition of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>. For thus — where the external air is drawn in and held internally in <s>pūraka</s>, there is a cessation of the movement of inhalation and exhalation. Where also the abdominal air is expelled and held externally in <s>recaka</s>, there too is a cessation of the movement of inhalation and exhalation. Likewise in <s>kumbhaka</s> as well. This is stated by the <s>bhāṣya</s> (commentary) — 'When the <s>āsana</s> [is accomplished]' etc. (2.49)

children.text: bāhyābhyantarastambhavṛttir deśakālasaṃkhyābhiḥ paridṛṣṭo dīrghasūkṣmaḥ //2.50//
children.translated_text: [<s>Prāṇāyāma</s>] has the operations of external, internal, and suspension; is regulated by place, time, and number; and becomes long and subtle. (2.50)

children.text:
prāṇāyāmaviśeṣatrayalakṣaṇaparaṃ sūtram avatārayati --- sa tv iti/
	  bāhyābhyantarastambhavṛttir deśakālasaṃkhyābhiḥ paridṛṣṭo dīrghasūkṣmaḥ/ vṛttiśabdaḥ
	  pratyekaṃ saṃbadhyate/ recakam āha --- yatra praśvāseti/ pūrakam āha --- yatra śvāseti/
	  kumbhakam āha --- tṛtīya iti/ tad eva sphuṭayati --- yatrobhayoḥ śvāsapraśvāsayoḥ sakṛd
	  eva vidhārakāt prayatnād abhāvo bhavati na punaḥ pūrvavad
	  āpūraṇaprayatnaughavidhārakaprayatno nāpi recakaprayatnaughavidhārakaprayatno+apekṣyate/
	  kiṃ tu yathā tapta upale nihitaṃ jalaṃ pariśuṣyat sarvataḥ saṃkocam āpadyata evam ayam
	  api māruto vahanaśīlo balavad vidhārakaprayatnaniruddhakriyaḥ śarīra eva
	  sūkṣmībhūto+avatiṣṭhate na tu pūrayati yena pūrakaḥ/ na tu recayati yena recaka iti/

iyān asya deśo viṣayaḥ prādeśavitastihastādiparimito nivātapradeśa
	  īśīkātūlādikriyānumito bāhya evam āntaro+apy āpādatalam āmastakaṃ
	  pipīlikāsparśasadṛśenānumitaḥ sparśena/ nimeṣakriyāvacchinnasya kālasya caturtho bhāgaḥ
	  kṣaṇas teṣām iyattāvadhāraṇenāvacchinnaḥ/ svajānumaṇḍalaṃ pāṇinā triḥ parāmṛśya
	  cchoṭikāvacchinnaḥ kālo mātrā tābhiḥ ṣaṭtriṃśatā mātrābhiḥ parimitaḥ prathama udghāto
	  mṛduḥ/ sa eva dviguṇīkṛto dvitīyo madhyamaḥ/ sa eva triguṇīkṛtas tṛtīyas tīvraḥ/ tam
	  imaṃ saṃkhyāparidṛṣṭaṃ prāṇāyāmam āha --- saṃkhyābhir iti/ svasthasya hi puṃsaḥ
	  śvāsapraśvāsakriyāvacchinnena kālena yathoktacchoṭikākālaḥ samānaḥ/
	  prathamodghātakarmatāṃ nīta udghāto vijito vaśīkṛto nigṛhītaḥ/ kṣaṇānām iyattā kālo
	  vivakṣitaḥ/ śvāsapraśvāseyattā saṃkhyeti kathaṃcid bhedaḥ/ sa khalv ayaṃ pratyaham
	  abhyasto divasapakṣamāsādikrameṇa deśakālapracayavyāpitayā dīrghaḥ/
