	  paramanaipuṇyasamadhigamanīyatayā ca sūkṣmo na tu mandatayā //2.50//
children.translated_text: Its 'place' (<s>deśa</s>) means the domain, measured in <s>prādeśa</s> (span), <s>vitasti</s> (extended span), <s>hasta</s> (cubit), etc., [namely] a windless area, inferred by the movement of a reed-tuft and the like — this is the external [measure]. Similarly the internal [measure is inferred] from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head, inferred by a sensation resembling the touch of an ant. A fourth part of the time delimited by the action of blinking is a <s>kṣaṇa</s> (moment); [<s>prāṇāyāma</s> is] delimited by the determination of their quantity. Touching one's own knee-circle with the palm three times, the time delimited by a finger-snap is a <s>mātrā</s> (measure-unit); [<s>prāṇāyāma</s>] measured by thirty-six such <s>mātrās</s> is the first <s>udghāta</s> (level), [which is] mild. That same [measure] doubled is the second, [which is] moderate. That same tripled is the third, [which is] intense. He states this <s>prāṇāyāma</s> regulated by number — 'By numbers' etc. For the time delimited by the action of inhalation and exhalation of a healthy person is equivalent to the time of the finger-snap as described. [The <s>prāṇāyāma</s>] brought to the state of being the object of the first <s>udghāta</s> is an <s>udghāta</s> conquered, mastered, controlled. The quantity of <s>kṣaṇas</s> is the intended meaning of 'time.' The quantity of inhalations and exhalations is 'number' — thus there is some distinction [between time and number]. This [<s>prāṇāyāma</s>], practiced daily, through the progressive increase of place and time over days, fortnights, months, etc., becomes 'long'; and because it is attainable only through supreme skill, it becomes 'subtle' — not because of weakness. (2.50)

He introduces the <s>sūtra</s> concerning the definition of the three types of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> — 'But that' etc. '[<s>Prāṇāyāma</s>] has the operations of external, internal, and suspension; is regulated by place, time, and number; and becomes long and subtle.' The word '<s>vṛtti</s>' (operation) is connected with each individually. He states <s>recaka</s> — 'Where exhalation' etc. He states <s>pūraka</s> — 'Where inhalation' etc. He states <s>kumbhaka</s> — 'The third' etc. He clarifies that very point — where there is the absence of both inhalation and exhalation by a single effort of retention, without requiring the effort of retention through a succession of filling efforts as before, nor the effort of retention through a succession of expelling efforts. Rather, just as water placed on a heated stone, drying up, undergoes contraction on all sides, so too this breath, whose nature is to flow, having its activity forcefully arrested by the effort of retention, remains in the body itself in a subtle state — it does not fill [the body] so as to be <s>pūraka</s>, nor does it expel so as to be <s>recaka</s>.

children.text: bāhyābhyantaraviṣayākṣepī caturthaḥ //2.51//
children.translated_text: The fourth [<s>prāṇāyāma</s>] transcends the domains of external and internal. (2.51)

children.text:
evaṃ trayo viśeṣā lakṣitāḥ/ caturthaṃ lakṣayati --- bāhyābhyantaraviṣayākṣepī
	  caturthaḥ/ vyācaṣṭe --- deśakālasaṃkhyābhir iti/ ākṣipto 'bhyāsavaśīkṛtād rūpād
	  avaropitaḥ so+api dīrghasūkṣma eva tatpūrvako bāhyābhyantaraviṣayaprāṇāyāmo
	  deśakālasaṃkhyādarśanapūrvakaḥ/ na cāsau caturthas tṛtīya iva sakṛtprayatnād ahnāya
	  jāyate kiṃ tv abhyasyamānas tāṃ tām avasthām āpannas tattadavasthāvijayānukrameṇa
	  bhavatīty āha --- bhūmijayād iti/ nanūbhayor gatyabhāvaḥ stambhavṛttāv apy astīti
	  ko+asmād asya viśeṣa ity ata āha --- tṛtīya iti/ anālocanapūrvaḥ
	  sakṛtprayatnanirvartitas

tṛtīyaḥ/ caturthas tv ālocanapūrvo
	  bahuprayatnanirvartanīya iti viśeṣaḥ/ tayoḥ pūrakarecakayor viṣayo+anālocito+ayaṃ tu
	  deśakālasaṃkhyābhir ālocita ity arthaḥ //2.51//
children.translated_text: is the third. The fourth, however, is preceded by contemplation and requires many efforts — this is the distinction. The domain of those two — <s>pūraka</s> and <s>recaka</s> — is unconsidered [in the third], but this [fourth] is considered with respect to place, time, and number — this is the meaning. (2.51)

Thus three types have been characterized. He characterizes the fourth — 'The fourth transcends the domains of external and internal.' He explains — 'By place, time, and number' etc. 'Transcends' means brought down from the form mastered through practice — and that too is long and subtle, preceded by the external and internal <s>prāṇāyāma</s> regulated by the observation of place, time, and number. And this fourth does not arise all at once from a single effort like the third, but rather, being practiced, having reached successive stages, comes about through the sequential mastery of each stage — thus he says: 'Through the conquest of stages' etc. But the absence of movement of both [inhalation and exhalation] exists in the suspension operation too — so what distinguishes this from it? To this he says: 'The third' etc. Without [prior] contemplation, accomplished by a single effort,

children.text: tataḥ kṣīyate prakāśāvaraṇam //2.52//
children.translated_text: From that, the covering of illumination is diminished. (2.52)

children.text:
prāṇāyāmasyāvāntaraprayojanam āha --- tataḥ kṣīyate prakāśāvaraṇam/ āvriyate+anena
	  buddhisattvaprakāśa ity āvaraṇaṃ kleśaḥ pāpmā ca/ vyācaṣṭe --- prāṇāyāmān iti/
	  jñāyate+aneneti jñānaṃ buddhisattvaprakāśo vivekasya jñānaṃ vivekajñānam/ vivekajñānam
	  āvṛṇotīti vivekajñānāvaraṇīyam/ bhavyageyapravacanīyādīnāṃ
pāṇinisūtram 3.4.68
children.translated_text: <s>Pāṇini</s>'s <s>sūtra</s> 3.4.68

children.text:
kartari nipātanasya pradarśanārthatvāt
	  kopanīyarañjanīyavad atrāpi kartari kṛtyapratyayaḥ/ karmaśabdena tajjanyam apuṇyaṃ
	  tatkāraṇaṃ kleśaṃ [ca] lakṣayati/ atraivāgaminām anumatim āha --- yat tad ācakṣata iti/
	  mahāmoho rāgaḥ, tadavinirbhāgavartiny avidyāpi tadgrahaṇena gṛhyate/ akāryam adharmaḥ/
	  nanu prāṇāyāma eva cet pāpmānaṃ kṣiṇoti kṛtaṃ tarhi tapasety ata āha --- durbalaṃ
	  bhavatīti/ na tu sarvathā kṣīyate+atas tatprakṣayāya tapo+apekṣyata iti/ atrāpy āgaminām
	  anumatim āha --- tathā coktam iti/
children.translated_text: — since the [irregular] listing [of this form] in the agent sense is merely illustrative, here too, like <s>kopanīya</s> (provocable) and <s>rañjanīya</s> (delightable), the <s>kṛtya</s> (gerundive) suffix is in the agent sense. By the word '<s>karma</s>' (action) he indicates the demerit produced by it and the <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) that is its cause. Here he cites the agreement of later authorities — 'What they declare' etc. <s>Mahāmoha</s> (great delusion) is <s>rāga</s> (passion); <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), which exists inseparably from it, is also included by that reference. '<s>Akārya</s>' (what ought not to be done) is <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness). But if <s>prāṇāyāma</s> alone destroys demerit, then what need is there for <s>tapas</s> (austerity)? To this he says: 'It becomes weakened' etc. But [the covering] is not entirely destroyed; therefore, for its complete destruction, <s>tapas</s> is also required. Here too he cites the agreement of later authorities — 'And thus it has been said' etc.

He states the subsidiary purpose of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> — 'From that, the covering of illumination is diminished.' That which covers the illumination of <s>buddhi-sattva</s> (the luminous aspect of intellect) is the covering — namely <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) and <s>pāpman</s> (demerit). He explains — 'Through <s>prāṇāyāma</s>' etc. That by which something is known is knowledge — the illumination of <s>buddhi-sattva</s> is the knowledge of discrimination, <s>vivekajñāna</s> (discriminative knowledge). That which covers <s>vivekajñāna</s> is <s>vivekajñānāvaraṇīya</s> (what is to be covered over discriminative knowledge). [This follows the pattern of] <s>bhavya</s>, <s>geya</s>, <s>pravacanīya</s>, and the like —

children.text: manur apy āha --- "prāṇāyamair dahed doṣān"
manusmṛtiḥ 6.72
children.translated_text: <s>Manusmṛti</s> 6.72

children.text: iti/
children.translated_text: Thus.
<s>Manu</s> also says: 'Through <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> one should burn away the defects' —

children.text: prāṇāyāmasya yogāṅgatā viṣṇupurāṇoktā ---
children.translated_text: The status of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> as a limb of <s>yoga</s> is stated in the <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> —

children.text:
"prāṇākhyam anilaṃ vaśyam abhyāsāt kurute tu yaḥ/ prāṇāyāmaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ sabījo+abīja
	  eva ca// paraspareṇābhibhavaṃ prāṇāpānau yadānilau/ kurutas tadvidhānena tṛtīyaṃ
	  saṃyamāt tayoḥ"
viṣṇupurāṇam 6.7.40--41
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> 6.7.40-41

'He who through practice brings under control the breath called <s>prāṇa</s> — that is to be known as <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, both with seed (<s>sabīja</s>) and without seed (<s>abīja</s>). When the two breaths, <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, mutually overcome each other, then through the regulation of both, a third [state arises] from their restraint.'

children.text: dhāraṇāsu ca yogyatā manasaḥ //2.53//
children.translated_text: And [from that arises] the fitness of the mind for <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration). (2.53)

children.text:
kiṃ ca --- dhāraṇāsu ca yogyatā manasaḥ/ prāṇāyāmo hi manaḥ sthirīkurvan dhāraṇāsu
	  yogyaṃ karoti //2.53//
children.translated_text: Furthermore — 'And [from that arises] the fitness of the mind for <s>dhāraṇā</s>.' For <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, by making the mind steady, renders it fit for <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration). (2.53)

children.text: svaviṣayāsaṃprayoge cittasvarūpānukāra ivendriyāṇāṃ pratyāhāraḥ //2.54//
children.translated_text: When there is non-contact with their own objects, the <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs) conforming as it were to the essential nature of <s>citta</s> (mind) — that is <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses). (2.54)

children.text:
tad evaṃ yamādibhiḥ saṃskṛtaḥ saṃyamāya pratyāhāram ārabhate/ tasya lakṣaṇasūtram
	  avatārayituṃ pṛcchati --- atheti/ svaviṣayāsaṃprayoge cittasvarūpānukāra ivendriyāṇāṃ
	  pratyāhāraḥ/ cittam api mohanīyarañjanīyakopanīyaiḥ śabdādibhir viṣayair na
	  saṃprayujyate tadasaṃprayogāc cakṣurādīny api na saṃprayujyanta iti so+ayam indriyāṇāṃ
	  cittasvarūpānukāraḥ/ yat punas tattvaṃ cittam abhiniviśate na tadindriyāṇi
	  bāhyaviṣayāṇīty ananukāro+api/ ata uktam anukāra iveti/ svaviṣayāsaṃprayogasya
	  sādhāraṇasya dharmasya cittānukāranimittatvaṃ saptamyā darśayati --- sveti/ anukāraṃ
	  vivṛṇoti --- cittanirodha iti/ dvayor nirodhahetuś ca prayatnas tulya iti sādṛśyam/
	  atraiva dṛṣṭāntam āha --- yathā madhukararājam iti/ dārṣṭāntike

yojayati
	  --- tatheti/ atrāpi viṣṇupurāṇavākyam ---
children.translated_text: he applies it — 'Similarly' etc. Here too there is a statement from the <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> —

Thus, having been refined by <s>yama</s> (restraints) and the rest, he commences <s>pratyāhāra</s> for the sake of <s>saṃyama</s> (combined practice). To introduce the <s>sūtra</s> defining it, he asks — 'Now' etc. 'When there is non-contact with their own objects, the <s>indriyas</s> conforming as it were to the essential nature of <s>citta</s> — that is <s>pratyāhāra</s>.' When the mind too is not in contact with objects such as sound etc. that are capable of deluding, coloring, and agitating, then due to that non-contact of the mind, the eyes and other [sense organs] also do not come into contact — this is the <s>indriyas</s>' conformity to the essential nature of <s>citta</s>. But the reality upon which the mind is focused — the <s>indriyas</s> do not [focus on] that, [for] they [focus on] external objects — so there is also non-conformity. Hence it is said 'conformity as it were.' The instrumental case [in the <s>sūtra</s>] shows that the non-contact with their own objects, being a common property, is caused by conformity to <s>citta</s> — 'Their own' etc. He explains the conformity — 'Cessation of <s>citta</s>' etc. The effort that is the cause of cessation of both [<s>citta</s> and <s>indriyas</s>] is the same — hence the resemblance. Here he gives an illustration — 'Just as the king of bees' etc. In the illustrandum,

children.text: "śabdādiṣv anuṣaktāni nigṛhyākṣāṇi yogavit/ kuryāc cittānukārīṇi pratyāhāraparāyaṇaḥ"//
viṣṇupurāṇam 6.7.43
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> 6.7.43
'The knower of <s>yoga</s>, devoted to <s>pratyāhāra</s>, restraining the senses that are attached to sound and other [objects], should make them conforming to <s>citta</s>.'

children.text: tasya prayojanaṃ tatraiva darśitam ---
children.translated_text: Its purpose is shown in the same place —

children.text: "vaśyatā paramā tena jāyate niścalātmanām/ indriyāṇām avaśyais tair na yogasādhakaḥ"
viṣṇupurāṇam 6.7.44
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> 6.7.44
'Thereby arises the supreme mastery of those whose selves are steady, over the <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs). One who has not mastered them is not an accomplisher of <s>yoga</s>.'

children.text: tataḥ paramā vaśyatendriyāṇām //2.55//
children.translated_text: From that [arises] the supreme mastery of the <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs). (2.55)

children.text: iti śrīpatañjaliviracitayogasūtreṣu dvitīyaḥ sādhanapādaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the second <s>Sādhanapāda</s> (Chapter on Practice) in the <s>Yogasūtras</s> composed by the venerable <s>Patañjali</s>. (2)

children.text:
asyānuvādakaṃ sūtram --- tataḥ paramā vaśyatendriyāṇām/ nanu santi kim anyā aparamā
	  indriyāṇāṃ vaśyatā yā apekṣya parameyam ucyate, addhā tā darśayati --- śabdādiṣv iti/
	  etad eva vivṛṇoti --- saktī rāgo vyasanam/ kayā vyupattyā (vyutpattyā), vyasyati kṣipati
	  nirasyaty enaṃ śreyasa iti/ tadabhāvo+avyasanaṃ vaśyatā/ aparām api vaśyatām āha ---
	  aviruddhā śrutyādyaviruddhaśabdādisevanaṃ tadviruddheṣv apravṛttiḥ, saiva nyāyyā nyāyād
	  anapetā yataḥ/ aparām api vaśyatām āha --- śabdādisaṃprayoga iti/ śabdādiṣv indriyāṇāṃ
	  saṃprayogaḥ svecchayā bhogyeṣu khalv ayaṃ svatantro na bhogyatantra ity arthaḥ/ aparām
	  api vaśyatām āha --- rāgadveṣābhāve sukhaduḥkhaśūnyaṃ mādhyasthyena śabdādijñānam ity
	  eke/ sūtrakārābhimatāṃ vaśyatāṃ paramarṣisaṃmatām āha --- cittasyaikāgryāt sahendriyair
	  apravṛttir eva śabdādiṣv iti jaigīṣavyaḥ/ asyāḥ paramatām āha --- paramā tv iti/ tuśabdo
	  vaśyatāntarebhyo viśinaṣṭi/ vaśyatāntarāṇi hi viṣayāśīviṣasaṃprayogaśālitayā
	  kleśaviṣasaṃparkaśaṅkāṃ nāpakrāmanti/ na hi viṣavidyāvitprakṛṣṭo+api vaśīkṛtabhujaṃgamo
	  bhujaṃgamam aṅke nidhāya svapiti viśrabdhaḥ/ iyaṃ tu vaśyatā
	  vidūrīkṛtanikhilaviṣayavyatiṣaṅgā

nirāśaṅkatayā paramety ucyate/
	  netarendriyajayavad iti/ yathā yatamānasaṃjñāyām ekendriyajaye+apīndriyāntarajayāya
	  prayatnāntaram apekṣante na caivaṃ cittanirodhe bāhyendriyanirodhāya
	  prayatnāntarāpekṣety arthaḥ //2.55//
children.translated_text: is called supreme because it is free from apprehension — not like the other forms of sense-conquest. Just as in the <s>Yatamānasaṃjñā</s> (stage of effort), even upon conquering one sense, a further effort is required for conquering the remaining senses; but not so [here] — upon the cessation of the mind, no separate effort is required for the cessation of the external senses — such is the meaning. (2.55)

The <s>sūtra</s> that restates this is: 'From that, the supreme mastery over the sense organs.' Now, are there other, non-supreme forms of mastery over the senses, in relation to which this one is called supreme? Indeed, he shows them — 'with regard to sound and the like,' etc. He explains this very point — 'attachment (<s>sakti</s>) is passion (<s>rāga</s>), [which is] addiction (<s>vyasana</s>).' By what derivation? — 'It scatters (<s>vyasyati</s>), throws, and casts one away from the good (<s>śreyas</s>).' The absence of that [addiction] is non-addiction — [that is] mastery. He states another form of mastery — 'non-opposed': the use of sound and the like that does not conflict with scripture and the rest, and non-engagement in what conflicts with them — this itself is proper, because it does not deviate from rightness (<s>nyāya</s>). He states yet another mastery — 'the contact with sound and the like': the engagement of the senses with sound and the like — this is at one's own will regarding the objects to be enjoyed; it is autonomous, not dependent on the objects — such is the meaning. He states yet another mastery — 'some [say]: in the absence of attachment and aversion, the knowledge of sound and the like is devoid of pleasure and pain, with equanimity.' He states the mastery intended by the author of the <s>sūtras</s>, approved by the great sage — '<s>Jaigīṣavya</s> [says]: from the one-pointedness of the mind, the very non-engagement of the senses together [with the mind] in sound and the like.' He states its supremacy — 'but the supreme': the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) distinguishes it from the other forms of mastery. For the other forms of mastery, being characterized by contact with the poison-serpent of sense objects, do not eliminate the fear of contact with the poison of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). For even the most expert snake-charmer does not place a subdued serpent on his lap and sleep with confidence. But this mastery, having completely removed all entanglement with sense objects,

children.text:
kriyāyogaṃ jagau kleśān vipākān karmaṇām iha/ tadduḥkhatvaṃ tathā vyūhān pāde yogasya
	  pañcakam // iti//1//
children.translated_text: He sang of <s>Kriyāyoga</s> (yoga of action), the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), the fruitions of actions, their being of the nature of suffering, and the arrangements — [these] five [topics] in the chapter on <s>yoga</s>. Thus. (1)

children.text:
iti śrīvācaspatimiśraviracitāyāṃ pātañjalayogasūtrabhāṣyavyākhyāyāṃ dvitīyaḥ
	  sādhanapādaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: Thus, in the commentary (<s>vyākhyā</s>) on the <s>Pātañjala Yogasūtra Bhāṣya</s>, composed by the revered <s>Vācaspatimiśra</s>, [ends] the second <s>Sādhanapāda</s> (Chapter on Practice). (2)

children.text: tatra tṛtīyo vibhūtipādaḥ/
children.translated_text: Therein, the third [is] the <s>Vibhūtipāda</s> (Chapter on Supernatural Powers).

children.text: deśabandhaś cittasya dhāraṇā //3.1//
children.translated_text: <s>Dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) is the binding of the mind to a place. (3.1)

children.text:
prathamadvitīyapādābhyāṃ samādhis tatsādhanaṃ coktam/ tṛtīyapāde tatpravṛttyanuguṇāḥ
	śraddhotpādahetavo vibhūtayo vaktavyāḥ/ tāś ca saṃyamasādhyāḥ/ saṃyamaś ca
	dhāraṇādhyānasamādhisamudāya iti vibhūtisādhanatayā pañcabhyaś ca yogāṅgebhyo
	bahiraṅgebhyo+asyāṅgatrayasyāntaraṅgatayā viśeṣajñāpanārtham atra trayasyopanyāsaḥ/
	tatrāpi ca dhāraṇādhyānasamādhīnāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvena niyatapaurvāparyatvāt
	tadanurodhenopanyāse krama iti prathamaṃ dhāraṇā lakṣaṇīyety āha --- uktānīti/
	deśabandhaś cittasya dhāraṇā/ ādhyātmikadeśam āha --- nābhicakra iti/ ādiśabdena
	tālvādayo grāhyāḥ/ bandhaḥ saṃbandhaḥ/ bāhyadeśam āha --- bāhya iti/ bāhye ca na
	svarūpeṇa cittasya saṃbandhaḥ saṃbhavatīty uktaṃ vṛttimātreṇa jñānamātreṇeti/ atrāpi
	purāṇam ---
children.translated_text: In the first and second chapters, <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) and its means have been stated. In the third chapter, the supernatural powers (<s>vibhūtis</s>), which are causes for the arising of faith and are in accord with that [samādhi] practice, are to be stated. And those are accomplished through <s>saṃyama</s> (perfect discipline). And <s>saṃyama</s> is the aggregate of <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>samādhi</s> (absorption). Thus, the supernatural powers

children.text:
"prāṇāyāmena pavanaṃ pratyāhāreṇa cendriyam/ vaśīkṛtya tataḥ kuryāc cittasthānaṃ
	śubhāśraye"
viṣṇupurāṇam 6.7.45
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> 6.7.45]
'Having brought the breath under control through <s>prāṇāyāma</s> and the senses through <s>pratyāhāra</s>, one should then establish the mind on an auspicious support.'

children.text: śubhāśrayā bāhyā hiraṇyagarbhavāsavaprajāpatiprabhṛtayaḥ/ idaṃ ca tatroktam ---
children.translated_text: The auspicious external supports are <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra), <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the like. And this was stated there —

children.text:
"mūrtaṃ bhagavato rūpaṃ sarvopāśrayaniḥspṛham/ eṣā vai dhāraṇā jñeyā yac cittaṃ tatra
	dhāryate// tac ca mūrtaṃ hare rūpaṃ yad vicintyaṃ narādhipa/ tac chrūyatām anādhārā
	dhāraṇā nopapadyate// prasannavadanaṃ cārupadmapatranibhekṣaṇam/ sukapolaṃ
	suvistīrṇalalāṭaphalakojjvalam// samakarṇāntavinyastacārukuṇḍalabhūṣaṇam/ kambugrīvaṃ
	suvistīrṇaśrīvatsāṅkitavakṣasam// valīvibhaṅginā magnanābhinā codareṇa ca/
	pralambāṣṭabhujaṃ viṣṇum athavāpi caturbhujam//

samasthitorujaṅghaṃ ca
	svastikāṅghrivarāmbujam/ cintayed brahmabhūtaṃ taṃ pītanirmalavāsasam//
	kirīṭacārukeyūrakaṭakādivibhūṣitam/ śārṅgacakragadākhaḍgaśaṅkhākṣavalayānvitam//
	cintayet tanmayo yogī samādhāyātmamānasam/ tāvad yāvad dṛḍhībhūtā tatraiva nṛpa
	dhāraṇā// etad ātiṣṭhato+anyad vā svecchayā karma kurvataḥ/ nāpayāti yadā cittaṃ siddhāṃ
	manyeta tāṃ tadā"
children.translated_text: 'With thighs and shanks evenly placed, and lotus-feet in <s>svastika</s> posture, one should contemplate Him as <s>Brahman</s> incarnate, wearing pure yellow garments, adorned with crown, beautiful armlets, and bracelets, bearing the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, discus, mace, sword, conch, rosary, and bracelet — the <s>yogin</s> should meditate, becoming one with Him.'

children.text: viṣṇupurāṇam 6.7.77--85
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> 6.7.77-85]
Thus. (3.1)

'The embodied form of the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Lord), free from all attachment and the refuge of all — this is to be known as <s>dhāraṇā</s>, wherein the mind is held on that. And that embodied form of <s>Hari</s> which is to be contemplated, O king — hear of it; <s>dhāraṇā</s> without a support is not possible.'

children.text: tatra pratyayaikatānatā dhyānam //3.2//
children.translated_text: Therein, the uninterrupted flow of the same cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>) is <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). (3.2)

children.text:
dhāraṇāsādhyaṃ dhyānaṃ lakṣayati --- tatra pratyayaikatānatā dhyānam/
	ekatānataikāgratā/ sugamaṃ bhāṣyam/ atrāpi purāṇam ---
children.translated_text: He defines <s>dhyāna</s> as that which is accomplished through <s>dhāraṇā</s> — 'Therein, the uninterrupted flow of the same cognition is <s>dhyāna</s>.' Uninterrupted flow means one-pointedness. The <s>bhāṣya</s> is clear. Here too [he cites] a <s>Purāṇa</s> —

children.text:
"tadrūpapratyayaikāgryasaṃtatiś cānyaniḥspṛhā/ tad dhyānaṃ prathamair aṅgaiḥ ṣaḍbhir
	niṣpādyate nṛpa"
viṣṇupurāṇam 6.7.89
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> 6.7.89]
Thus. (3.2)
'The continuous stream of one-pointed cognition of that form, free from [distraction toward] other [objects] — that <s>dhyāna</s> is accomplished by the preceding six limbs, O king.'

children.text: tad evārthamātranirbhāsaṃ svarūpaśūnyam iva samādhiḥ //3.3//
children.translated_text: That very [meditation], when it shines forth as the object alone, as if empty of its own form, is <s>samādhi</s> (absorption). (3.3)

children.text:
dhyānasādhyaṃ samādhiṃ lakṣayati --- tad evārthamātranirbhāsaṃ svarūpaśūnyam iva
	samādhiḥ/ vyācaṣṭe --- dhyānam eveti/ dhyeyākāranirbhāsam iti/ dhyeyākārasyaiva nirbhāso
	na dhyānākārasyeti/ ata evāha --- śūnyam iti/ nanu śūnyaṃ cet kathaṃ dhyeyaṃ prakāśetety
	ata āha --- iveti/ atraiva hetum āha --- dhyeyasvabhāvāveśād iti/ atrāpi purāṇam ---
children.translated_text: He defines <s>samādhi</s> as that which is accomplished through <s>dhyāna</s> — 'That very [meditation], when it shines forth as the object alone, as if empty of its own form, is <s>samādhi</s>.' He explains — '<s>dhyāna</s> itself,' etc. 'Shining forth in the form of the object of meditation' — it is the shining forth of the form of the meditated object alone, not of the form of meditation [itself]. Hence he says —

children.text:
"tasyaiva kalpanāhīnaṃ svarūpagrahaṇaṃ hi yat/ manasā dhyānaniṣpādyaṃ samādhiḥ
	so+abhidhīyate"
viṣṇupurāṇam 6.7.90
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> 6.7.90]

children.text: iti//
children.translated_text: Thus.
'That apprehension of [the object's] own nature which is devoid of conceptual construction, accomplished by the mind through meditation — that is called <s>samādhi</s>.'

children.text:
dhyeyād dhyānasya bhedaḥ kalpanā taddhīnam ity arthaḥ/ aṣṭāṅgayogam uktvā khāṇḍikyāya
	keśidhvaja upasaṃjahāra ---
children.translated_text: The difference of <s>dhyāna</s> from the object of meditation is conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>); 'devoid of that' means devoid of [such conceptual construction] — such is the meaning. Having stated the eightfold <s>yoga</s>, <s>Keśidhvaja</s> concluded [his teaching] to <s>Khāṇḍikya</s> —

children.text:
"kṣetrajñaḥ karaṇī jñānaṃ karaṇaṃ tad acetanam/ niṣpādya muktikāryaṃ vai kṛtakṛtyaṃ
	nivartate"
viṣṇupurāṇam 6.7.92
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> 6.7.92]
Thus. (3.3)

'The <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field, i.e., the Self) is the agent; knowledge is the instrument, and that [instrument] is non-conscious. Having accomplished the purpose of liberation, it has fulfilled its task and ceases.'

children.text: trayam ekatra saṃyamaḥ //3.4//
children.translated_text: The three [together] upon a single [object] constitute <s>saṃyama</s> (perfect discipline). (3.4)

children.text:
dhāraṇādhyānasamādhir ity etattrayasya tatra tatra niyujyamānasya
	prātisvikasaṃjñoccāraṇe gauravaṃ syād iti lāghavārthaṃ paribhāṣāsūtram avatārayati ---
	trayam ekatra saṃyamaḥ/ vyācaṣṭe --- ekaviṣayāṇīti (tad etad iti)/ vācakatvaśaṅkām
	apanayati --- tad asyeti/ tantryate vyutpādyate yogo yena śāstreṇa tat tantraṃ tadbhavā
	tāntrikī/ saṃyamapradeśāḥ "pariṇāmatrayasaṃyamāt-"
yogasūtram 3.16
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>Yogasūtra</s> 3.16]

children.text: ityevamādayaḥ //3.4//
children.translated_text: and so forth. (3.4)

Since separately pronouncing the individual names of the triad — <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> — whenever they are applied to various [objects] would be cumbersome, he introduces a definitional <s>sūtra</s> for the sake of brevity: 'The three upon a single [object] constitute <s>saṃyama</s>.' He explains — 'on a single object,'

children.text: tajjayāt prajñālokaḥ //3.5//
children.translated_text: From the mastery of that [<s>saṃyama</s>], there arises the light of wisdom (<s>prajñāloka</s>). (3.5)

children.text:
saṃyamavijayasyābhyāsasādhanasya phalam āha --- tajjayāt prajñālokaḥ/
	pratyayāntarānabhibhūtasya nirmalapravāhe+avasthānam ālokaḥ prajñāyāḥ/ sugamaṃ
	bhāṣyam //3.5//
children.translated_text: He states the fruit of the conquest of <s>saṃyama</s>, which is accomplished through practice — 'From the mastery of that, the light of wisdom.' The state of abiding in a pure stream [of cognition], not overcome by other cognitions, is the 'light' (<s>āloka</s>) of wisdom. The <s>bhāṣya</s> is clear. (3.5)

children.text: tasya bhūmiṣu viniyogaḥ //3.6//
children.translated_text: Its application is in stages (<s>bhūmis</s>). (3.6)

children.text:
kva punar viniyuktasya saṃyamasya phalam etad ity ata āha --- tasya bhūmiṣu viniyogaḥ/
	bhūmiṃ viśeṣayati bhāṣyakāraḥ --- tasyeti/ jitāyā bhūmer yānantarā bhūmir avasthājitā
	tatra viniyogaḥ/ sthūlaviṣaye savitarke samādhau vaśīkṛte saṃyamena saṃyamasyāvijite
	nirvitarke viniyogaḥ/ tasminn api vaśīkṛte savicāre viniyogaḥ/ evaṃ nirvicāre viniyoga
	ity arthaḥ/ ata eva sthūlaviṣayasamāpattisiddhau satyāṃ purāṇe
	tattadāyudhabhūṣaṇāpanayena sūkṣmaviṣayaḥ samādhir avatāritaḥ ---
children.translated_text: Where, then, when applied, does <s>saṃyama</s> yield this fruit? Hence he says — 'Its application is in stages.' The <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) specifies the stage — 'of that,' etc. [One should apply saṃyama] in the stage immediately following the stage that has been conquered — the stage [just beyond] the conquered state; there is the application. The gross

children.text:
"tataḥ śaṅkhagadācakraśārṅgādirahitaṃ budhaḥ/ cintayed bhagavadrūpaṃ praśāntaṃ
	sākṣasūtrakam//

yadā ca dhāraṇā tasminn avasthānavatī tataḥ/
	kirīṭakeyūramukhair bhūṣaṇai rahitaṃ smaret// tadaikāvayavaṃ devaṃ so+ahaṃ ceti punar
	budhaḥ/ kuryāt tato hy aham iti praṇidhānaparo bhavet//"
children.translated_text: 'And when <s>dhāraṇā</s> on that [form] becomes stable, then one should meditate on [the form] without crown, armlets, and other ornaments. The wise one should [contemplate] the deity as a single [undifferentiated] part, [thinking] "He am I"; then, [thinking] "I" [alone], one should become absorbed in meditation (<s>praṇidhāna</s>).'

children.text: viṣṇupurāṇam 6.7.86--88
children.translated_text: [Reference: <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> 6.7.86-88]

children.text: iti//
children.translated_text: Thus.
'Then the wise one should contemplate the form of the <s>Bhagavān</s> without conch, mace, discus, <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, and the like — serene, [wearing only] the rosary and sacred thread.'

children.text:
kasmāt punar adharāṃ bhūmiṃ vijityottarāṃ vijayate viparyayaḥ kasmān na bhavatīty ata
	āha --- na hy ajitādharabhūmir iti/ na hi śilāhradād gaṅgāṃ prati prasthito+aprāpya
	meghavanaṃ gaṅgāṃ prāpnoti/ īśvaraprasādāj jitottarabhūmikasya ceti kasmāt
	tadarthasyottarabhūmivijayasya pratyāsannasyānyata eveśvarapraṇidhānād evāvagatatvāt/
	niṣpāditakriye karmaṇy aviśeṣādhāyinaḥ sādhanasya sādhananyāyātipātād iti/ syād etad
	āgamataḥ sāmānyato+avagatānām apy avāntarabhūmibhedānāṃ kutaḥ paurvāparyāvagatir ity ata
	āha --- bhūmer asyā iti/ jitaḥ pūrvo yoga uttarasya yogasya jñānapravṛttyadhigamahetuḥ/
	avasthaivāvasthāvān ity abhipretyaitad draṣṭavyam //3.6//
children.translated_text: Why does one conquer the lower stage first and then the higher? Why does the reverse not occur? Hence he says — 'For one who has not conquered the lower stage,' etc. Just as one who has set out from a rocky lake toward the <s>Gaṅgā</s> does not reach the <s>Gaṅgā</s> without reaching <s>Meghavana</s> [first]. 'And of one who has conquered the higher stage through <s>Īśvara</s>'s grace' — why, when the conquest of the higher stage, which serves that purpose, is near at hand, [should one seek] from elsewhere — since it is already known from <s>Īśvara-praṇidhāna</s> alone? Because a means that contributes nothing special to an action whose purpose has already been accomplished transgresses the proper method of means. One might say: even though the distinctions of sub-stages are known in general from scripture, how is their sequential order known? Hence he says — 'of this stage,' etc. The earlier <s>yoga</s> that has been mastered is the cause for the attainment of knowledge and activity in the subsequent <s>yoga</s>. This should be understood with the intention that 'the state itself is the possessor of the state.' //3.6//

children.text: trayam antaraṅgaṃ pūrvebhyaḥ //3.7//
children.translated_text: 'The three [<s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samādhi</s>] are inner limbs (<s>antaraṅga</s>) relative to the preceding [five].' //3.7//

children.text:
kasmāt punar yogāṅgatvāviśeṣe+api saṃyamasya tatra tatra viniyogo nerareṣāṃ pañcānām
	ity ata āha --- trayam antaraṅgaṃ pūrvebhyaḥ/ tad idaṃ sādhanatrayaṃ
	sādhyasamānaviṣayatvenāntaraṅgaṃ na tv evaṃ yamādayas tasmāt te bahiraṅgā ity arthaḥ //3.7//
children.translated_text: Why is <s>saṃyama</s> applied to various objects here and there, and not the other five [limbs], given that there is no difference in their being limbs of <s>yoga</s>? Hence he says — 'The three are inner limbs relative to the preceding.' This triad of means is inner (<s>antaraṅga</s>) because it shares the same object as the goal (<s>sādhya</s>); but <s>yama</s> and the rest are not thus — hence they are outer (<s>bahiraṅga</s>) — such is the meaning. //3.7//

children.text: tad api bahiraṅgaṃ nirbījasya //3.8//
children.translated_text: 'Even that [triad] is outer (<s>bahiraṅga</s>) relative to the seedless (<s>nirbīja</s>) [<s>samādhi</s>].' //3.8//

children.text:
sādhanatrayasya saṃprajñāta evāntaraṅgatvaṃ na tv asaṃprajñāte tasya nirbījatayā taiḥ
	saha samānaviṣayatvābhāvāt teṣu ciraniruddheṣu
	saṃprajñātaparamakāṣṭhāparanāmajñānaprasādarūpaparavairāgyānantaram utpādāc cety āha ---
	tad iti/ tad api bahiraṅgaṃ nirbījasya/ samānaviṣayatvam antaraṅgatvaprayojakam iha na
	tu tadanantarabhāvas tasya bahiraṅgeśvarapraṇidhānavartitayā savyabhicāratvād iti sthite
	savyabhicāram apy antaraṅgalakṣaṇaṃ tadanantarabhāvitvam asya nāsti/ tasmād
	dūrāpetāntaraṅgatā saṃyamasyāsaṃprajñāta iti darśayituṃ tadabhāve bhāvād ity uktam //3.8//
children.translated_text: The inner-limb nature of the triad of means belongs to <s>saṃprajñāta</s> [<s>samādhi</s>] alone, not to <s>asaṃprajñāta</s>, since the latter, being seedless (<s>nirbīja</s>), does not share the same object with those [three]; and since, after those [three] have been suppressed for a long time, [<s>asaṃprajñāta</s>] arises after the supreme <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) in the form of <s>jñānaprasāda</s> (clarity of knowledge), which is the alternative name for the ultimate limit of <s>saṃprajñāta</s> — hence he says — 'that,' etc. 'Even that is outer relative to the seedless.' Sharing the same object is what makes something an inner limb here, not [merely] being immediately subsequent — since that [criterion of immediate subsequence] would be deviant, because [<s>asaṃprajñāta</s>] also occurs through the outer [limb of] <s>Īśvara-praṇidhāna</s>. Given this, even the deviant characteristic of inner-limb-hood — being immediately subsequent — does not belong to this [<s>saṃyama</s> in relation to <s>asaṃprajñāta</s>]. Therefore, in order to show that the inner-limb-hood of <s>saṃyama</s> is far removed from <s>asaṃprajñāta</s>, it is said 'arising in its absence.' //3.8//

children.text:
vyutthānanirodhasaṃskārayor abhibhavaprādurbhāvau nirodhakṣaṇacittānvayo
	  nirodhapariṇāmaḥ //3.9//
children.translated_text: 'The suppression and emergence of the <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions) of the outgoing state (<s>vyutthāna</s>) and cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), occurring in conjunction with the mind at the moment of cessation — that is the cessation-transformation (<s>nirodha-pariṇāma</s>).' //3.9//

children.text:
pariṇāmatrayasaṃyamād ity atropayokṣyamāṇapariṇāmatrayaṃ pratipipādayiṣur
	nirbījaprasaṅgena pṛcchati --- atheti/ vyutthānasaṃprajñātayoś cittasya
	sphuṭatarapariṇāmabhedapracayānubhavān na praśnāvatāro nirodhe tu nānubhūyate pariṇāmaḥ/
	na cānanubhūyamāno nāsti, cittasya triguṇatayā calatvena guṇānāṃ kṣaṇam apy
	apariṇāmasyāsaṃbhavād ity arthaḥ/ praśnottaraṃ sūtram --- vyutthānanirodhasaṃskārayor
	abhibhavaprādurbhāvau nirodhakṣaṇacittānvayo nirodhapariṇāmaḥ/ asaṃprajñātaṃ samādhim
	apekṣya saṃprajñāto vyutthānam/ nirudhyate 'neneti nirodho jñānaprasādaḥ paraṃ vairāgyaṃ
	tayor vyutthānanirodhasaṃskārayor abhibhavaprādurbhāvau/ tatra
	vyutthānasaṃskārasyābhibhavo nirodhasaṃskārasyāvirbhāvaś cittasya dharmiṇo
	nirodhakṣaṇasya nirodhāvasarasya dvayor avasthayor anvayaḥ/ na hi cittaṃ dharmi
	saṃprajñātāvasthāyām asaṃprajñātāvasthāyāṃ ca saṃskārābhibhavaprādurbhāvayoḥ svarūpeṇa
	bhidyata iti/ nanu yathottare kleśā avidyāmūlā avidyānivṛttau nivartanta iti na tu
	tannivṛttau pṛthak prayatnāntaram āsthīyata evaṃ vyutthānapratyayamūlāḥ saṃskārā
	vyutthānapratyayanivṛttāv eva

nivartanta iti tannivṛttau na
	nirodhasaṃskāro+apekṣitavya ity ata āha --- vyutthānasaṃskārā iti/ na
	kāraṇamātranivṛttiḥ kāryanivṛttihetur mā bhūt kuvindanivṛttāv api paṭasya nivṛttir api
	tu yatkāraṇātmakaṃ yatkāryaṃ tatkāraṇanivṛttau tatkāryanivṛttiḥ/ uttare ca kleśā
	avidyātmāna ity uktam atas tannivṛttau teṣāṃ nivṛttir upapannā/ na tv evaṃ
	pratyayātmānaḥ saṃskārāś ciraniruddhe pratyaye saṃprati smaraṇadarśanāt/ tasmāt
	pratyayanivṛttāv api tannivṛttau nirodhasaṃskārapracaya evopāsanīya ity arthaḥ/ sugamam
	anyat //3.9//
children.translated_text: and they would cease [upon cessation of their cause] — and in their cessation, the <s>nirodha-saṃskāra</s> would not be needed. Hence he says — 'the <s>vyutthāna-saṃskāras</s>,' etc. The mere cessation of a cause is not the cause of the cessation of its effect — lest upon the cessation of a weaver, the cloth too should cease. Rather, when an effect is essentially identical with its cause, upon the cessation of that cause, that effect ceases. And the subsequent <s>kleśas</s> have been said to be of the nature of <s>avidyā</s> — hence their cessation upon <s>avidyā</s>'s cessation is justified. But <s>saṃskāras</s>, which are of the nature of <s>pratyaya</s> (cognition), are not thus — for even long after the cognition has been suppressed, the memory born of [those <s>saṃskāras</s>] is observed at present. Therefore, even upon the cessation of the cognition, for their cessation, the accumulation of <s>nirodha-saṃskāras</s> alone is to be cultivated — such is the meaning. The rest is easy to understand. //3.9//

Wishing to explain the threefold transformation that will be employed [later] in 'through <s>saṃyama</s> on the three transformations,' in connection with the seedless [<s>samādhi</s>] he asks — 'now,' etc. In the outgoing and <s>saṃprajñāta</s> [states] of the mind, there is no occasion for the question, since the succession of distinct transformations is more clearly experienced. But in <s>nirodha</s>, the transformation is not experienced. Yet what is not experienced does not thereby not exist — since the mind, being composed of the three <s>guṇas</s>, is ever in motion, and the non-transformation of the <s>guṇas</s> is impossible even for a single moment — such is the meaning. The <s>sūtra</s> that answers the question: 'The suppression and emergence of the <s>saṃskāras</s> of the outgoing state and cessation, occurring in conjunction with the mind at the moment of cessation — that is the cessation-transformation.' Relative to <s>asaṃprajñāta samādhi</s>, <s>saṃprajñāta</s> is the 'outgoing state' (<s>vyutthāna</s>). 'That by which [the mind] is restrained (<s>nirudhyate</s>) is <s>nirodha</s>' — the clarity of knowledge (<s>jñānaprasāda</s>), the supreme <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion). Of those two — the <s>vyutthāna</s> and <s>nirodha</s> <s>saṃskāras</s> — there are suppression and emergence. Therein, the suppression of the <s>vyutthāna-saṃskāra</s> and the emergence of the <s>nirodha-saṃskāra</s> — these two states accompany (<s>anvaya</s>) the mind as the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) at the moment of cessation. For the mind as the property-bearer is not different in essential nature between the <s>saṃprajñāta</s> state and the <s>asaṃprajñāta</s> state in regard to the suppression and emergence of <s>saṃskāras</s>. [Objection:] Just as the subsequent <s>kleśas</s>, rooted in <s>avidyā</s>, cease upon the cessation of <s>avidyā</s>, and no separate additional effort is applied for their cessation — so too, the <s>saṃskāras</s> rooted in the <s>vyutthāna-pratyaya</s> (outgoing cognition) would cease upon the cessation of the <s>vyutthāna-pratyaya</s> alone,

children.text: tasya praśāntavāhitā saṃskārāt //3.10//
children.translated_text: 'Its [the mind's] flow of tranquility (<s>praśāntavāhitā</s>) [arises] from the <s>saṃskāra</s> [of cessation].' //3.10//

children.text:
sarvathā vyutthānasaṃskārābhibhave tu balavatā nirodhasaṃskāreṇa cittasya kīdṛśaḥ
	pariṇāma ity ata āha --- tasya praśāntavāhitā saṃskārāt/
	vyutthānasaṃskāramalarahitanirodhasaṃskāraparamparāmātravāhitā praśāntavāhitā/ kasmāt
	punaḥ saṃskārapāṭavam apekṣate na tu saṃskāramātram ity ata āha --- tatsaṃskāramāndya
	iti/ tad iti nirodhaṃ parāmṛśati/ ye tu nābhibhūyata iti paṭhanti te tadā vyutthānaṃ
	parāmṛśanti //3.10//
children.translated_text: When the <s>vyutthāna-saṃskāras</s> have been completely suppressed by the powerful <s>nirodha-saṃskāra</s>, what kind of transformation does the mind undergo? Hence he says — 'Its flow of tranquility from the <s>saṃskāra</s>.' The flow (<s>vāhitā</s>) consisting solely of the unbroken succession of <s>nirodha-saṃskāras</s>, free from the defilement of <s>vyutthāna-saṃskāras</s>, is the <s>praśāntavāhitā</s> (flow of tranquility). Why does [this] require proficiency (<s>pāṭava</s>) of <s>saṃskāra</s> and not mere <s>saṃskāra</s>? Hence he says — 'the weakness of that <s>saṃskāra</s>,' etc. 'That' refers to <s>nirodha</s>. But those who read 'is not suppressed' refer [it] to <s>vyutthāna</s>. //3.10//

children.text: sarvārthataikāgratayoḥ kṣayodayau cittasya samādhipariṇāmaḥ //3.11//
children.translated_text: 'The decline of all-pointedness (<s>sarvārthatā</s>) and the rise of one-pointedness (<s>ekāgratā</s>) [in] the mind — that is the <s>samādhi</s>-transformation (<s>samādhi-pariṇāma</s>).' //3.11//

children.text:
saṃprajñātasamādhipariṇāmāvasthāṃ cittasya darśayati --- sarvārthataikāgratayoḥ
	kṣayodayau cittasya samādhipariṇāmaḥ/ vikṣiptatā sarvārthatā/ san na vinaśyatīti kṣayas
	tirobhāvo nāsad utpadyata iti udaya āvirbhāvaḥ/ svātmabhūtayoḥ sarvārthataikāgratayor
	dharmayor yāv apāyopajanau

sarvārthatāyā apāya ekāgratāyā upajanas tayor
	anugataṃ cittaṃ samādhīyate pūrvāparībhūtasādhyamānasamādhiviśeṣaṇaṃ bhavatīti //3.11//
children.translated_text: the decrease of all-pointedness and the increase of one-pointedness — the mind, following both of these, becomes concentrated (<s>samādhīyate</s>), becomes qualified by the <s>samādhi</s> that is being progressively accomplished. //3.11//

He shows the state of the mind's <s>samādhi</s>-transformation in <s>saṃprajñāta-samādhi</s> — 'The decline of all-pointedness and the rise of one-pointedness of the mind — that is the <s>samādhi</s>-transformation.' All-pointedness (<s>sarvārthatā</s>) is the scattered state (<s>vikṣiptatā</s>). 'Decline' (<s>kṣaya</s>) — what exists does not perish — is concealment. 'Rise' (<s>udaya</s>) — what does not exist does not come into being — is manifestation. Of the two <s>dharmas</s> (properties) — all-pointedness and one-pointedness — which are the mind's own nature, their respective decrease and increase —

children.text: tataḥ punaḥ śāntoditau tulyapratyayau cittasyaikāgratāpariṇāmaḥ //3.12//
children.translated_text: 'Then again, when the quiescent (<s>śānta</s>) and the arisen (<s>udita</s>) [cognitions] are similar (<s>tulyapratyaya</s>), [there is] the one-pointedness-transformation (<s>ekāgratā-pariṇāma</s>) of the mind.' //3.12//

children.text:
tataḥ punaḥ śāntoditau tulyapratyayau cittasyaikāgratāpariṇāmaḥ/ punaḥ samādheḥ
	pūrvāparībhūtāyā avasthāyāḥ samādhiniṣpattau satyāṃ śāntoditāv atītavartamānau, tulyau
	ca tau pratyayau ceti tulyapratyayau/ ekāgratāyāṃ tu dvayoḥ sādṛśyam/ samāhitacittasyeti
	samādhiniṣpattir darśitā/ tathaivaikāgram eva/ avadhim āha --- ā samādhibhreṣād bhraṃśād
	iti //3.12//
children.translated_text: 'Then again, when the quiescent and the arisen are similar cognitions — the one-pointedness-transformation of the mind.' 'Again' — from the state in which <s>samādhi</s> had been progressive [i.e., being accomplished], when <s>samādhi</s> has been fully accomplished, 'quiescent and arisen' means past and present; 'similar cognitions' means both of them are similar cognitions. In one-pointedness, the two [cognitions] are alike. 'Of the concentrated mind' shows the accomplishment of <s>samādhi</s>. 'Likewise one-pointed alone.' He states the limit — 'until the break (<s>bhreṣa</s>) of <s>samādhi</s>, the fall.' //3.12//

children.text: etena bhūtendriyeṣu dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmā vyākhyātāḥ //3.13//
children.translated_text: 'By this, the transformations of property (<s>dharma</s>), character (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), and state (<s>avasthā</s>) in the elements (<s>bhūta</s>) and sense organs (<s>indriya</s>) are explained.' //3.13//

children.text:
prāsaṅgikaṃ ca vakṣyamāṇaupayikaṃ ca bhūtendriyapariṇāmaṃ vibhajate --- etena
	bhūtendriyeṣu dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmā vyākhyātāḥ/ vyācaṣṭe --- eteneti/ nanu
	cittapariṇatimātram uktaṃ na tu tatprakārā dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmās tat kathaṃ teṣām
	atideśa ity ata āha --- tatra vyutthānanirodhayor iti/ dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāśabdāḥ paraṃ
	noccāritā na tu dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmā noktā iti saṃkṣepārthaḥ/ tathā hi
	vyutthānanirodhasaṃskārayor ity atraiva sūtre dharmapariṇāma uktaḥ/ imaṃ ca
	dharmapariṇāmaṃ darśayatā tenaiva dharmādhikaraṇo

lakṣaṇapariṇāmo+api
	sūcita evety āha --- lakṣaṇapariṇāma iti/ lakṣyate 'neneti lakṣaṇaṃ kālabhedaḥ/ tena hi
	lakṣitaṃ vastu vastvantarebhyaḥ kālāntarayuktebhyo vyavacchidyata iti/ nirodhas
	trilakṣaṇaḥ/ asyaiva vyākhyānaṃ tribhir adhvabhir yuktaḥ/ adhvaśabdaḥ kālavacanaḥ/ sa
	khalv anāgatalakṣaṇam adhvānaṃ prathamaṃ hitvā, tat kim adhvavaddharmatvam apy atipatati
	nety āha --- dharmatvam anatikrānto vartamānalakṣaṇaṃ pratipannaḥ/ ya eva
	nirodho+anāgata āsīt sa eva saṃprati vartamāno na tu nirodho 'nirodha ity arthaḥ/
	vartamānatāsvarūpavyākhyānam --- yatrāsya svarūpeṇa svocitārthakriyākāriṇā
	rūpeṇābhivyaktiḥ samudācāraḥ/ eṣo+asya prathamam anāgatam adhvānam apekṣya
	dvitīyo+adhvā/ syād etad anāgatam adhvānaṃ hitvā ced vartamānatām āpannas tāṃ ca
	hitvātītatām āpatsyate hanta bhor adhvanām utpādavināśau syātām/ na ceṣyete, na hy asata
	utpādo nāpi sato vināśa ity ata āha --- na cātītānāgatābhyāṃ sāmānyātmanāvasthitābhyāṃ
	viyukta iti/ anāgatasya nirodhasya vartamānatālakṣaṇaṃ darśayitvā
	vartamānavyutthānasyātītatāṃ tṛtīyam adhvānam āha --- tathā vyutthānam iti/ tat kiṃ
	nirodha evānāgato na vyutthānaṃ nety āha --- evaṃ punar vyutthānam iti/
	vyutthānajātyapekṣayā punarbhāvo na vyaktyapekṣayā/ na hy atītaṃ punarbhavatīti/
	svarūpābhivyaktir arthakriyākṣamasyāvirbhāvaḥ/ sa caivaṃlakṣaṇapariṇāma uktas
	tajjātīyeṣu paunaḥpunyena vartata ity ata āha --- evaṃ punar iti/
children.translated_text: The <s>lakṣaṇapariṇāma</s> (transformation of characteristic/time-phase) is also indicated — thus he says: '<s>lakṣaṇapariṇāma</s>.' That by which [a thing] is characterized (<s>lakṣyate</s>) is the characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) — [namely,] the distinction of time. For by that, the thing characterized is distinguished from other things associated with other times. <s>Nirodha</s> (cessation) has three characteristics. The explanation of this: 'endowed with three time-paths (<s>adhvan</s>).' The word '<s>adhvan</s>' denotes time. That [<s>nirodha</s>], having first abandoned the characteristic of the future time-path — does it also transcend its property-nature? To that he says: 'not having transcended its property-nature, it has assumed the characteristic of the present.' The very <s>nirodha</s> that was future is now present — [but] <s>nirodha</s> does not [become] non-<s>nirodha</s>. This is the meaning. The explanation of the nature of presentness: 'where there is its manifestation, its operation, in its own form — in a form capable of its appropriate function.' This is its second time-path, with reference to the first [time-path of] the future. One might say: if, having abandoned the future time-path, it has attained presentness, and having abandoned that, will attain pastness — alas! — there would be origination and destruction of time-paths! And that is not desired, for there is neither origination of what is non-existent nor destruction of what exists. To this he replies: 'And it is not disconnected from the past and future, which subsist in their universal form (<s>sāmānyātman</s>).' Having shown the present characteristic of future <s>nirodha</s>, he states the third time-path — the pastness of present emergence (<s>vyutthāna</s>): 'likewise emergence.' Is it only <s>nirodha</s> that was future and not emergence? No — hence he says: 'likewise emergence again.' 'Again' (<s>punar</s>) refers to recurrence with respect to the class (<s>jāti</s>), not with respect to the individual instance (<s>vyakti</s>). For what is past does not recur [as the same individual]. The manifestation of its own form is the appearance of what is capable of [its appropriate] function. And that <s>lakṣaṇapariṇāma</s> (transformation of time-phase), thus defined, recurs repeatedly among instances of the same class — hence he says: 'likewise again.'

children.text:
dharmapariṇāmasūcitam evāvasthāpariṇāmam āha --- tatheti/ dharmāṇāṃ vartamānādhvanāṃ
	balavattvābalavattve avasthā tasyāḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ tāratamyaṃ pariṇāmaḥ/ upasaṃharati ---
	eṣa iti/ pariṇāmabhedānāṃ saṃbandhibhedān nirdhārayati --- tatrānubhavānusārād dharmiṇa
	iti/ tat kim eṣa pariṇāmo guṇānāṃ kādācitko nety āha --- evam iti/ kasmāt punar ayaṃ
	pariṇāmaḥ sadātana ity ata āha --- calaṃ ceti/ co hetvarthaḥ/ vṛttaṃ pracāraḥ/ etad eva
	kuta ity ata āha --- guṇasvābhāvyam iti/ uktam atraiva purastāt/ so+ayaṃ trividho+api
	cittapariṇāmo bhūtendriyeṣu sūtrakāreṇa nirdiṣṭa ity āha --- eteneti/ eṣa
	dharmapariṇāmabhedo dharmadharmiṇor bhedam ālakṣya/ tatra bhūtānāṃ pṛthivyādīnāṃ
	dharmiṇāṃ gavādir ghaṭādir vā dharmapariṇāmaḥ/ dharmāṇāṃ cātītānāgatavartamānarūpatā
	lakṣaṇapariṇāmaḥ/ vartamānalakṣaṇāpannasya gavāder bālyakaumārayauvanavārdhakyam
	avasthāpariṇāmaḥ/ ghaṭādīnām api navapurātanatāvasthāpariṇāmaḥ/ evam indriyāṇām api
	dharmiṇāṃ tattannīlādyālocanaṃ dharmapariṇāmo dharmasya vartamānatādilakṣaṇapariṇāmo
	vartamānalakṣaṇasya ratnādyālocanasya sphuṭatvāsphuṭatvādir avasthāpariṇāmaḥ/ so+ayam
	evaṃvidho bhūtendriyapariṇāmo dharmiṇo dharmalakṣaṇāvasthānāṃ bhedam āśritya veditavyaḥ/
	abhedam āśrityāha --- paramārthatas tv iti/ tuśabdo bhedapakṣād viśinaṣṭi/
	pāramārthikatvam asya jñāpyate na tv anyasya pariṇāmatvaṃ niṣidhyate/ kasmāt ---
	dharmisvarūpamātro hīti/ nanu yadi dharmivikriyaiva dharmaḥ katham asaṃkarapratyayo loke
	pariṇāmeṣv ity
children.translated_text: He states the <s>avasthāpariṇāma</s> (transformation of condition), which was indicated by the <s>dharmapariṇāma</s> (transformation of property): 'likewise.' The condition (<s>avasthā</s>) of properties — [i.e.,] of those in the present time-path — is their being strong or weak; its progressive gradation at each moment is the transformation. He concludes: 'this.' He determines the distinctions in the transformations according to the distinctions in their substrata: 'therein, according to the sequence of experience, [the transformations are] of the substratum (<s>dharmin</s>).' Is this transformation of the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents) occasional? No — hence he says: 'thus.' Why is this transformation perpetual? To this he says: 'and because activity [of the <s>guṇas</s>] is restless.' The word 'ca' (and) has causal force. '<s>Vṛtta</s>' means operation. But why is this so? To this he says: 'it is the inherent nature of the <s>guṇas</s>.' This has been stated earlier in this very [commentary]. This threefold transformation of the mind has been indicated by the author of the <s>sūtras</s> also with respect to the [gross] elements and sense-organs — hence he says: 'by this.' This classification of <s>dharmapariṇāma</s> is made by observing the distinction between property (<s>dharma</s>) and substratum (<s>dharmin</s>). Therein, for the substrata, the [gross] elements earth, etc. — the <s>dharmapariṇāma</s> [consists of] cow, etc., or pot, etc. The assuming of past, future, and present forms by the properties is the <s>lakṣaṇapariṇāma</s>. For a cow, etc., that has assumed the present characteristic — childhood, youth, maturity, and old age is the <s>avasthāpariṇāma</s>. For pots, etc., too — the conditions of being new or old, etc. is the <s>avasthāpariṇāma</s>. Likewise for the sense-organs as substrata — the apprehension of this or that [object], such as blue, etc., is the <s>dharmapariṇāma</s>; the property's [assuming of] present, etc. characteristics is the <s>lakṣaṇapariṇāma</s>; of the present-characterized apprehension of a jewel, etc., its being clear or unclear, etc. is the <s>avasthāpariṇāma</s>. This kind of transformation of elements and sense-organs should be understood by distinguishing the substratum's property, characteristic, and condition. He states the undifferentiated [view]: 'But in ultimate truth.' The word 'tu' (but) distinguishes from the differentiation-approach. The ultimate truth of this [undifferentiated transformation] is being indicated, not the transformativeness of the other [differentiated ones] being denied. Why? 'For it is merely the essential nature of the substratum.' Now, if the modification of the substratum itself is the property, how [can there be] the cognition of non-confusion in the world regarding transformations?

children.text:
ata āha --- dharmadvāreti/ dharmaśabdena
	dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāḥ parigṛhyante/ taddvāreṇa dharmiṇa eva vikriyety ekā cāsaṃkīrṇā ca/
	taddvārāṇām abhede+api dharmiṇaḥ parasparasaṃkarāt/ nanu dharmāṇām abhinnatve
	dharmiṇo+adhvanāṃ ca bhede dharmiṇo 'nanyatvena dharmeṇāpīha dharmivad bhavitavyam ity
	ata āha --- tatra dharmasyeti/ bhāvaḥ saṃsthānabhedaḥ/ suvarṇāder yathā bhājanasya
	rucakasvastikavyapadeśabhedo bhavati tanmātram anyathā bhavati na tu dravyaṃ suvarṇam
	asuvarṇatām upaiti atyantabhedābhāvād iti/ vakṣyamāṇābhisaṃdhir ekāntavādinaṃ bauddham
	utthāpayati --- apara āheti/ dharmā eva hi rucakādayas tathotpannāḥ paramārthasanto na
	punaḥ suvarṇaṃ nāma kiṃcid ekam anekeṣv anugataṃ dravyam iti/ yadi punar nivartamāneṣv
	api dharmeṣu dravyam anugataṃ bhavet tato na citiśaktivat pariṇametāpi tu
	kauṭasthyenaiva parivarteta/ pariṇāmātmakaṃ rūpaṃ parihāya rūpāntareṇa kauṭasthyena
	parivartanaṃ parivṛttiḥ/ yathā citiśaktir anyathānyathābhāvaṃ bhajamāneṣv api guṇeṣu
	svarūpād apracyutā kūṭasthanityaivaṃ suvarṇādy api syān na ceṣyate/ tasmān na dravyam
	atiriktaṃ dharmebhya iti/ pariharati --- ayam adoṣa iti/ kasmāt/ ekāntatānabhyupagamāt/
	yadi citiśakter iva dravyasyaikāntikīṃ nityatām abhyupagacchema tata evam upālabhyemahi/
	na tv aikāntikīṃ nityatām ātiṣṭhāmahe kiṃ tu tad etat trailokyaṃ na tu dravyamātraṃ
	vyakter arthakriyākāriṇo rūpād apaiti/
children.translated_text: To this he replies: 'through the gateway of properties.' By the word 'property,' properties, characteristics, and conditions are included. It is the substratum alone that is modified through these gateways — it is one and unmixed. But if those gateways were not different [from the substratum], there would be mutual confusion of the substrata [themselves]. Now, if the properties are not different [from the substratum], and the time-paths are different [from each other], then since the substratum is not different from the property, it too should here have [the same nature as the substratum] — like the substratum. To this he replies: 'therein, of the property.' '<s>Bhāva</s>' means a difference of configuration. Just as for gold, etc., there are different designations for vessels — such as 'bracelet,' '<s>svastika</s>-ornament' — only that much changes, but the substance, gold, does not become non-gold, because there is no absolute difference. He raises the objection of the absolutist (<s>ekāntavādin</s>), the <s>Bauddha</s> (Buddhist), with a view to what will be stated: 'Another says.' For the properties alone — bracelets, etc. — having arisen in that manner, are real in the ultimate sense. But there is no single substance called 'gold' that pervades many [forms]. For if a substance persisted even when properties change, it would not undergo transformation like the <s>citiśakti</s> (power of consciousness), but would persist merely in immutability (<s>kūṭasthya</s>). '<s>Parivṛtti</s>' (change) is the alteration by which [a thing], having abandoned one transformative form, persists in immutability through another form. Just as <s>citiśakti</s>, while the <s>guṇas</s> undergo change, remains undeviated from its own form, eternally immutable — so too gold, etc., would be [if it were an unchanging substance]. And this is not desired. Therefore, there is no substance over and above the properties. He resolves [the objection]: 'This is no fault.' Why? 'Because absolute [eternity] is not accepted.' If we accepted an absolute eternity of substance, like the <s>citiśakti</s>, then we could indeed be so criticized. But we do not maintain absolute eternity. Rather, this entire three-world [system] — not the substance alone — does not deviate from the manifest, functionally efficacious form.

children.text:
kasmān nityatvapratiṣedhāt
	pramāṇena/ yadi hi ghaṭo vyakter nāpeyāt kapālaśarkarācūrṇādiṣv avasthāsv api vyakto
	ghaṭa iti pūrvavad upalabdhyarthakriye kuryāt tasmād anityaṃ trailokyam/ astu tarhy
	anityam evopalabdhyarthakriyārahitatvena gaganāravindavad atitucchatvād ity ata āha ---
	apetam apy asti, nātyantatucchatā yenaikāntato+anityaṃ syād ity arthaḥ/ kasmād
	vināśapratiṣedhāt pramāṇena/ tathā hi yat tucchaṃ na tat kadācid apy upalabdhyarthakriye
	karoti/ yathā gaganāravindam/ karoti caitat trailokyaṃ kadācid upalabdhyarthakriye iti/
	tathotpattimaddravyatvadharmalakṣaṇāvasthāyogitvādayo+apy
	atyantatucchagagananalinanaraviṣāṇādivyāvṛttāḥ sattvahetava udāhāryāḥ/ tathā ca dharmī
	nātyantaṃ nityo yena citiśaktivat kūṭasthanityaḥ syāt kiṃ tu kathaṃcin nityaḥ/ tathā ca
	pariṇāmīti siddham/ etena mṛtpiṇḍādyavasthāsu kāryāṇāṃ ghaṭādīnām anāgatānāṃ sattvaṃ
	veditavyam/ syād etat/ apetam api ced asti kasmāt pūrvavan nopalabhyata ity ata āha ---
	saṃsargāt svakāraṇalayāt saukṣmyaṃ darśanānarhatvaṃ tataś cānupalabdhir iti/ tad evaṃ
	dharmapariṇāmaṃ samarthya lakṣaṇapariṇāmam api lakṣaṇānāṃ parasparānugamanena
	samarthayate --- lakṣaṇapariṇāma iti/ ekaikaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ lakṣaṇāntarābhyāṃ samanugatam ity
	arthaḥ/ nanv ekalakṣaṇayoge lakṣaṇāntare nānubhūyete tat kathaṃ tadyoga ity ata āha ---
	yathā puruṣa iti/ na hy anubhavābhāvaḥ pramāṇasiddham apalapati, tadutpāda eva tatra
	tatsadbhāve pramāṇam asata utpādāsaṃbhavān naraviṣāṇavad iti/ paroktaṃ doṣam utthāpayati
	--- atra lakṣaṇapariṇāma iti/ yadā dharmo vartamānas tadaiva yady atīto+anāgataś ca tadā
	trayo+apy adhvānaḥ saṃkīryerann anukrameṇa cādhvanāṃ bhāve+asadutpādaprasaṅga
children.translated_text: Why? Because eternity is negated by a means of valid cognition. For if a pot did not deviate from manifestation, then even in the conditions of [being broken into] potsherds, gravel, powder, etc., the pot, being manifest, would produce the same cognition and function as before. Therefore, the three-world [system] is impermanent. 'Then let it be utterly impermanent — being devoid of perceivability and functional efficacy, it would be supremely trifling, like a sky-flower' — to this he replies: 'even though departed, it exists.' There is no utter triviality such that it would be absolutely impermanent — this is the meaning. Why? Because destruction is negated by a means of valid cognition. For whatever is utterly trifling never produces perceivability or function — like a sky-flower. But this three-world [system] does sometimes produce perceivability and function. Likewise, being possessed of origination, substantiality, having property-characteristics and conditions, etc. — [these] are distinguishable from the utterly trifling, such as sky-lotuses, man-horns, and the like, and are to be cited as reasons for existence. And thus, the substratum is not absolutely eternal such that it would be immutable like <s>citiśakti</s>; rather, it is eternal in some respect. And thus, it is transformable — this is established. By this, the existence of effects such as pots, etc., in the stages of clay-lump, etc. — being future — should be understood. One might say: if [the effect], though departed, exists, why is it not perceived as before? To this he replies: 'from the merging into its own cause (<s>svakāraṇalaya</s>), there is subtlety (<s>saukṣmya</s>) — unworthiness of being perceived — and hence non-apprehension.' Thus, having discussed <s>dharmapariṇāma</s>, he also establishes <s>lakṣaṇapariṇāma</s> through the mutual accompaniment of the characteristics: '<s>lakṣaṇapariṇāma</s>.' Each characteristic is accompanied by the other two characteristics — this is the meaning. Now, when one characteristic is operative, the other two are not experienced; so how can they be [simultaneously] present? To this he replies: 'just as <s>puruṣa</s>...' For the absence of experience does not invalidate what is established by a means of valid cognition; the very arising [of a characteristic in that state] is the proof of its existence there, since the arising of what is non-existent is impossible — like a man-horn. He raises the objection stated by the opponent: 'here, in the <s>lakṣaṇapariṇāma</s>...' If a property is simultaneously present, past, and future, then the three time-paths would be confused. And if the time-paths were [to occur] successively, there would be the undesirable consequence of origination from non-existence.

children.text:
iti bhāvaḥ/ pariharati --- tasya parihāra iti/ vartamānataiva hi dharmāṇām
	anubhavasiddhā tataḥ prākpaścātkālasaṃbandham avagamayati/ na khalv asad utpadyate na ca
	sad vinaśyati/ tad idam āha --- evaṃ hi na cittam iti/ krodhottarakālaṃ hi cittaṃ
	rāgadharmakam anubhūyate/ yadā ca rāgaḥ krodhasamaye+anāgatatvena nāsīt katham asāv
	utpadyetānutpannaś ca katham anubhūyeteti/ bhavatv evaṃ tathāpi kuto+adhvanām asaṃkara
	iti pṛcchati --- kiṃ ceti/ kiṃ kāraṇam asaṃkare/ caḥ punararthe/ uttaram āha ---
	trayāṇāṃ lakṣaṇānāṃ yugapan nāsti saṃbhavaḥ/ kasminn ekasyāṃ cittavṛttau/ krameṇa tu
	lakṣaṇānām ekatamasya svavyañjakāñjanasya bhāvo bhavet saṃbhavel lakṣyādhīnanirūpaṇatayā
	lakṣaṇānāṃ lakṣyākāreṇa tadvattā/ atraiva pañcaśikhācāryasaṃmatim āha --- uktaṃ ceti/
	etac ca prāg eva vyākhyātam/ upasaṃharati --- tasmād iti/
	āvirbhāvatirobhāvarūpaviruddhadharmasaṃsargād asaṃkaro+adhvanām iti/ dṛṣṭāntam āha ---
	yathā rāgasyeti/ pūrvaṃ krodhasya rāgasaṃbandhāvagamo darśita iti/ idānīṃ tu
	viṣayāntaravartino rāgasya viṣayāntaravartinā rāgāntareṇa saṃbandhāvagama iti/
	dārṣṭāntikam āha --- tathā lakṣaṇasyetīti/ nanu saty apy
	anekāntābhyupagame+abhedo+astīti dharmalakṣaṇāvasthānyatve tadabhinnasya dharmiṇo
children.translated_text: This is the purport. He resolves [the difficulty] — 'the resolution of that' etc. For the present existence of <s>dharmas</s> (properties) is established through experience; from that, one infers their connection with past and future time. Indeed, what is non-existent does not arise, and what is existent does not perish. This is what he states — 'for thus the <s>citta</s> (mind)' etc. For the <s>citta</s> at the time subsequent to anger is experienced as having the property of passion (<s>rāga</s>). And when <s>rāga</s> did not exist at the time of anger, being future, how could it arise? And if it has not arisen, how could it be experienced? Granted this is so; nevertheless, how is there non-intermixture of the time-paths (<s>adhvan</s>)? He asks — 'moreover' etc. 'What is the reason for non-intermixture?' The particle 'ca' has the sense of 'again.' He states the answer — 'there is no possibility of the three characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇas</s>) [existing] simultaneously in any single <s>cittavṛtti</s> (mental modification).' But sequentially, there may be the existence — the occurrence — of one among the characteristics, [namely] its own manifesting collyrium, since characteristics are determined in dependence on what is characterized, [they partake of] the form of the characterized. To this very point, he states the view approved by the teacher <s>Pañcaśikha</s> — 'and it has been said' etc. And this has already been explained earlier. He concludes — 'therefore' etc. Due to the association with mutually opposed properties in the form of manifestation and concealment, there is non-intermixture of the time-paths. He gives an illustration — 'just as of passion (<s>rāga</s>)' etc. Earlier, the understanding of the connection of anger with passion was shown. Now, however, the understanding of the connection of passion directed toward one object with another passion directed toward a different object [is shown]. He states the application — 'thus, of the characteristic' etc. But even granting the non-absolute [nature of the properties], there is [still] non-difference — [one might object that] in the transformation of <s>dharma</s>, <s>lakṣaṇa</s>, and <s>avasthā</s>, there would be the absurd consequence of the <s>dharmin</s> (substance), which is non-different from them, also becoming different.

children.text:
+apy anyatvaprasaṅgaḥ/ sa eva ca neṣyate tadanugamānubhavavirodhād ity ata
	āha --- na dharmī tryadhvā yatas tadabhinnā dharmās tryadhvānaḥ/ dharmāṇām
	adhvatrayayogam eva sphorayati --- te lakṣitā abhivyaktā vartamānā iti yāvat/ alakṣitā
	anabhivyaktā anāgatā atītā iti (atītāś ceti) yāvat/ tatra lakṣitās tāṃ tām avasthāṃ
	balavattvadurbalatvādikāṃ prāpnuvanto 'nyatvena pratinirdiśyante+avasthāntarato na
	dravyāntarataḥ/ avasthāśabdena dharmalakṣaṇāvasthā ucyante/ etad uktaṃ bhavati ---
	anubhava eva hi dharmiṇo dharmādīnāṃ bhedābhedau vyavasthāpayati/ na hy aikāntike+abhede
	dharmādīnāṃ dharmiṇo dharmirūpavad dharmāditvam/ nāpy aikāntike bhede gavāśvavad
	dharmāditvam/ sa cānubhavo+anaikāntikatvam avasthāpayann api
	dharmādiṣūpajanāpāyadharmakeṣv api dharmiṇam ekam anugamayan dharmāṃś ca parasparato
	vyāvartayan pratyātmam anubhūyata iti tadanusāriṇo vayaṃ na tam ativartya svecchayā
	dharmānubhavān vyavasthāpayitum īśmaha iti/ atraiva laukikaṃ dṛṣṭāntam āha --- yathaikā
	rekheti/ yathā tad eva rekhāsvarūpaṃ tattatsthānāpekṣayā śatāditvena vyapadiśyata evaṃ
	tad eva dharmirūpaṃ tattaddharmalakṣaṇāvasthābhedenānyatvena pratinirdiśyata ity arthaḥ/
	dārṣṭāntikārthaṃ dṛṣṭāntāntaram āha --- yathā caikatve+apīti/ atrāntare paroktaṃ doṣam
	utthāpayati --- avastheti/ avasthāpariṇāme dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāme
	kauṭasthyadoṣaprasaṅga ukto dharmidharmalakṣaṇāvasthānām/ pṛcchati --- katham iti/
	uttaram --- adhvano vyāpāreṇeti/ dadhnaḥ kila yo 'nāgato+adhvā tasya vyāpāraḥ kṣīrasya
	vartamānatvaṃ tena vyavahitatvād dhetoḥ/ yadā dharmo dadhilakṣaṇaḥ svavyāpāraṃ
	dādhikādyārambhaṃ kṣīre sann api na karoti tadānāgataḥ/ yadā karoti tadā vartamānaḥ/
children.translated_text: And that [consequence] is exactly what is not desired, since it would contradict the experience of the persistence [of the substance]. Therefore he says — 'the <s>dharmin</s> (substance) is not [itself] of three time-paths, since the <s>dharmas</s>, which are non-different from it, are of three time-paths.' He elaborates on the very connection of <s>dharmas</s> with the three time-paths — 'those that are characterized,' i.e., manifest, are present; 'those that are uncharacterized,' i.e., unmanifest, are future and past. Among these, the characterized [dharmas], attaining various states such as being predominant or subordinate, are designated as different — different in state, not in substance. By the word 'state' (<s>avasthā</s>), the states of <s>dharma</s>, <s>lakṣaṇa</s>, and <s>avasthā</s> are meant. What is thereby stated is this: it is experience alone that establishes both the difference and non-difference of <s>dharma</s> and the rest from the <s>dharmin</s>. For in absolute non-difference, the <s>dharma</s>-hood and the rest of <s>dharmas</s> etc. [would not obtain], just as they would not for the form of the <s>dharmin</s> itself. Nor in absolute difference would <s>dharma</s>-hood etc. [obtain], any more than between a cow and a horse. And that experience, while establishing the non-absoluteness [of the distinction] even in <s>dharmas</s> that possess the properties of arising and cessation, also maintains the unity of the <s>dharmin</s> and distinguishes the <s>dharmas</s> from one another — [this experience] is had by each individual. Therefore, we who follow that [experience] are not able to arbitrarily establish the experiences of <s>dharmas</s> by overriding it through our own wish. To this very point, he gives a mundane illustration — 'just as a single line' etc. Just as that very nature of the line is designated as a hundred, etc., in relation to different positions, so too that very form of the <s>dharmin</s> is designated as different by virtue of the distinction of <s>dharma</s>, <s>lakṣaṇa</s>, and <s>avasthā</s> states — this is the meaning. He gives another illustration for the analogical meaning — 'and just as, even in unity' etc. In the interval, he raises an objection stated by others — '<s>avasthā</s>' etc. In the transformation of state — the transformation of <s>dharma</s>, <s>lakṣaṇa</s>, and <s>avasthā</s> — the objection of immutability (<s>kauṭasthya</s>) has been raised with regard to <s>dharmin</s>, <s>dharma</s>, <s>lakṣaṇa</s>, and <s>avasthā</s>. He asks — 'how?' The answer — 'by the operation of the time-paths' etc. The operation of the future time-path of curds, so to speak, is the present-ness of milk; by that, [curds are future] due to being separated [from the present]. When the <s>dharma</s> characterized as curds, even while existing in milk, does not perform its own operation — the initiation of buttermilk and the like — then it is future. When it performs [that operation], then it is present.

children.text:
yadā kṛtvā nivṛttaḥ sann eva svavyāpārād dādhikādyārambhāt tadātīta iti/
	evaṃ traikālye+api sattvād dharmadharmiṇor lakṣaṇānām avasthānāṃ ca kauṭasthyaṃ
	prāpnoti/ sarvadā sattā hi nityatvaṃ, caturṇām api ca sarvadā sattve+asattve vā
	notpādaḥ, tāvanmātraṃ ca lakṣaṇaṃ kūṭasthanityatāyāḥ/ na hi citiśakter api
	kūṭasthanityāyāḥ kaścid anyo viśeṣa iti bhāvaḥ/ pariharati --- nāsau doṣaḥ, kasmād
	guṇinityatve 'pi guṇānāṃ vimardo+anyonyābhibhāvyābhibhāvakatvaṃ tasya vaicitryāt/ etad
	uktaṃ bhavati --- yady api sarvadā sattvaṃ caturṇām api guṇiguṇānāṃ tathāpi
	guṇavimardavaicitryeṇa tadātmabhūtatadvikārāvirbhāvatirobhāvabhedena pariṇāmaśālitayā na
	kauṭasthyam/ citiśaktes tu na svātmabhūtavikārāvirbhāvatirobhāva iti kauṭasthyam/
	yathāhuḥ ---
children.translated_text: When, having performed [its operation], it has ceased from its own function — the initiation of buttermilk and the like — while still existing, then it is past. Thus, even though [<s>dharma</s>, <s>dharmin</s>, <s>lakṣaṇa</s>, and <s>avasthā</s>] exist in all three times, the objection of immutability (<s>kauṭasthya</s>) of <s>dharma</s> and <s>dharmin</s>, of characteristics and states, would follow. For existence at all times is eternality; and if all four exist or do not exist at all times, there is no origination; and that alone is the defining mark of absolute immutable eternality. For there is no other distinguishing feature even for the <s>citiśakti</s> (power of consciousness), which is immutably eternal — this is the purport. He resolves [the difficulty] — 'that is not a fault,' because even when the substance (<s>guṇin</s>) is eternal, there is the mutual clash (<s>vimarda</s>) of the qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) — their mutual domination and subordination — and from the variety of that [clash, transformation follows]. What is thereby stated is this: although all four — substance and qualities — exist at all times, nevertheless, through the variety of the clash of qualities, through the difference of manifestation and concealment of modifications that are of their nature, [the substance] possesses the character of transformation and is therefore not immutable. But for <s>citiśakti</s> (the power of consciousness), there is no manifestation and concealment of modifications that are of its own nature — hence its immutability. As they say —

He classifies the transformation of elements and sense organs, which is both incidental and useful for what is to be stated — 'By this, the transformations of property, character, and state in the elements and sense organs are explained.' He explains — 'by this,' etc. [Objection:] Only the transformation of the mind has been stated, not the specific varieties — transformations of property, character, and state — how then is there extension (<s>atideśa</s>) of these [to elements and sense organs]? Hence he says — 'therein, of <s>vyutthāna</s> and <s>nirodha</s>,' etc. The words 'property, character, and state' were merely not pronounced — but the transformations of property, character, and state were not left unstated — such is the intent of the summary. For indeed, in the very <s>sūtra</s> 'of the <s>saṃskāras</s> of <s>vyutthāna</s> and <s>nirodha</s>,' the <s>dharma-pariṇāma</s> (property-transformation) is stated. And by showing this <s>dharma-pariṇāma</s>, by that very [exposition], the property-based —

children.text: "nityaṃ tam āhur vidvāṃso yatsvabhāvo na naśayti" iti/
children.translated_text: 'The wise declare that to be eternal whose own nature does not perish.'

children.translated_text: he states — 'of a substance that remains' etc. The word '<s>dharma</s>' [here], due to being dependent [on the dharmin], denotes <s>dharma</s>, <s>lakṣaṇa</s>, and <s>avasthā</s>. (3.13)

He shows the variety of the clash [of <s>guṇas</s>] as the cause of the variety of modifications in both the original substance (<s>prakṛti</s>) and its modifications (<s>vikṛti</s>) — 'just as configuration (<s>saṃsthāna</s>), which is the characteristic of the transformation of earth and the like, has a beginning and is merely a <s>dharma</s>, perishable and subject to concealment; but it is [produced] in dependence on its own effects — the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — which are imperishable and not subject to concealment.' He shows [this] in the original substance (<s>prakṛti</s>) — 'thus the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body)' etc. In that, the designation 'modification' applies, but the <s>citiśakti</s> (power of consciousness) does not have modifications in this way — this is the purport. Having thus cited both modification and original substance as established by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> investigators, he illustrates the variety of the clash of <s>guṇas</s> as the cause of the variety of transformation of <s>dharma</s>, <s>lakṣaṇa</s>, and <s>avasthā</s> in the commonly known modification alone — 'here is this illustration' etc. And this is not a restriction that only characteristics undergo state-transformation. Since all distinctions of <s>dharma</s>, <s>lakṣaṇa</s>, and <s>avasthā</s> are denoted by the word 'state,' there is but one state-transformation common to all — thus he says — 'of the <s>dharmin</s> also' etc. The pervasive definition of transformation

children.text: śāntoditāvyapadeśyadharmānupātī dharmī //3.14//
children.translated_text: The <s>dharmin</s> (substance) is that which follows the properties that are quiescent (<s>śānta</s>), arisen (<s>udita</s>), and indeterminate (<s>avyapadeśya</s>). (3.14)

yasyaiṣa trividhaḥ pariṇāmas taṃ dharmiṇaṃ sūtreṇa lakṣayati --- tatra ---
	śāntoditāvyapadeśyadharmānupātī dharmī/ dharmo+asyāstīti dharmīti nāvijñāte dharme sa
	śakyo jñātum iti dharmaṃ darśayati --- yogyateti/ dharmiṇo dravyasya mṛdādeḥ śaktir eva

tad evaṃ dharmāṇāṃ bhedasādhanam abhidhāya taṃ bhedaṃ
	vibhajate --- tatra ye khalv iti/ uditā iti vartamānā ity arthaḥ/ adhvanāṃ paurvāparyaṃ

	bhavanti vartamānāḥ/ hetum āha siddhāntī --- pūrvapaścimatāyā abhāvāt/ viṣayeṇa

	yathānāgatavartamānayor iti/ upasaṃharati --- tat tasmād anāgata eva samanantaraḥ
	pūrvatvena bhavati vartamānasya nātītaḥ/ atītasya vartamānaḥ pūrvatvena samanantaro
	nāvyapadeśyaḥ/ tasmād adhvanāṃ yaviṣṭho+atīta iti siddham/ syād etad
	anubhūyamānānubhūtatayoditātītau śakyāv unnetum avyapadeśyās tu punar dharmā
	avyapadeśyatayaivaṃ śakyā nonnetum ity āśayavān pṛcchati --- athāvyapadeśyāḥ ke keṣu
	samīkṣāmahe/ atrottaram āha --- sarvaṃ sarvātmakam iti/ yatroktam iti/ tad evopapādayati
	--- jalabhūmyor iti/ jalasya hi rasarūpasparśaśabdavato bhūmeś ca
	gandharasarūpasparśaśabdavatyāḥ pāriṇāmikaṃ vanaspatilatāgulmādiṣu
	mūlaphalaprasavapallavādigatarasādivaiśvarūpyaṃ dṛṣṭam/ so+ayam anevamātmikāyā bhūmer
	anīdṛśasya vā jalasya na pariṇāmo bhavitum arhati/ upapāditaṃ hi nāsad utpadyata iti/
	tathā sthāvarāṇāṃ pāriṇāmikaṃ jaṅgameṣu manuṣyapaśumṛgādiṣu rasādivaicitryaṃ dṛṣṭam/
	upayuñjānā hi te phalādīni rūpādibhedasaṃpadam āsādayanti/ evaṃ jaṅgamānāṃ pāriṇāmikaṃ
	sthāvareṣu dṛṣṭam/ rudhirāvasekāt kila dāḍimīphalāni
children.translated_text: Having thus stated the proof of the distinction of <s>dharmas</s> (properties), he classifies that distinction — 'Therein, those indeed' etc. '<s>Udita</s>' means present — this is the meaning. He determines the sequential order of the time-paths (<s>adhvans</s>) — 'And those' etc. He raises an objection — 'For what purpose' etc. For what reason are those that are past not immediately followed by the present? The proponent (<s>siddhāntin</s>) states the reason — 'Because of the absence of priority and posteriority.' He indicates, through the object, the non-apprehension of the objective [relation]. He demonstrates the non-apprehension itself through its difference from apprehension — 'Just as in the case of future and present' etc. He concludes — 'Therefore, it is only the future that is immediately prior to the present, not the past. The present is immediately prior to the past, not the undesignatable (<s>avyapadeśya</s>). Therefore, the youngest of the time-paths is the past — this is established.' One might think: the arisen (<s>udita</s>) and the past (<s>atīta</s>) can be inferred through their being experienced and having-been-experienced, but the undesignatable <s>dharmas</s>, being precisely undesignatable, cannot be so inferred — with this concern he asks: 'Now, which undesignatable [<s>dharmas</s>] do we observe in what?' To this he replies — 'Everything is constituted of everything.' 'As has been stated' etc. He establishes that very point — 'Of water and earth' etc. For we observe the transformative diversity of tastes and the like in trees, creepers, shrubs, and the like — in their roots, fruits, blossoms, sprouts, etc. — belonging to water, which possesses taste, form, touch, and sound, and to earth, which possesses smell, taste, form, touch, and sound. This transformation could not belong to earth not having such a nature, or to water not being of that kind. For it has been established that what is non-existent does not come into being. Similarly, the transformative diversity of taste and the like is observed in mobile beings — humans, domestic animals, wild animals, etc. — belonging to immobile [plants]. For those [mobile beings], consuming fruits and the like, attain the wealth of diverse forms and the rest. Similarly, the transformative [diversity] of mobile beings is observed in immobile [plants]. By sprinkling with blood, indeed, the fruits of the pomegranate tree
