children.translated_text: Thus, having explained the differentiation of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest by their respective actions and locations, he introduces the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> — 'from mastery of <s>udāna</s>': one who has performed <s>saṃyama</s> on <s>udāna</s>, from the mastery of that, is not obstructed by water and the like. And the ascent [at death] occurs through the path of the <s>arcis</s> (flame) and the like.

Since [life] is to be characterized by them [the prāṇas], the action of that effort is fivefold. <s>Prāṇa</s> is situated from the tip of the nose to the heart. <s>Samāna</s> conducts the transformed essence of eaten and drunk food, the <s>rasa</s> (nutrient fluid), to its appropriate locations uniformly and proportionately. From the heart

children.text: samānajayāj jvalanam //3.40//
children.translated_text: From mastery of <s>samāna</s> (the equalizing vital breath), effulgence [arises]. (3.40)

children.text: samājanayāj jvalanam/ tejasaḥ śārīrasyopadhmānam uttejanam //3.40//
children.translated_text: From mastery of <s>samāna</s>, effulgence — the kindling, the intensification of the bodily fire (<s>tejas</s>). (3.40)

children.text: śrotrākāśayoḥ saṃbandhasaṃyamād divyaṃ śrotram //3.41//
children.translated_text: From <s>saṃyama</s> on the relation between the ear and space (<s>ākāśa</s>), divine hearing [arises]. (3.41)

children.text:
svārthasaṃyamād anvācayaśiṣṭaṃ śrāvaṇādy uktaṃ saṃprati śrāvaṇādyarthād eva saṃyamāc
	chrāvaṇādi bhavatīty āha --- śrotrākāśayoḥ saṃbandhasaṃyamād divyaṃ śrotram/
	saṃyamaviṣayaṃ śrotrākāśayoḥ saṃbandham ādhārādheyabhāvam āha --- sarvaśrotrāṇām
	āhaṃkārikāṇām apy ākāśaṃ karṇaśaṣkulīvivaraṃ pratiṣṭhā tadāyatanaṃ śrotraṃ
	tadupakārāpakārābhyāṃ śrotrasyopakārāpakāradarśanāt/ śabdānāṃ ca śrotrasahakāriṇāṃ
	pārthivādiśabdagrahaṇe kartavye karṇaśaṣkulīsuṣiravarti śrotraṃ
	svāśrayanabhogatāsādhāraṇaśabdam apekṣate/ gandhādiguṇasahakāribhir ghrāṇādibhir bāhyaṃ
	pṛthivyādivartigandhādyālocane kārye dṛṣṭam/ āhaṃkārikam api
	ghrāṇrasanatvakcakṣuḥśrotraṃ bhūtādhiṣṭhānam eva bhūtopakārāpakārābhyāṃ ghrāṇādīnām
	upakārāpakāradarśanād ity uktam/ tac cedaṃ śrotram āhaṃkārikam ayaḥpratimam
	ayaskāntamaṇikalpena vaktṛvaktrasamutpannena vaktrasthena śabdenākṛṣṭaṃ
	svavṛttiparamparayā vaktṛvaktram āgataṃ śabdam ālocayati/

tathā ca
	digdeśavartiśabdapratītiḥ prāṇabhṛnmātrasya nāsati bādhake+apramāṇīkṛtā bhaviṣyatīti/
	tathā ca pañcaśikhasya vākyam --- tulyadeśaśravaṇānām ekadeśaśrutitvaṃ sarveṣāṃ
	bhavatīti/ tulyadeśāni śravaṇāni śrotrāṇi yeṣāṃ caitrādīnāṃ te tathoktāḥ/ sarveṣāṃ
	śravaṇāny ākāśavartīnīty arthaḥ/ tac ca śrotrādhiṣṭhānam ākāśaṃ śabdaguṇatanmātrād
	utpannaṃ śabdaguṇakaṃ yena śabdena sahakāriṇā pārthivādīñ śabdān gṛhṇāti/ tasmāt
	sarveṣām ekajātīyā śrutiḥ śabda ity arthaḥ/ tad anena śrotrādhiṣṭhānatvam ākāśasya
	śabdaguṇatvaṃ ca darśitam iti/ tac caikadeśaśrutitvam ākāśasya liṅgam/ sā hy ekajātīyā
	śabdavyañjikā śrutir yadāśrayā tad evākāśaśabdavācyam/ na hīdṛśīṃ śrutim antareṇa
	śabdavyaktiḥ/ na cedṛśī śrutiḥ pṛthivyādiguṇas tasya svātmani
	vyaṅgyavyañjakatvānupapatter iti/ anāvaraṇaṃ cākāśaliṅgam/ yady ākāśaṃ nābhaviṣyad
	anyonyasaṃpiṇḍitāni mūrtāni na sūcībhir apy abhetsyanta/ tataś ca sarvair eva sarvam
	āvṛtaṃ syāt/ na ca mūrtadravyābhāvamātrād evānāvaraṇam asyābhāvasya bhāvāśritatvena
	tadabhāve+abhāvāt/ na ca citiśaktis tadāśrayā bhavitum arhati/
	apariṇāmitayāvacchedakatvābhāvāt/ na ca dikkālādayaḥ pṛthivyādidravyavyatiriktāḥ santi/
	tasmāt tādṛśaḥ pariṇatibhedo nabhasa eveti sarvam avadātam/ anāvaraṇe cākāśaliṅge siddhe
	yatra yatrānāvaraṇaṃ tatra tatra sarvatrākāśam iti sarvagatatvam apy ākāśasya siddham
	ity āha --- tathāmūrtasyeti/ śrotrasadbhāve pramāṇam āha --- śabdagrahaṇeti/ kriyā hi
	karaṇasādhyā dṛṣṭā/ yathā chidādir vāsyādisādhyā/ tad iha śabdagrahaṇakriyayāpi
	karaṇasādhyayā bhavitavyaṃ, yac ca karaṇaṃ tac ca śrotram iti/ athāsyāś cakṣurādaya eva
	kasmāt karaṇaṃ na bhavantīty ata āha --- badhirābadhirayor iti/ anvayavyatirekābhyām
	avadhāraṇam/ upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat tvagvātayoś cakṣustejaso rasanodakayor nāsikāpṛthivyoḥ
	saṃbandhasaṃyamād divyatvagādy apy ūhanīyam //3.41//
children.translated_text: And thus, the perception of sounds located in [any] direction and place will not be invalidated for any living being in the absence of an obstructing factor. And so is the statement of <s>Pañcaśikha</s>: 'For those whose hearing is from the same location, the hearing from a single location becomes [the hearing] of all.' 'Same location' [means]

Having stated the auditory [power] and the like as resulting from <s>saṃyama</s> on one's own [faculties], now he states that the auditory [power] and the like arise from <s>saṃyama</s> on the very objects of hearing and the like — 'From <s>saṃyama</s> on the relation between the ear and space, divine hearing.' The object of <s>saṃyama</s> is the relation between the ear and space.

children.text: kāyākāśayoḥ saṃbandhasaṃyamāl laghutūlasamāpatteś cākāśagamanam //3.42//
children.translated_text: From <s>saṃyama</s> on the relation between the body and space (<s>ākāśa</s>), and from <s>samāpatti</s> (meditative absorption) on [something as] light as cotton, [there arises] traversal of space. (3.42)

children.text:
kāyākaśayoḥ saṃbandhasaṃyamāl laghutūlasamāpatteś cākāśagamanam/
	kāyākāśasaṃbandhasaṃyamād vā laghuni vā tūlādau kṛtasaṃyamāt samāpattiṃ cetasas
	tatsthatadañjanatāṃ labdhveti/ siddhikramam āha --- jala iti //3.42//
children.translated_text: From <s>saṃyama</s> on the relation between the body and space, and from <s>samāpatti</s> on [something as] light as cotton and the like, [there arises] traversal of space — from <s>saṃyama</s> on the relation between the body and space, or from having performed <s>saṃyama</s> on something light such as cotton and the like, having attained <s>samāpatti</s> — the mind's state of being colored by and imbued with that [lightness]. He states the order of [attaining] the <s>siddhi</s> — 'first,'

children.text: bahir akalpitā vṛttir mahāvidehā tataḥ prakāśāvaraṇakṣayaḥ //3.43//
children.translated_text: [When there is] an external, non-imagined modification [of the mind], that is <s>mahāvidehā</s> (the great bodiless state); from that, the destruction of the covering of light. (3.43)

children.text:
aparam api paraśarīrāveśahetuṃ saṃyamaṃ kleśakarmavipākakṣayahetuṃ cāha --- bahir
	akalpitā vṛttir mahāvidehā tataḥ prakāśāvaraṇakṣayaḥ/ videhām āha --- śarīrād iti/
	akalpitāyā mahāvidehāyā ya upāyas tatpradarśanāya kalpitāṃ videhām āha --- sā yadīti/
	vṛttimātraṃ kalpanājñānamātraṃ tena/ mahāvidehām āha --- yā tv iti/ upāyopeyate
	kalpitākalpitayor āha --- tatreti/ kiṃ paraśarīrāveśamātram ito nety āha --- tataś ceti/
	tato dhāraṇāto mahāvidehāyā manaḥpravṛtteḥ siddhiḥ/ kleśaś ca karma ca tābhyāṃ

vipākatrayaṃ jātyāyurbhogāḥ/ tad etad rajastamomūlaṃ vigalitarajastamasaḥ
	sattvamātrād vivekakhyātimātrasamutpādāt/ tad etad vipākatrayaṃ rajastamomūlatayā
	tadātmakaṃ sadbuddhisattvam āvṛṇoti/ tatkṣayāc ca nirāvaraṇaṃ yogicittaṃ yathecchaṃ
	viharati vijānāti ceti //3.43//
children.translated_text: the three types of vipāka (fruition) are birth, lifespan, and experience. This is rooted in rajas and tamas; when rajas and tamas have dissolved, from pure sattva alone arises the production of mere vivekakhyāti (discriminative discernment). This threefold vipāka, being rooted in rajas and tamas and being of their nature, covers the sattva of the buddhi (intellect). And from the destruction of that, the yogin's mind, now unveiled, moves and knows as it wishes. //3.43//

He also states another saṃyama (meditative constraint) that causes entry into another's body, and that causes the destruction of kleśa (afflictions), karma, and vipāka (fruition) — "An external, non-imagined modification is mahāvidehā (the great bodiless state); from that, the destruction of the covering of light." He explains videhā (the bodiless state) — 'from the body' and so on. To demonstrate the means for the non-imagined mahāvidehā, he explains the imagined videhā — 'That, when' and so on. The mere modification is mere imagined ignorance, by that [he explains]. He explains mahāvidehā — 'But that which' and so on. Regarding the means and end of both the imagined and non-imagined, he says — 'There' and so on. Is it merely entry into another's body, or something more? To this he says — 'And from that' and so on. From that dhāraṇā (concentration), through the mental activity of mahāvidehā, comes siddhi (perfection). Kleśa (afflictions) and karma — from these two,

children.text: sthūlasvarūpasūkṣmānvayārthavattvasaṃyamād bhūtajayaḥ //3.44//
children.translated_text: From saṃyama (meditative constraint) on the gross, essential nature, subtle, inherent connection, and purposefulness, [comes] mastery over the elements. //3.44//

children.text:
sthūlasvarūpasūkṣmānvayārthavattvasaṃyamād bhūtajayaḥ/ sthūlaṃ ca svarūpaṃ ca sūkṣmaṃ
	cānvayaś cārthavattvaṃ ceti sthūlasvarūpasūkṣmānvayārthavattvāni teṣu saṃyamāt tajjayaḥ/
	sthūlam āha --- tatreti/ pārthivāḥ pāthasīyās taijasā vāyavīyā ākāśīyāḥ
	śabdasparśarūparasagandhā yathāsaṃbhavaṃ viśeṣāḥ ṣaḍjagāndhārādayaḥ śītoṣṇādayo
	nīlapītādayaḥ kaṣāyamadhurādayaḥ surabhyādayaḥ/ ete hi nāmarūpaprayojanaiḥ parasparato
	bhidyanta iti viśeṣāḥ/ eteṣāṃ pañca pṛthivyāṃ gandhavarjaṃ catvāro+apsu gandharasavarjaṃ
	trayas tejasi gandharasarūpavarjaṃ dvau nabhasvati śabda evākāśe/ ta eva īdṛśā viśeṣāḥ
	sahākārādibhir dharmaiḥ sthūlaśabdena paribhāṣitāḥ śāstre/ tatrāpi pārthivās tāvad
	dharmāḥ ---
children.translated_text: From saṃyama on the gross, essential nature, subtle, inherent connection, and purposefulness, [comes] mastery over the elements. The gross, essential nature, subtle, inherent connection, and purposefulness — from saṃyama on these, [comes] mastery over them. He explains the gross — 'There' and so on. The viśeṣas (particulars) belonging to earth, water, fire, air, and space — namely sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, as applicable — are the ṣaḍja, gāndhāra, and other [notes]; cold, hot, and the like; blue, yellow, and the like; astringent, sweet, and the like; fragrant and the like. For these are differentiated from one another by name, form, and function, hence they are called viśeṣas. Of these, five [qualities] belong to earth; excluding smell, four belong to water; excluding smell, taste, and color, three belong to fire; excluding smell, taste, and color [two belong to air]; in space, there is sound alone. These very viśeṣas, being of such nature, together with their auxiliary properties, are designated by the term 'gross' in the śāstra (treatise). Among these, the properties of earth are —

children.text:
"ākāro gauravaṃ raukṣyaṃ varaṇaṃ sthairyam eva ca/ vṛttir bhedaḥ kṣamā kārṣṇyaṃ
	kāṭhinyaṃ sarvabhogyatā"//
children.translated_text: "Form, heaviness, roughness, covering, stability, activity, divisibility, endurance, darkness, and hardness — [these are] the enjoyability of all."

children.text: apāṃ dharmāḥ ---
children.translated_text: The properties of water are —

children.text:
"snehaḥ saukṣmyaṃ prabhā śauklyaṃ mārdavaṃ gauravaṃ ca yat/ śaityaṃ rakṣā pavitratvaṃ
	saṃdhānaṃ caudakā guṇāḥ"//
children.translated_text: "Viscosity, subtlety, luster, whiteness, softness, heaviness, coldness, protection, purity, and cohesion — these are the qualities of water."

children.text: taijasā dharmāḥ ---
children.translated_text: The properties of fire are —

children.text:
"ūrdhvabhāk pācakaṃ dagdhṛ pāvakaṃ laghu bhāsvaram/ pradhvaṃsy ojasvi vai tejaḥ
	pūrvābhyāṃ bhinnalakṣaṇam"//
children.translated_text: "Moving upward, cooking, burning, purifying, light, luminous, destructive, vigorous — indeed fire is distinct in its characteristics from the previous two [elements]."

children.text: vāyavīyā dharmāḥ ---
children.translated_text: The properties of air are —

children.text:
"tiryagyānaṃ pavitratvam ākṣepo nodanaṃ balam/ calamacchāyatā raukṣyaṃ vāyor dharmāḥ
	pṛthagvidhāḥ"//
children.translated_text: "Lateral movement, purification, propulsion, impelling, strength, instability, shadowlessness, roughness — these are the various properties of air."

children.text: ākāśīyā dharmāḥ ---
children.translated_text: The properties of space are —

children.text:
"sarvatogatir avyūho+aviṣṭambhaś ceti te trayaḥ/ ākāśadharmā vyākhyātāḥ
	pūrvadharmavilakṣaṇāḥ" iti//
children.translated_text: "All-pervasiveness, non-obstruction, and non-resistance — these three are explained as the properties of space, distinct from the properties of the previous [elements]."

children.text:
ta eta ākāraprabhṛtayo dharmās taiḥ saheti/ ākāraś ca sāmānyaviśeṣo gotvādiḥ/ dvitīyaṃ
	rūpam āha --- dvitīyaṃ rūpaṃ svasāmānyam/ mūrtiḥ sāṃsiddhikaṃ kāṭhinyam/ sneho jalaṃ
	mṛjāpuṣṭibalādhānahetuḥ/ vahnir uṣṇatodarye saurye bhaume ca sarvatraiva tejasi

samavetoṣṇateti/ sarvaṃ caitad dharmadharmiṇor abhedavivakṣayābhidhānam/
	vāyuḥ praṇāmī vahanaśīlaḥ/ tad āha ---
children.translated_text: has co-inherent heat. And all this is stated with the intention of non-difference between dharma (property) and dharmin (property-bearer). Vāyu (air) is that which bends, having the nature of carrying. Thus he says —

These very properties beginning with form [are meant by] 'together with these.' And 'form' [here refers to] the universal and particular, such as cowness and the like. He states the second form — 'The second form is its own universal.' Mūrti (solidity) is the innate hardness. Sneha (viscosity) is water, which is the cause of cleansing, nourishment, and strengthening. Fire [is characterized by] heat and energy, both solar and terrestrial — in all cases, fire

children.text: "calanena tṛṇādīnāṃ śarīrasyāṭanena ca/ sarvagaṃ vāyusāmānyaṃ nāmitvam anumīyate"//
children.translated_text: "From the movement of grass and the like, and from the wandering of the body, the universal nature of air, namely its bending quality, is inferred."

children.text:
sarvatogatir ākāśaḥ sarvatra śabdopalabdhidarśanāt/ śrotrāśrayākāśaguṇena hi śabdena
	pārthivādiśabdopalabdhir ity upapāditam adhastāt/ etat svarūpaśabdenoktam/ asyaiva
	mūrtyādisāmānyasya śabdādayaḥ ṣaḍjādaya uṣṇatvādayaḥ śuklatvādayaḥ kaṣāyatvādayaḥ
	surabhitvādayo mūrtyādīnāṃ sāmānyānāṃ bhedāḥ/ sāmānyāny api mūrtyādīni
	jambīrapanasāmalakaphalādīni rasādibhedāt parasparaṃ vyāvartante/ tenaiteṣām ete
	rasādayo viśeṣāḥ/ tathā coktam --- ekajātisamanvitānāṃ pratyekaṃ pṛthivyādīnām ekaikayā
	jātyā mūrtisnehādinā samanvitānām eṣāṃ ṣaḍjādidharmamātravyāvṛttir iti/ tad evaṃ
	sāmānyaṃ mūrtyādy uktaṃ viśeṣāś ca śabdādaya uktāḥ/ ye cāhuḥ sāmānyaviśeṣāśrayo dravyam
	iti tān pratyāha --- sāmānyaviśeṣasamudāyo+atra darśane dravyam/ ye+api tadāśrayo
	dravyam āsthiṣata tair api tatsamudāyo+anubhūyamāno nāpahnotavyaḥ/ na ca tadapahnave
	tayor ādhāro dravyam iti bhavati/ tasmāt tad evāstu dravyam/ na tu tābhyāṃ tatsamudāyāc
	ca tadādhāram aparaṃ dravyam upalabhāmahe/ grāvabhyo grāvasamudāyād iva ca tadādhāram
	aparaṃ pṛthagvidhaṃ śikharam/ samūho dravyam ity uktaṃ tatra samūhamātraṃ dravyam iti
	bhramāpanuttaye samūhaviśeṣo dravyam iti nirdhārayituṃ samūhaprakārān āha --- dviṣṭho
	hīti/ yasmād evaṃ tasmān na samūhamātraṃ dravyam ity arthaḥ/ dvābhyāṃ prakārābhyāṃ
	tiṣṭhatīti dviṣṭhaḥ/ ekaṃ prakāram āha --- pratyastamiteti/ pratyastamito bhedo yeṣām
	avayavānāṃ te tathoktāḥ/ pratyastamitabhedā avayavā yasya sa tathoktaḥ/ etad uktaṃ
	bhavati --- śarīravṛkṣayūthavanaśabdebhyaḥ samūhaḥ pratīyamāno+apratītāvayavabhedas
	tadvācakaśabdāprayogāt samūha eko+avagamyata iti/ yutāyutasiddhāvayavatvena
	cetanācetanatvena codāharaṇacatuṣṭayam/ yutāyutasiddhāvayavatvaṃ cāgre vakṣyate/

dvitīyaṃ prakāram āha --- śabdenopāttabhedāvayavānugataḥ samūha ubhaye
	devamanuṣyā iti/ devamanuṣyā iti hi śabdenobhayaśabdavācyasya samūhasya bhāgau bhinnāv
	upāttau/ nanūbhayaśabdāt tāvad avayavabhedo na pratīyate tat katham
	upāttabhedāvayavānugata ity ata āha --- tābhyāṃ bhāgābhyām eva samūho+abhidhīyate/
	ubhayaśabdena bhāgadvayavāciśabdasahitena samūho vācyaḥ, vākyasya vākyārthavācakatvād
	iti bhāvaḥ/ punar dvaividhyam āha --- sa ceti/ bhedena cābhedena ca vivakṣitaḥ/
	bhedavivakṣitam āha --- āmrāṇāṃ vanaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ saṃgha iti/ bheda eva ṣaṣṭhīśruteḥ,
	yathā gargāṇāṃ gaur iti/ abhedavivakṣitam āha --- āmravaṇaṃ brāhmaṇasaṃgha iti/ āmrāś ca
	te vanaṃ ceti samūhasamūhinor abhedaṃ vivakṣitvā sāmānādhikaraṇyam ity arthaḥ/
	vidhāntaram āha --- sa punar dvividhaḥ/ yutasiddhāvayavaḥ samūhaḥ/ yutasiddhāḥ
	pṛthaksiddhāḥ sāntarālā avayavā yasya sa tathoktaḥ, yūthaṃ vanam iti/ sāntarālā hi
	tadavayavā vṛkṣāś ca gāvaś ca/ ayutasiddhāvayavaś ca samūho vṛkṣo gauḥ paramāṇur iti/
	nirantarā hi tadavayavāḥ sāmānyaviśeṣā vā sāsnādayo veti/ tad eteṣu samūheṣu
	dravyabhūtaṃ samūhaṃ nirdhārayati --- ayutasiddheti/ tad evaṃ prāsaṅgikaṃ dravyaṃ
	vyutpādya prakṛtam upasaṃharati --- etat svarūpam ity uktam iti/ tṛtīyaṃ rūpaṃ vivakṣuḥ
	pṛcchati --- atheti/ uttaram āha --- tanmātram iti/ tasyaiko+avayavaḥ parimāṇabhedaḥ
	paramāṇuḥ, sāmānyaṃ mūrtiḥ, śabdādayo viśeṣās tadātmā, ayutasiddhā nirantarā ye+avayavāḥ
	sāmānyaviśeṣās tadbhedeṣv anugataḥ samudāyaḥ/ yathā ca
children.translated_text: He states the second mode — 'An aggregate following upon parts whose divisions have been grasped by words, both gods and humans.' For by the word 'both' (ubhaya), two distinct parts of the aggregate denoted by the word 'both' have been grasped. [Objection:] But from the word 'both' itself, the division of parts is not cognized; so how can it be said to follow upon parts whose divisions have been grasped? To this he says — 'The aggregate is denoted by those very two parts.' The aggregate is to be denoted by the word 'both' together with the word denoting two parts, because a sentence conveys the meaning of a sentence — this is the purport. He states another twofold distinction — 'And that' and so on. [The aggregate is] intended with division and without division. He explains the one intended with division —

children.text:
paramāṇuḥ sūkṣmaṃ
	rūpam evaṃ sarvatanmātrāṇi sūkṣmaṃ rūpam iti/ upasaṃharati --- etad iti/ atha bhūtānāṃ
	caturthaṃ rūpaṃ khyātikriyāsthitiśīlā guṇāḥ kāryasvabhāvam anupatitum anugantuṃ śīlaṃ
	yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ/ ata evānvayaśabdenoktāḥ/ athaiṣāṃ pañcamaṃ rūpam arthavattvaṃ
	vivṛṇoti --- bhogeti/ nanv evam api santu guṇā arthavantas tatkāryāṇāṃ tu
	kuto+arthavattvam ity ata āha --- guṇā iti/ bhautikā goghaṭādayaḥ/ tad evaṃ
	saṃyamaviṣayam uktvā saṃyamaṃ tatphalaṃ cāha --- teṣv iti/ bhūtaprakṛtayo
	bhūtasvabhāvāḥ //3.44//
children.translated_text: The atom is the subtle form; similarly all <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) are the subtle form. He summarizes — 'this.' Now, the fourth aspect of the elements: the <s>guṇas</s> whose nature is to follow and conform to the nature of their effects are called those characterized by illumination, activity, and stability (<s>khyāti-kriyā-sthiti-śīla</s>). For this very reason they are designated by the word 'anvaya' (conformity). Now he explains the fifth aspect, purposefulness (<s>arthavattva</s>) — '[for] experience.' But even if the <s>guṇas</s> are purposeful, whence comes the purposefulness of their products? To this he says — '<s>guṇāḥ</s>.' The material things are cows, pots, and the like. Having thus stated the object of <s>saṃyama</s>, he states the <s>saṃyama</s> and its fruit — 'on these.' The natures of the elements (<s>bhūta-prakṛtayaḥ</s>) are the essential characteristics of the elements. (3.44)

Ākāśa (space) is all-pervading, because sound is perceived everywhere. For it has been established earlier that the perception of earthly and other sounds occurs through sound, which is the quality of space that serves as the substratum of hearing. This is what is meant by the term 'essential nature.' The viśeṣas (particular differentiations) of the universals such as solidity and the like — belonging to this very [set of universals] — are sound and the like, ṣaḍja and the like, heat and the like, whiteness and the like, astringency and the like, fragrance and the like. The universals such as solidity and the like are also mutually distinguished — like jambīra, panasa, āmalaka fruits — by differences in taste and the like. Therefore, these tastes and the like are their viśeṣas. And thus it is said — 'Of the individual earth-elements and the like, which share a single class, each one by a single class'

children.text: tato+aṇimādiprādurbhāvaḥ kāyasaṃpat taddharmānabhighātaś ca //3.45//
children.translated_text: From that, the manifestation of <s>aṇimā</s> and other [powers], perfection of the body, and non-obstruction by the properties [of the elements]. (3.45)

children.text:
saṃkalpānuvidhāne bhūtānāṃ kiṃ yoginaḥ sidhyatīty ata āha --- tato+aṇimādiprādurbhāvaḥ
	kāyasaṃpat taddharmānabhighātaś ca/ sthūlasaṃyamajayāc catasraḥ siddhayo bhavantīty āha
	--- tatrāṇimā mahān api bhavaty aṇuḥ/ laghimā mahān api laghur bhūtveṣīkātūla ivākāśe
	viharati/ mahimālpo+api nāganagagaganaparimāṇo bhavati/ prāptiḥ sarve bhāvāḥ saṃnihitā
	bhavanti yoginaḥ/ tadyathā bhūmiṣṭha evāṅgulyagreṇa spṛśati candramasam/
	svarūpasaṃyamavijayāt siddhim āha --- prākāmyam icchānabhighāto nāsya rūpaṃ
	bhūtasvarūpair mūrtyādibhir hanyate/ bhūmāv unmajjati nimajjati ca yathodake/
	sūkṣmaviṣayasaṃyamajayāt siddhim

āha --- vaśitvaṃ bhūtāni pṛthivyādīni
	bhautikāni goghaṭādīni teṣu vaśī svatantro bhavati, teṣāṃ tv avaśyas
	tatkāraṇatanmātrapṛthivyādiparamāṇuvaśīkārāt tatkāryavaśīkāras tena yāni
	yathāvasthāpayati tāni tathāvatiṣṭhanta ity arthaḥ/ anvayaviṣayasaṃyamajayāt siddhim āha
	--- īśitṛtvaṃ teṣāṃ bhūtabhautikānāṃ vijitamūlaprakṛtiḥ san yaḥ prabhava utpādo yaś
	cāpyayo vināśo yaś ca vyūho yathāvadavasthāpanaṃ teṣāṃ īṣṭe/ arthavattvasaṃyamāt siddhim
	āha --- yatra kāmāvasāyitvaṃ satyasaṃkalpatā/ vijitaguṇārthavattvo hi yogī
	yadyadarthatayā saṃkalpayati tat tasmai prayojanāya kalpate/ viṣam apy amṛtakārye
	saṃkalpya bhojayañ jīvayatīti/ syād etad yathā śaktiviparyāsaṃ karoty evaṃ
	padārthaviparyāsam api kasmān na karoti/ tathā ca candramasam ādityaṃ kuryāt kuhūṃ ca
	sinīvālīm ity ata āha --- na ca śakto+apīti/ na khalv ete yatra kāmāvasāyinas
	tatrabhavataḥ parameśvarasyājñām atikramitum utsahante/ śaktayas tu padārthānāṃ
	jātideśakālāvasthābhedenāniyatasvabhāvā iti yujyate tāsu tadicchānuvidhānam iti/ etāny
	aṣṭāv aiśvaryāṇi/ taddharmānabhighāta iti/ aṇimādiprādurbhāva ity anenaiva
	taddharmānabhighātasiddhau punar upādānaṃ kāyasiddhivad etat
	sūtropabaddhasakalaviṣayasaṃyamaphalavattvajñāpanāya/ sugamam anyat //3.45//
children.translated_text: <s>Vaśitā</s> (mastery): the power of creation. One becomes lord over the elements, both stationary and moving. Thus, from <s>saṃyama</s> on the gross, essential nature, subtle, conformity, and purposefulness, [comes] mastery — he says 'from mastery over the elements.' Of these six or eight <s>siddhis</s>, the word 'from that' indicates immediate succession. Moreover, from that <s>aṇimā</s> and other <s>siddhis</s> [comes] perfection of the body. He explains that — 'form.' For what purpose? For the body functions according to his will and not otherwise. And how is that? Non-obstruction by the properties — of properties such as grossness and the like, born from mastery through <s>saṃyama</s> on the gross — non-obstruction. (3.45)

What does the <s>yogin</s> accomplish through the conformity of the elements to his will? To this he says — 'From that, the manifestation of <s>aṇimā</s> and other [powers], perfection of the body, and non-obstruction by the properties [of the elements].' From mastery through <s>saṃyama</s> on the gross, four <s>siddhis</s> arise, he says — Among these, <s>aṇimā</s>: even though large, one becomes minute. <s>Laghimā</s>: even though large, becoming light, one moves through space like a tuft of cotton from a reed. <s>Mahimā</s>: even though small, one attains the dimensions of mountains, cities, and the sky. <s>Prāpti</s> (reaching): all things become proximate to the <s>yogin</s> — for example, while standing on the ground, he touches the moon with his fingertip. He states the <s>siddhi</s> from mastery through <s>saṃyama</s> on the essential nature — <s>Prākāmya</s> (irresistible will): non-obstruction of desire — his form is not destroyed by the essential natures of the elements such as solidity and the like; he emerges from and submerges into the earth as if in water. He states the <s>siddhi</s> from mastery through <s>saṃyama</s> on the subtle object —

children.text: rūpalāvaṇyabalavajrasaṃhananatvāni kāyasaṃpat //3.46//
children.translated_text: Beauty of form, gracefulness, strength, and diamond-like hardness constitute bodily perfection. (3.46)

children.text:
kāyasaṃpadam āha --- rūpalāvaṇyabalavajrasaṃhananatvāni kāyasaṃpat/ vajrasyeva
	saṃhananam avayavavyūho dṛḍho nibiḍo yasya sa tathoktaḥ //3.46//
children.translated_text: He explains bodily perfection — 'form.' Diamond-like hardness (<s>vajra-saṃhananatva</s>) is compactness like a diamond. Just as even the side of a diamond is so well-compacted that it cannot be split, so the body of the <s>yogin</s> is endowed with diamond-like compactness — this too arises implicitly from mastery over the elements. (3.46)

children.text: grahaṇasvarūpāsmitānvayārthavattvasaṃyamād indriyajayaḥ //3.47//
children.translated_text: From <s>saṃyama</s> on apprehension, essential nature, <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness), conformity, and purposefulness, [comes] mastery over the sense organs. (3.47)

children.text:
jitabhūtasya yogina indriyajayopāyam āha --- grahaṇasvarūpāsmitānvayārthavattvasaṃyamād
	indriyajayaḥ/ grahaṇaṃ ca svarūpaṃ cāsmitā cānvayaś cārthavattvaṃ ca teṣu saṃyamas
	tasmād ity arthaḥ/ gṛhītir grahaṇaṃ, tac ca grāhyādhīnanirūpaṇam iti grāhyaṃ darśayati
	--- sāmānyaviśeṣātmeti/ grāhyam uktvā grahaṇam āha --- teṣv iti/ vṛttir ālocanaṃ
	viṣayākārā pariṇatir iti yāvat/ ye tv āhuḥ --- sāmānyamātragocarendriyavṛttir iti tān
	pratyāha --- na ceti/ gṛhyata iti grahaṇam/ na sāmānyamātragocaraṃ grahaṇam/
	bāhyendriyatantraṃ hi mano bāhye pravartate/ anyathāndhabadhirādyabhāvaprasaṅgāt/ tad
	iha yadi na viśeṣaviṣayam indriyaṃ tenāsāv anālocito viśeṣa iti kathaṃ
	manasānuvyavasīyeta/ tasmāt sāmānyaviśeṣaviṣayam indriyālocanam iti/ tad etad grahaṇam
	indriyāṇāṃ prathamaṃ rūpam/ dvitīyaṃ rūpam āha --- svarūpaṃ punar iti/ ahaṃkāro hi
	sattvabhāgenātmīyenendriyāṇy ajījanat/ ato yat tatra karaṇatvaṃ sāmānyaṃ yac ca
	niyatarūpādiviṣayatvaṃ viśeṣas tadubhayam api prakāśātmakam ity arthaḥ/ teṣāṃ tṛtīyaṃ
	rūpam iti/ ahaṃkāro hīndriyāṇāṃ kāraṇam iti yatrendriyāṇi tatra tena bhavitavyam iti
	sarvendriyasādhāraṇyāt sāmānyam indriyāṇām ity arthaḥ/ caturthaṃ rūpam iti/ guṇānāṃ hi
	dvairūpyaṃ vyavaseyātmakatvaṃ vyavasāyātmakatvaṃ ca/ tatra vyavaseyātmakatāṃ grāhyatām
	āsthāya pañca tanmātrāṇi bhūtabhautikāni nirmimīte/ vyavasāyātmakatvaṃ tu grahaṇarūpam
	āsthāya sāhaṃkārāṇīndriyāṇīty arthaḥ/ śeṣaṃ sugamam //3.47//
children.translated_text: Having stated mastery over the elements, he states mastery over the sense organs, which follows the same pattern — 'apprehension.' The distinction is this much: regarding the elements, the gross, essential nature, and subtle were stated; here, apprehension means apprehension of objects, which is the gross; essential nature means the essential nature of the sense organ — this is the same in both cases. There it was said that the subtle is the <s>tanmātra</s> (subtle element), but here it is <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness) — this alone is the distinction. Furthermore, for the elements, subtlety extends up to <s>asmitā</s>, but for the sense organs, <s>asmitā</s> itself is the subtlety — hence the distinction. Purposefulness, however, is the same. Now he explains apprehension — 'the seeing of form.' The same reasoning applies to the remaining apprehensions as well —

children.text: tato manojavitvaṃ vikaraṇabhāvaḥ pradhānajayaś ca //3.48//
children.translated_text: this is the meaning of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. The essential nature is the <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) sense organ — the eye, ear, and so forth. <s>Asmitā</s> is the essence of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), for that alone is denoted by the word <s>asmitā</s>. Conformity (<s>anvaya</s>) is the generality of the <s>guṇas</s>. Purposefulness (<s>arthavattva</s>) is serving the purposes of experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). He summarizes the <s>sūtra</s> preceded by [the discussion of] the <s>guṇas</s> — 'thus.' (3.47)

children.text:
pañcarūpendriyajayāt siddhīr āha --- tato manojavitvaṃ vikaraṇabhāvaḥ pradhānajayaś ca/
	videhānām indriyāṇāṃ karaṇabhāvo vikaraṇabhāvaḥ/ deśaḥ kāśmīrādiḥ/ kālo 'tītādiḥ/
	viṣayaḥ sūkṣmādiḥ/ sānvayendriyajayāt sarvaprakṛtivikāravaśitvaṃ pradhānajayaḥ/ tā etāḥ
	siddhayo madhupratīkā ity ucyante yogaśāstraniṣṇātaiḥ/ syād etad indriyajayād indriyāṇi
	saviṣayāṇi vaśyāni bhavantu, pradhānādīnāṃ tatkāraṇānāṃ kim āyātam ity ata āha --- etāś
	ceti/ karaṇānām indriyāṇāṃ pañca rūpāṇi grahaṇādīni teṣāṃ jayāt/ etad uktaṃ bhavati ---
	nendriyamātrajayasyaitāḥ siddhayo+api tu pañcarūpasya tadantargataṃ ca pradhānādīti //3.48//
children.translated_text: From that [comes] swiftness of mind, the state of being without instruments, and mastery over <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). (3.48)

children.text: sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrasya sarvabhāvādhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ sarvajñātṛtvaṃ ca //3.49//
children.translated_text: He states the fruit of mastery over the sense organs — 'From that, swiftness of mind, the state of being without instruments, and mastery over <s>pradhāna</s>.' All sense organs [acquire] rapid movement like the mind. The state of being without instruments (<s>vikaraṇa-bhāva</s>) is the capacity to enter other bodies and the like through sense organs without [their physical] instruments. Mastery over <s>pradhāna</s> as well. Having stated the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> in general, he distinguishes — 'of the cognitive sense organs, like the mind' — swiftness in apprehending objects. Similarly, of the bodily sense organs, like the mind, rapidity of action in accordance with will —

children.text:
ta ete jñānakriyārūpaiśvaryahetavaḥ saṃyamāḥ sākṣāt pāramparyeṇa ca
	svasiddhyupasaṃhārasaṃpāditaśraddhādvāreṇa yadarthās tasyāḥ sattvapuruṣānyatākhyāter
	avāntaravibhūtīr darśayati --- sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrasya sarvabhāvādhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ
	sarvajñātṛtvaṃ ca/ nirdhūtarajastamomalatayā vaiśāradyaṃ tataḥ parā vaśīkārasaṃjñā
	rajastamobhyām upaplutaṃ hi cittasattvam avaśyam āsīt tadupaśame tu tadvaśyaṃ yogino
	vaśinas tasmin vaśye yoginaḥ sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrarūpapratiṣṭhasya
	sarvabhāvādhiṣṭhātṛtvam/ etad eva vivṛṇoti --- sarvātmāna iti/ vyavasāyavyavaseyātmāno

jaḍaprakāśarūpā ity arthaḥ/ tad anena kriyaiśvaryam uktam/ jñānaiśvaryam
	āha --- sarvajñātṛtvam iti/ asyā api dvividhāyāḥ siddher vairāgyāya yogijanaprasiddhāṃ
	saṃjñām āha --- eṣā viśoketi/ kleśāś ca bandhanāni ca karmāṇi tāni kṣīṇāni yasya sa
	tathā //3.49//
children.translated_text: For one who has merely the discernment of the distinction between <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>, [there is] sovereignty over all states of existence and omniscience. (3.49)

in moving about and other activities. What else? — 'without instruments.' And when objects are proximate but are not apprehended by the wise one, that non-cognition is the state of being without instruments (<s>vikaraṇa-bhāva</s>). The meaning is this: mastery over the sense organs has two applications — one, that the <s>yogin</s> does not experience even proximate objects through the sense organs, due to the complete cessation of the activity of the sense organs; the second, that he pervades every place through the sense organs. (3.48)

children.text: tadvairāgyād api doṣabījakṣaye kaivalyam //3.50//
children.translated_text: Having stated mastery over the elements and sense organs, he states mastery over their cause — 'For one who has merely the discernment of the distinction between <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>, sovereignty over all states of existence and omniscience.' The reality is the purity of <s>buddhi-sattva</s> — and the discriminative knowledge (<s>viveka-khyāti</s>) of <s>puruṣa</s>, which is the principle of <s>asmitā</s>. He states what arises for one established in that discernment — 'because <s>sattva</s> is of the nature of light.' For that <s>puruṣa</s>, <s>sattva</s>, through the manifestation of its self-luminous nature, becomes fit for all experience. Therefore, for one who has attained the discernment of the distinction between <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> — and it has been said that this is that very discernment, 'there' — for him there are two fruitful <s>siddhis</s>: sovereignty over all entities,

children.text:
saṃyamāntarāṇāṃ puruṣārthābhāsaphalatvād vivekakhyātisaṃyamārthatāṃ darśayituṃ
	vivekakhyāteḥ paravairāgyopajananadvāreṇa kaivalyaṃ phalam āha --- tadvairāgyād api
	doṣabījakṣaye kaivalyam/ yadāsya yoginaḥ kleśakarmakṣaya evaṃ jñānaṃ bhavati/ kiṃbhūtam
	ity āha --- sattvasyāyaṃ vivekapratyayo dharmaḥ/ śeṣaṃ tatra tatra vyākhyātatvāt
	sugamam //3.50//
sthānyupanimantraṇe saṅgasmayākaraṇaṃ punar aniṣṭaprasaṅgāt //3.51//

saṃprati kaivalyasādhane pravṛttasya yoginaḥ pratyūhasaṃbhave tannirākaraṇakāraṇam
	upadiśati --- sthānyupanimantraṇe saṅgasmayākaraṇaṃ punar aniṣṭaprasaṅgāt/ sthānāni
	yeṣāṃ

santi te sthānino mahendrādayas tair upanimantraṇaṃ tasmin saṅgaś ca
	smayaś ca na kartavyaḥ punar aniṣṭaprasaṅgāt/ tatra yaṃ devāḥ sthānair upamantrayante
	taṃ yoginam ekaṃ nirdhārayituṃ yāvanto yoginaḥ saṃbhavanti tāvata evāha --- catvāra iti/
	tatra prāthamakalpikasya svarūpam āha --- tatrābhyāsīti/ pravṛttamātraṃ na punar
	vaśīkṛtaṃ jyotir jñānaṃ paracittādiviṣayaṃ yasya sa tathā/ dvitīyam āha ---
	ṛtaṃbharaprajña iti/ yatredam uktam --- "ṛtaṃbharā tatra prajñā"
yogasūtram 1.48

iti/
	sa hi bhūtendriyāṇi jigīṣuḥ/ tṛtīyam āha --- bhūtendriyajayīti/ tena hi
	sthūlādisaṃyamena grahaṇādisaṃyamena ca bhūtendriyāṇi jitāni/ tam evāha --- sarveṣu
	bhāviteṣu niṣpāditeṣu bhūtendriyajayāt paracittādijñānādiṣu kṛtarakṣābandho yatas tebhyo
	na cyavate bhāvanīyeṣu niṣpādanīyeṣu viśokādiṣu paravairāgyaparyanteṣu
	kartavyasādhanavān puruṣaprayatnasya sādhanaviṣayasyaiva sādhyaniṣpādakatvāt/ caturtham
	āha --- caturtha iti/ tasya hi bhagavato jīvanmuktasya caramadehasya cittapratisarga eko
	'rthaḥ/ tad eteṣu yogiṣūpanimantraṇaviṣayaṃ yoginam avadhārayati --- tatra madhumatīm
	iti/ prāthamakalpike tāvan mahendrādīnāṃ tatprāptiśaṅkaiva nāsti/ tṛtīyo+api tair
	nopanimantraṇīyo bhūtendriyavaśitvenaiva tatprāpteḥ/ caturtho+api paravairāgyasaṃpatter
	āsaṅgaśaṅkā dūrotsāritaiveti pāriśeṣyād dvitīya eva ṛtaṃbharaprajñas
	tadupanimantraṇaviṣaya iti/ vaihāyasam ākāśagāmi, akṣayam avināśi, ajaraṃ sadābhinavam/

smayakaraṇe doṣam āha --- smayād ayam iti/ smayāt susthitaṃmanyo
	nānityatāṃ bhāvayiṣyati, na tasyāṃ praṇidhāsyatīty arthaḥ/ sugamam anyat //3.51//
kṣaṇatatkramayoḥ saṃyamād vivekajaṃ jñānam //3.52//

uktā kvacit kvacit saṃyamāt sarvajñatā, sā ca na niḥśeṣajñatā/ api tu
	prakāramātravivakṣayā, yathā sarvair vyañjanair bhuktam iti/ atra hi yāvanto
	vyañjanaprakārās tair bhuktam iti gamyate na tu niḥśeṣair iti/ asti ca niḥśeṣavacanaḥ
	sarvaśabdo yathopanītam annaṃ sarvam aśitaṃ prāśakeneti/ tatra hi niḥśeṣam iti gamyate/
	tad iha niḥśeṣajñatālakṣaṇasya vivekajajñānasya sādhanaṃ saṃyamam āha ---
	kṣaṇatatkramayoḥ saṃyamād vivekajaṃ jñānam/ kṣaṇapadārthaṃ nidarśanapūrvakam āha ---
	yatheti/ loṣṭasya hi pravibhajyamānasya yasminn avayave+alpatvatāratamyaṃ vyavatiṣṭhate
	so 'pakarṣaparyantaḥ paramāṇur yathā tathāpakarṣaparyantaḥ kālaḥ kṣaṇaḥ,
	pūrvāparabhāgavikalakālakaleti yāvat/ tam eva kṣaṇaṃ prakārāntareṇa darśayati --- yāvatā
	veti/ paramāṇumātraṃ deśam atikrāmed ity arthaḥ/ kramapadārtham āha --- tatpravāheti/
	tatpadena kṣaṇaḥ parāmṛśyate/ na cedṛśaḥ kramo vāstavaḥ kiṃ tu kālpanikas tasya
	samāhārarūpasyāyugapadupasthiteṣu vāstavatvena vicārāsahatvād ity āha ---
	kṣaṇatatkramayor iti/ ayugapadbhāvikṣaṇadharmatvāt

kramasya
	kṣaṇasamāhārasyāvāstavatvāt kṣaṇatatkramayor apy avāstavatvaṃ samāhārasya
	naisargikavaitaṇḍikabuddhyatiśayarahitā laukikāḥ pratikṣaṇa eva vyutthitadarśanā bhrāntā
	ye kālam īdṛśaṃ vāstavam abhimanyanta iti/ tat kiṃ kṣaṇo+apy avāstavo nety āha ---
	kṣaṇas tu vastupatito vāstava ity arthaḥ/ kramasyāvalambanam avalambaḥ so+asyāstīti
	krameṇāvalambyate vaikalpikenety arthaḥ/ kramasya kṣaṇāvalambanatve hetum āha --- kramaś
	ceti/ kramasyāvāstavatve hetum āha --- na ceti/ co hetvarthe/ yas tu vaijātyāt
	sahabhāvam upeyāt taṃ pratyāha --- kramaś ca na dvayor iti/ kasmād asaṃbhava ity ata āha
	--- pūrvasmād iti/ upasaṃharati --- tasmād iti/ tat kim idānīṃ śaśaviṣāṇāyamānā eva
	pūrvottarakṣaṇā nety āha --- ye tv iti/ anvitāḥ sāmyena samanvāgatā ity arthaḥ/
	upasaṃharati --- teneti/ vartamānasyaivārthakriyāsu svocitāsu sāmarthyād iti //3.52//
jātilakṣaṇadeśair anyatānavacchedāt tulyayos tataḥ pratipattiḥ //3.53//

yady apy etad vivekajaṃ jñānaṃ niḥśeṣabhāvaviṣayam ity agre vakṣyate tathāpy
	atisūkṣmatvāt prathamaṃ tasya viṣayaviśeṣa upakṣipyate --- jātilakṣaṇadeśair
	anyatānavacchedāt tulyayos tataḥ pratipattiḥ/ laukikānāṃ jātibhedo+anyatāyā
	jñāpakahetuḥ/ tulyā jātir gotvaṃ tulyaś ca deśaḥ

pūrvādiḥ/
	kālākṣīsvastimatyor lakṣaṇabhedaḥ param iti/ dvayor āmalakayos tulyāmalakatvajātir
	vartulādi lakṣaṇaṃ tulyaṃ deśabhedaḥ param iti/ yadā tu yogijñānaṃ jijñāsunā kenacit
	pūrvāmalakam anyavyagrasya yogino jñātur uttaradeśa upāvartyata uttaradeśam āmalakaṃ
	tato+apasārya pidhāya vā tadā tulyadeśatve pūrvam etad uttaram etad iti
	pravibhāgānupapattiḥ prājñasya laukikasya tripramāṇīnipuṇasyāsaṃdigdhena ca
	tattvajñānena bhavitavyaṃ vivekajajñānavato yoginaḥ saṃdigdhatvānupapatteḥ/ ata uktaṃ
	sūtrakṛtā --- tataḥ pratipattiḥ/ tata iti vyācaṣṭe --- vivekajajñānād iti/
	kṣaṇatatkramasaṃyamāj jātaṃ jñānaṃ katham āmalakaṃ tulyajātilakṣaṇadeśād āmalakāntarād
	vivecayatīti pṛcchati --- katham iti/ uttaram āha --- pūrvāmalakasahakṣaṇo deśaḥ
	pūrvāmalakenaikakṣaṇo deśas tena saha nirantarapariṇāma iti yāvat/
	uttarāmalakasahakṣaṇād deśād uttarāmalakanirantarapariṇāmād bhinno bhavatu deśayor
	bhedaḥ kim āyātam āmalakabhedasyety ata āha --- te cāmalake svadeśakṣaṇānubhavabhinne,
	svadeśasahito yaḥ kṣaṇas tasyāmalakasya kālakalā svadeśena
	sahauttarādharyarūpapariṇāmalakṣitā sā svadeśakṣaṇas tasyānubhavaḥ prāptir vā jñānaṃ vā
	tena bhinne āmalake yayor āmalakayoḥ pūrvottarābhyāṃ deśābhyām
	auttarādharyapariṇāmakṣaṇa āsīt tayor deśāntarauttarādharyapariṇāmakṣaṇaviśiṣṭatvam
	anubhavan saṃyamī te bhinne eva pratyeti/ saṃprati taddeśapariṇāme+api
	pūrvabhinnadeśapariṇāmād viśiṣṭasya caitaddeśapariṇāmakṣaṇasya saṃyamataḥ sākṣātkaraṇāt/
	tad idam uktam ---

anyadeśakṣaṇānubhavas tu tayor anyatve hetur iti/
	anenaiva nidarśanena laukikaparīkṣakasaṃvādādinā paramāṇor apīdṛśasya bhedo
	yogīśvarabuddhigamyaḥ śraddheya ity āha --- eteneti/ apare tu varṇayanti/ varṇanam
	udāharati --- ya iti/ vaiśeṣikā hi nityadravyavṛttayo+antyā viśeṣā ity āhuḥ/ tathā hi
	--- yogino muktāṃs tulyajātideśakālān vyavadhirahitān parasparato bhedena pratyekaṃ
	tattvena ca pratipadyante/ tasmād asti kaścid antyo viśeṣa iti/ tathā ca sa eva nityānāṃ
	paramāṇvādīnāṃ dravyāṇāṃ bhedaka iti/ tad etad dūṣayati --- tatrāpīti/ jātideśalakṣaṇāny
	udāhṛtāni/ mūrtiḥ saṃsthānaṃ yathaikaṃ viśuddhāvayavasaṃsthānopapannam apasārya tasminn
	eva deśe+anyavyagrasya draṣṭuḥ kutsitāvayavasaṃniveśa upāvartyate tadā tasya
	saṃsthānabhedena bhedapratyayaḥ, śarīraṃ vā mūrtis tatsaṃbandhenātmanāṃ saṃsāriṇāṃ
	muktātmanāṃ vā bhūtacareṇa yādṛśatādṛśena bheda iti sarvatra
	bhedapratyayasyānyathāsiddher nāntyaviśeṣakalpanā/ vyavadhir bhedakāraṇam/ yathā
	kuśapuṣkaradvīpayor deśasvarūpayor iti/ yato jātideśādibhedā lokabuddhigamyā ata uktaṃ
	--- kṣaṇabhedas tu yogibuddhigamya eveti/ evakāraḥ kṣaṇabhedam avadhārayati na
	yogibuddhigamyatvaṃ, tena bhūtacareṇa dehasaṃbandhena muktātmanām api bhedo
	yogibuddhigamya unneya iti/ yasya tūktā bhedahetavo na santi tasya pradhānasya bhedo
	nāstīty ācaāryo mene/ yasmād ūce "kṛtārthaṃ prati naṣṭam apy anaṣṭaṃ
	tadanyasādhāraṇatvāt"
yogasūtram 2.22

iti/ tad āha --- mūrtivyavadhīti/
	uktabhedahetūpalakṣaṇam etat/ jaganmūlasya pradhānasya pṛthaktvaṃ bhedo nāstīty
	arthaḥ //3.53//
tārakaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ sarvathāviṣayam akramaṃ ceti vivekajaṃ jñānam //3.54//

tad evaṃ viṣayaikadeśaṃ vivekajajñānasya darśayitvā vivekajaṃ jñānaṃ lakṣayati ---
	tārakaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ sarvathāviṣayam akramaṃ ceti vivekajaṃ jñānam/ vivekajaṃ jñānam iti
	lakṣyanirdeśaḥ/ śeṣaṃ lakṣaṇam/ saṃsārasāgarāt tārayatīti tārakam/ pūrvasmāt prātibhād
	viśeṣayati --- sarvathāviṣayam iti/ paryāyā avāntaraviśeṣāḥ/ ata eva vivekajaṃ jñānaṃ
	paripūrṇaṃ nāsya kvacit kiṃcit kathaṃcit kadācid agocara ity arthaḥ/ āstāṃ tāvaj
	jñānāntaraṃ saṃprajñāto+api tāvad asyāṃśaḥ/ tasmād ataḥ paraṃ kiṃ paripūrṇam ity āha ---
	asyaivāṃśo yogapradīpaḥ saṃprajñātaḥ/ kim upakramaḥ kim avasānaś cāsāv ity āha ---
	madhumatīm iti/ ṛtaṃbharā prajñaiva madhu modakāraṇatvāt/ yathoktaṃ prajñāprāsādam
	āruhyeti/ tadvatī madhumatī dhiyo+avasthā tām upādāya yāvad asya parisamāptiḥ saptadhā
	prāntabhūmiḥ prajñā/ ata eva vivekajaṃ jñānaṃ tārakaṃ bhavati/ tadaṃśasya yogapradīpasya
	tārakatvād iti //3.54//
sattvapuruṣayoḥ śuddhisāmye kaivalyam iti //3.55//
iti śrīpatañjaliviracitayogasūtreṣu tṛtīyo vibhūtipādaḥ //3//

tad evaṃ paramparayā kaivalyasya hetūn savibhūtīn saṃyamān uktvā
	sattvapuruṣānyatājñānaṃ sākṣāt kaivalyasādhanam ity atra sūtram avatārayati ---
	prāpteti/ vivekajaṃ jñānaṃ bhavatu mā vā bhūt sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātis tu
	kaivalyaprayojikety arthaḥ/ sattvapuruṣayoḥ śuddhisāmye kaivalyam iti/ itiḥ
	sūtrasamāptau/ īśvarasya pūrvoktaiḥ saṃyamair jñānakriyāśaktimato+anīśvarasya vā
	samanantaroktena saṃyamena vivekajajñānabhāgina itarasya vānutpannajñānasya na

vibhūtiṣu kācid apekṣāstīty āha --- na hīti/ nanu yady anapekṣitā vibhūtayaḥ
	kaivalye vyarthas tarhi tāsām upadeśa ity ata āha --- sattvaśuddhidvāreṇeti/
	itthaṃbhūtalakṣaṇe tṛtīyā/ nātyantam ahetavaḥ kaivalye vibhūtayaḥ kiṃ tu na sākṣād ity
	arthaḥ/ jñānaṃ vivekajam upakrāntaṃ yac ca pāramparyeṇa kāraṇaṃ tad aupacārikaṃ na tu
	mukhyaṃ, paramārthas tu khyātir eva mukhyam ity arthaḥ/ jñānād iti prasaṃkhyānād ity
	arthaḥ //3.55//

"atrāntaraṅgāṇy aṅgāni pariṇāmāḥ prapañcitāḥ/ saṃyamād bhūtasaṃyogas tāsu jñānaṃ
	vivekajam" iti
padārthasaṃgrahaślokaḥ

iti śrīvācaspatimiśraviracitāyāṃ pātañjalabhāṣyavyākhyāyāṃ tattvavaiśāradyāṃ
	vibhūtipādas tṛtīyaḥ //3//
tatra caturthaḥ kaivalyapādaḥ/
janmauṣadhimantratapaḥsamādhijāḥ siddhayaḥ //4.1//

tad evaṃ prathamadvitīyatṛtīyapādaiḥ samādhitatsādhanatadvibhūtayaḥ prādhānyena
      vyutpāditāḥ/ itarat tu prāsaṅgikam aupodghātikaṃ coktam ihedānīṃ taddhetukaṃ kaivalyaṃ
      vyutpādanīyam/ na caitat kaivalyabhāgīyaṃ cittaṃ paralokaṃ ca paralokinaṃ
      vijñānātiriktaṃ cittakaraṇakasukhādyātmakaśabdādyupabhoktāram ātmānaṃ ca
      prasaṃkhyānaparamakāṣṭhāṃ ca vinā vyutpādya śakyaṃ vaktum iti tad etat sarvam atra pāde
      vyutpādanīyam itarac ca prasaṅgād upodghātād vā/ tatra prathamaṃ siddhacitteṣu
      kaivalyabhāgīyaṃ cittaṃ nirdhārayitukāmaḥ pañcatayīṃ siddhim āha ---
      janmauṣadhimantratapaḥsamādhijāḥ siddhayaḥ/ vyācaṣṭe --- dehāntariteti/
      svargopabhogabhāgīyāt karmaṇo manuṣyajātīyācaritāt kutaścin nimittāl labdhaparipākāt
      kvacid devanikāye jātamātrasyaiva divyadehāntaritā siddhir aṇimādyā bhavatīti/
      oṣadhisiddhim āha --- asurabhavaneṣv iti/ manuṣyo hi kutaścin nimittād asurabhavanam
      upasaṃprāptaḥ kamanīyābhir asurakanyābhir upanītaṃ rasāyanam upayujyājarāmaraṇatvam
      anyāś ca siddhīr āsādayati/ ihaiva vā rasāyanopayogena yathā māṇḍavyo munī rasopayogād
      vindhyavāsīti/ mantrasiddhim āha --- mantrair iti/ tapaḥsiddhim āha --- tapaseti/
      saṃkalpasiddhim āha --- kāmarūpīti/ yad eva kāmayate+aṇimādi tad ekapade+asya bhavatīti/
      yatra kāmayate śrotuṃ vā mantuṃ vā tatra tad eva śṛṇoti manute veti/ ādiśabdād
      darśanādayaḥ saṃgṛhītā iti //4.1//
jātyantarapariṇāmaḥ prakṛtyāpūrāt //4.2//

samādhijāḥ siddhayo vyākhyātā adhastane pāde/ atha catasṛṣu siddhiṣv auṣadhādisādhanāsu
      teṣām eva kāyendriyāṇāṃ jātyantarapariṇatir iṣyate/ sā punar na tāvad upādānamātrāt/ na
      hi tāvanmātram upādānaṃ nyūnādhikadivyādivyabhāve+asya bhavati/ no khalv avilakṣaṇaṃ
      kāraṇaṃ kāryavailakṣaṇyāyālam/ māsyākasmikatvaṃ bhūd ity āśaṅkya pūrayitvā sūtraṃ

paṭhati --- tatra kāyendriyāṇām anyajātīyapariṇatānāṃ --- jātyantapariṇāmaḥ
      prakṛtyāpūrāt/ manuṣyajātipariṇatānāṃ kāyendriyāṇāṃ yo devatiryagjātipariṇāmaḥ sa khalu
      prakṛtyāpūrāt/ kāyasya hi prakṛtiḥ pṛthivyādīni bhūtāni/ indriyāṇāṃ ca prakṛtir asmitā,
      tadavayavānupraveśa āpūras tasmād bhavati/ tad idam āha --- pūrvapariṇāmeti/ nanu yady
      āpūreṇānugrahaḥ kasmāt punar asau na sadātana ity ata āha --- dharmādīti/ tad anena
      tasyaiva śarīrasya bālyakaumārayauvanavārdhakādīni ca nyagrodhadhānāyāṃ
      nyagrodhatarubhāvaś ca vahnikaṇikāyās tṛṇarāśiniveśitāyā vā
      prodbhavajjvālāsahasrasamāliṅgitagaganamaṇḍalatvaṃ ca vyākhyātam //4.2//
children.translated_text: He reads — 'therein, of the body and sense organs transformed into another class' — the transformation into another class is from the filling up of <s>prakṛti</s> (material nature). The transformation of the body and sense organs, which are configured in the human class, into the divine or animal class occurs from the filling up (<s>āpūra</s>) of <s>prakṛti</s>. For the <s>prakṛti</s> of the body consists of earth and other elements, and the <s>prakṛti</s> of the sense organs is <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness); the entry of its constituent parts is the filling up, and from that it occurs. This is what he states — 'the previous transformation.' Now, if [the transformation is] assisted by the filling up, why is it not always present? To this he says — 'by <s>dharma</s> and the rest.' By this [it is shown that] the transformations of that very body through childhood, youth, maturity, and old age —

children.text: nimittam aprayojakaṃ prakṛtīnāṃ varaṇabhedas tu tataḥ kṣetrikavat //4.3//
children.translated_text: The incidental cause does not directly impel the <s>prakṛtis</s>; rather, [it acts] through the removal of obstacles, like a farmer. (4.3)

children.text:
prakṛtyāpūrād ity uktaṃ tatredaṃ saṃdihyate --- kim āpūraḥ prakṛtīnāṃ svābhāviko
      dharmādinimitto veti/ kiṃ prāptaṃ satīṣv api prakṛtiṣu kadācid āpūrād
      dharmādinimittaśravaṇāc ca tannimitta eveti prāptam/ evaṃ prāpta āha --- nimittam
      aprayojakaṃ prakṛtīnāṃ varaṇabhedas tu tataḥ kṣetrikavat/ satyaṃ dharmādayo nimittaṃ na
      tu prayojakās teṣām api prakṛtikāryatvāt/ na ca kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ prayojayati tasya
      tadadhīnotpattitayā kāraṇaparatantratvāt/ svatantrasya ca prayojakatvāt/ na khalu
      kulālam antareṇa

mṛddaṇḍacakrasalilādaya utpitsitenotpannena vā ghaṭena
      prayujyante/ kiṃ tu svatantreṇa kulālena/ na ca puruṣārtho+api pravartakaḥ/ kiṃ tu
      taduddeśeneśvaraḥ/ uddeśyatāmātreṇa puruṣārthaḥ pravartaka ity ucyate/ utpitsos tv asya
      puruṣārthasyāvyaktasya sthitikāraṇatvaṃ yuktam/ na caitāvatā dharmādīnām animittatā
      pratibandhāpanayanamātreṇa kṣetrikavad upapatter īśvarasyāpi dharmādhiṣṭhānārthaṃ
      pratibandhāpanaya eva vyāpāro veditavyaḥ/ tad etan nigadavyākhyātena bhāṣyeṇoktam //4.3//
children.translated_text: Clay, stick, wheel, water, and the like are not impelled by the pot that is desired or produced; rather, [they are impelled] by the independent potter. Nor is <s>puruṣārtha</s> (the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>) the impeller; rather, <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) [acts] for its sake. <s>Puruṣārtha</s> is called the impeller only in the sense of being the objective. However, for this <s>puruṣārtha</s>, which is unmanifest and about to arise, it is appropriate that [<s>prakṛti</s>] serves as the sustaining cause. Nor does this mean that <s>dharma</s> and the rest have no causal role, for [they function] merely by removing obstacles, like a farmer — [and] it should be understood that <s>Īśvara</s>'s operation too, for the purpose of presiding over <s>dharma</s>, is merely the removal of obstacles. This is stated through the <s>Bhāṣya</s> explained by running commentary —

It was said 'from the filling up of <s>prakṛti</s>'; here a doubt arises — is the filling up of the <s>prakṛtis</s> natural or caused by <s>dharma</s> and the rest? What is established? Since even when the <s>prakṛtis</s> are present, the filling up sometimes [occurs and sometimes does not], and since there is mention of <s>dharma</s> and the rest as causes, it is established that they are indeed the cause. With this established, he says — 'The incidental cause does not directly impel the <s>prakṛtis</s>; rather, [it acts] through the removal of obstacles, like a farmer.' True, <s>dharma</s> and the rest are the incidental cause, but they are not the direct impellers, because they too are effects of <s>prakṛti</s>. And an effect does not impel its cause, because the effect, being dependent on the cause for its origination, is subordinate to the cause. And [only] what is independent can be an impeller —

children.text: nirmāṇacittāny asmitāmātrāt //4.4//
children.translated_text: The created minds [arise] from <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness) alone. (4.4)

children.text:
prakṛtyāpūreṇa siddhīḥ samarthya siddhivinirmitanānākāyavarticittaikatvanānātve
      vicārayati --- yadā tv iti/ tatra nānāmanastve kāyānāṃ praticittam abhiprāyabhedād
      ekābhiprāyānurodhaś ca parasparapratisaṃdhānaṃ ca na syātāṃ puruṣāntaravat/ tasmād ekam
      eva cittaṃ pradīpavad visāritayā bahūn api nirmāṇakāyān vyāpnotīti prāpta āha ---
      nirmāṇacittāny asmitāmātrāt/ yad yāvaj jīvaccharīraṃ tat sarvam
      ekaikāsādhāraṇacittānvitaṃ dṛṣṭam/ tadyathā caitramaitrādiśarīram/ tathā ca nirmāṇakāyā
      iti siddhaṃ teṣām api prātisvikaṃ mana ity abhiprāyeṇāha --- asmitāmātram iti //4.4//
children.translated_text: Having established the <s>siddhis</s> through the filling up of <s>prakṛti</s>, he investigates the unity and plurality of the minds operating in the various bodies created by the <s>siddha</s> (perfected one) — 'when, however.' There, if there were multiple minds, there would be no coordination of intention among the bodies — due to the difference of purpose for each mind — and no mutual memory, as with different persons. Therefore, it is established that one single mind pervades many created bodies, like a lamp [spreading its light]. To this he says — 'The created minds [arise] from <s>asmitā</s> alone.' Whatever body is alive, all of it is seen to be accompanied by a mind unique to each one — for example, the bodies of <s>Caitra</s>, <s>Maitra</s>, and others. Likewise,

children.text: pravṛttibhede prayojakaṃ cittam ekam anekeṣām //4.5//
children.translated_text: In the diversity of activities, the one mind is the director of the many. (4.5)

children.text:
yad uktam anekacittatva ekābhiprāyānurodhaś ca pratisaṃdhānaṃ ca na syātām iti
      tatrottaraṃ sūtram --- pravṛttibhede prayojakaṃ cittam ekam anekeṣām/ abhaviṣyad eṣa
      doṣo yadi cittam ekaṃ nānākāyavarti manonāyakaṃ na niramāsyat, tannirmāṇe tv adoṣaḥ/ na
      caikaṃ gṛhītvā kṛtaṃ prātisvikair manobhiḥ kṛtaṃ vā nāyakanirmāṇena nijasyaiva manaso
      nāyakatvād iti vācyam/ pramāṇasiddhasya niyogaparyanuyogānupapatter iti/ atra purāṇaṃ
      bhavati ---
children.translated_text: To the objection stated — that if there were multiple minds, there would be no coordination of intention or mutual memory — the <s>sūtra</s> responds: 'In the diversity of activities, the one mind is the director of the many.' This fault would have arisen if the one mind operating in many bodies had not created a leading mind as the guide; but in its creation, there is no fault. Nor can it be said that having grasped one [body], what is done by the individual minds or what is done through the creation of the leader [is contradictory], because the leader is the leader of one's own mind — for something established by valid means cannot be questioned about its purpose. Here there is an ancient [verse] —

children.text:
"ekas tu prabhuśaktyā vai bahudhā bhavatīśvaraḥ/ bhūtvā yasmāt tu bahudhā bhavaty ekaḥ
      punas tu saḥ// tasmāc ca manaso bhedā jāyante caita eva hi/
vāyupurāṇam 66.143
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyupurāṇa</s> 66.143

children.text:
ekadhā sa dvidhā caiva tridhā ca bahudhā punaḥ//
      yogīśvaraḥ śarīrāṇi karoti vikaroti ca/ prāpnuyād viṣayān kaiścit kaiścid ugraṃ tapaś
      caret// saṃharec ca punas tāni sūryo raśmigaṇān iva"
children.translated_text: In one form, in two, in three, and again in manifold [forms], the lord of <s>yogins</s> creates and transforms bodies. With some he enjoys sense objects, with others he performs fierce <s>tapas</s> (austerity). And he withdraws them again, like the sun its multitude of rays."

children.text: vāyupurāṇam 66.152
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyupurāṇa</s> 66.152

children.text: iti//
children.translated_text: Thus.
"By the power of lordship indeed, the one Lord becomes manifold; having become manifold, he becomes one again. From that, the divisions of the mind arise, and these very [divisions] —

children.text: tad etenābhiprāyeṇāha --- bahūnāṃ cittānām iti //4.5//
children.translated_text: With this intention he says — 'of the many minds.' (4.5)

children.text: tatra dhyānajam anāśayam //4.6//
children.translated_text: Of those, the one born of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is without residual deposits (<s>anāśaya</s>). (4.6)

children.text:
tad evam uditeṣu pañcasu siddhacitteṣv apavargabhāgīyaṃ cittaṃ nirdhārayati --- tatra
      dhyānajam anāśayam/ āśerata ity āśayāḥ karmavāsanāḥ kleśavāsanāś ca/ ta ete na vidyante
      yasmiṃs tad anāśayaṃ cittam apavargabhāgīyaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ/ yato rāgādinibandhanā
      pravṛttir nāsty ato nāsti puṇyapāpābhisaṃbandhaḥ/ kasmāt punā rāgādijanitā pravṛttir
      nāstīty ata āha --- kṣīṇakleśatvād iti/ dhyānajasyānāśayasya mano+antarebhyo viśeṣaṃ
      darśayitum itareṣām āśayavattām āha --- itareṣāṃ tv iti //4.6//
children.translated_text: Having thus enumerated the five types of perfected minds, he determines which is conducive to liberation — 'Of those, the one born of <s>dhyāna</s> is without residual deposits.' Those in which [karmic impressions] rest are <s>āśayas</s> (residual deposits) — namely, <s>karma-vāsanās</s> (impressions of action) and <s>kleśa-vāsanās</s> (impressions of afflictions). That in which these do not exist is <s>anāśaya</s> (without residual deposits) — the mind conducive to liberation. Since there is no activity rooted in <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and the rest, there is no connection with merit and demerit. Why is there no activity born of <s>rāga</s> and the rest? To this he says — 'because of the destruction of the <s>kleśas</s>.' To show the distinction of the <s>dhyāna</s>-born [mind], which is without residual deposits, from the other [minds], he states that the others possess residual deposits —

children.text: karmāśuklākṛṣṇaṃ yoginas trividham itareṣām //4.7//
children.translated_text: The <s>karma</s> of a <s>yogin</s> is neither white nor black; for others it is threefold. (4.7)

children.text:
tatraiva ca hetuparaṃ sūtram avatārayati --- yata iti/ karmāśuklākṛṣṇaṃ yoginas
      trividham itareṣām/ padaṃ sthānam/ cartuṣu samavetā catuṣpadī/ yad yāvad
      bahiḥsādhanasādhyaṃ tatra sarvatrāsti kasyacit pīḍā/ na hi vrīhyādisādhane+api karmaṇi
      parapīḍā nāsty avaghātādisamaye 'pi pipīlikādivadhasaṃbhavāt/ antato bījādivadhena
      stambādibhedotpattipratibandhāt/ anugrahaś ca dakṣiṇādinā brāhmaṇāder iti/ śuklā
      tapaḥsvādhyāyadhyānavatām asaṃnyāsinām/ śuklatvam upapādayati --- sā hīti/ aśuklākṛṣṇā
      saṃnyāsinām/ saṃnyāsino darśayati --- kṣīṇeti/ karmāsaṃbhavāt/ karmasaṃnyāsino hi na
      kvacid bahiḥsādhanasādhye karmaṇi pravṛttā iti na caiṣām asti kṛṣṇaḥ karmāśayaḥ/
      yogānuṣṭhānasādhyasya karmāśayaphalasyeśvare samarpaṇān na śuklaḥ karmāśayaḥ/
      niratyayaphalo hi śukla ucyate/ yasya phalam eva nāsti kutas tasya niratyayaphalatvam
      ity arthaḥ/ tad evaṃ catuṣṭayīṃ karmajātim uktvā katamā kasyety avadhārayati ---
      tatrāśuklam iti //4.7//
children.translated_text: He introduces the <s>sūtra</s> concerning the cause of that very [distinction] — 'because.' 'The <s>karma</s> of a <s>yogin</s> is neither white nor black; for others it is threefold.' A station (<s>pada</s>) is a place. The fourfold [classification] is combined in four stations. Whatever external action requires external means, in all of that there is some harm to someone. For even in actions such as rice cultivation, harm to others is unavoidable, since at the time of threshing and the like there is the possibility of killing ants and the like. Even ultimately, by destroying seeds and the like, the growth of stalks and the like is obstructed. And there is also beneficence through gifts and the like to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and others. White [<s>karma</s> belongs to] those engaged in <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), and <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) who are not renunciants. He establishes the whiteness —

children.text: tatas tadvipākānuguṇānām evābhivyaktir vāsanānām //4.8//
children.translated_text: From that, the manifestation of only those <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) that correspond to the fruition [of that karma]. (4.8)

children.text:
karmāśayaṃ vivicya kleśāśayagatim āha --- tatas tadvipākānuguṇānām evābhivyaktir
      vāsanānām/ yajjātīyasya puṇyajātīyasyāpuṇyajātīyasya vā karmaṇo yo vipāko divyo vā
      nārako vā jātyāyurbhogas tasya vipākasyānuguṇāḥ/ tā evāha ---

yā vāsanāḥ
      karmavipākam anuśerate+anukurvanti/ divyabhogajanitā hi divyakarmavipākānuguṇā vāsanāḥ/
      na hi manuṣyabhogavāsanābhivyaktau divyakarmaphalopabhogasaṃbhavaḥ/ tasmāt
      svavipākānuguṇā eva vāsanāḥ karmābhivyañjanīyā iti bhāṣyārthaḥ //4.8//
children.translated_text: those <s>vāsanās</s> that follow and conform to the fruition of <s>karma</s>. For <s>vāsanās</s> generated by divine enjoyment correspond to the fruition of divine <s>karma</s>. Indeed, the manifestation of <s>vāsanās</s> of human enjoyment is not possible during the experience of the fruit of divine <s>karma</s>. Therefore, only <s>vāsanās</s> corresponding to one's own fruition should manifest the <s>karma</s> — this is the meaning of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. (4.8)

Having analyzed the deposits of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāśaya</s>), he states the course of the deposits of afflictions (<s>kleśāśaya</s>) — 'From that, the manifestation of only those <s>vāsanās</s> that correspond to the fruition [of that karma].' The fruition (<s>vipāka</s>) of whatever class of <s>karma</s> — whether of the meritorious or demeritorious class — is either divine or infernal, consisting of birth, lifespan, and experience. Those [<s>vāsanās</s>] that correspond to that fruition — he states what these are —

children.text: jātideśakālavyavahitānām apy ānantaryaṃ smṛtisaṃskārayor ekarūpatvāt //4.9//
children.translated_text: Even when separated by birth, place, and time, there is continuity, because memory and <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions) are of one form. (4.9)

children.text:
syād etat/ manuṣyasya prāyaṇānantaram adhigatamārjārabhāvasyānantaratayā
      manuṣyavāsanāyā evābhivyaktvā bhavitavyam/ na khalv asti saṃbhavo yad
      anantaradivasānubhūtaṃ na smaryate vyavahitadivasānubhūtaṃ ca smaryata ity ata āha ---
      jātideśakālavyavahitānām apy ānantaryaṃ smṛtisaṃskārayor ekarūpatvāt/ bhavatu
      vṛṣadaṃśavāsanāyā jātyādivyavadhis tathāpi tasyāḥ phalata ānantaryaṃ vṛṣadaṃśavipākena
      karmaṇā tasyā eva svavipākānuguṇāyā abhivyaktau tatsmaraṇasamutpādād ity āha ---
      vṛṣadaṃśavipākodaya iti/ udety asmād ity udayaḥ karmāśayaḥ/ punaś ca svavyañjakāñjana
      evodiyāt, abhivyajyeta vipākārambhābhimukhaḥ kriyetety arthaḥ/ abhisaṃskārakriyā upādāya
      gṛhītvā vyajyeta/ yadi vyajyeta svavipākānuguṇā eva vāsanā gṛhītvā vyajyetety arthaḥ/
      ānantaryam eva phalataḥ kāraṇadvārakam upapādya kāryadvārakam upapādayati --- kutaś ca
      smṛtīti/ ekarūpatā sādṛśyam/ tad evāha --- yatheti/ nanv anubhavasarūpāś cet saṃskārās
      tathā saty anubhavā viśarārava ity ete+api viśarāravaḥ kathaṃ cirabhāvine+anubhavāya

kalperann ity ata āha --- te ca karmavāsanānurūpāḥ/ yathāpūrvaṃ sthāyi
      kṣaṇikakarmanimittam apy evaṃ kṣaṇikānubhavanimitto+api saṃskāraḥ sthāyī kiṃcid
      bhedādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca sārūpyam anyathābhede tattvena sādṛśyānupapatter ity arthaḥ/ sugamam
      anyat //4.9//
children.translated_text: Hence he says — 'And those conform to <s>karma</s> and <s>vāsanā</s>.' Just as a stable [entity], even though caused by momentary <s>karma</s>, [is enduring], so too a <s>saṃskāra</s>, even though caused by a momentary experience, is stable. And similarity is the basis of difference — otherwise, in the absence of [actual] difference, similarity in reality would be impossible — this is the meaning. The rest is easy to understand. (4.9)

One might object: for a human, immediately after death upon obtaining the state of a cat, since [the cat-birth] is immediate, only the human <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) should manifest. It is not possible that what was experienced on the immediately preceding day is not remembered, while what was experienced on a separated day is remembered. Therefore he says — 'Even for those separated by birth, place, and time, there is continuity, because of the identity in form of memory and <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression).' Even though the bull-fly <s>vāsanā</s> is separated by birth and the rest, still there is continuity through its result — because the <s>karma</s> that is the ripening of the bull-fly [birth], upon arising, brings about the manifestation of only that [<s>vāsanā</s>] which is compatible with its own ripening, thereby producing the remembrance of that. Hence he says — 'the arising of the bull-fly ripening': <s>udaya</s> (arising) means the <s>karmāśaya</s> (karmic repository) from which it arises. And again, it would arise only in conjunction with its own manifesting agent — that is, it would be manifested, made ripe for the commencement of its fruition — this is the meaning. 'Taking up the activity of imprinting' — having taken up, having grasped, it would manifest. 'If it would manifest, it would do so only by grasping the <s>vāsanā</s> compatible with its own ripening' — this is the meaning. Having established the continuity through result by way of the cause, he establishes it by way of the effect — 'and because of memory' etc. 'Identity in form' means similarity. That he states — 'as' etc. Now, if the <s>saṃskāras</s> are of the same form as the experience, then, the experiences being momentary, these [<s>saṃskāras</s>] too would be momentary — how could they be adequate for an experience long deferred?

children.text: tāsām anāditvaṃ cāśiṣo nityatvāt //4.10//
children.translated_text: And the beginninglessness of those [<s>vāsanās</s>] is because of the eternality of the will-to-live (<s>āśis</s>). (4.10)

children.text:
syāt etad vyajyeran pūrvapūrvatarajanmābhisaṃskṛtā vāsanāḥ/ yadi
      pūrvapūrvatarajanmasadbhāve pramāṇaṃ syāt tad eva tu nāsti/ na ca jātamātrasya jantor
      harṣaśokadarśanamātraṃ pramāṇaṃ bhavitum arhati, padmādisaṃkocavikāsavat svābhāvikatvena
      tadupapatter ity ata āha --- tāsām anāditvaṃ cāśiṣo nityatvāt/ tāsāṃ vāsanānām anāditvaṃ
      ca na kevalam ānantaryam iti cārthaḥ/ āśiṣo nityatvāt/ ātmāśiṣo vāsanānām anāditve
      nityatvāvyabhicārād iti/ nanu svābhāvikatvenāpy upapatter asiddham āśiṣo nityatvam ity
      ata āha --- yeyam iti/ nāstikaḥ pṛcchati --- kasmāt/ uttaraṃ --- jātamātrasya jantor
      iti/ ata evaitasmiñ janmany ananubhūtamaraṇadharmakasya maraṇam eva dharmaḥ
      so+ananubhūto yena sa tathoktas tasya mātur aṅkāt praskhalataḥ kampamānasya
      māṅgalyacakrādilāñchitaṃ taduraḥsūtram atigāḍhaṃ pāṇigrāham avalambamānasya bālakasya
      kampabhedānumitā dveṣānuṣakte duḥkhe yā smṛtis tannimitto maraṇatrāsaḥ kathaṃ bhaved
      iti/ nanūktaṃ svabhāvād ity ata āha --- na ca svābhāvikaṃ vastu nimittam upādatte
      gṛhṇāti svotpattau/ etad uktaṃ bhavati --- bālakasyedṛśo dṛśyamānaḥ kampo
      bhayanibandhana īdṛśakampatvād asmadādikampavat/ bālakasya bhayaṃ
      dveṣaduḥkhasmṛtinimittaṃ

bhayatvād asmadādibhayavat/
      āgāmipratyavāyotprekṣālakṣaṇaṃ ca bhayaṃ na duḥkhasmṛtimātrād bhavati, api tu yato
      bibheti tasya pratyavāyahetubhāvam anumāya saṃpraty api pratyavāyaṃ bhayaṃ ca vidadhyād
      iti śaṅkate/ tasmād yajjātīyād anubhūtacarād dveṣānuṣaktaṃ duḥkham upapāditaṃ tasya
      smaraṇāt tajjātīyasyānubhūyamānasya tadduḥkhahetutvam anumāya tato bibheti/ na ca
      bālakenāsmiñ janmani skhalanasyānyatra duḥkhahetutvam avagatam/ na ca tādṛśaṃ duḥkham
      upalabdham/ tasmāt prāgbhavīyo 'nubhavaḥ pariśiṣyate/ tac caitad evaṃ prayogam ārohati
      --- jātamātrasya bālasya smṛtiḥ pūrvānubhavanibandhanā smṛtitvād asmadādismṛtivad iti/
      na ca padmasaṃkocavikāsāv api svābhāvikau/ na hi svābhāvikaṃ kāraṇāntaram apekṣate,
      vahner auṣṇyaṃ praty api kāraṇāntarāpekṣāprasaṅgāt/ tasmād āgantukam
      aruṇakarasaṃparkamātram eva kamalinīvikāsakāraṇam/ saṃkocakāraṇaṃ ca saṃskāraḥ
      sthitisthāpaka iti/ evaṃ smitādyanumitaharṣādayo+api prāci bhave hetavo veditavyāḥ/ tad
      āstāṃ tāvat prakṛtam upasaṃharati --- tasmād iti/ nimittaṃ labdhavipākakālaṃ karma/
      pratilambho+abhivyaktiḥ/ prasaṅgataś cittaparimāṇavipratipattiṃ nirācikīrṣur
      vipratipattim āha --- ghaṭaprāsādeti/ dehapradeśavartikāryadarśanād dehād bahiḥ sadbhāve
      cittasya na pramāṇam asti/ na caitad aṇuparimāṇaṃ dīrghaśaṣkulībhakṣaṇādāv aparyāyeṇa
      jñānapañcakānutpādaprasaṅgāt/ na cānanubhūyamānakramakalpanāyāṃ pramāṇam asti/ na caikam
      aṇu mano nānādeśair indriyair aparyāyeṇa saṃbandhum arhati/ tat pāriśeṣyāt kāyaparimāṇaṃ
      cittaṃ ghaṭaprāsādavartipradīpavat/ saṃkocavikāśau puttikāhastidehayor asyotpatsyete/
      śarīraparimāṇam evākāraḥ parimāṇaṃ yasyety apare pratipannāḥ/ nanv evaṃ katham asya
      kṣetrabījasaṃyogaḥ/ na khalv etad anāśrayaṃ mṛtaśarīrān mātṛpitṛdehavartinī lohitaretasī
      prāpnoti paratantratvāt/ na hi sthāṇvādiṣv agacchatsu tacchāyā gacchati/ na cāgacchati
      paṭe tadāśrayaṃ citraṃ gacchati/ tathā ca na saṃsāraḥ syād ity ata āha --- tathā
      cāntarābhāvaḥ saṃsāraś ca yukta iti/ tathā ca śarīraparimāṇatve dehāntaraprāptaye
children.translated_text: because it is fear, like our own fear. And fear, which has the nature of apprehension of future calamity, does not arise merely from the memory of suffering; rather, having inferred that what one fears has the capacity to cause calamity, one experiences both calamity and fear even in the present — thus he raises the objection. Therefore, from the remembrance of suffering connected with aversion of that very kind previously experienced, having inferred that a presently experienced thing of that same kind is a cause of such suffering, one fears it. But the baby has not recognized in this birth that falling is a cause of suffering elsewhere. Nor has it experienced such suffering. Therefore, the experience from a previous existence is what remains [as the explanation]. And this amounts to the following formal argument: the memory of a newborn baby is based on prior experience — because it is memory, like our own memory. Nor is the closing and opening of the lotus natural [in the relevant sense]. For a natural [property] does not require an external cause — otherwise even the heat of fire would require an external cause. Therefore, the adventitious contact with the rays of the sun alone is the cause of the lotus's opening. And the cause of its closing is the restorative <s>saṃskāra</s> (impressions tending to restore the original state). Similarly, the joy and other [emotions] inferred from smiling and the like should also be understood as having their causes in previous existence. Setting that aside, he concludes the topic at hand — 'therefore' etc. 'Cause' (<s>nimitta</s>) means <s>karma</s> whose time for ripening has arrived. 'Attainment' means manifestation. Incidentally wishing to resolve the dispute about the size of the mind, he states the dispute — 'pot, palace' etc. Since we observe effects located in [particular] parts of the body, there is no evidence for the mind's existence outside the body. Nor is this [mind] atomic in size, because in the simultaneous consumption of a long pastry, there would follow the impossibility of the five cognitions arising simultaneously. Nor is there evidence for positing a sequence that is not actually experienced. Nor can a single atomic mind have simultaneous contact with sense organs located in different parts [of the body]. Therefore, by elimination, the mind is body-sized, like a lamp placed in a pot or a palace. Its contraction and expansion would occur [proportionally] in the bodies of an insect and an elephant. Shape alone — the bodily dimension — is its size, as others have held. But then how does this [mind] conjoin with the field and seed [i.e., with the place and cause of rebirth]? For this [mind], not being without a substrate, does not — being dependent [on the body] — reach the blood and semen residing in the bodies of the mother and father from a dead body. For when posts and the like do not move, their shadows do not move [independently]. Nor when a cloth does not move does the painting on it move. And so there would be no <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) — hence he says: 'And so the intermediate state and <s>saṃsāra</s> are justified.' And so, if [the mind] is body-sized, for the attainment of another body,

children.text:
pūrvadehatyāgo dehāntaraprāptiś cāntarāsyātivāhikaśarīrasaṃyogād bhavatas
      tena khalv ayaṃ dehāntare saṃcaret/ tathā ca purāṇam ---
children.translated_text: the abandonment of the previous body and the attainment of another body occur through conjunction with the intermediate subtle body (<s>ātivāhika-śarīra</s>); through that, indeed, [the soul] transmigrates to another body. And so [says] the <s>Purāṇa</s> —

One might object: let the <s>vāsanās</s> imprinted by previous and still earlier births manifest — but only if there is proof for the existence of such previous births; and that proof does not exist. Nor can the mere observation of joy and sorrow in a newborn creature serve as proof, since that can be explained as natural, like the closing and opening of a lotus — hence he says: 'And the beginninglessness of those [<s>vāsanās</s>] is because of the eternality of the will-to-live.' 'Of those' — of the <s>vāsanās</s>. 'And beginninglessness' — not merely continuity, the word 'and' indicates this additional meaning. 'Because of the eternality of the will-to-live' — because the eternality of the self-directed will-to-live (<s>ātmāśis</s>) is invariably concomitant with the beginninglessness of <s>vāsanās</s>. Now, since this can also be explained as natural, the eternality of the will-to-live is unestablished — hence he says — 'this which' etc. The materialist asks: 'why?' The answer: 'of a creature just born' etc. Therefore, for a being that has not experienced death in this very birth — 'death is its <s>dharma</s> (fate); that which is unexperienced' — one who has not experienced that [death] is so described — the fear of death, inferred from the trembling of a baby who, slipping from the mother's lap, while trembling, grasps extremely tightly the auspicious thread on her chest marked with the <s>māṅgalya-cakra</s> and the like — that trembling, [which indicates] memory related to suffering connected with aversion — how could it arise? Now, it was said 'from nature' — hence he says: 'A natural thing does not require a cause for its own arising.' What has been said amounts to this: the trembling of such a kind observed in a baby is rooted in fear — because it is such trembling, like our own trembling. The fear of the baby is caused by memory of suffering connected with aversion,

children.text:
so+ayam antarābhāvaḥ/ ata eva saṃsāraś ca yukta iti/ tad etad amṛṣyamāṇaḥ svamatam āha
      --- vṛttir evāsya vibhunaś cittasya saṃkocavikāsinīty ācāryaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ pratipede/ idam
      atrākūtaṃ --- yady anāśrayaṃ cittaṃ na dehāntarasaṃcāri katham etad ātivāhikam āśrayate,
      tatrāpi dehāntarakalpanāyām anavasthā/ na cāsya dehān niṣkarṣaḥ sātivāhikasya
      saṃbhavati/ niṣkṛṣṭasya cetasas tatsaṃbandhāt/ astu tarhi sūkṣmaśarīram evā sargād ā ca
      mahāpralayān niyataṃ cittānām adhiṣṭhānaṃ ṣāṭkauśikaśarīram adhyavarti/ tena hi cittam ā
      satyalokād ā cāvīces tatra tatra śarīre saṃcarati/ niṣkarṣaś cāsyopapannaḥ ṣāṭkauśikāt
      kāyāt/ tatra hi tadantarābhāvas tasya niyatatvāt/ na cāsyāpi sadbhāve pramāṇam asti/ na
      khalv etad adhyakṣagocaraḥ/ na ca saṃsāro+asyānumānam/ ācāryamatenāpy upapatteḥ/ āgamas
      tu puruṣasya niṣkarṣam āha/ na ca cittaṃ vā sūkṣmaśarīraṃ vā puruṣaḥ kiṃ tu citiśaktir
      apratisaṃkramā/ na cāsyā niṣkarṣaḥ saṃbhavatīty aupacāriko vyākhyeyaḥ/ tathā ca citeś
      cittasya ca tatra tatra vṛttyabhāva eva niṣkarṣārthaḥ/ yac ca smṛtītihāsapurāṇeṣu
      maraṇānantaraṃ pretaśarīraprāptis tadvimokaś ca sapiṇḍīkaraṇādibhir ity uktaṃ tad
      anujānīmaḥ/ ātivāhikatvaṃ tasya na mṛṣyāmahe/ na cātrāsti kaścid āgamaḥ/ labdhaśarīra
      eva ca yamapuruṣair api pāśabaddho nīyate/ na tv ātivāhikaśarīraḥ/ tasmād āhaṃkārikatvāc
      cetaso 'haṃkārasya ca gaganamaṇḍalavat trailokyavyāpitvād vibhutvaṃ manasaḥ/ evaṃ ced
      asya vṛttir api vibhvīti sarvajñatāpattir ity ata uktaṃ vṛttir evāsyeti/ syād etat/
      cittamātrādhīnāyā vṛtteḥ saṃkocavikāsau kutaḥ kādācitkāv ity ata āha --- tac ca cittaṃ
      dharmādinimittāpekṣam/ vṛttau nimittaṃ vibhajate --- nimittaṃ ceti/
      ādigrahaṇenendriyadhanādayo gṛhyante/ śraddhādīty atrāpi vīryasmṛtyādayo gṛhyante/
      āntaratve saṃmatim ācāryāṇām āha --- tathā coktam/

vihāro vyāpāraḥ/
      prakṛṣṭaṃ śuklaṃ, tayor bāhyābhyantarayor madhye/ jñānavairāgye tajjanito dharmaḥ
      (tajjanitau dharmau) kena bāhyasādhyena dharmeṇātiśayyete abhibhūyete/ jñānavairāgyajāv
      eva dharmau tam abhibhavataḥ, bījabhāvād apanayata ity arthaḥ/ atraiva suprasiddham
      udāharaṇam āha --- daṇḍakāraṇyam iti //4.10//
children.translated_text: <s>vihāra</s> means activity. <s>Prakṛṣṭa</s> means pure white; between those two, the external and internal. The <s>dharma</s> (merit) born of knowledge and detachment — by what externally accomplished <s>dharma</s> is it surpassed or overcome? The <s>dharmas</s> born of knowledge and detachment alone overcome that, removing it from its seed-state — this is the meaning. He gives a well-known example for this very point — '<s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s>' and so on. //4.10//

This is the intermediate state. And therefore transmigration (<s>saṃsāra</s>) is also justified. Not accepting this, he states his own view — 'The modification alone of this all-pervading mind contracts and expands' — thus the teacher <s>Svayambhū</s> understood. Here the intention is this: if the mind without a support does not transmigrate to another body, how can it take on the <s>ātivāhika</s> (transmigrating) [body]? Even there, in postulating another body, there would be infinite regress. Nor is it possible for the mind together with the <s>ātivāhika</s> body to be extracted from the [gross] body, because even when extracted the mind would still be connected to it. Let it be then that the subtle body (<s>sūkṣmaśarīra</s>) alone — the body composed of six sheaths — existing from creation until the great dissolution, is the fixed substratum of minds. For by means of that, the mind moves from body to body, from <s>Satyaloka</s> all the way down to <s>Avīci</s>. And its extraction from the six-sheathed body is justified, for the intermediate state exists therein due to its permanence. But there is no valid means of knowledge for its existence either. For this is not an object of direct perception. Nor is transmigration an inference for it, since it is explained by the teacher's doctrine as well. Scripture, however, speaks of the extraction of the <s>Puruṣa</s>. But neither the mind nor the subtle body is the <s>Puruṣa</s>; rather, it is the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>), which does not transmigrate. And since extraction is not possible for it, [the scriptural statement] should be interpreted figuratively. Thus, for consciousness and for the mind, the absence of activity here and there is what is meant by 'extraction.' And what is said in the <s>smṛti</s>, <s>itihāsa</s>, and <s>purāṇas</s> — that after death there is attainment of a ghostly body and liberation from it through <s>sapiṇḍīkaraṇa</s> and other rites — that we accept. But we do not accept its being <s>ātivāhika</s> in nature. And there is no scriptural authority for this. One who has obtained a [new gross] body is led bound by the noose of <s>Yama</s>'s servants — not one with an <s>ātivāhika</s> body. Therefore, since the mind is a product of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), and since <s>ahaṃkāra</s> pervades the three worlds like the expanse of the sky, the mind is all-pervading. If so, then its modification too would be all-pervading, resulting in omniscience — to this he says 'the modification alone of this' and so on. There might be this [objection]: whence the occasional contraction and expansion of the modification, which depends on the mind alone? To this he says — 'And that mind depends on causes such as <s>dharma</s> and the like.' He distributes the causes of the modification — 'And the cause' and so on. By the word 'and the like' [after <s>dharma</s>], sense organs, wealth, and so on are included. In 'beginning with <s>śraddhā</s> (faith),' <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), <s>smṛti</s> (memory), and the like are also included. Regarding the internal nature,

children.text: hetuphalāśrayālambanaiḥ saṃgṛhītatvād eṣām abhāve tadabhāvaḥ //4.11//
children.translated_text: Because they are held together by cause, fruit, substratum, and support, in their absence there is the absence of those [<s>vāsanās</s>]. //4.11//

children.text:
athaitāś cittavṛttayo vāsanāś cānādayaś cet katham āsām ucchedaḥ/ na khalu citiśaktir
      anādir ucchidyata ity ata āha --- hetuphalāśrayālambanaiḥ saṃgṛhītatvād eṣām abhāve
      tadabhāvaḥ/ anāder api samucchedo dṛṣṭaḥ/ tadyathānāgatatvasyeti savyabhicāratvād
      asādhanam/ citiśaktis tu vināśakāraṇābhāvān na vinaśyati, na tv anāditvāt/ uktaṃ ca
      vāsanānām anādīnām api samucchede kāraṇaṃ sūtreṇeti/ anugrahopaghātāv api
      dharmādharmādinimittam upalakṣayataḥ/ tena surāpānādayo+api saṃgṛhītā bhavanti/ netrī
      nāyikā/ atraiva hetum āha --- mūlam iti/ pratyutpannatā vartamānatā na tu
      dharmasvarūpotpādaḥ/ atraiva hetum āha --- na hīti/ yad abhimukhībhūtaṃ vastu
      kāminīsaṃparkādi/ vyāpakābhāve vyāpyasyābhāva iti sūtrārthaḥ //4.11//
children.translated_text: Now, if these mental modifications (<s>cittavṛttis</s>) and <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) are beginningless, how can they be eradicated? Surely the beginningless power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>) is not eradicated — to this he says: 'Because they are held together by cause, fruit, substratum, and support, in their absence there is the absence of those.' Even of what is beginningless, complete eradication is observed. For example, the state of being future [of something] — but this is inconclusive and therefore not a valid proof. The power of consciousness, however, does not perish due to the absence of a cause of destruction — not because of its beginninglessness. And it has been said that the <s>sūtra</s> states the cause for the complete eradication of <s>vāsanās</s> even though they are beginningless. 'Assistance and harm' also indicate causes such as <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) and the like. By this, drinking of liquor and the like are also included. <s>Netrī</s> means the leading one. He gives the reason for this very point — 'the root' and so on. Contemporaneity means existing in the present.

children.text: atītānāgataṃ svarūpato+asty adhvabhedād dharmāṇām //4.12//
