      satyaṃ bho ity arthaḥ/ avibhajya vacanīyam uktvā pravibhajya vacanīyaṃ praśnam āha ---
      atha sarva iti/ vibhajya vacanīyatām āha --- vibhajyeti/ vibhajya vacanīyam eva
      praśnāntaraṃ vispaṣṭārtham āha --- tathā manuṣyeti/ ayaṃ tv avacanīya ekāntataḥ/ na hi
      sāmānyena kuśalākuśalapuruṣasaṃsārasyāntavattvam anantavattvaṃ vā śakyam ekāntato
      vaktum/ yathā prāṇabhṛnmātrasya śreyastvam aśreyastvaṃ vā naikāntataḥ śakyam
      avadhārayitum/ yathā jātamātrasya maraṇam ekāntataḥ/ vibhajya punaḥ śakyāvadhāraṇam ity
      āha --- kuśalasyeti/ ayam abhisaṃdhiḥ --- krameṇa mokṣe sarveṣāṃ mokṣāt saṃsāroccheda
      ity anumānaṃ, tac cāgamasiddhamokṣāśrayaṃ, tathā
      cābhyupagatamokṣapratipādakāgamapramāṇabhāvaḥ kathaṃ tam evāgamaṃ
      pradhānavikāranityatāyām apramāṇīkuryāt/ tasmād āgamabādhitaviṣayam etad anumānaṃ na
      pramāṇam/ śrūyate hi śrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇeṣu sargapratisargaparamparāyā anāditvam
      anantatvaṃ ceti/ api ca sarveṣām evātmanāṃ saṃsārasya na tāvad yugapaducchedaḥ saṃbhavī/
      na hi paṇḍitarūpāṇām apy anekajanmaparamparābhyāsapariśramasādhyā vivekakhyātipratiṣṭhā/
      kiṃ punaḥ prāṇabhṛnmātrasya sthāvarajaṅgamāder ekadākasmād bhavitum arhati/ na ca
      kāraṇāyaugapadye kāryayaugapadyaṃ yujyate/ krameṇa tu vivekakhyātāv asaṃkhyeyānāṃ
      krameṇa muktau na saṃsārocchedo+anantatvāj jantūnām asaṃkhyeyatvād iti sarvam
      avadātam //4.33//
children.translated_text: the absurd consequence of impermanence [would follow]. Nor is the appearance of unprecedented <s>sattvas</s> (beings) accepted, by which there would be infinity [of beings]. In that case, since beginninglessness would be contradicted, the absurd consequence of the destruction of the meaning of all scripture would arise — this is the purport. He answers — 'This is unanswerable' (<s>avacanīya</s>), unworthy of an answer. To show the absolute unanswerability of this, he shows a question that is absolutely answerable — 'There is a question...' The question and answer 'Every born being will die' — 'Yes, indeed' (<s>oṃ bho</s>). 'Truly, sir' is the meaning. Having stated what is answerable without distinction, he states a question that is answerable by making a distinction — 'Now, whether all...' He states the answerability by distinction — 'By distinguishing...' He states another question answerable by distinction with a clearer meaning — 'Thus, a human being...' But this one is absolutely unanswerable. For neither the finiteness nor the infiniteness of the <s>saṃsāra</s> of <s>puruṣas</s> in general — both virtuous and non-virtuous — can be stated absolutely. Just as the beneficialness or non-beneficialness of a mere living being cannot be determined absolutely. Just as death is certain for what is born. But by making a distinction, it can be determined — hence he says — 'Of the virtuous...' The intended meaning is this: the inference that 'through gradual <s>mokṣa</s>, because of the liberation of all, there would be cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s>' — that inference depends on <s>mokṣa</s> established by scripture. And so, having accepted the authoritative status of the scripture that teaches <s>mokṣa</s>, how could one deny the authoritativeness of that same scripture regarding the eternality of the transformations of <s>pradhāna</s>? Therefore, this inference, whose subject matter is contradicted by scripture, is not authoritative. For it is heard in <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>itihāsa</s>, and <s>purāṇa</s> that the succession of creation and dissolution is beginningless and endless. Moreover, the simultaneous cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s> for all selves is not possible. For even for those who are wise, the establishment of <s>viveka-khyāti</s> (discriminative discernment) requires effort achieved through the practice of numerous successions of births. How much less could it happen suddenly for all beings — stationary and moving? Nor is the simultaneity of effects possible without the simultaneity of causes. But through gradual attainment of <s>viveka-khyāti</s>, and through the gradual liberation of innumerable beings, there is no cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s>, because of the infinitude and innumerability of living beings — thus everything is clarified. (4.33)

At this juncture, he asks about the sequence of transformation — 'now what is this' etc. 'Sequence, which correlates with moments and is apprehended at the final stage of transformation.' The 'sequence of transformation' correlates with moments — that whose correlate is the moment is so described. The meaning is: it depends on an accumulation of moments. Sequence can never be determined without something that possesses sequence. Nor does a single moment have sequence. Therefore, what remains is that [sequence] depends on an accumulation of moments. This he states — 'the unbroken succession of moments' etc. He states the proof of the sequence of transformation — 'of transformation' etc. For even a new cloth, though carefully preserved, after a long time is seen to become old. This final stage of transformation — the terminus — is the conclusion; by that the sequence of transformation [is known]. Prior to that oldness too, the successive order of [states such as] subtle, subtler, subtlest, gross, grosser, grossest, and so on is inferred. He shows this very point through the negative formulation — 'for indeed not' etc. 'That which has not been experienced, not attained' — the moment of sequence [so described]. Now, this sequence is not possible for <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial nature), since it is eternal — hence he says —

children.text:
puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ guṇānāṃ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṃ svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā citiśaktir
	iti //4.34//
children.translated_text: <s>Kaivalya</s> (liberation) is the counter-involution (<s>pratiprasava</s>) of the <s>guṇas</s> that are devoid of purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s>, or [it is] the establishment of the power of consciousness (<s>citi-śakti</s>) in its own nature (<s>svarūpa-pratiṣṭhā</s>). (4.34)

children.text: iti śrīpatañjaliviracitayogasūtreṣu caturthaḥ kaivalyapādaḥ //4//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>Kaivalya Pāda</s> (Chapter on Liberation) in the <s>Yoga Sūtras</s> composed by Śrī <s>Patañjali</s>. (4)

children.text:
kaivalyarūpāvadhāraṇaparasya sūtrasyāvāntarasaṃgatim āha --- guṇādhikāreti/
      puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ guṇānāṃ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṃ svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā citiśaktir iti/
      kṛtakaraṇīyatayā puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ yaḥ pratiprasavaḥ svakāraṇe pradhāne layas teṣāṃ
      kāryakāraṇātmakānāṃ guṇānāṃ vyutthānasamādhinirodhasaṃskārā manasi līyante mano
      'smitāyām asmitā liṅge liṅgam aliṅga iti/ yo+ayaṃ guṇānāṃ kāryakāraṇātmakānāṃ
      pratisargas tat kaivalyam/ yaṃ kaṃcit puruṣaṃ prati pradhānasya mokṣaḥ svarūpapratiṣṭhā
      vā puruṣasya mokṣa ity āha --- svarūpeti/ asti hi mahāpralaye+api svarūpapratiṣṭhā
      citiśaktiḥ/ na cāsau mokṣa ity ata āha --- punar iti/ sautra itiśabdaḥ
      śāstraparisamāptau //4.34//
children.translated_text: He states the internal coherence of the <s>sūtra</s> whose purpose is the ascertainment of the nature of <s>kaivalya</s> — 'The subject of the <s>guṇas</s>...' '<s>Kaivalya</s> is the counter-involution of the <s>guṇas</s> that are devoid of purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s>, or the establishment of the power of consciousness in its own nature.' The counter-involution (<s>pratiprasava</s>) of the <s>guṇas</s> — which consist of cause and effect — that are devoid of purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s> because their task has been accomplished, is the dissolution into their cause, <s>pradhāna</s>: the <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions) of <s>vyutthāna</s> (outward-turning), <s>samādhi</s>, and <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) dissolve into <s>manas</s> (mind), <s>manas</s> into <s>asmitā</s> (I-sense), <s>asmitā</s> into <s>liṅga</s> (the manifest), <s>liṅga</s> into <s>aliṅga</s> (the unmanifest). This counter-involution of the <s>guṇas</s>, consisting of cause and effect, is <s>kaivalya</s>. The liberation of <s>pradhāna</s> with respect to any particular <s>Puruṣa</s>, or the establishment of <s>Puruṣa</s> in his own nature as liberation — this he says: 'In its own nature...' For even in <s>mahāpralaya</s> (great dissolution) there is the establishment of <s>citi-śakti</s> (power of consciousness) in its own nature. But that is not <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — to this he says: 'Again...' The word '<s>iti</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> marks the conclusion of the treatise. (4.34)

children.text:
muktyarhacittaṃ paralokameyajñasiddhaye dharmaghanaḥ samādhiḥ/ dvayī ca muktiḥ
      pratipāditāsmin pāde prasaṅgād api cānyad uktam //1// nidānaṃ tāpānām
      uditam atha tāpāś ca kathitāḥ sahāṅgair aṣṭābhir vihitam iha yogadvayam api// kṛto
      mukter adhvā guṇapuruṣabhedaḥ sphuṭataro viviktaṃ kaivalyaṃ parigalitatāpā citir
      asau //2//
children.translated_text: <s>Samādhi</s> [is taught] as a mass of <s>dharma</s> for the sake of the mind fit for liberation, and for establishing knowledge of the world beyond and the <s>meya</s> (knowable). And twofold liberation has been set forth in this chapter, and other [topics] have been stated incidentally as well. (1) The cause of afflictions (<s>tāpas</s>) has been taught, and the afflictions have been described; together with the eight limbs, the twofold <s>yoga</s> has been prescribed herein. The path to liberation has been made, the distinction between <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> made clearer; <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) is set apart — this consciousness (<s>citi</s>), freed from afflictions, is that [liberation]. (2)

children.text: iti śrīvācaspatimiśraviracitāyāṃ pātañjalabhāṣyavyākhyāyāṃ kaivalyapādaś caturthaḥ //4//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>Kaivalya Pāda</s> (Chapter on Liberation) in the commentary on the <s>Pātañjala Bhāṣya</s> composed by Śrī <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>. (4)

body.translated_text: Thus is completed this <s>Pātañjala Yoga Darśana</s> (Patañjali's Yoga Philosophy) together with the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) and <s>Ṭīkā</s> (subcommentary).
